title: Carbon and nitrogen stoichiometry of saprotrophic fungal biomass during litter decomposition: evidence from ergosterol and amino sugar analysis
abstract: To assess stoichiometric constraints on fungal decomposers, we measured ergosterol (fungal biomass proxy), glucosamine (chitin-derived, total fungal cell wall), and muramic acid (bacterial biomass proxy) in litter samples collected from three oak-hornbeam stands on Fruška Gora across four decomposition stages spanning 24 months. Fungal C:N ratios estimated from glucosamine-corrected biomass ranged from 8.1 to 14.3, consistent with published values for ascomycete-dominated early-stage communities shifting to basidiomycete-dominated late-stage communities. Bacterial biomass (muramic acid) was consistently 6–12 times lower than fungal biomass across all stages. Nitrogen immobilisation in fungal biomass was greatest during the middle decomposition stage (months 6–14), coinciding with peak lignocellulolytic enzyme activity and a transient decrease in litter N concentration. The ratio of ergosterol to glucosamine decreased significantly from stage I to stage IV (from 3.8 to 1.9 µg mg⁻¹), reflecting a shift in community from ergosterol-rich ascomycetes to ergosterol-poor basidiomycetes. These data provide quantitative support for the succession model proposed in earlier field studies from these sites.

title: Revisiting twenty years of litter decomposition data from Fruška Gora: trends under changing precipitation patterns
abstract: This synthesis revisits litter decomposition and saprotrophic fungal biomass data collected at three permanent sites on Fruška Gora between 1997 and 2019, integrating published datasets with unpublished archival records totalling 22 site-years. Linear mixed models were fitted to test for temporal trends in annual mass loss rate, ergosterol concentration, and laccase activity, with mean annual precipitation (MAP) and mean growing-season temperature as covariates. Annual mass loss rates showed a marginally significant declining trend over the study period (β = −0.006 yr⁻¹, p = 0.048), associated with a decrease in MAP of approximately 38 mm per decade recorded at the nearby Irig meteorological station. Ergosterol concentrations declined in parallel (β = −4.1 µg g⁻¹ decade⁻¹, p = 0.031). Temperature showed no independent significant effect after accounting for precipitation. These patterns are consistent with regional climate projections for the southern Pannonian lowlands and suggest that if precipitation continues to decline, carbon accumulation in forest floors of this region may increase modestly over coming decades.
venue: Acta Mycologica Pannonica

title: Building a Bilingual Learner Corpus for Serbian–Hungarian Code-Switching Research
abstract: This paper describes the design, collection, and annotation methodology of the SerbHun Learner Corpus (SHLC), a resource intended to support computational and applied linguistic research on Serbian–Hungarian bilingual production. The corpus contains 1,200 spoken and written samples collected from 310 bilingual speakers in Subotica, Senta, and Ada between 2010 and 2013. Spoken data were transcribed using a modified CHAT format and aligned with audio recordings stored at 44.1 kHz. Written samples include school essays, informal messages, and administrative texts. Annotation layers cover language choice at the token level, part-of-speech tags assigned with a custom rule-based tagger, and manually verified morphosyntactic labels. The paper discusses tokenisation challenges specific to Hungarian agglutinative morphology when embedded in Serbian matrix clauses. Inter-annotator agreement for language-boundary detection is reported at 0.81 kappa. The corpus currently holds 1.4 million tokens and is accessible under a Creative Commons licence through the university repository.

title: A Rule-Based Morphosyntactic Tagger for Serbian–Hungarian Code-Switched Text
abstract: Automatic part-of-speech tagging of code-switched text presents difficulties not addressed by monolingual taggers, particularly when the switched language (Hungarian) is morphologically much richer than the matrix language (Serbian). This paper presents a rule-based tagger developed specifically for Serbian–Hungarian mixed text, built on finite-state transducers implemented in the Foma toolkit. The system operates in two stages: a language identification layer assigns a language label to each token using a character n-gram model trained on 500,000 tokens per language, followed by language-specific morphological analysis modules. On a held-out test set of 18,400 tokens drawn from the SHLC corpus, the tagger achieves 84.2% token-level accuracy overall, rising to 88.9% on Serbian-origin tokens and falling to 78.1% on Hungarian-origin tokens due to greater morphological ambiguity. Error analysis reveals that noun-case disambiguation accounts for 43% of remaining errors. The tagger is released as an open-source Python package.

title: Contrastive Analysis of Nominal Case Systems in Serbian and Hungarian: Implications for Automated Error Classification
abstract: Serbian and Hungarian both employ rich nominal case systems, but the underlying structural principles diverge substantially: Serbian case suffixes encode syntactic function and agreement, while Hungarian postpositional cases often encode spatial and semantic roles with limited agreement morphology. This paper presents a systematic contrastive analysis of the two nominal systems, drawing on descriptive grammars and a parallel corpus of 210 translated administrative and literary texts (approximately 320,000 words per language). Alignment was performed semi-automatically using a modified Gale–Church algorithm. The analysis identifies 34 recurrent cross-language mappings and 12 structurally ambiguous correspondences that are predicted to generate systematic learner errors in both directions. Each mapping is formalised as a rewrite rule suitable for incorporation into an error-classification module. A pilot evaluation on 2,300 annotated learner sentences shows that rule application improves F1 for case-error detection from 0.61 to 0.73 compared to a baseline lexicon-only classifier. The paper includes a detailed appendix of contrastive rule tables.

title: Automatic Detection of Morphosyntactic Transfer Errors in Serbian–Hungarian Bilingual Writing
abstract: This paper presents the computational component of the author's doctoral research: a pipeline for detecting morphosyntactic transfer errors in written Serbian produced by Hungarian L1 speakers. The system combines the rule-based tagger described in earlier work with a maximum-entropy classifier trained on 6,400 annotated sentences from the SHLC corpus, using features derived from the contrastive rule tables. Five error types are targeted: verbal aspect, case government, definiteness marking, adjectival agreement, and word order in embedded clauses. On a separate test partition of 1,100 sentences, the pipeline achieves macro-averaged F1 scores ranging from 0.58 (word order) to 0.79 (adjectival agreement). Comparison with human annotators on a 200-sentence blind sample shows that the system identifies 71% of errors flagged by at least two of three annotators. Discussion addresses limitations related to sparse training data for lower-frequency error types and proposes augmentation strategies using back-translation.

title: A Grammar-Error Detection Tool for Serbian Language Teachers Working in Bilingual Schools
abstract: This paper describes the design and classroom evaluation of GrEDSH, a browser-based tool that assists Serbian language teachers in identifying and categorising morphosyntactic errors in student writing in schools where Hungarian is the primary language of instruction. The tool builds on the error-detection pipeline developed in prior work, packaged as a REST API with a lightweight web front-end. Teachers paste or upload student texts; the tool highlights suspected errors and provides short contrastive explanations in both Serbian and Hungarian. A pilot study involving 14 teachers across six schools in Vojvodina compared teachers' unaided correction of 40 student texts against correction assisted by GrEDSH over a four-week period. Assisted correction identified 22% more errors and reduced average correction time by 11 minutes per text. Teacher satisfaction ratings (five-point Likert scale) averaged 3.9 for usefulness and 3.6 for interface usability. Known limitations include a false-positive rate of 18% for word-order flagging.

title: Switch-Point Prediction in Serbian–Hungarian Code-Switched Text Using Syntactic Dependency Features
abstract: Predicting where a speaker will switch languages within a sentence is useful for both theoretical modelling and downstream NLP tasks such as language identification and parsing. This study frames switch-point prediction as a sequence labelling problem and experiments with three model architectures: a bidirectional LSTM, a CRF over hand-crafted features, and a fine-tuned adapter layer on top of the continued-pre-training XLM-R model from earlier work. Features include dependency arc labels extracted by a cross-lingual dependency parser, character n-grams, and morphological complexity scores. Experiments use 28,000 code-switched sentences from SHLC, split 70/15/15. The adapter-based model achieves a token-level F1 of 0.83 for switch-point detection, compared to 0.76 for the BiLSTM and 0.71 for the CRF. Analysis of errors shows that the model struggles most at noun-phrase boundaries involving Hungarian possessive suffixes attached to Serbian loanword stems, a pattern discussed in detail.

title: Hydrothermal synthesis of monoclinic BiVO₄ powders: influence of pH and reaction time on crystal morphology and optical absorption
abstract: Monoclinic scheelite BiVO₄ powders were synthesised hydrothermally at temperatures between 140 °C and 200 °C, varying pH from 3 to 9 and reaction time from 4 to 24 hours. X-ray diffraction confirmed phase-pure monoclinic product above 160 °C at pH 7. Scanning electron microscopy revealed a transition from irregular aggregates to well-defined decahedral particles with increasing temperature. UV-Vis diffuse reflectance spectroscopy showed direct optical band gaps in the range 2.38–2.46 eV depending on particle size. BET specific surface areas ranged from 2.1 to 6.8 m² g⁻¹. Preliminary photocatalytic tests with methyl orange under a 150 W tungsten-halogen lamp indicated up to 64% decolourisation in 120 minutes for the sample prepared at 180 °C, pH 7, 12 hours. These results establish a reproducible baseline synthesis protocol for subsequent composite studies.

title: Preparation of BiVO₄/TiO₂ composites by mechanical mixing and sol-gel coating: structural and optical comparison
abstract: Two preparation routes were compared for fabricating BiVO₄/TiO₂ composites with BiVO₄ weight fractions of 10, 20, 30, and 50 wt%. In the mechanical mixing route, individually synthesised powders were ball-milled for 2 hours. In the sol-gel coating route, pre-formed BiVO₄ particles were coated with a titanium isopropoxide-derived TiO₂ layer and calcined at 400 °C. XRD analysis showed no new crystalline phases in either series. UV-Vis DRS demonstrated a red-shift in absorption edge and reduced band gap (2.65–2.72 eV) compared to pure TiO₂ (3.18 eV) for sol-gel coated samples. Photoluminescence measurements indicated effective charge carrier separation at the heterojunction in the sol-gel series. Degradation of Acid Orange 7 (20 mg L⁻¹) under visible irradiation reached 82% in 90 minutes for the 30 wt% sol-gel composite, compared to 54% for its mechanically mixed counterpart and 21% for pure TiO₂.

title: Reactive oxygen species in BiVO₄/TiO₂ photocatalysis: scavenger experiments and EPR spin-trapping evidence
abstract: The dominant reactive species responsible for azo dye degradation over a 30 wt% BiVO₄/TiO₂ composite were identified using a combination of scavenger experiments and electron paramagnetic resonance spin-trapping with DMPO. Addition of isopropanol (hydroxyl radical scavenger, 10 mM) reduced Reactive Blue 4 degradation from 88% to 31% after 120 minutes under visible light, while benzoquinone (superoxide scavenger, 1 mM) reduced it to 52%. DMPO–OH adducts were clearly detected by EPR after 10 minutes of irradiation in aqueous suspension. Hole scavenging with EDTA (5 mM) reduced degradation to 61%, indicating a secondary but significant direct oxidation pathway. Control experiments in the dark confirmed negligible adsorption-driven removal. These findings indicate that hydroxyl radicals are the primary oxidant in this system, with superoxide radicals contributing as secondary species.

title: Influence of TiO₂ polymorph (anatase vs. rutile vs. P25-equivalent) on the photocatalytic performance of BiVO₄/TiO₂ composites
abstract: Three TiO₂ polymorphs—laboratory-synthesised anatase, rutile, and a commercial mixed-phase powder equivalent to P25—were used to prepare 30 wt% BiVO₄/TiO₂ composites by the sol-gel coating route. Phase purity was confirmed by XRD; anatase crystallite sizes were 12 nm, rutile 28 nm, and mixed-phase 21 nm (mean anatase). BET surface areas were 48, 9, and 52 m² g⁻¹ respectively. Under visible-light irradiation (λ > 420 nm), the anatase-based composite degraded Direct Red 23 (15 mg L⁻¹, pH 5.5) by 91% in 150 minutes, compared to 68% for mixed-phase and 44% for rutile-based composites. First-order rate constants were 0.0148, 0.0089, and 0.0042 min⁻¹. Higher surface area and favourable conduction band alignment with BiVO₄ are proposed to explain the anatase advantage. Reuse experiments over five cycles showed less than 7% activity loss for the anatase composite.

title: Photocatalytic degradation kinetics of Reactive Yellow 145 in simulated textile wastewater matrices using BiVO₄/TiO₂
abstract: The degradation of Reactive Yellow 145 (RY145) was studied in three matrices: ultrapure water, a synthetic textile effluent (NaCl 5 g L⁻¹, Na₂SO₄ 2 g L⁻¹, Na₂CO₃ 1 g L⁻¹) and a real textile mill effluent obtained from a fabric dyeing facility near Novi Sad. Catalyst loading was optimised at 0.75 g L⁻¹. In ultrapure water, pseudo-first-order degradation of RY145 (20 mg L⁻¹) was complete in 120 minutes (k = 0.028 min⁻¹). In synthetic effluent, rate decreased by 43% due to carbonate radical scavenging. In real effluent, colour removal reached 74% but TOC removal was only 29% after 180 minutes, indicating the presence of persistent co-contaminants. LC-MS analysis identified four intermediate products, all with cleaved azo bonds, and detected aniline derivatives that decreased below quantification limits after 180 minutes of extended irradiation.

title: Tungsten doping of BiVO₄ in BiVO₄/TiO₂ composites: effect on visible-light absorption and photocatalytic rate
abstract: Tungsten-doped BiVO₄ (W/V molar ratios 0.01, 0.03, 0.05) was prepared hydrothermally and incorporated into 30 wt% composites with anatase TiO₂. XRD confirmed retention of monoclinic scheelite structure up to W/V = 0.03, with secondary phase emergence at 0.05. UV-Vis DRS showed progressive narrowing of the optical band gap from 2.41 eV (undoped) to 2.28 eV (W/V = 0.03). Mott-Schottky analysis indicated increased donor density (from 1.8 × 10¹⁷ to 4.3 × 10¹⁷ cm⁻³) with W substitution. Photocatalytic degradation of Acid Red 88 (25 mg L⁻¹, pH 5) improved from 78% (undoped composite) to 91% (W/V = 0.03) in 90 minutes. Beyond 0.03, performance declined due to recombination centres introduced by lattice strain. Impedance spectroscopy under illumination confirmed reduced charge transfer resistance at the optimal doping level.

title: Co-exposure toxicity assessment of azo dye degradation products from BiVO₄/TiO₂ photocatalysis using Daphnia magna and Chlorella vulgaris bioassays
abstract: Photocatalytically treated solutions of Reactive Black 5, Acid Orange 7, and Reactive Yellow 145 (each 20 mg L⁻¹, 90% colour removal endpoint) were subjected to acute toxicity testing with Daphnia magna (48 h immobility test, EC₅₀) and growth inhibition testing with Chlorella vulgaris (72 h, ISO 8692). Untreated dye solutions showed EC₅₀ values of 14–48 mg L⁻¹ for Daphnia and 18–62 mg L⁻¹ growth inhibition thresholds for Chlorella. After photocatalytic treatment, Daphnia toxicity was reduced in all three cases; however, treated Acid Orange 7 solution retained significant Chlorella inhibition (EC₅₀ shift from 18 to 31 mg L⁻¹), attributed to persistent sulphanilic acid derivatives identified by HPLC-MS. These results demonstrate that colour removal alone is not a sufficient treatment endpoint and support the use of bioassays alongside chemical measurements in photocatalytic process evaluation.

title: Synthesis of BiVO₄/TiO₂/reduced graphene oxide ternary composites and their photocatalytic activity under natural solar irradiation
abstract: Ternary composites were prepared by incorporating reduced graphene oxide (rGO, 0.5–3 wt%) into a 30 wt% BiVO₄/anatase TiO₂ matrix via a facile hydrothermal route. Raman spectroscopy confirmed the D/G band intensity ratio indicative of partial reduction (I_D/I_G ≈ 1.12). Transient photocurrent measurements showed a 2.3-fold increase in photocurrent density for the 1 wt% rGO composite compared to rGO-free material, indicating improved charge transport through the graphene network. Outdoor degradation experiments (June, Novi Sad, 43.8°N, solar irradiance 650–820 W m⁻²) with Direct Blue 71 (30 mg L⁻¹) in a 2 L open glass trough showed 94% colour removal and 61% TOC removal after 5 hours for the 1 wt% rGO composite. Higher rGO loadings decreased performance, attributed to light-blocking effects. Catalyst recovery by sedimentation exceeded 95% after three outdoor cycles.

title: Photocatalytic removal of the azo dye Disperse Orange 25 from synthetic polyester dyebath effluent: pH effects and reuse of catalyst in a fluidised bed configuration
abstract: Disperse Orange 25 (DO25) is a sulphonate-free azo dye used predominantly for polyester dyeing and represents a poorly studied substrate for photocatalysis. Experiments at pH 3, 5, 7, and 9 with 30 wt% BiVO₄/TiO₂ (0.5 g L⁻¹) under visible light showed maximum degradation at pH 5 (96% colour removal, 68% TOC removal in 120 min) due to favourable electrostatic interaction between the positively charged catalyst surface and the neutral dye. A laboratory-scale fluidised bed reactor (300 mL, glass bead catalyst support) was operated in continuous mode at 10 mL min⁻¹ influent. Steady-state colour removal at pH 5 was 81% after 90 minutes of hydraulic residence time. Catalyst-coated bead stability was evaluated over 20 operating days; XRD and ICP-OES of effluent showed no significant leaching of Bi or V above 0.05 mg L⁻¹. Colour and COD measurements complied with Serbian effluent discharge limits (Regulation 67/2011) after treatment.

title: Hedging in Research Articles by Novice and Experienced Serbian EFL Writers: A Comparative Analysis
abstract: The paper compares hedging density and device type in research articles written in English by two groups: postgraduate students (n=45) and established academics with at least ten publications (n=45), all affiliated with universities in Vojvodina. A purpose-built corpus of 270 articles (approximately 1.8 million words) was annotated for hedges following a taxonomy adapted from Hyland (2005). Statistical comparison used Mann–Whitney U tests. Novice writers produced significantly fewer lexical hedges per thousand words (3.1 vs. 5.4) but relied more heavily on modal verbs relative to other hedge types. Experienced writers showed greater variety, including more frequent use of approximators and attitude verbs. The discussion addresses whether the difference reflects rhetorical competence, academic socialisation, or genre familiarity, and recommends targeted instructional interventions at the doctoral training stage.

title: A Pedagogical Grammar of Hedging for Serbian Doctoral Candidates Writing in English
abstract: This book chapter presents a descriptive-pedagogical account of hedging grammar developed from a 600,000-word corpus of Serbian academic English. The chapter covers four categories: modal auxiliaries, lexical verbs of cognition and speech, approximators and shields, and compound hedges. For each category, annotated corpus examples are provided alongside contrastive examples from native-speaker academic prose. The chapter argues that existing pedagogical grammars of English academic writing, largely based on native-speaker data, require supplementation with corpus evidence from specific EFL communities to address the actual transfer errors and avoidance patterns those communities exhibit. Frequency tables, example concordance lines, and a set of guided practice exercises are included. The chapter forms part of a wider edited volume on academic writing instruction in South-East European higher education.

title: Modal Downtoners in Serbian Medical English: The Case of 'Suggest' and 'Indicate' in Discussion Sections
abstract: Medical research articles present a specific challenge for hedging research because of the high-stakes nature of knowledge claims. This study focuses on the verbs 'suggest' and 'indicate' as hedging devices in the Discussion sections of 120 medical research articles written in English by Serbian authors, drawn from journals in internal medicine, cardiology, and oncology. A total of 648 instances of the two verbs were identified and analysed for their syntactic frames (followed by that-clause, NP, or infinitival construction) and the propositional content of the claim hedged. 'Suggest' occurs 2.8 times more frequently than 'indicate', and both appear more often in first-person constructions than in equivalent texts by British and American medical researchers. The pattern may reflect an interaction between L1 pragmatic norms and genre expectations acquired through translation of local-language research norms.

title: Teaching Epistemic Modality to Serbian Undergraduates: Outcomes of a Corpus-Informed Instruction Module
abstract: This paper reports on a quasi-experimental classroom study conducted at the Faculty of Philosophy, University of Novi Sad, involving 68 third-year English Studies undergraduates divided into a treatment group receiving corpus-informed instruction on epistemic modality (eight sessions, 45 minutes each) and a control group receiving standard coursebook-based instruction. Pre- and post-tests required participants to write a 300-word argumentative abstract and to complete a gap-fill recognition task. Texts were scored for hedge frequency, hedge variety, and appropriateness of hedge placement by two independent raters (inter-rater Cohen's κ = 0.81). The treatment group showed significantly greater gains in hedge variety (p < 0.01) and placement appropriateness (p < 0.05), though overall frequency gains did not reach significance. Student feedback indicated that concordance-based activities were perceived as useful but time-consuming.

title: Hedging Norms in Serbian Social Sciences: Evidence from a Multi-Genre Corpus
abstract: Social science disciplines in the Serbian academic tradition have a distinct relationship with empiricism and theoretical argumentation that may leave traces in the epistemic framing of English-language publications. This study draws on a multi-genre corpus of 340 texts (research articles, review articles, and conference papers, approximately 1.1 million words) from sociology, political science, and psychology, all authored by Serbian academics. Across genres, review articles contain the highest density of hedges (8.1 per thousand words), followed by conference papers (6.3) and research articles (5.9). Psychology texts are the most heavily hedged within the social sciences sample, consistent with the discipline's alignment with experimental norms. Hedging in sociology and political science shows greater reliance on approximators and epistemic parentheticals, which the paper links to the argumentative writing tradition prevalent in those disciplines.

title: Epistemic Stance in Grant Proposal English Written by Serbian Researchers: Obligation, Uncertainty, and Persuasion
abstract: Grant proposals constitute a relatively under-studied genre in corpus-based academic writing research, particularly for non-native English writer communities. This study analyses a purpose-built corpus of 60 project proposals submitted to competitive national and European funding calls by Serbian researchers between 2012 and 2017 (approximately 240,000 words). Stance annotation distinguishes epistemic hedges, deontic modals, and boosting expressions. Deontic modality is proportionally far more prominent in proposals than in research articles, accounting for 38% of all modal verb occurrences. Epistemic hedges cluster in the sections describing preliminary results and expected impact, while certainty markers dominate in sections presenting problem statements. The paper argues that the genre demands a distinctive blend of epistemic tentativeness and rhetorical assertiveness that is not adequately addressed in existing academic English writing guides for Serbian researchers.

title: Vague Language and Hedging in Serbian Science Journalism Translated from English: A Parallel Corpus Approach
abstract: Hedging and vague language do not survive translation uniformly; pragmatic norms of the target language and the conventions of popularising discourse can jointly distort the epistemic profile of scientific claims. This paper uses a parallel corpus of 80 science news articles originally published in English and their Serbian translations (total approximately 95,000 words per language) to examine how hedging devices are rendered. Systematic cross-linguistic mapping shows that 34% of English hedges are omitted in Serbian translation, 18% are strengthened (hedge replaced by assertion), and 11% are weakened (assertion replaced by hedge). Omission rates are highest for approximators and lowest for modal verbs. The findings are discussed in relation to science literacy and the public communication of uncertainty, with implications for translators and science communication educators.

title: Diachronic Change in Hedging Frequency in Serbian Academic English: 1995–2020
abstract: This longitudinal corpus study tracks changes in hedging frequency and device type in English-language research articles authored by Serbian academics across a 25-year period. A stratified diachronic corpus of 500 articles (ca. 2.5 million words) was constructed, sampling five disciplines at five-year intervals from 1995 to 2020. Overall hedge frequency per thousand words increased from 3.8 (1995–1999 sub-period) to 5.6 (2016–2020), consistent with greater integration of Serbian researchers into international publication norms. The increase is most pronounced in natural sciences and least pronounced in humanities. Epistemic modal verbs show the smallest proportional change, while lexical hedging verbs and approximators show the largest growth, suggesting that serialisation in international venues is teaching Serbian authors a broader repertoire of hedging devices over time. Methodological limitations concerning corpus comparability across periods are discussed.

title: Annotating Hedges in a Low-Resource Setting: Guidelines and Reliability Study for Serbian Academic English
abstract: Manual annotation of hedging is time-intensive and subject to annotator disagreement, particularly when working with non-native English texts where the boundary between hedge and assertion is less conventionalised. This paper describes the development of annotation guidelines for a hedging-focused corpus of Serbian academic English and reports on a reliability study involving four annotators (two linguists, one computational linguist, one domain-specialist with no linguistics background) who each annotated the same 15,000-word sample. Inter-annotator agreement was measured using Cohen's κ and Krippendorff's α. Agreement was highest for modal verb hedges (κ = 0.87) and lowest for approximators (κ = 0.61). Sources of disagreement are analysed qualitatively. The guidelines are made available as a supplementary resource and are designed to be compatible with existing hedging taxonomies to allow cross-corpus comparability.

title: Hedging in AI-Assisted Academic Writing: A Comparison of Texts Produced by Serbian Researchers and Large Language Model Outputs
abstract: As large language models become tools that Serbian researchers use to draft or revise English-language texts, questions arise about whether machine-generated academic prose matches, exceeds, or diverges from the hedging norms that characterise expert non-native academic English. This study compares 40 research article introductions written by experienced Serbian academics with 40 introductions generated by a publicly accessible LLM, prompted to write on equivalent topics and targeting the same word length. The human corpus (approximately 60,000 words) and the LLM corpus (approximately 58,000 words) were annotated following the guidelines established in Mijatović et al. (2022). LLM texts contain significantly more hedges per thousand words (7.9 vs. 5.3), exhibit greater device variety, and show markedly higher rates of compound hedging. The results suggest that LLM outputs may overperform on surface-level hedging metrics while potentially misrepresenting the actual epistemic commitments of the discipline.

title: Epistemic Modality in Serbian Academic English Across Career Stages: A Cross-Sectional Corpus Study
abstract: This paper investigates whether the use of epistemic modality in English-language research articles varies systematically across career stages of Serbian academics. A corpus of 360 articles (ca. 1.7 million words) was compiled, stratified by career stage (doctoral candidate, postdoctoral researcher, associate professor, full professor) and by discipline (four fields: linguistics, biology, law, and mechanical engineering). Corpus annotation followed a four-category taxonomy. Results show a curvilinear pattern: doctoral candidates and full professors use fewer epistemic hedges than mid-career academics, though for apparently different reasons. Qualitative discourse analysis of a selected 20-article sub-sample suggests that doctoral candidates favour assertions for confidence presentation, while senior academics in some disciplines shift to a more authoritative declarative style. The paper discusses the implications of these patterns for doctoral writing instruction and for mentoring norms.

title: Comparing Stopping Criteria for Pool-Based Active Learning in Multi-Class Settings
abstract: Deciding when to stop querying is a practical problem that receives less attention than query strategy design. This study evaluates six stopping criteria—including stabilising predictions, maximum confidence threshold, and a performance-delta rule—on four publicly released multi-class tabular datasets with between 5 and 12 classes. Experiments use support vector machines with RBF kernels and report accuracy, labelling cost as a fraction of pool size, and premature-stop rate across 30 independent runs per dataset and criterion. The stabilising-predictions criterion achieves the best balance, stopping on average at 31 % of pool size while staying within 1.2 percentage points of the oracle accuracy. The maximum-confidence threshold is most sensitive to class imbalance, occasionally stopping before any minority-class example has been queried. We provide an open-access implementation and recommend the stabilising-predictions criterion as a safe default for practitioners without prior knowledge of dataset difficulty.

title: Uncertainty Calibration in Active Learning Loops: Does Temperature Scaling Help?
abstract: Uncertainty estimates produced by neural classifiers are often poorly calibrated, which can mislead query strategies that rely on predicted entropy or margin. This paper investigates whether post-hoc temperature scaling, applied at each retraining step, improves the quality of uncertainty-driven queries in an active learning loop. Experiments use a convolutional text classifier trained on a customer-feedback corpus of 18,000 labelled items, with 500 items reserved for calibration and 2,000 for testing. We measure Expected Calibration Error before and after scaling at each of 20 query rounds and track downstream macro-F1. Temperature scaling consistently reduces ECE by 30–45 % across rounds, and entropy-based querying with calibrated probabilities selects measurably more informative instances than the uncalibrated variant, yielding a 1.8-point macro-F1 gain at the same labelling budget. We argue that calibration should be treated as a first-class component of active learning pipelines rather than an optional post-processing step.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Annotation for Named Entity Recognition: Workflow Design and Annotator Agreement Analysis
abstract: Named entity recognition annotation is iterative by nature: early model outputs guide annotators toward difficult spans, but annotator disagreement can compound over successive rounds if the workflow is not carefully designed. We constructed a workflow in which two annotators independently label each query batch, adjudication is performed by a third expert only when inter-annotator agreement falls below a Cohen's κ threshold of 0.75, and the adjudicated labels feed directly into the next retraining cycle. The corpus covers biomedical text from a Serbian-language clinical discharge summary dataset of 6,400 sentences. Across 12 rounds of 50 sentences each, κ averages 0.81 with adjudication invoked in 4 of 12 rounds. Final NER F1 on a fixed test set reaches 83.4 %, compared with 79.1 % under a single-annotator baseline with the same labelling budget. We discuss how adjudication frequency and annotator fatigue interact and propose a simple fatigue proxy based on session response time.

title: Active Learning with Monte Carlo Dropout: Empirical Comparison on Tabular and Text Benchmarks
abstract: Monte Carlo Dropout (MCD) has been proposed as an inexpensive approximation to Bayesian inference in deep networks and has been adopted as an uncertainty source for active learning queries. This paper provides a systematic empirical comparison of MCD-based entropy, BALD, and variation ratios against softmax-entropy and least-confidence baselines on six tabular and four text classification benchmarks, using feed-forward and LSTM architectures. Dropout rates of 0.1, 0.2, and 0.3 and forward-pass counts of 10, 20, and 50 are crossed in a full factorial design. MCD-based BALD outperforms softmax entropy on 7 of 10 datasets when 20 or more forward passes are used, but the margin is below 1 percentage point in four of those cases. Training time overhead from MCD inference at 20 passes is 4–6× relative to single-pass softmax. We conclude that MCD is worth the overhead mainly on datasets with high aleatoric uncertainty and recommend against it for tabular data with clean labels.

title: Annotator Disagreement as a Signal: Reframing Noisy Labels in Active Learning
abstract: Standard active learning pipelines discard annotator disagreement after adjudication, treating the consensus label as ground truth. We argue that retained disagreement vectors carry information about instance difficulty and can be used to weight training examples and to flag near-boundary instances for future re-query. We implement this idea in a sentiment analysis pipeline operating on 9,500 product reviews annotated by three non-expert crowdworkers per item. Disagreement is encoded as a Dirichlet distribution over classes and used as a label-smoothing signal during fine-tuning of a pre-trained transformer. Models trained with disagreement-weighted smoothing outperform hard-label baselines by 1.4 points in macro-F1 at a labelling budget of 1,500 items. Ablation studies confirm that both the re-query mechanism and the smoothing contribute roughly equally to the gain. We also find that instances with high three-way disagreement cluster near sentiment boundaries, validating their informativeness for future annotation rounds.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Active Learning
abstract: This book chapter surveys the intersection of active learning and human factors, covering query strategy taxonomy, annotator cognitive models, interface design principles, and workflow orchestration. The chapter discusses how annotator expertise, fatigue, and incentive structures affect label quality and how these factors can be incorporated into the active learning loop through adaptive batch sizing, session scheduling, and dynamic re-routing of ambiguous instances to more experienced annotators. A case study section presents three deployed systems in medical imaging, legal document review, and e-commerce catalogue labelling, with quantitative breakdowns of labelling cost savings and accuracy outcomes. The chapter closes with a discussion of evaluation methodology, arguing that labelling budget in wall-clock hours is a more honest metric than number of labels for real-world deployments.

title: Query-by-Committee with Heterogeneous Ensembles for Low-Resource Relation Extraction
abstract: Relation extraction in low-resource domains requires maximising information gained from each annotated sentence. Query-by-Committee is theoretically attractive but sensitive to ensemble composition. We investigate ensembles combining a conditional random field, a BiLSTM-CRF, and a fine-tuned transformer, measuring committee disagreement via vote entropy and Kullback–Leibler divergence among member probability distributions. Experiments use a corpus of 3,200 manually annotated sentences from Serbian-language technical patents, with 200 sentences as initial seed. Committee-based selection reaches 80 % F1 at 850 annotated sentences; the best single-model uncertainty baseline requires 1,100 sentences for the same performance. Ensemble inference overhead is roughly 3× single-model cost but remains under two seconds per batch of 50 sentences on a single GPU. We also report that transformer committee members dominate vote entropy in later rounds, suggesting a staged ensemble strategy that retires weaker members as data accumulates.

title: Selective Annotation Re-Query: Identifying Stale Labels in Iterative Model Refinement
abstract: As models improve over successive active learning rounds, some labels collected early—when the model was weak and queries were noisy—may have been assigned to ambiguous instances by annotators who had less context. We propose a re-query criterion that identifies labelled instances whose current model uncertainty exceeds a threshold, flags them as potentially stale, and routes a subsample back to annotators for verification. On a medical text triage dataset of 7,800 sentences annotated over 18 rounds, applying the re-query criterion at rounds 10 and 15 recollects labels for 4.2 % of previously annotated data and improves final macro-F1 by 1.6 points relative to a no-re-query baseline at equal total annotation cost. Analysis shows that re-queried items are disproportionately from the earliest annotation rounds, confirming the staleness hypothesis. The overhead of routing and tracking re-queries is modest and is fully handled by the annotation platform developed within our group.

title: Discourse Framing of Artificial Intelligence in Central and Eastern European Online Media: A Longitudinal Cross-Country Topic Analysis
abstract: Public discourse about artificial intelligence in Central and Eastern Europe has received less empirical attention than coverage in Western European or North American media. This study applies a cross-lingual HDP model to a four-country comparable corpus of online news articles (Serbia, Romania, Hungary, Slovakia; 2017–2025; approximately 490,000 articles) to characterise how AI framing has evolved over eight years. Seven recurring frames are identified: economic opportunity, labour displacement, scientific achievement, regulatory concern, military application, ethical risk, and science fiction metaphor. Frame proportions shift noticeably after the public release of large language model products in late 2022, with a 2.3-fold increase in ethical-risk framing and a concurrent decline in science-fiction metaphor framing. Country-level comparisons show that Hungarian and Slovak outlets emphasise economic frames more strongly than Serbian and Romanian outlets. All data, fitted model artefacts, and the cross-lingual evaluation scripts are released under an open licence.

title: Comparative evaluation of resampling strategies for imbalanced cervical cytology classification
abstract: Cervical cytology screening datasets frequently exhibit severe class imbalance, with abnormal cell classes comprising less than 5% of samples. This paper systematically compares seven resampling approaches—including random oversampling, SMOTE, Borderline-SMOTE, ADASYN, random undersampling, Tomek links, and a combined SMOTE–Tomek method—applied before training of a random forest classifier on a dataset of 3,200 Pap smear cell images. Cell-level features were extracted using a 128-dimensional descriptor combining shape and intensity statistics. Experiments were repeated across ten stratified splits, and results are reported in terms of macro F1, geometric mean, and area under the precision–recall curve. ADASYN and Borderline-SMOTE yielded the best geometric mean scores (0.79 and 0.77 respectively), while random oversampling produced the highest variance. The study provides practical guidance on resampling selection for cytology classification tasks where collecting additional minority-class samples is clinically expensive.

title: Deep convolutional features for patch-level breast histopathology classification under data scarcity
abstract: This work examines the applicability of deep convolutional neural networks to patch-level classification of breast histopathology images when labelled data are scarce. Features extracted from the fourth convolutional block of a VGG-16 network pre-trained on natural images were used as input to a logistic regression classifier, bypassing the need for full fine-tuning. Experiments were conducted on a proprietary dataset of 1,140 annotated patches (four classes: normal, benign, in situ carcinoma, invasive carcinoma) provided by the Institute of Oncology of Vojvodina. Class sizes ranged from 97 to 610 patches, creating a moderate imbalance ratio of approximately 1:6. Transfer learning substantially reduced the minimum data requirement, achieving 81.4% overall accuracy with as few as 80 training samples per class after SMOTE augmentation. The study quantifies the trade-off between patch size (40 µm, 80 µm, and 160 µm at 20× magnification) and classification accuracy, finding 80 µm to be the best compromise.

title: GAN-based synthesis of H&E-stained patches for augmenting underrepresented tumour grades in prostate histopathology
abstract: Gleason grading of prostate tissue from haematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole slide images suffers from extreme scarcity of high-grade (Gleason 4+3 and 5) examples. This paper investigates a conditional deep convolutional GAN (cDCGAN) trained to generate 256×256-pixel tissue patches conditioned on Gleason grade label. The model was trained on 4,800 real patches from 62 prostatectomy specimens. Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and multi-scale structural similarity (MS-SSIM) were used to quantify image quality. Synthetic patches at FID ≤ 28 were mixed with real data at ratios of 1:1, 2:1, and 3:1 and used to fine-tune an InceptionV3 classifier. The 1:1 mixed strategy improved macro F1 from 0.63 to 0.71 compared to training on real data alone. Pathologist visual assessments confirmed that 74% of generated high-grade patches were rated as plausible. The study documents common failure modes including glandular structure collapse at high noise-to-signal ratios.

title: Stain normalisation as a preprocessing step for GAN training on multi-site histopathology datasets
abstract: When histopathology images originate from multiple laboratories with different staining protocols, GAN models trained without normalisation tend to learn stain-specific artefacts rather than tissue morphology. This study evaluates four stain normalisation methods—Macenko, Vahadane, Reinhard, and a learned histogram-matching approach—as preprocessing steps before cDCGAN training on a combined lung adenocarcinoma dataset collected from three sites in Serbia and Hungary (total 6,200 patches, three classes). Image quality metrics (FID, FID per class) and downstream classification performance of an EfficientNet-B2 classifier are used as criteria. Vahadane normalisation reduced inter-site FID variance by 38% and improved macro F1 by 0.06 on a held-out single-site test set. The paper also reports that no normalisation strategy fully eliminates site-dependent texture bias, and recommends site-stratified validation as a standard evaluation practice for multi-institutional histopathology studies.

title: Conditional image synthesis with auxiliary classifier GAN for rare mitosis class augmentation in breast pathology
abstract: Mitotic figure detection in breast histopathology is critical for tumour grading but severely limited by the rarity of mitotic events, typically fewer than 20 per high-power field even in high-grade tumours. This work applies an auxiliary classifier GAN (ACGAN) to synthesise realistic 64×64-pixel crops centred on candidate mitotic and hard-negative regions. The training set comprised 2,980 annotated crops from 23 whole slides, with a 1:14 mitosis-to-non-mitosis ratio. Quantitative evaluation combined FID with a pathologist scoring task in which two experienced pathologists rated crops as mitotic, non-mitotic, or uncertain. The ACGAN reduced the FID of synthetic mitotic crops from 61.4 (DCGAN baseline) to 44.7. Augmenting a ResNet-50 detector with synthetic mitotic crops improved precision from 0.71 to 0.78 and recall from 0.68 to 0.75 on the TUPAC16-style evaluation protocol. Training instability and mode collapse events are documented and mitigations are proposed.

title: Generative models for medical image synthesis: methods, evaluation criteria, and clinical validation challenges
abstract: This book chapter reviews the landscape of generative model architectures—VAEs, GANs, and normalising flows—as applied to the synthesis of medical images for data augmentation. The chapter covers evaluation methodology in detail, distinguishing between pixel-level fidelity metrics (FID, IS, MS-SSIM), task-utility metrics (downstream classifier improvement), and the less formalised clinical plausibility assessments performed by domain experts. Particular attention is paid to histopathology, dermoscopy, and retinal fundus imaging. The chapter argues that FID alone is insufficient as a quality criterion and provides a checklist of recommended evaluation practices. Regulatory and ethical considerations around the use of synthetic data in clinical AI development are discussed, with reference to current EU Medical Device Regulation guidance. The chapter is intended as a practical reference for graduate students and researchers entering the field of medical image synthesis.

title: Evaluation of StyleGAN2-generated synthetic thyroid cytology images as training data for follicular lesion classification
abstract: Thyroid fine-needle aspiration cytology produces highly imbalanced datasets because follicular lesions of undetermined significance (FLUS) are far less common than benign colloid nodules in routine practice. This study applies StyleGAN2 to synthesise FLUS-class cytology images from a dataset of 2,100 real images across four Bethesda categories. Quality was assessed by FID, kernel inception distance (KID), and a blinded evaluation by three cytopathologists who classified 200 real and 200 synthetic FLUS images using the Bethesda criteria. Cytopathologists correctly identified synthetic images at a rate of 58%, only marginally above chance. Incorporating synthetic FLUS images into ResNet-18 training at a 2:1 synthetic-to-real ratio increased FLUS-specific recall from 0.54 to 0.67 while maintaining benign-class precision above 0.90. Failure cases show that StyleGAN2 occasionally generates nuclear grooves with incorrect orientation, a finding noted in pathologist feedback.

title: Contrastive learning pre-training as an alternative to GAN-based augmentation for few-shot histopathology classification
abstract: GAN-based augmentation requires substantial training data even for the generative model itself, limiting applicability in extreme few-shot regimes. This paper compares SimCLR and MoCo v2 contrastive pre-training against cDCGAN augmentation for a five-way classification task on a lung histopathology dataset where each class has between 60 and 200 labelled patches. Pre-training was performed on 18,000 unlabelled patches from the same domain. Results show that MoCo v2 pre-training followed by linear probing yields a macro F1 of 0.74 at 80 labelled patches per class, compared to 0.69 for cDCGAN augmentation and 0.61 for a standard supervised baseline. The gap narrows as labelled data grows beyond 150 samples per class, at which point cDCGAN augmentation matches contrastive pre-training. The study recommends contrastive pre-training as the default strategy when fewer than 100 labelled samples per class are available, while GAN augmentation remains competitive in moderate-data regimes.

title: Latent space interpolation in conditional GAN models for continuous-grade augmentation of renal cell carcinoma histology
abstract: Renal cell carcinoma grading by the WHO/ISUP system involves ordinal grades (1–4) that reflect continuous underlying morphological changes. This study explores whether interpolation between adjacent grade latent vectors in a conditional GAN can generate intermediate-grade synthetic patches that improve classifier robustness to ambiguous boundary cases. A cStyleGAN2 model was trained on 9,600 patches from 48 nephrectomy specimens. Linear interpolation at step sizes of 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75 between adjacent grade conditioning vectors generated three levels of synthetic intermediate patches. A five-fold cross-validation framework with grade-3 boundary patches held out for testing was used. Classifiers augmented with 0.5-step interpolations showed the greatest improvement in grade-3 recall (from 0.58 to 0.67), at the cost of a modest precision decrease. Pathologist assessments confirmed that 0.5-step interpolations were rated as ambiguous by three out of four reviewers, validating the morphological plausibility of the approach.

title: Benchmarking diffusion model synthesis against GAN-based augmentation for class-imbalanced lymphoma subtype classification
abstract: Denoising diffusion probabilistic models (DDPMs) have recently attracted attention as an alternative to GANs for image synthesis due to their training stability and mode coverage. This paper presents a systematic benchmark of DDPM-based augmentation versus cDCGAN, cStyleGAN2, and real-only baselines for four-class lymphoma subtype classification (diffuse large B-cell, follicular, mantle cell, and marginal zone lymphoma) on a dataset of 7,200 patches from 55 biopsies. The minority class (marginal zone) comprised 6.8% of patches. DDPM synthesis was conditioned via classifier-free guidance at guidance scales of 1.5, 3.0, and 5.0. At guidance scale 3.0, DDPM augmentation achieved the highest macro F1 (0.81), compared to 0.78 for cStyleGAN2 and 0.74 for cDCGAN. DDPM training time was 4.2× longer than StyleGAN2 on equivalent hardware. The paper provides a cost-performance analysis intended to inform practical augmentation decisions.

title: Effect of GAN-augmented training data on calibration and uncertainty estimation in histopathology classifiers
abstract: Most studies evaluating GAN-based augmentation focus on accuracy and F1 metrics, leaving model calibration and uncertainty estimates largely unexplored. This paper measures the effect of synthetic data augmentation on Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and predictive entropy for an EfficientNet-B3 classifier trained on a skin biopsy dataset with five diagnostic classes and a 1:9 minority-to-majority ratio. Three augmentation strategies are compared: cStyleGAN2, DDPM, and Mixup. Without augmentation, the classifier was significantly overconfident on minority-class predictions (ECE = 0.14). Both cStyleGAN2 and DDPM augmentation reduced ECE to approximately 0.09, while Mixup achieved 0.07 but at the cost of lower minority-class recall. Temperature scaling post-training further reduced ECE uniformly across all conditions. Results suggest that synthetic augmentation has a meaningful positive secondary effect on calibration, which is practically relevant for clinical decision-support applications where confidence scores influence triage decisions.

title: Domain-adaptive GAN augmentation for cross-scanner generalisation in cervical histopathology classification
abstract: Histopathology scanners from different manufacturers produce images with systematic colour and sharpness differences that reduce classifier generalisation. This preprint proposes a domain-adaptive conditional GAN framework in which a shared generator is trained simultaneously on patches from two scanners (Aperio GT450 and Philips iSyntax equivalent, represented by fictional scanner equivalents in the dataset) using a domain discriminator auxiliary loss. Training data comprised 10,400 cervical biopsy patches across three CIN grades from 72 slides scanned on both devices. The domain-adaptive generator reduced the domain gap measured by maximum mean discrepancy by 44% compared to a non-adaptive cStyleGAN2. A ViT-Small classifier trained with domain-adaptive augmentation achieved a macro F1 of 0.79 on the target-scanner test set versus 0.71 for the non-adaptive baseline. Ablation experiments isolate the contribution of the domain discriminator loss weight. Code and model weights will be released upon journal acceptance.

title: Robust Unscented Kalman Filtering Under Non-Gaussian Process Noise for Building Energy Management
abstract: Building energy management systems often operate with sensors that exhibit heavy-tailed noise distributions caused by occupant behaviour and HVAC transients. Standard Unscented Kalman Filters (UKF) assume Gaussian process noise and degrade significantly under these conditions. This paper proposes replacing the Gaussian noise assumption with a Student-t distribution whose degrees-of-freedom parameter is estimated online via an expectation-maximisation step embedded in the filter recursion. The estimator is applied to a multi-zone thermal model of a five-floor office building in Novi Sad, calibrated using 14 months of logged temperature and energy-consumption data. The degrees-of-freedom estimate converged reliably within 20 filter steps across 200 experiment repetitions. Compared with a standard UKF, the proposed filter reduced mean absolute estimation error for zone temperature by 0.31 °C on average, and reduced peak error by up to 0.9 °C. Computational overhead relative to a standard UKF was less than 12 % per time step.

title: Towards Linearisable Causality Metadata in Distributed Ledger-Backed Audit Logs
abstract: Audit logs in regulated industries must record not only what happened but also a tamper-evident causal ordering of events across multiple writing parties. We examine whether a permissioned distributed ledger can serve as a causality metadata store for an eventually-consistent application layer, and what consistency overheads this introduces. We build a prototype in which application nodes write causal tokens derived from dotted version vectors to a four-node BFT-ordered log, while data itself remains in an eventually-consistent store. We measure the added latency imposed by anchoring causal metadata to ledger commits under two ordering protocols. In our test setup, median write latency increases from 3.1 ms to 17.4 ms, but reads requiring causal verification are unaffected. We identify three design choices that determine whether causality metadata remains consistent with application-layer ordering, and provide formal conditions for each.

title: Measurement-Based Path-Loss Model for 868 MHz Links Through Maize Canopies
abstract: This paper presents an empirical path-loss model derived from a controlled field campaign conducted in a mature maize plantation near Novi Sad during two growing seasons. Received signal strength was logged at 868 MHz using calibrated dipole antennas mounted at heights of 0.5 m, 1.0 m, and 1.5 m above ground, with transmitter-to-receiver separations ranging from 5 m to 120 m. A total of 4 800 measurement points were collected across four canopy density stages. The data were fitted to a modified dual-slope log-distance model that incorporates a vegetation depth exponent estimated at 2.7 for the dense-canopy phase. Seasonal variation in attenuation was found to reach up to 14 dB between bare-soil and peak-biomass conditions. Comparison against the ITU-R P.833 vegetation attenuation model shows systematic underestimation by the standard model at distances beyond 40 m. The proposed model reduces RMS prediction error from 6.1 dB to 2.4 dB over the measurement range. Results are directly applicable to link budget planning for agricultural sensor deployments in the Vojvodina region.

title: Diurnal Variation of 433 MHz Signal Attenuation in Deciduous Forest: A Seasonal Study
abstract: Wireless links operating beneath deciduous forest canopies are subject to attenuation that changes with foliage state, moisture content, and time of day. This study reports on a 14-month continuous measurement campaign conducted in a mixed oak-hornbeam stand in the Fruška Gora National Park. Two fixed transceivers operating at 433 MHz were positioned 85 m apart at 1.2 m height, logging received power every five minutes. The dataset spans leafless winter, leaf-flush spring, full-canopy summer, and senescence autumn phases. Mean additional attenuation attributable to full foliage versus leafless state was measured at 9.8 dB. Diurnal cycles correlated with leaf water potential, with a repeatable 2.1 dB amplitude oscillation in summer linked to stomatal conductance. A generalised additive model fitted to day-of-year and hour-of-day predictors explains 71% of variance in the residual after removing the deterministic log-distance component. Practical implications for duty-cycle planning in forest monitoring networks are discussed.

title: A Stochastic Geometry Model for Gateway Placement in LoRaWAN-Based Vineyard Monitoring
abstract: Gateway siting in low-power wide-area networks deployed over agricultural terrain must account for irregular propagation caused by row crops and terrain undulation. This paper applies a stochastic geometry framework to evaluate coverage probability as a function of gateway density for LoRaWAN deployments in vineyard rows. The propagation component uses a log-normal shadowing model with parameters estimated from a dedicated 868 MHz measurement campaign across three commercial vineyards in Sremski Karlovci. Shadowing standard deviation was found to be 5.6 dB along-row and 8.3 dB across-row, confirming significant directional asymmetry. Monte Carlo simulations over 10 000 gateway configurations are used to produce coverage probability maps. The analysis shows that a single gateway achieves 90% coverage within a 400 m radius along rows but only 210 m across rows. A simple row-orientation-aware gateway placement heuristic derived from the model reduces the required number of gateways by approximately 30% compared with isotropic placement. Results are validated against an experimental deployment of 47 sensor nodes.

title: Energy Consumption Characterisation of LoRa End-Nodes Under Varying Spreading Factor Scheduling
abstract: The selection of spreading factor (SF) in LoRa modulations directly controls the trade-off between link budget, airtime, and current draw. This paper provides a detailed energy consumption characterisation of a custom end-node platform across the full SF7–SF12 range at 14 dBm transmit power and 868 MHz centre frequency. Current waveforms were captured with a shunt-resistor logger at 100 kSa/s resolution over 5 000 individual transmission events for each SF setting. Mean energy per transmitted byte was found to range from 12 µJ at SF7 to 780 µJ at SF12. A discrete-event simulation model parameterised with the measured data was then used to project battery lifetime for a 2 400 mAh lithium cell under three duty-cycle scenarios representative of soil-moisture, livestock-tracking, and flood-warning applications. The simulation predicts lifetimes of 4.1 years, 1.7 years, and 0.3 years respectively at SF9. Sensitivity analysis identifies sleep-mode leakage current as the dominant lifetime-limiting factor at low duty cycles, motivating hardware-level optimisation.

title: Adaptive Slotted ALOHA with Channel-State Feedback for Dense LoRaWAN Deployments
abstract: Standard LoRaWAN relies on ALOHA-class channel access, which degrades rapidly as node density increases. This paper proposes an adaptive slotted ALOHA scheme in which the gateway periodically broadcasts a congestion indicator derived from decoded packet inter-arrival statistics, allowing nodes to adjust their transmission probability without requiring synchronisation infrastructure beyond the existing downlink channel. The scheme is analysed using a discrete-time Markov chain model and validated through a software-defined radio testbed experiment involving 120 emulated nodes sharing a single 125 kHz LoRa channel. Under a target load of 0.7 Erlangs, the proposed scheme achieves a throughput of 0.31 compared with 0.18 for pure ALOHA and 0.27 for a static slotted baseline. Packet delivery ratio at 200 nodes improves from 51% to 74%. The feedback overhead is a single byte per downlink frame, making the scheme compatible with the existing LoRaWAN class-A specification without firmware changes to commercially available modules. Latency and fairness metrics are also characterised.

title: Sub-GHz Radio Propagation in Agricultural Environments: Measurement Methods and Models
abstract: This book chapter reviews empirical and analytical approaches to characterising sub-GHz radio propagation in agricultural settings, covering arable crops, orchards, and open pasture. The chapter opens with a discussion of antenna placement conventions and calibration procedures specific to field campaigns, then surveys published measurement datasets at 433 MHz, 868 MHz, and 915 MHz, tabulating path-loss exponents and shadowing standard deviations reported across seventeen studies. Semi-empirical models based on excess vegetation attenuation are compared against full-wave simulation results from the literature. A section on temporal variability covers wind-induced fading, growth-stage dependence, and the effect of precipitation on near-surface links. The chapter closes with practical guidance on translating channel model outputs into link budget margins for sensor network planning, including worked examples for maize and sunflower deployments representative of Pannonian Plain conditions. Open measurement datasets cited in the chapter are listed in an appendix.

title: Received Signal Strength Tomography for Soil Moisture Estimation in Sunflower Fields
abstract: Radio-frequency tomography exploits multi-link received signal strength (RSS) to infer spatial distributions of a target quantity within a monitored area. This paper investigates the feasibility of using cross-link RSS variation at 868 MHz to estimate relative soil moisture patterns in a commercial sunflower field of 2.4 ha. A mesh of 24 nodes was deployed on a 40 m × 60 m grid, yielding 276 unique bidirectional link measurements taken at ten-minute intervals over one growing season. Gravimetric soil samples and capacitive probe readings served as ground truth at 18 calibration points. A regularised linear inversion algorithm reconstructed two-dimensional soil moisture maps with spatial resolution of approximately 8 m. Pearson correlation between tomographic estimates and probe readings was 0.71 at the calibration points and 0.63 at five held-out validation locations. Temporal tracking of an artificial irrigation event showed a detectable RSS shift within one measurement cycle. Limitations related to crop-induced multi-path and the confounding effect of canopy water content on link attenuation are quantified.

title: Power Spectral Occupancy of the 868 MHz ISM Band in Peri-Urban Vojvodina: A 72-Hour Survey
abstract: The 868 MHz Industrial, Scientific and Medical band hosts LoRaWAN, Sigfox, wireless M-Bus, and several proprietary protocols, yet systematic measurements of actual occupancy in Serbian peri-urban environments are absent from the published literature. This paper reports a 72-hour continuous spectrum survey conducted at three sites in Novi Sad and two rural locations in Vojvodina using a calibrated software-defined radio receiver and a horn antenna at 5 m height. Spectrograms were logged with 10 kHz resolution bandwidth and processed to compute channel occupancy, duty-cycle distribution, and signal classification via a random forest classifier trained on signal feature vectors. Mean channel occupancy across 868.0–868.6 MHz was 3.1% at urban sites and 0.9% at rural sites. LoRa-like chirp signals accounted for 61% of detected events, wireless M-Bus for 22%, and unclassified narrowband signals for 17%. Peak occupancy episodes lasting more than 30 seconds were observed on four occasions, all attributable to meter-reading infrastructure. Results serve as an empirical baseline for coexistence studies.

title: Phenolic Composition and Colour Parameters of Sila Red Wine Vinified Without Sulphur Dioxide Addition
abstract: Sila is a red-berried autochthonous variety cultivated in the Srem region of Vojvodina. This study investigated the effects of sulphur dioxide omission during vinification on the phenolic composition, colour parameters (CIELab), and oxidative stability of Sila wines over 12 months of bottle ageing. Twelve 20-litre lots were produced in a pilot winery during the 2016 vintage, with and without SO2 addition at crushing and at bottling. Total polyphenol index, anthocyanin content, and individual phenolic acids were determined by spectrophotometry and HPLC-DAD. Wines without SO2 showed a 23% reduction in monomeric anthocyanins after 12 months compared with 14% in the control, but retained statistically comparable total polyphenol index values. Colour density decreased at a higher rate in SO2-free wines; however, browning index values remained within acceptable limits for all treatments through month nine. The results indicate that Sila's naturally high tannin content provides partial protection against oxidative degradation under low-intervention conditions.

title: Consumer Segmentation and Preference Mapping for Autochthonous Serbian Wines at an Urban Wine Fair
abstract: A consumer test was conducted at a wine fair in Novi Sad involving 186 participants recruited from the general public. Eight wines made from four Serbian autochthonous varieties (Neoplanta, Sila, Začinak, and Tamjanika crvena) were evaluated for liking on a 9-point hedonic scale and for six attribute intensity ratings. Cluster analysis based on liking scores identified three consumer segments: one preferring aromatic, low-tannin styles (n=74), one favouring structured reds (n=62), and one exhibiting moderate, undifferentiated preferences (n=50). External preference mapping showed that Začinak wines were positioned centrally and attracted the broadest positive response. Demographic data (age, gender, wine purchase frequency, and self-reported familiarity with domestic varieties) were collected; familiarity with autochthonous varieties correlated positively with segment membership in the structured-red cluster (r=0.41, p<0.01). The study provides baseline preference data useful for producers positioning wines in urban Serbian markets.

title: Terpene Profiles of Tamjanika and Začinak Grape Musts and Wines: Effect of Skin-Contact Duration
abstract: Tamjanika (red-berried muscat type) and Začinak are aromatic autochthonous Serbian varieties for which systematic terpene data under varying maceration conditions are scarce. This study applied 0, 4, 8, and 24 hours of pre-fermentative skin contact to musts from both varieties, harvested in the 2018 vintage from a single estate in Vršac. Free and glycosidically bound terpenes were quantified by GC-MS after enzymatic hydrolysis. Linalool, geraniol, and nerol were the dominant free terpenes in both varieties; Tamjanika showed 2.3-fold higher total free terpene concentration than Začinak at all maceration durations. Extended skin contact increased free linalool in Tamjanika wines from 148 µg/L (0 h) to 412 µg/L (24 h), remaining well above the reported perception threshold of 25 µg/L. In Začinak, gains were more moderate (62 to 134 µg/L). A trained panel confirmed that prolonged skin contact increased floral intensity scores (p < 0.01) in Tamjanika but not significantly in Začinak, suggesting variety-specific limits to terpene extraction.

title: Autochthonous Varieties and Low-Intervention Winemaking in the Western Balkans: Status and Prospects
abstract: This book chapter surveys the current state of cultivation and commercial vinification of autochthonous grape varieties across Serbia, North Macedonia, and Slovenia, with particular attention to the adoption of low-intervention practices (absence or reduction of sulphur dioxide, uninoculated fermentations, unfined and unfiltered wines) among small and medium producers. Drawing on a structured questionnaire survey of 47 wineries completed between 2019 and 2020, the chapter characterises producer motivations, technical constraints, and market positioning strategies. Results indicate that low-intervention practices are more prevalent in Serbia among producers with fewer than 15,000 bottles annual output and are most frequently applied to white and orange wine styles. The chapter discusses challenges including fermentation inconsistency, elevated volatile acidity in warmer vintages, and consumer communication of 'natural' wine concepts in regional markets. It concludes with a comparative overview of sensory research needs for varieties that remain undercharacterised in the scientific literature.

title: Descriptive Sensory Analysis of Neoplanta Wines from Three Vojvodina Subregions Using a Fixed-Vocabulary Lexicon
abstract: A Neoplanta-specific sensory lexicon of 22 descriptors (14 aroma, 5 taste/mouthfeel, 3 appearance) was developed and anchored with reference standards through six training sessions with an eight-member expert panel. The lexicon was applied to evaluate 24 Neoplanta wines from the 2019 and 2020 vintages sourced from producers in Fruška Gora, Vršac, and Subotica–Horgoš subregions. Analysis of variance identified significant subregion effects on citrus aroma (p=0.003), herbal aroma (p=0.011), and perceived acidity (p<0.001). Fruška Gora wines scored higher on stone-fruit descriptors; Vršac wines were distinguished by elevated mineral and flint notes. Vintage had a significant main effect on overall aromatic intensity and on green/grassy descriptors, with 2019 (warmer, drier season) wines scoring lower on grassy notes than 2020. The developed lexicon is made available as a supplementary resource for standardised evaluation of this variety across Serbian producers.

title: Fermentation Temperature and Its Interaction with Spontaneous Versus Inoculated Protocols in Sila Red Wine: Colour, Polyphenols, and Sensory Outcomes
abstract: A factorial experiment (two fermentation temperatures: 18 °C and 26 °C; two yeast protocols: spontaneous and inoculated with a commercial Saccharomyces cerevisiae RC212 strain) was carried out in a pilot winery over the 2021 vintage using Sila grapes from a single plot in Irig municipality. Each treatment was replicated three times (100 L tanks, 12 treatments total). Wine chemistry (total anthocyanins, total polyphenol index, colour density, volatile acidity, pH, titratable acidity) was determined at the end of alcoholic fermentation and after six months in bottle. At 26 °C, spontaneously fermented wines showed higher volatile acidity (mean 0.82 g/L vs. 0.61 g/L for inoculated, expressed as acetic acid), remaining below regulatory limits but approaching sensory detection thresholds. Colour density was highest in inoculated wines at 26 °C. A nine-member trained panel evaluated the wines blind; no significant interaction between temperature and yeast protocol was observed for overall quality ratings, but inoculated 18 °C wines received the highest median scores for aroma cleanliness (7.8/10).

title: Willingness to Pay for Low-Intervention Serbian Autochthonous Wines: A Choice Experiment with Urban Consumers
abstract: A discrete choice experiment was administered to 241 wine-purchasing adults recruited in Novi Sad and Belgrade through intercept sampling at retail outlets and wine bars. Respondents chose among hypothetical wine profiles varying in grape variety (Neoplanta, Sila, Začinak, and an international variety control), winemaking label claim (conventional, organic certified, low-intervention/natural), price (three levels: 600, 900, and 1,400 RSD per bottle), and regional origin label presence. Mixed logit models were estimated. A positive and significant willingness-to-pay premium was found for the low-intervention label claim (mean 187 RSD, 95% CI: 114–261) and for regional origin labelling (mean 142 RSD). Sila was the only autochthonous variety showing a significant positive utility coefficient relative to the international control variety. Education level and frequency of wine purchase moderated willingness-to-pay estimates. Results suggest that low-intervention labelling may carry commercial value in urban Serbian markets, particularly when combined with origin cues.

title: Short-Term Sensory Changes in Bottled Neoplanta Wine Under Three Closure Types: Screwcap, Natural Cork, and Technical Cork
abstract: Forty-eight Neoplanta wine bottles sealed with natural cork, technical (agglomerate) cork, and aluminium screwcap were stored horizontally at 14 °C for 18 months starting from bottling in October 2024. Samples were withdrawn at 0, 6, 12, and 18 months. At each time point, dissolved oxygen and free SO2 were measured; sensory evaluation was conducted by a seven-member trained panel assessing oxidation notes, fruit intensity, freshness, and overall harmony on structured line scales. At 18 months, screwcap-sealed wines retained the highest fruit intensity (mean score 6.9/10) and lowest perceived oxidation (1.2/10), while natural cork wines showed greater variability across replicates (SD=1.4 for fruit intensity vs. SD=0.6 for screwcap). Three of twelve natural cork bottles exhibited cork taint confirmed by 2,4,6-trichloroanisole detection above 5 ng/L. The study is ongoing; 24-month and 30-month intervals are planned.

title: Calibration of a red-edge active optical sensor for winter wheat nitrogen estimation under field conditions in Vojvodina
abstract: This study evaluated the suitability of a prototype red-edge active optical sensor (AOS) for estimating leaf nitrogen concentration (LNC) in winter wheat across three commercial fields in the Vojvodina plain during the 2010 growing season. The sensor emitted at 670 nm and 730 nm and recorded reflectance at a 10 Hz sampling rate from a tractor-mounted boom at 1.2 m above the canopy. Destructive leaf samples (n = 144) were collected at Zadoks GS 30–32 and analysed by Kjeldahl digestion. A multivariate regression between the normalised red-edge difference index (NREDI) and LNC yielded R² = 0.71 and RMSE = 0.28% dry weight. Sensor output was compared against a Yara N-Sensor ALS operated simultaneously on the same transects. The two instruments agreed within ±6% across 87% of measurement positions. Results indicate that the calibration must be adjusted for cultivar and background soil colour, with dark Chernozem soils inflating NREDI by up to 9% at low biomass stages.

title: Effect of canopy architecture on active optical sensor readings in maize at four growth stages
abstract: Canopy geometry changes substantially as maize develops, and this study quantified how those changes affect reflectance-based nitrogen indices measured with a ground-based active optical sensor. Measurements were taken at V4, V6, V8, and VT stages across a nitrogen rate trial (0, 60, 120, 180 kg N ha⁻¹) on a Chernozem soil near Rimski Šančevi in 2012. The sensor was operated at a fixed height of 1.5 m, yielding varying fractions of soil, stalk, and leaf in the field of view. NREDI values at V4 were poorly correlated with concurrent plant nitrogen uptake (R² = 0.38) but improved substantially at V6 and beyond (R² = 0.74–0.82). A simple geometric correction based on measured plant height and row spacing improved V4 performance to R² = 0.61. These findings have practical implications for the timing of sensor-guided sidedress nitrogen applications, suggesting that delaying the first pass until V6 reduces prediction uncertainty without compromising agronomic outcome at typical yield-goal nitrogen rates.

title: Spectral indices for nitrogen estimation in sunflower: a comparison of passive and active sensing platforms
abstract: Sunflower is a relatively understudied crop in proximal spectral sensing literature, partly because its large, oriented leaf canopy creates strong directional reflectance effects. This study compared measurements from a handheld passive spectroradiometer (SR-3500), a tractor-mounted active optical sensor, and a UAV-mounted four-band multispectral camera across a nitrogen rate experiment (n = 5 rates, 4 replicates) on a farm near Sombor during the 2016 season. Leaf chlorophyll content measured by SPAD-502 served as a proxy for nitrogen status. Among 14 evaluated spectral indices, the red-edge chlorophyll index (CIre) derived from the active sensor showed the strongest correlation with SPAD (r = 0.84), outperforming the UAV-derived equivalent (r = 0.76), likely due to the active sensor's insensitivity to solar angle variation. Passive spectroradiometer measurements at nadir under diffuse-sky conditions performed comparably to the active sensor (r = 0.82). The study recommends AOS-based CIre as the primary real-time index for sunflower nitrogen management, with UAV imagery as a complementary diagnostic layer.
