title: Insulin clamp-derived hepatic insulin sensitivity index in patients across the NAFLD spectrum: relationship to liver fat fraction and NAS
abstract: The hyperinsulinaemic-euglycaemic clamp is considered the reference method for quantifying insulin sensitivity, yet its hepatic component has rarely been correlated with both quantitative liver fat and histology in the same cohort. We performed two-step clamps (low dose 0.3 mU/kg/min; high dose 1.0 mU/kg/min) in 48 NAFLD patients stratified by NAS and liver fat fraction measured by 1H-MRS. Endogenous glucose production was assessed by [6,6-²H₂]glucose isotope dilution. Hepatic insulin sensitivity index (HISI) was calculated as 1/(fasting EGP × fasting insulin). HISI decreased progressively from NAS 0–2 to NAS ≥5 (median 0.081, 0.053, and 0.031 respectively; p<0.001 Kruskal-Wallis). Liver fat fraction explained 44% of HISI variance (r²=0.44). In multivariate regression, liver fat fraction and NAS ballooning score were independent predictors of HISI. Hepatic insulin resistance was thus quantitatively graded across the NAFLD spectrum, reinforcing its central role in disease progression.

title: Metabolic and inflammatory outcomes of a 12-week low-carbohydrate versus low-fat dietary intervention in patients with biopsy-confirmed NAFLD
abstract: Dietary composition influences hepatic fat accumulation and insulin resistance, but few randomised trials have assessed liver-specific outcomes with biopsy confirmation in Southeastern European patients with NAFLD. We randomised 60 biopsy-confirmed NAFLD patients (NAS 3–6) to a low-carbohydrate diet (LCD, <50 g/day carbohydrates) or an isocaloric low-fat diet (LFD, <25% energy from fat) for 12 weeks. Primary outcomes were change in liver fat fraction by 1H-MRS and change in fasting insulin. Both diets reduced liver fat fraction (LCD: −8.4±2.9 percentage points; LFD: −5.1±2.6 percentage points; between-group difference p=0.03). Fasting insulin fell more in the LCD group (−7.3 µU/mL vs −3.8 µU/mL, p=0.04). ALT normalised in 53% of LCD and 37% of LFD participants. CRP did not differ between groups at 12 weeks. Adherence, assessed by 3-day dietary recall, was comparable between arms. These results suggest that LCD may offer a modestly greater reduction in hepatic fat and insulin over 12 weeks.

title: Machine learning-based prediction of NASH from routine clinical variables: a multicentre retrospective analysis
abstract: Non-invasive identification of NASH remains an unmet clinical need. We assembled a retrospective dataset of 421 biopsy-confirmed NAFLD patients from three centres in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania, with 47 clinical and biochemical variables collected at the time of biopsy. We trained and validated random forest, gradient boosting, and logistic regression classifiers to distinguish NASH (NAS ≥5) from non-NASH using nested cross-validation and an external hold-out set (n=84). The gradient boosting model achieved the highest AUROC of 0.83 (95% CI 0.76–0.90) on the hold-out set. The five most important features were ALT, the cytokeratin-18 M30 fragment, fasting insulin, waist circumference, and the LAR. Calibration was acceptable (Brier score 0.17). The model did not outperform an experienced hepatologist's clinical assessment but performed comparably to the NFS score and better than FIB-4 for NASH classification specifically. These findings suggest that structured routine data can support NASH screening in settings without MR spectroscopy access.

title: Pathophysiology of insulin resistance in non-alcoholic fatty liver disease
abstract: This chapter provides a comprehensive summary of the mechanisms by which ectopic hepatic lipid accumulation disrupts canonical insulin signalling. It covers the roles of diacylglycerol-mediated PKCε activation, ceramide-driven inhibition of Akt, and IRS-1 serine phosphorylation downstream of inflammatory kinases JNK1 and IKKβ. The chapter integrates evidence from rodent genetic models, isotope tracer studies in humans, and transcriptomic profiling of human NAFLD biopsies. It also discusses how altered hepatokine secretion—particularly FGF21, fetuin-A, and selenoprotein P—links hepatic insulin resistance to systemic metabolic consequences including skeletal muscle and adipose tissue insulin resistance. A section is devoted to the role of lipid droplet-associated proteins (perilipin 2 and 5) in regulating triglyceride turnover and diacylglycerol availability. The chapter concludes with a discussion of current and investigational pharmacological targets arising from this mechanistic framework, including ASK1 inhibitors and ACC inhibitors.

title: Serum sphingolipid profiling in NAFLD progression: ceramide and sphingosine-1-phosphate as candidate biomarkers
abstract: Ceramides and their metabolite sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) have opposing effects on cell survival and insulin signalling, but their joint circulating profiles across the NAFLD spectrum have not been systematically mapped in a Southeastern European cohort. We performed LC-MS/MS-based targeted sphingolipidomics in serum from 105 biopsy-confirmed NAFLD patients (35 simple steatosis, 35 borderline NASH, 35 definite NASH) and 35 metabolically healthy controls. Total ceramide was elevated in NAFLD versus controls (p<0.001) and increased incrementally with NAS. Species C16:0 and C24:1 ceramide were the main contributors. S1P was paradoxically reduced in definite NASH compared with both controls and simple steatosis (p=0.002). The ceramide-to-S1P ratio discriminated definite NASH from simple steatosis with AUC 0.77. Ceramide C16:0 correlated with hepatic insulin resistance index derived from the clamp (r=0.54, p<0.001). These results position the ceramide–S1P axis as a biochemically accessible correlate of both insulin resistance severity and histological stage in NAFLD.

title: Hepatic transcriptomic signatures of early versus late insulin resistance in a longitudinal mouse model of diet-induced NAFLD
abstract: Distinguishing the transcriptomic changes that initiate insulin resistance from those that accompany established disease is important for identifying early intervention targets. We performed RNA sequencing (bulk, poly-A selection) on liver tissue from C57BL/6J mice fed a western diet at weeks 4, 8, 16, and 24 (n=6 per time point) alongside chow-fed controls. Differential gene expression analysis (DESeq2, FDR<0.05, |log2FC|>1) identified 312 genes dysregulated at week 4, expanding to 1,847 by week 24. Gene ontology enrichment showed that lipid metabolic processes and ER protein folding were predominantly altered early, while inflammatory response and extracellular matrix remodelling pathways dominated late time points. IRS-1 and IRS-2 mRNA were already reduced at week 8. GSEA against a published human NAFLD gene signature showed moderate concordance at week 16 (NES 1.68). This temporal resolution suggests a window between weeks 4 and 8 during which metabolic reprogramming precedes overt inflammation.

title: Bedform migration rates along a regulated reach of the lower Tisa River derived from repeated echo-sounding surveys
abstract: Dunes and ripples on the lower Tisa riverbed were monitored over a 14-month period using single-beam echo-sounding transects at five cross-sections between river kilometres 54 and 112. Surveys were conducted monthly under baseflow conditions and within 48 hours of three flood events with return periods of approximately 2, 5, and 12 years. Bedform height ranged from 0.15 m to 1.4 m depending on discharge, and migration rates calculated from successive longitudinal profiles varied between 0.3 and 2.1 m per day. Bedload flux estimates derived from bedform kinematics were compared with concurrent ADCP-based measurements, yielding differences of 8–22 percent. Results indicate that sediment transport is episodically concentrated during rising limb conditions and that the surveyed reach has been in a state of net bedload deficit since upstream flow regulation was completed in the 1980s. The findings are discussed in the context of long-term thalweg lowering observed at Szeged gauging records.

title: Grain-size variability of surficial bed material in the Middle Danube between river kilometres 1255 and 1330
abstract: A systematic bed material sampling campaign was carried out at 22 cross-sections along the Middle Danube in the Vojvodina sector during low-water conditions in autumn 2012. Samples were collected at three lateral positions per cross-section using a Shipek grab sampler and analysed by dry sieving. Median grain diameters ranged from 0.38 mm near the thalweg to 1.62 mm on bar crests, with a general fining trend from upstream to downstream consistent with a reduction in competence below the Novi Sad railway bridge constriction. Sediment sorting coefficients indicated bimodal distributions at seven cross-sections, likely reflecting reworking of older gravel lag material. Spatial patterns were compared with historical datasets from 1974 and 1993, showing a coarsening of the thalweg material by approximately 0.3 phi units over the four-decade interval. This coarsening is interpreted as an armoring response to long-term reduction in peak discharge magnitude following upstream dam construction.

title: Morphological response of a gravel–sand transition zone to an extreme flood: the 2013 Danube flood event near Apatin
abstract: The June 2013 flood on the Middle Danube, which reached a stage of 8.97 m at Apatin with a return period exceeding 100 years, provided an opportunity to assess large-magnitude morphological change in a sector where gravel and sand coexist. Pre- and post-flood bathymetric surveys were conducted at 18 cross-sections using an ADCP mounted on an unmanned survey vessel. Net erosion volumes exceeded net deposition by 310 000 m³ across the 28 km study reach. Point bar crests were lowered by up to 1.2 m while mid-channel areas experienced scour of 0.4–0.8 m. Channel width measured at bankfull stage increased by an average of 4.3 percent. Recovery surveying 14 months after the flood indicated partial refilling of scour holes but persistent thalweg lowering of 0.15–0.35 m. Comparison with 1998 cross-section data suggests the extreme event accelerated an ongoing incision trend rather than producing a new morphological state.

title: Sediment budget estimation for a 90 km lowland river segment using multi-source bathymetric data
abstract: A reach-scale sediment budget was constructed for the Tisa River between Kanjiža and the confluence with the Danube using bathymetric data collected in 2005, 2012, and 2017. Cross-section data from the Serbian Water Directorate archive were supplemented with targeted ADCP transects at 34 additional positions. Volumetric change analysis was performed using a triangulated irregular network approach in GIS. The budget revealed a persistent deficit of approximately 42 000 m³ per kilometre per decade, with the largest losses concentrated in a 22 km reach downstream of the Novi Bečej diversion structure. Total storage loss across the study segment over the 12-year period was estimated at 3.4 million m³. Uncertainty in the interpolated surfaces, assessed by leave-one-out cross-validation, amounted to ±12 percent of gross erosion volume. Implications for navigation depth maintenance and flood wave propagation speed are discussed. Specific recommendations are offered for monitoring frequency needed to detect significant budget changes within a five-year management cycle.

title: Flow resistance estimation in vegetated lowland channels: field measurements and comparison of empirical equations
abstract: Hydraulic resistance was assessed in six drainage channels in the Vojvodina irrigation network during summer low-flow and autumn post-harvest conditions, capturing contrasting macrophyte cover densities. At each site, water surface slope was measured with differential GPS over reaches of 80–120 m, cross-sectional geometry was surveyed, and discharge was gauged with an electromagnetic current meter. Manning's n values calculated from measurements ranged from 0.028 to 0.074. These values were compared against predictions from eight empirical resistance equations reported in the literature. Equations based solely on hydraulic radius and grain roughness underestimated n by 40–60 percent under dense vegetation conditions. A composite resistance approach splitting grain and vegetation drag provided the best match (mean absolute error 0.007). Vegetation density, quantified as projected frontal area per unit channel length, was the strongest predictor variable, explaining 71 percent of variance in Manning's n across the dataset. Practical implications for drainage network maintenance scheduling are outlined.

title: Coupling a 1D hydraulic model with a sediment transport module to simulate bed level change in the lower Tisa under projected discharge scenarios
abstract: A one-dimensional hydraulic model of the lower Tisa River (km 0–170) was coupled with a non-cohesive sediment transport module to simulate bed level evolution under three discharge scenarios derived from regional climate projections for the 2041–2070 period. The baseline model was calibrated against measured water surface profiles for eight historical events and validated against observed bed level changes between 2010 and 2020. Transport capacity was computed using the van Rijn (1984) formula applied to spatially distributed median grain size data collected in 2018. Scenario simulations indicated that a 15 percent reduction in mean annual discharge combined with unchanged flood peak frequency would accelerate existing incision by approximately 20 percent relative to the reference period, increasing mean thalweg lowering from 0.9 to 1.1 cm per year. A scenario with reduced flood frequency produced less thalweg change but greater bed coarsening. Limitations of the one-dimensional approach in capturing bend-scale variability are discussed.

title: Phosphorus sorption capacity of fine-grained floodplain sediments along the Tisa River and its implications for nutrient storage
abstract: Overbank deposition of fine-grained sediment during flood events can act as a significant phosphorus sink in agricultural catchments. Surface and subsurface sediment samples were collected at 31 floodplain locations along the Tisa River in Serbia following the 2021 spring flood, targeting three geomorphic units: natural levees, backswamp areas, and abandoned channel fills. Phosphorus sorption isotherms were fitted using the Langmuir model, yielding maximum sorption capacities ranging from 180 mg P kg⁻¹ on levee sands to 1140 mg P kg⁻¹ in backswamp clays. Organic carbon content was the strongest predictor of sorption capacity (r² = 0.78). Annual phosphorus sequestration for the study reach was estimated at 18–46 tonnes, depending on assumptions about overbank deposition thickness. These estimates are compared with nutrient load data from the Water Framework Directive monitoring programme. The results suggest that maintaining natural floodplain connectivity would preserve a measurable nutrient retention function currently constrained by embankment geometry.

title: Farmer Participation in Irrigation Scheduling Decisions: Evidence from Three WUAs in the South Bačka District
abstract: Participatory irrigation scheduling is formally mandated under Serbian water legislation introduced in 1997, yet the degree to which farmers meaningfully influence delivery timetables varies considerably across associations. This paper reports on a structured participatory assessment conducted across three water-user associations in the South Bačka administrative district between 2000 and 2002. A mixed-method protocol combined seasonal attendance records of general assembly meetings (n = 847 farmer-meeting events), a 112-respondent household survey, and in-depth interviews with nine WUA board members. Participation levels measured by the Degree of Participation Scale (adapted from Pretty 1995) were predominantly nominal or consultative, with genuine decision-making authority retained by elected boards in all three cases. Crop type and land tenure security were significantly associated with higher participation scores. The paper argues that legal mandates for participation are insufficient without corresponding capacity-building investments and transparent grievance mechanisms at the association level.

title: Lumped-mass dynamic model for a six-cable spatial CDPR under varying payload inertia
abstract: This paper presents a lumped-mass formulation for a six-cable, six-degree-of-freedom cable-driven parallel robot intended for large-volume positioning. Each cable is modelled as a series of three lumped masses connected by linear springs and dampers, with parameters identified from free-vibration tests on a 3 m × 3 m × 2.5 m testbed. The resulting system of 54 ordinary differential equations is integrated using a fourth-order Runge–Kutta scheme with a 0.5 ms fixed step. Cable sag and elasticity effects are quantified at payload masses of 10, 25, and 50 kg. End-effector pose errors predicted by the model are compared against motion-capture measurements across 120 point-to-point trajectories; root-mean-square position errors stay below 2.1 mm and orientation errors below 0.8° in all tested configurations. The model accuracy degrades near workspace boundaries where cable tensions approach minimum admissible values, an effect attributed to the onset of cable slack not captured by the linear spring assumption.

title: Energy consumption in point-to-point motions of cable-driven parallel robots: effect of trajectory shape and cable pre-tension
abstract: Minimising electrical energy in cable-driven parallel robots requires simultaneous selection of trajectory shape and cable tension distribution, because motor torque depends on both end-effector acceleration and internal force levels. This study formulates a direct collocation problem on a five-segment polynomial spline, minimising total motor electrical energy subject to dynamic feasibility, joint torque limits, and wrench-feasibility constraints. Forty-eight representative point-to-point tasks are solved on the testbed robot using interior-point optimisation, and energy measurements from motor drive sensors are compared against predictions. Lowering pre-tension from 60 N to 20 N reduces mean electrical energy by 18% for slow trajectories but increases it by 9% for fast trajectories owing to reactive power demands from cable oscillation damping. Optimal cable pre-tension is shown to scale approximately with the square root of peak end-effector acceleration, providing a practical tuning guideline.

title: Identification of cable viscoelastic parameters using inverse dynamics and recursive least squares
abstract: Accurate dynamic models of cable-driven parallel robots require reliable cable viscoelastic parameters, which vary with cable age, temperature, and loading history. This paper describes an identification procedure that combines inverse dynamics with a recursive least-squares algorithm applied to tension and elongation measurements recorded during a set of chirp-excitation trajectories. Synthetic data generated from a reference model are used to verify convergence properties; the algorithm recovers stiffness and damping coefficients within 1.5% and 4.2% respectively. Physical experiments on 8 mm diameter polyamide cables show that stiffness decreases by approximately 12% over 200 h of cyclic loading, while damping coefficients vary by less than 5%. Parameter estimates updated online during a 30-minute positioning sequence reduce model prediction errors by 35% compared to using fixed nominal values. The procedure is designed to run on the dSPACE real-time platform without interrupting normal operation.

title: Trajectory planning for a cable-suspended crane robot in large-volume prefabricated construction
abstract: Cable-suspended robots with under-constrained cable sets are used as lightweight alternatives to gantry cranes in prefabricated construction. This book chapter reviews trajectory planning methods applicable to under-constrained CDPRs, covering quasi-static path planning, dynamic feasibility conditions, and residual vibration suppression. The authors present a case study in which a four-cable suspended robot positions 200 kg concrete panels over a 12 m × 8 m work cell. A time-scaling approach combined with input shaping reduces settling time at target positions from 3.4 s to 0.9 s without increasing peak cable tensions beyond 2.8 kN. Energy per placement cycle decreases by 22% compared to trapezoidal velocity profiles used in baseline trials. Practical considerations for anchor installation in construction environments and sensor redundancy for fault detection are discussed in the context of field deployment.

title: Comparison of minimum-time and minimum-energy trajectory criteria for a six-cable CDPR: experimental results
abstract: Minimum-time and minimum-energy trajectories differ substantially in shape and in the trade-off between positioning speed and electrical demand. This paper presents a systematic experimental comparison for a six-cable CDPR over a set of 30 point-to-point tasks spanning the central 60% of the wrench-feasible workspace. Both criteria are solved using direct collocation with a Gaussian quadrature mesh and CasADi for automatic differentiation. For the tested payload of 20 kg and a move distance of 1.5 m, minimum-energy trajectories are on average 31% slower than minimum-time trajectories but consume 44% less electrical energy. At move distances below 0.4 m the energy saving drops to 11% because acceleration phases dominate both profiles. Reproducibility is assessed across five repeat runs per task; standard deviations of total energy and transfer time are below 0.8% and 0.3% respectively, confirming testbed consistency. Force plate measurements show no difference in cable anchor loads between the two criteria beyond measurement noise.

title: Fault detection in CDPRs using cable tension residuals: sensitivity to motor encoder resolution
abstract: Cable slack or sensor failure in a CDPR can cause trajectory deviations or structural damage if undetected. This paper examines a residual-based fault detection method that compares measured cable tensions against tensions predicted from an inverse dynamics model running in parallel with the controller. Residual thresholds are derived from a statistical characterisation of model uncertainty across 200 nominal operating trajectories. The influence of motor encoder resolution (12, 14, and 16 bits) on false alarm rate and detection delay is evaluated in simulation and on the physical testbed. With 14-bit encoders, faults corresponding to a 15 N step tension drop are detected within 45 ms with a false alarm rate of 0.7 per hour. Increasing to 16-bit encoders reduces the minimum detectable fault magnitude to 9 N and the false alarm rate to 0.2 per hour. Cable fatigue-induced gradual stiffness degradation is distinguishable from abrupt faults in 88% of simulated cases using a sliding-window trend filter.

title: Scalability of energy-optimal trajectory planning to CDPRs with eight cables: computational benchmarks
abstract: Extending energy-optimal trajectory planning from six- to eight-cable CDPRs increases both the state dimension and the nullspace dimension of the tension distribution problem, raising computational cost substantially. This preprint reports computational benchmarks for direct collocation with Radau quadrature applied to eight-cable CDPRs across three mesh densities (50, 100, and 200 collocation intervals) and three move distances. Solver wall-clock time scales roughly as O(n^1.7) with the number of collocation intervals on a 32-core workstation, compared to O(n^1.5) for the six-cable case, attributed to denser Jacobian fill-in. Warm-starting from a scaled six-cable solution reduces solve time by 35–52% depending on mesh density. Feasibility rates and solution quality metrics are comparable to the six-cable case, with average energy-consumption predictions agreeing within 3% of simulated ground truth values. The benchmarks use a publicly archived problem set covering 60 representative positioning tasks.

title: Predictive growth models for Botrytis on soft fruit in the cold chain
abstract: Botrytis cinerea is the primary postharvest pathogen limiting the commercial shelf life of soft fruits during cold-chain distribution. This work presents a suite of predictive growth models calibrated for B. cinerea on raspberry, strawberry, and blueberry substrates across a temperature range of 0–20 °C and relative humidity levels of 85–100%. Square-root (Ratkowsky) and modified Gompertz primary models were fitted to colony diameter and spore germination data collected under isothermal laboratory conditions. Secondary models describing the influence of temperature and water activity on maximum specific growth rate (μmax) and lag phase duration (λ) were subsequently developed and validated. Model performance was assessed using root mean square error (RMSE), bias factor (Bf), and accuracy factor (Af), with Af values below 1.15 indicating satisfactory predictive capacity across all fruit substrates. Dynamic temperature validation trials using step-change and realistic cold-chain temperature profiles confirmed that the models retained predictive reliability under non-isothermal conditions. The resulting model library is intended for integration into cold-chain decision-support software, enabling logistics operators and packers to forecast spoilage risk in real time. Limitations relating to cultivar variability and co-inoculation with yeast species are discussed as priorities for future model refinement.

title: Temperature abuse during transport: a sensor study of fruit exports
abstract: Temperature deviations during postharvest transport — commonly termed temperature abuse — are a leading driver of premature spoilage and economic loss in the fresh fruit export sector. This study employed a network of miniaturized wireless temperature and relative humidity data loggers deployed across 18 commercial refrigerated truck consignments of Serbian berries (raspberry, blueberry, strawberry) destined for markets in Germany, Austria, and Slovenia. Sensor placement covered pallet core, pallet surface, and truck door-proximal positions to capture spatial heterogeneity. Results revealed that door-proximal positions experienced mean temperature elevations of 3.8 °C above target during loading and unloading events, with cumulative abuse time averaging 4.2 hours per journey. Principal component analysis of sensor profiles identified loading sequence and pre-cooling status as the two strongest predictors of abuse severity. Correlation analysis linked abuse incidents with elevated Botrytis incidence and firmness loss quantified at destination. The study provides a field-validated evidence base for the adoption of stricter pre-cooling protocols and improved door-management procedures, and introduces a temperature abuse index (TAI) metric applicable to cold-chain audit frameworks. Recommendations for future sensor infrastructure investment by exporters are presented.

title: Active packaging with natural antimicrobial sachets for blueberry shelf-life extension
abstract: Active packaging systems incorporating volatile antimicrobial agents derived from plant extracts represent a promising complement to conventional modified atmosphere packaging (MAP) for fresh blueberries. This study assessed the efficacy of sachets containing encapsulated thymol and carvacrol — sourced from wild thyme and oregano — integrated into clamshell packaging under a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ atmosphere at 2 °C. Blueberry quality was monitored over 18 days for firmness, total anthocyanin content, weight loss, and microbiological load (total aerobic count and Botrytis incidence). Active MAP sachets reduced total aerobic counts by 1.8 log CFU/g relative to passive MAP controls at day 12 and delayed visible mold onset by four days. Anthocyanin retention was significantly higher in active MAP treatments (p < 0.05), suggesting a secondary antioxidant protective effect. Consumer acceptability scores obtained through a 40-member sensory panel confirmed marketable quality at day 14 for saline-active MAP versus day 10 for passive MAP controls. Migration testing confirmed that thymol and carvacrol residues in fruit tissue remained below European regulatory thresholds. This work demonstrates the practical feasibility of combining MAP gas composition with natural antimicrobial active elements for export-grade blueberry packaging.

title: Integrating predictive microbiology into cold-chain digital twins for berry logistics
abstract: Digital twin frameworks — virtual replicas of physical supply chains updated by real-time sensor data — offer a new paradigm for proactive spoilage management in perishable food logistics. This paper describes the integration of validated predictive microbial growth models for Botrytis cinerea and total aerobic bacteria into a digital twin architecture developed for Serbian berry cold-chain operations. The system ingests temperature and relative humidity streams from IoT sensors placed within refrigerated transport units and storage rooms, feeding real-time inputs into a model library calibrated for raspberry, blueberry, and strawberry substrates. A graphical dashboard presents logistics managers with dynamically updated remaining shelf-life estimates and spoilage risk scores for each consignment. A 12-month pilot deployment covering four exporting companies and 240 consignments demonstrated that digital twin alerts correctly flagged 88% of consignments subsequently confirmed to exhibit elevated spoilage at destination. False-positive rates were 9%, attributed primarily to anomalous sensor placement near evaporator coils. Integration with enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems for automated re-routing decisions is discussed as a near-term development pathway. The study establishes a reproducible blueprint for deploying predictive microbiology within commercial cold-chain digital twin platforms in the Serbian fruit export sector.

title: Effect of pre-cooling rate on modified atmosphere equilibration and raspberry quality
abstract: Rapid and uniform pre-cooling of freshly harvested raspberries prior to MAP sealing is critical for establishing the target equilibrium atmosphere within packaging. This experimental study examined three pre-cooling protocols — forced-air cooling at 2 m/s, hydrocooling at 1 °C, and room cooling as control — applied to raspberry punnets subsequently sealed under a 5% O₂/15% CO₂ MAP at 2 °C storage. Headspace gas composition was monitored at 0, 6, 12, 24, and 48 hours post-sealing using an inline gas analyzer. Fruit core temperature profiles, firmness, respiration rate (CO₂ evolution), and drip loss were recorded throughout a 10-day storage trial. Forced-air cooling achieved target core temperature in 38 minutes compared to 210 minutes for room cooling, and resulted in target headspace O₂ equilibration 14 hours earlier than the room-cooled control. Faster equilibration was associated with significantly lower Botrytis incidence (p < 0.01) and superior firmness retention at day 8. Hydrocooling achieved comparable equilibration speed but introduced elevated free moisture that promoted calyx decay. The findings quantify the shelf-life benefit of investing in forced-air cooling infrastructure and inform revised pre-cooling standard operating procedures for export packers.

title: Shelf-life prediction for strawberries under fluctuating cold-chain temperatures using a stochastic modelling approach
abstract: Deterministic predictive models assume fixed temperature inputs, which rarely reflect the stochastic nature of real-world cold-chain environments. This study presents a stochastic modelling framework for predicting the remaining shelf life of fresh strawberries under realistic fluctuating temperature conditions. A Monte Carlo simulation approach was applied to propagate uncertainty in temperature distribution parameters — derived from 180 sensor-monitored consignments — through a validated secondary model for total aerobic count growth on strawberry. Output distributions of predicted shelf life were compared against observed microbiological end-point data from the same consignments. The stochastic model significantly outperformed its deterministic equivalent in capturing the spread of observed outcomes, with prediction intervals covering 91% of empirical data points. Sensitivity analysis identified mean transport temperature and frequency of door-opening events as the two variables contributing most to shelf-life variance. A simplified probabilistic shelf-life index (PSI) was derived for use by quality managers without specialist modelling expertise. The framework is applicable to other soft fruits and other pathogen or spoilage organism combinations, provided primary growth data are available. This work advances the practical deployment of quantitative risk-informed decision-making in Serbian berry export supply chains.

title: Packaging material permeability screening for MAP of mixed-berry trays
abstract: Mixed-berry trays combining raspberry, blueberry, and blackberry are commercially attractive but present packaging engineering challenges because each species has a distinct optimal modified atmosphere range and a different respiration rate at equivalent temperatures. This study evaluated 12 commercially available polymeric packaging films differing in oxygen transmission rate (OTR) and carbon dioxide transmission rate (CO₂TR) for their suitability in MAP of mixed-berry trays stored at 2 °C. Headspace equilibrium gas compositions were measured at 24-hour intervals over eight days and compared against species-specific target ranges determined from prior single-species trials. Microbiological and firmness data were collected at four-day intervals. A film with OTR of 3,800 cm³/m²/day and CO₂TR of 18,000 cm³/m²/day delivered headspace conditions within acceptable ranges for all three species simultaneously and reduced mold incidence by 55% relative to a standard polyethylene control. Finite element modelling of gas permeation through the film was used to confirm experimental headspace trends and to predict equilibrium under alternative tray fill-weight scenarios. The results provide film specification guidance for packers handling mixed-berry formats and demonstrate that a single film solution can satisfy the conflicting atmosphere requirements of co-packaged fruit species.

title: Food preservation engineering for horticultural products: packaging and cold-chain perspectives
abstract: This book chapter provides a comprehensive treatment of the engineering principles underpinning postharvest preservation of fresh horticultural products, with emphasis on modified atmosphere packaging and cold-chain management. The chapter opens with a review of the biochemical and microbiological deterioration mechanisms that govern shelf life in soft fruits, including ethylene-mediated ripening, oxidative browning, and fungal pathogen proliferation. It then develops the engineering framework for MAP system design, covering gas mass balance modelling, film permeability selection, and tray geometry effects on headspace equilibration dynamics. Cold-chain management is addressed through the lens of predictive microbiology, explaining how primary and secondary models can be linked to temperature monitoring data to generate real-time shelf-life estimates. A section on supply chain integration discusses how MAP and predictive modelling tools can be embedded in digital logistics systems. Case studies drawn from Serbian berry export operations illustrate the translation of laboratory models into operational practice, including a worked example of a forced-air pre-cooling and MAP line for a mid-sized raspberry exporter. The chapter concludes with a forward-looking discussion of emerging active packaging technologies and AI-assisted cold-chain optimisation. It is intended for graduate students and food industry engineers seeking a practically oriented reference.

title: Sensor-based remaining shelf-life labelling for berry exports: a feasibility study
abstract: Static best-before labelling does not reflect the actual quality state of perishable foods subjected to variable cold-chain conditions. This paper reports a feasibility study for implementing sensor-based dynamic remaining shelf-life (RSL) labelling on raspberry and blueberry consignments exported from Serbia. Time-temperature indicator (TTI) labels from two commercial suppliers were benchmarked against data-logger-calibrated predictive model outputs for Botrytis growth and total aerobic count across 24 simulated and 16 real export consignments. TTI colour-response kinetics were characterised at 0, 4, 8, and 12 °C and integrated into an RSL calculation algorithm using an Arrhenius-based temperature dependence model. Agreement between TTI-derived RSL and model-derived RSL was within ±1.2 days for 79% of consignments, which was deemed commercially acceptable by participating exporters. A cost–benefit analysis estimated that TTI-based RSL labelling could reduce consignment rejection rates at destination by 18–24%, yielding a positive return on investment for exporters operating above 50 tonnes per season. Regulatory and labelling compliance considerations under EU food law are discussed, along with the data requirements for formal TTI validation. The study supports the case for piloting RSL labelling in the Serbian berry export sector as part of a broader cold-chain quality assurance programme.

title: Automated extraction of road edge lines from mobile laser scanning data using intensity gradients and geometric constraints
abstract: Road edge delineation from mobile laser scanning (MLS) point clouds is complicated by occlusions, varying scan density, and the presence of roadside clutter. This study presents a pipeline that combines intensity gradient analysis with local planarity filtering to isolate edge candidates from MLS data collected along 42 km of suburban roads in Vojvodina. A RANSAC-based fitting step then enforces geometric continuity. The method was evaluated against manual delineation by two independent operators; mean lateral deviation was 4.7 cm over the full corridor with completeness of 93.1 %. Runtime on a standard workstation was approximately 18 minutes per kilometre of raw data. Comparison with a region-growing baseline showed a 12-percentage-point improvement in completeness in areas with dense vegetation. The approach is implemented as a post-processing module compatible with LAS 1.4 format files and tested on data acquired with a Riegl VMX-250 system.

title: Planar segmentation of terrestrial laser scans for façade modelling of historic masonry structures
abstract: Documenting historic masonry façades for conservation purposes requires millimetre-level accuracy and the ability to distinguish architectural features such as window surrounds, cornices, and recessed panels. This paper applies a region-growing planar segmentation algorithm to three terrestrial laser scans of a 19th-century administrative building in Novi Sad, acquired with a Leica ScanStation C10 at four scan positions. Segment normals and bounding extents are used to classify regions into wall faces, openings, and decorative elements according to a four-class scheme. Compared with a manually produced 2D elevation drawing, the automated reconstruction achieved a geometric deviation below 8 mm for 87 % of planar surfaces. The main failure mode was shallow-relief decoration, where scan density fell below 5 pts/cm². The output is exported as an IFC 2x3 partial model suitable for import into standard BIM authoring tools. Scan registration error across stations was 2.1 mm RMS.

title: Ground filtering of airborne LiDAR over heterogeneous terrain in the Pannonian lowland using adaptive TIN densification
abstract: Standard ground-filtering algorithms were developed primarily for hilly or forested terrain and perform inconsistently over the flat, agriculturally dominated landscapes of the Pannonian basin. This study systematically evaluates adaptive TIN densification with varied slope threshold and initial seed-point spacing parameters on six 1 km² tiles from an ALS campaign over Vojvodina, acquired at 4 pts/m² average density. Reference ground points were collected by RTK GNSS along 38 km of transects. Optimal parameter combinations differed significantly between cropland, orchard, and settlement cover types, reducing Type I error from 9.4 % to 3.1 % in orchard areas. A stratified parameter selection scheme based on land-cover classification prior to filtering is proposed and achieves 2.3 cm normalised median absolute deviation against RTK reference across all tiles. Results suggest that single-parameter configurations commonly used in national mapping programmes introduce systematic DTM biases of up to 14 cm in orchard zones.

title: Scan-to-BIM workflow for reinforced concrete bridge decks: point cloud segmentation and IFC parametric object generation
abstract: As-built documentation of reinforced concrete bridge decks typically relies on 2D drawings that do not capture deformation or dimensional variation accumulated during construction. This paper describes a workflow in which a terrestrial laser scan of a two-span highway bridge near Ruma, Serbia, is processed to extract geometric parameters for a parametric IFC model. Segmentation combines a vertical slice projection to isolate the deck soffit from abutments and piers, followed by least-squares cylinder fitting for column members. Processed point cloud density was 6 pts/cm² on the soffit. The generated IFC model reproduced measured span lengths with deviations below 11 mm and detected 23 locations where deck soffit elevation deviated from design by more than 15 mm, attributed to formwork settlement. Total processing time from registered point cloud to IFC export was approximately 4.5 hours for the 340 m bridge. The workflow was tested against conventional total-station survey on 120 check points.

title: Comparison of voxel-based and point-based feature descriptors for semantic labelling of railway infrastructure point clouds
abstract: Semantic labelling of railway corridor point clouds must distinguish rails, sleepers, ballast, catenary poles, and trackside vegetation from a single merged scan. This study compares three feature descriptor strategies — voxel occupancy histograms, FPFH descriptors computed at the raw point level, and a hybrid approach combining both — when used as input to a random forest classifier. Training and test data were taken from a 6.2 km MLS survey of a single-track line in northern Serbia, manually labelled into six classes across 22 million points. The hybrid approach achieved mean class accuracy of 81.4 % versus 74.6 % for voxel-only and 78.9 % for FPFH-only, with the largest gains for the rail and sleeper classes. Classifier training was performed with 5-fold cross-validation; results were consistent across three independently labelled 500 m test sections. Processing speed differences between the three strategies were minor once voxelisation time was included.

title: Deep learning-based semantic segmentation of outdoor LiDAR point clouds: a benchmark on infrastructure classes in the Western Balkans
abstract: Several deep learning architectures for 3D point cloud segmentation have been developed on datasets dominated by urban environments in Western Europe or North America. This study constructs a labelled benchmark dataset of 14 airborne and terrestrial LiDAR scenes from road, bridge, and utility corridor surveys in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and North Macedonia, covering approximately 480 million labelled points across nine infrastructure classes. Three architectures — PointNet++, RandLA-Net, and KPConv — are evaluated without and with domain-adaptive fine-tuning. Without fine-tuning, mean intersection-over-union (mIoU) across the nine classes was 54.3 %, 61.7 %, and 63.8 %, respectively. Fine-tuning with 15 % of the local dataset improved all three by 8–11 mIoU points. The benchmark dataset is publicly released under a Creative Commons licence through the Faculty of Technical Sciences data repository. Failure analysis highlights challenges with thin linear objects such as guardrails and overhead cables.

title: Automatic detection of delamination and spalling on concrete bridge elements from terrestrial laser scan data using surface normal deviation maps
abstract: Surface defects on concrete bridge elements are conventionally detected by visual inspection, which is subjective and difficult on high elements. This study investigates whether terrestrial laser scanning can reliably detect delaminated and spalled areas through surface normal deviation maps computed from registered scans. Data were collected on five concrete bridges in Vojvodina at an average density of 4 pts/cm². Reference defect maps were produced by two certified inspectors. Normal deviation maps thresholded at 5° identified 78 % of confirmed delamination areas of 100 cm² or larger and achieved a false-positive rate of 9 % per scan face. Smaller defects below 30 cm² were rarely detected at the achieved scan density. A simple decision rule combining local roughness and normal deviation reduced false positives to 4 % with a minor completeness reduction to 74 %. The paper discusses scan planning guidelines for defect-oriented surveys and the influence of incident angle on detection sensitivity.

title: Integration of LiDAR-derived as-built geometry with structural analysis models for existing reinforced concrete frames
abstract: Structural re-analysis of existing buildings typically relies on design drawings, which may not reflect actual constructed dimensions. This paper presents a method for generating finite-element input geometry directly from terrestrial LiDAR scans of a four-storey reinforced concrete frame building on the University of Novi Sad campus. Column and beam centreline positions and cross-section dimensions were extracted via principal-axis fitting to cylindrical and rectangular prism segments; extracted dimensions showed deviations of up to 27 mm from design drawings in column positions. The extracted geometry was imported into a plane-frame analysis model and seismic response analysis was repeated under Eurocode 8 load cases. Differences in first natural frequency between design and scan-derived models reached 4.3 %, attributable mainly to column eccentricities. The paper discusses the sensitivity of key response quantities to dimensional uncertainty and recommends a scan density of at least 3 pts/cm² for this application.

title: Evaluation of graph neural networks for instance segmentation of bridge components in merged terrestrial and UAV LiDAR point clouds
abstract: Merging terrestrial and UAV LiDAR captures complementary coverage of bridge geometry — the UAV covers the deck surface and approach fill, while terrestrial scans capture soffit and substructure. This creates multi-density, multi-view point clouds that challenge instance segmentation. This study applies three graph neural network architectures (DGCNN, SpiderCNN, and PointConv) to instance segmentation of 12 bridge component classes across a dataset of eight short- and medium-span concrete bridges in Serbia scanned in 2022–2023. After multi-scan registration, merged point densities ranged from 1.5 to 18 pts/cm² depending on location. Mean average precision at IoU threshold 0.5 was 58.4 %, 55.1 %, and 61.7 % for the three architectures; performance was substantially lower for thin elements such as parapets and drainage pipes. Training used a leave-two-bridges-out protocol. The paper also examines the effect of density normalisation as a preprocessing step on cross-density generalisation.

title: Point cloud-based change detection for periodic structural health monitoring of a concrete arch bridge: a two-year longitudinal study
abstract: Periodic structural health monitoring through repeat LiDAR scanning can detect geometric change accumulation without instrumenting a structure permanently. This paper reports a two-year study of a single-span concrete arch bridge in Srem, Serbia, with six scan epochs acquired at approximately four-month intervals using a Leica RTC360. A consistent registration protocol anchored to four embedded reflector targets achieves epoch-to-epoch registration accuracy of 1.3 mm RMS. M3C2 distance computation between consecutive epochs reveals a statistically significant downward displacement of 6.8 mm at mid-span between epochs 2 and 3, coinciding with a recorded heavy load event. No further progressive displacement was observed in subsequent epochs. Seasonal temperature variation correlated with reversible arch crown displacement of 2.1 mm peak-to-peak, consistent with thermal elongation calculations. The study demonstrates that repeat scanning at this accuracy level is a practical complement to conventional deformation monitoring for medium-span bridges with limited access.

title: Geometry–Pressure Mapping for Multi-Chamber Soft Grippers Using Reduced-Order Finite Element Surrogates
abstract: Full finite element simulations of pneumatic soft grippers are too slow for use inside real-time control loops, typically requiring several minutes per pressure increment. This work constructs a reduced-order surrogate by sampling a parametric FE model of a three-fingered gripper across a grid of 1,200 pressure combinations spanning 0–100 kPa per chamber. Principal component analysis is applied to the resulting nodal displacement fields, retaining 12 modes that capture 97.3% of shape variance. A radial basis function network trained on 900 samples and tested on 300 predicts finger-tip Cartesian position with a mean absolute error of 1.4 mm and evaluates in under 2 ms on a standard x86 core. Physical validation used a gripper fabricated from a Yeoh-characterised silicone and an optical tracking system with 0.3 mm resolution. Agreement between surrogate predictions and measured positions was within 2.1 mm across 48 unseen pressure states. The surrogate is integrated into a model-based feedforward path in a subsequent control study.

title: Closed-Loop Pressure Control of a Pneumatic Continuum Gripper Using a PI Controller with Anti-Windup Saturation
abstract: This paper presents the design, implementation, and experimental evaluation of a closed-loop pressure control system for a three-fingered pneumatic soft gripper intended for handling irregularly shaped food items. Each chamber is regulated independently by a miniature proportional valve driven by a microcontroller running at 1 kHz. A discrete-time proportional–integral controller with back-calculation anti-windup is tuned for each channel using a step-response identification procedure at operating pressures between 0 and 90 kPa. Reference tracking experiments across step amplitudes of 10, 30, and 60 kPa show settling times below 180 ms and steady-state errors below 0.8 kPa. Disturbance rejection tests, in which a 200 g mass is placed on a finger mid-trial, demonstrate pressure recovery within 220 ms. Grip trials on five produce items—cherry tomatoes, strawberries, a peach, a bell pepper, and a courgette—measured contact force via load cells embedded in the palm structure. No surface damage was recorded at the selected pressure profiles, and successful transfer was achieved in 94 of 100 trials across all items.
venue: Acta Technica Mechatronica

title: Effect of Mould Tolerances and Mixing Ratio Deviations on the Mechanical Repeatability of Cast Silicone Actuator Segments
abstract: Soft actuator performance in production settings depends on the consistency of the fabrication process. This study quantifies how two controllable process variables—mould dimensional tolerance (±0.1 mm versus ±0.3 mm) and silicone part-A/part-B mixing ratio deviation (±1%, ±3%, ±5% by mass)—affect the mechanical output repeatability of single-chamber bending actuator segments. Twelve batches of ten segments each were produced across a full factorial design. Each segment was characterised by tip-displacement at 60 kPa and Shore A hardness at three locations. Analysis of variance showed that mixing ratio deviation was the dominant factor, accounting for 68% of tip-displacement variance; mould tolerance contributed 19%. A ±3% mixing deviation produced a coefficient of variation in tip displacement of 11.4%, rising to 23.7% at ±5%. Hardness maps revealed a consistent stiffness gradient along segment length that correlated with incomplete degassing. Practical tolerance recommendations are given for small-batch laboratory fabrication, and a simple gravimetric mixing protocol is described that reduced mixing-ratio error to below ±0.8% in follow-up trials.

title: Comparison of CRF and BiLSTM models for fault-type extraction from distribution network work orders
abstract: Automatic identification of fault types from free-text work orders can reduce the manual effort required for failure statistics compilation in power utilities. This study benchmarks two sequence-labelling architectures—a linear-chain Conditional Random Field (CRF) with hand-crafted features and a bidirectional LSTM with character-level embeddings—on the annotated corpus described in earlier work. Experiments use 80/10/10 train/development/test splits with five-fold cross-validation. The BiLSTM model trained on 100-dimensional embeddings pre-trained on a general Serbian news corpus achieved an F1 of 0.79 on the fault-descriptor class, compared with 0.73 for the CRF baseline. Performance dropped to 0.71 for both models on records shorter than fifteen tokens, which represent 22 percent of the corpus. Error analysis identified equipment-specific jargon as the dominant source of misclassification. The study recommends domain-adapted embeddings as a priority for future work.

title: Structured failure data recovery from legacy maintenance archives: a hybrid extraction pipeline for distribution transformers
abstract: Many electricity operators hold decades of maintenance history in scanned paper documents or inconsistently formatted spreadsheets that cannot be directly used for reliability analysis. This paper presents a pipeline combining optical character recognition, rule-based post-correction, and a fine-tuned BERT-based entity extractor to recover structured failure records from a 22-year archive of distribution transformer maintenance documents. The archive comprised 6,400 scanned forms from a Serbian operator, with variable print quality. After OCR and correction, the entity extractor was fine-tuned on 2,100 manually labelled sentences from the target domain. Extraction quality was assessed against 800 fully hand-transcribed reference records: macro-averaged F1 reached 0.82 for equipment identifiers and 0.77 for fault descriptors. The recovered dataset contained 5,890 usable transformer records with at least one fault event, enabling subsequent statistical analysis of failure rates by transformer age group and manufacturer type. Three age cohorts showed statistically significant differences in mean time between failures at the 0.05 significance level.

title: Integrating text-extracted failure events into Weibull reliability models for medium-voltage cable joints
abstract: Reliability models for electrical infrastructure assets conventionally rely on structured inspection databases, yet a substantial portion of failure information resides only in free-text maintenance records. This paper demonstrates a workflow in which failure events extracted via NLP from 8,300 work orders are fed into parametric survival models. The study focuses on medium-voltage cable joints maintained by a regional Serbian operator over 15 years. After extraction and deduplication, 1,940 failure events were identified, compared with 1,410 events available in the operator's structured database, representing a 37 percent increase in usable failure records. Two-parameter Weibull models were fitted to both the structured-only and combined datasets using maximum likelihood estimation. The combined dataset yielded a shape parameter of 2.31 (95% CI: 2.14–2.49) versus 2.07 (1.87–2.28) for the structured-only set, suggesting a stronger wear-out failure mode when more complete data are used. Implications for inspection interval optimisation are discussed.

title: Topic modelling of corrective maintenance records to identify recurrent failure patterns in urban distribution networks
abstract: Unsupervised topic modelling offers a way to surface recurring maintenance themes without predefined fault taxonomies. This study applies Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) and a Neural Topic Model (NTM) to 21,000 corrective maintenance records from an urban distribution network in Vojvodina, spanning 2010 to 2021. Records were pre-processed using a domain-adapted stop-word list and lemmatiser. Models with topic counts ranging from 10 to 40 were evaluated using coherence score and perplexity on a held-out 15 percent subset. The optimal LDA configuration (k=22) achieved a coherence score of 0.54, while the NTM reached 0.61 at k=20. Five dominant topics were identified relating to overhead line conductor fatigue, substation switchgear cleaning, cable trench water ingress, meter tampering, and vegetation contact. Temporal analysis showed that the water-ingress topic increased in relative frequency by 18 percentage points over the study period, consistent with changes in local precipitation patterns. Results were validated through structured interviews with five network planning engineers.

title: Predicting unplanned outage probability for overhead line sections using features extracted from historical work orders
abstract: Predicting which overhead line sections are at elevated risk of unplanned outage within a 90-day horizon is operationally useful for preventive maintenance scheduling. This study constructs a supervised classification model using features derived entirely from historical work-order text, supplemented by line age and network topology attributes. Text features include fault-type counts per section, temporal gap statistics between successive maintenance visits, and sentiment-proxy scores derived from technician comment polarity. The dataset covers 1,230 overhead line sections in a Vojvodina distribution network over a ten-year observation window, with 312 sections experiencing at least one unplanned outage in each rolling 90-day period. A gradient boosting classifier achieved an AUC of 0.78 on a held-out test set using stratified five-fold cross-validation, compared with 0.71 for a logistic regression baseline using only age and length features. SHAP analysis identified fault-recurrence frequency and mean inter-maintenance interval as the two most influential predictors. The model has been deployed in a pilot evaluation with the cooperating operator since early 2024.

title: Benchmark evaluation of information extraction pipelines on a multi-operator Serbian electrical maintenance corpus
abstract: Evaluating how well information extraction systems generalise across different operators and record-keeping styles is important for practical deployment. This preprint describes a benchmark dataset assembled from maintenance records contributed by three Serbian distribution operators, comprising 34,500 sentences with entity and relation annotations. Four extraction pipelines are compared: a rule-based baseline, a CRF system, a fine-tuned BERT-base-multilingual model, and a fine-tuned domain-adapted model developed by the authors. Performance is evaluated separately for each operator subset to assess cross-operator generalisation. The domain-adapted model achieves the highest mean F1 of 0.80 across all operators and entity types, but shows a performance drop of 9 percentage points when applied to Operator C, whose records use a distinct abbreviation convention. The benchmark dataset and evaluation scripts are deposited in an open repository. The paper is currently under review at a peer-reviewed journal.

title: Dynamic Race Detection at Runtime for Embedded Systems Using Shadow Memory with Fixed Overhead
abstract: Dynamic data-race detectors based on shadow memory, such as those following the ThreadSanitizer design, impose memory overhead proportional to the monitored address space. On microcontrollers with 8–256 kB of RAM this overhead is generally unacceptable. This paper proposes a fixed-overhead shadow-memory scheme that maintains race-detection state only for a configurable set of shared variables explicitly declared by the developer, reducing RAM overhead to a user-tuned constant. A prototype is implemented as a set of C macros and a lightweight runtime library occupying 1.4 kB of flash and 48 bytes of RAM. The approach is evaluated in simulation using QEMU emulating an STM32F4 target. On 14 benchmark programs containing injected races the tool detected 11 of 14 injected races at runtime with no false positives during a two-hour test run per program. The paper discusses the trade-off between coverage and overhead, and compares coverage against two static tools on the same benchmarks.

title: Lightweight Anomaly Detection for Resource-Constrained ICS Gateways: A Quantisation and Pruning Study
abstract: Many ICS sites route traffic through ARM-based gateways with 256 MB RAM and single-core processors. This paper evaluates the effect of weight quantisation (32-bit to 8-bit and 4-bit floating point) and structured pruning (removing 10%, 25%, 50% of autoencoder units) on detection performance and inference latency for traffic-based anomaly detectors. Experiments used three autoencoder architectures differing in depth (2, 4, 6 hidden layers) trained on Modbus/TCP and DNP3 captures. 8-bit quantisation reduced model size by 3.7× and inference time by 2.1× with an average AUROC reduction of 0.012. 4-bit quantisation introduced a 0.041 AUROC drop. Structured pruning at 25% improved inference speed by 1.4× with negligible performance loss; at 50%, AUROC declined by 0.028. A combined 8-bit quantised, 25%-pruned model achieved inference at 0.9 ms per 10-second window on an ARM Cortex-A7 target, fitting within a 10 ms cycle budget, making real-time deployment feasible without dedicated hardware accelerators.

title: Aspectual Errors in Written Production of Beginner English-Speaking Learners of Serbian
abstract: This study examined written texts produced by 38 beginner-level adult learners of Serbian as a foreign language enrolled in a university language course in Novi Sad during one academic semester. Learner texts were collected at three intervals and annotated for verb tokens; 412 finite verb forms were identified and coded for aspect selection accuracy. Results showed that learners selected the imperfective aspect correctly in 71% of cases where it was target-like, but overused imperfective forms in telic contexts at a rate of 54%. Perfective forms were used in only 18% of obligatory contexts at the start of the course, rising to 34% by the final collection point. The data suggest that learners initially map imperfective morphology onto a general non-past interpretation, delaying the acquisition of the perfective–imperfective opposition. Pedagogical implications for the sequencing of aspect instruction in Serbian L2 courses are discussed.

title: Prefixation as Perfectivisation: What L2 Learners Know About Prefix–Stem Pairings in Serbian
abstract: Serbian verbal prefixation involves both lexical meaning modification and aspectual change. This study used a forced-choice acceptability judgement task presented to 74 intermediate and advanced L2 learners of Serbian (L1 English and L1 German, roughly equal split) alongside a native-speaker control group of 20 participants. Stimuli consisted of 48 minimal pairs contrasting prefixed perfective verbs with their imperfective base forms in sentence contexts with perfective-forcing and imperfective-forcing adverbials. Learners at the intermediate level accepted prefixed forms in imperfective-forcing contexts significantly more often than controls (error rate 38% vs. 7%), suggesting difficulty in disentangling aspectual from lexical functions of prefixes. Advanced learners approached control performance (error rate 12%). An interaction between prefix type and proficiency was found: empty perfectivisers (e.g., na-, po- with minimal semantic contribution) were harder for learners than semantically transparent prefixes regardless of proficiency level.

title: Explicit Grammar Instruction and the Acquisition of Aspectual Contrasts in Serbian: A Pre–Post Classroom Study
abstract: This paper reports a pre–post quasi-experimental study testing whether explicit instruction on the imperfective–perfective opposition improves accuracy in a group of adult L2 Serbian learners over a four-week period. Three intact classes (n = 67 total) in a university Serbian-for-foreigners programme were assigned to explicit instruction, implicit exposure, and control conditions. Pre-test, immediate post-test, and delayed post-test data were collected using a sentence completion task targeting 24 aspect contexts. Mixed-effects logistic regression showed that the explicit instruction group improved significantly from pre-test to immediate post-test (β = 1.43, SE = 0.31, p < .001) and retained the gains at the delayed post-test six weeks later. The implicit and control groups showed no significant change. These findings support the effectiveness of form-focused instruction for aspectual morphology in L2 Serbian and are discussed in the context of processability theory.

title: Aspect in Serbian: A Pedagogical Description for L2 Teaching Contexts
abstract: This book chapter provides a linguistically grounded yet pedagogically oriented description of the Serbian aspectual system intended for curriculum designers and instructors working in formal L2 teaching contexts. The chapter covers the morphological expression of aspect through prefixation, suffixation, and suppletion; the distribution of aspects in past, present, and future tenses; aspectual interaction with quantification and negation; and the major pragmatic uses of the present imperfective. Each section is accompanied by annotated example sentences drawn from a 150,000-token corpus of contemporary Serbian prose and from learner error data collected by the author over five years. The chapter also reviews empirical acquisition findings relevant to instruction, identifies the aspectual contrasts that prove most persistent as sources of error for English-speaking and German-speaking learners, and offers a set of criteria for sequencing aspect-related content across proficiency levels from A1 to B2.

title: Reaction Times in Aspectual Decision Tasks: L1 and L2 Speakers of Serbian Compared
abstract: Using a binary forced-choice paradigm, this study measured reaction times of 26 native speakers of Serbian and 52 advanced L2 learners of Serbian (L1 English, n = 27; L1 Hungarian, n = 25) on 60 sentence contexts each requiring selection of a perfective or imperfective verb form. Stimuli were presented via a browser-based experiment platform adapted for use in the university computer lab. Native speakers responded significantly faster than both L2 groups (mean RT difference approximately 380 ms) and showed near-ceiling accuracy (97.2%). L2 learners achieved comparable accuracy to natives (91.4% for L1 English, 89.8% for L1 Hungarian) but with substantially higher RT variance, pointing to continued reliance on controlled processing. L1 Hungarian learners were not significantly faster than L1 English learners despite Hungarian's having a grammaticalised aspect distinction, suggesting that positive L1 transfer does not straightforwardly speed up L2 processing at the advanced level.

title: Empty vs. Lexically Transparent Prefixes: Acquisition Difficulty in Adult L2 Serbian
abstract: Serbian verbal prefixes range from those contributing a precise directional or quantificational meaning (lexically transparent) to those that primarily mark aspect change with minimal lexical modification (often called empty or light prefixes). This study examines whether this distinction predicts acquisition difficulty for adult learners. Participants were 88 learners of Serbian distributed across three proficiency levels (A2, B1, B2) assessed by a standardised placement test. They completed an error detection and correction task involving 56 verb sentences manipulating prefix type and aspectual context. Binomial mixed-effects models showed a significant interaction between prefix type and proficiency level: at A2 and B1, error rates were substantially higher for empty prefixes (48% and 31%) than transparent prefixes (27% and 14%); by B2 the gap narrowed but remained significant. Learners appeared to rely on lexical–semantic cues when available and struggled to infer aspect solely from morphological form with empty prefixes.

title: Building a Learner Corpus of Written Serbian: Design, Annotation Scheme, and Pilot Study
abstract: This paper describes the design and construction of the Novi Sad Learner Corpus of Serbian (NoSLeCS), a collection of written texts produced by adult L2 learners of Serbian in a university instructional setting. The pilot version of the corpus comprises 210,000 tokens from 1,140 texts submitted by learners at six proficiency levels (A1–C1) between 2016 and 2021. The annotation scheme covers learner L1, proficiency level, task type, and a morphosyntactic tagset adapted from the standard Serbian morphosyntactic description, with an additional error tier for aspect and prefixation. The paper discusses practical decisions taken in annotation, inter-annotator reliability measures (Cohen's κ = 0.81 for the aspect error tier), and presents a pilot frequency analysis showing that learner texts at A2 level contain a significantly higher proportion of imperfective finite verbs compared with a matched sample of native-speaker texts. Plans for corpus expansion and public access are outlined.

title: Does Aspect Instruction Transfer Across Tenses? Evidence from Past and Future Contexts in L2 Serbian
abstract: Most classroom instruction on verbal aspect in Serbian L2 courses focuses on past-tense contexts, where the contrast is most consistently taught and tested. This study asks whether explicit aspect instruction in past-tense contexts generalises to future-tense contexts. Sixty adult learners of Serbian at B1 level were randomly assigned to an instruction group and a comparison group. The instruction group received six hours of explicit instruction targeting aspect in past-tense narratives; the comparison group received equivalent exposure to Serbian texts without aspect focus. Both groups were tested on past-tense and future-tense aspect contexts before instruction, immediately after, and six weeks later. The instruction group showed clear gains in past-tense contexts (d = 0.94) and moderate, statistically significant transfer to future-tense contexts (d = 0.52). Gain scores in the two contexts were correlated (r = .61), suggesting that learners form a more generalised aspectual representation rather than a tense-specific one, though the transfer was partial.

title: Aspect and Negation in L2 Serbian: Are Learners Sensitive to the Imperfective Preference Under Negation?
abstract: In Serbian, negation creates a strong preference for imperfective aspect in many contexts where perfective would otherwise be the default. This study investigates whether adult L2 learners of Serbian at B1 and B2 levels are sensitive to this constraint. Ninety-two learners and 25 native-speaker controls completed a sentence acceptability rating task (7-point scale) in which 40 critical sentences manipulated aspect (perfective vs. imperfective) and negation (negated vs. affirmative) in four context types. Native speakers rated perfective forms under negation substantially lower than imperfective forms in the same contexts (mean difference 2.8 scale points). B2 learners showed a similar but weaker pattern (mean difference 1.6 points), while B1 learners showed no reliable sensitivity to the constraint (mean difference 0.4 points). Results suggest that the aspect–negation interaction is acquired relatively late, consistent with its low salience in standard classroom instruction materials.

title: Frequency Effects in the Acquisition of Serbian Prefix–Base Pairs: Evidence from Corpus and Experiment
abstract: This preprint reports an in-progress study combining corpus frequency data from a 50-million-token reference corpus of contemporary Serbian with experimental data from 110 L2 learners of Serbian at three proficiency levels. For each of 80 target prefix–base verb pairs, corpus frequency and frequency of the perfective/imperfective ratio in naturalistic text were computed. Learners completed a fill-in-the-blank production task targeting these pairs. Preliminary mixed-effects modelling indicates that corpus frequency of the prefixed form is a significant predictor of production accuracy (β = 0.38, SE = 0.08, p < .001) after controlling for proficiency level and prefix type. Pairs in which the prefixed form accounts for over 70% of occurrences in the corpus are produced accurately by B1 learners at a rate of 63%, compared with 31% for pairs with lower perfective-form dominance. The study calls for frequency-informed sequencing of vocabulary instruction for prefixed verbs in Serbian L2 courses.

title: Mapping slow-moving slope failures in Fruška Gora loess using C-band InSAR coherence time series
abstract: Loess slopes along the southern margin of Fruška Gora are susceptible to shallow translational failures that accumulate displacements of a few millimetres per year, making them difficult to detect by conventional field surveys. This study used 42 descending Sentinel-1 SLC acquisitions from 2017 to 2019 to produce coherence difference maps and two-pass differential interferograms at 20 m posting. Spatial clustering of low-coherence zones was compared against a regional inventory of reported mass movements and a 1:25 000 geological map. Eleven active loess flow lobes were delineated with plan areas between 0.3 and 4.8 hectares. Mean line-of-sight velocity within the identified zones reached −6.1 mm/yr, with peak seasonal excursions of ±9 mm coinciding with spring snowmelt periods identified in ERA5 soil-moisture records. The coherence-based screening reduced the candidate area requiring field validation by 63 % compared to slope-angle thresholding alone. Results indicate that routine Sentinel-1 coherence monitoring can serve as a low-cost early indicator of reactivating loess failures before visible scarps form.

title: Comparison of StaMPS and MintPy time-series solutions for a loess slope test site in Vojvodina
abstract: Two widely used persistent scatterer and small-baseline processing chains, StaMPS and MintPy, were applied to an identical stack of 61 Sentinel-1 descending acquisitions over a 25 km² loess test site in western Vojvodina to evaluate consistency of derived displacement time series. Atmospheric correction in MintPy used ERA5 tropospheric delay estimates; StaMPS relied on spatial-temporal filtering. Median absolute deviation between corresponding pixel velocities was 0.7 mm/yr for stable reference areas and rose to 2.1 mm/yr within active deformation zones, where phase unwrapping errors in StaMPS introduced isolated artefacts. MintPy small-baseline subsets achieved 18 % higher scatterer density owing to relaxed amplitude dispersion thresholds. Seasonal deformation signals with amplitudes of 3–5 mm were reproduced consistently by both methods. Recommendations are provided for selecting processing parameters appropriate to low-scatterer-density agricultural loess environments, where industrial reflectors or corner reflectors may be needed to augment natural scatterer networks.

title: Corner reflector network design for SAR deformation monitoring in low-density scatterer environments: lessons from loess slopes
abstract: Persistent scatterer methods underperform in rural loess landscapes where natural and built scatterers are sparse. This paper describes the design, installation, and first-year performance of a network of 12 trihedral aluminium corner reflectors deployed on three loess slope sites in the Vojvodina–Srem transition zone. Reflector dimensions were sized for a radar cross-section exceeding 30 dBm² at Sentinel-1 C-band incidence angles of 33–46°. Amplitude dispersion index values for all reflectors remained below 0.15 throughout 52 acquisitions from April 2022 to April 2023, satisfying the standard threshold for persistent scatterers. Phase quality assessment showed temporal coherence above 0.92. Initial displacement time series at three sites revealed velocity gradients of 1.8–7.6 mm/yr along slope profiles of 60–140 m length, resolvable only because the reflector spacing was deliberately set to 15–25 m to capture sub-lobe kinematics. Installation and maintenance costs per reflector are reported to enable cost–benefit assessment for operational monitoring programmes.

title: SAR-based landslide inventory update for the Serbian loess belt: 2015–2024 displacement catalogue
abstract: An updated inventory of active loess landslides along the Danube and Sava river corridors in Serbia was compiled by systematic analysis of Sentinel-1 ascending and descending track pairs. Mean-velocity maps were generated for 38 independent tracks using MintPy small-baseline processing of the full 2015–2024 archive, totalling over 2 400 acquisitions. Automated detection using a threshold of −3 mm/yr identified 214 candidate deformation zones, of which 178 were confirmed as landslide-related after cross-checking with topographic derivatives and existing geological maps. The confirmed inventory covers a total planimetric area of 83 km² and replaces a previous field-based inventory of 91 features. Median displacement rate across all confirmed features was −5.4 mm/yr in LOS. Temporal analysis reveals that 34 features showed episodic behaviour with quiescent intervals exceeding 18 months, complicating monitoring strategies that rely on short revisit windows. The catalogue is made available as an open GeoPackage dataset.

title: Seasonal deformation cycles in Pannonian loess slopes resolved by Sentinel-1 time series and GNSS benchmarks
abstract: Loess slopes in the Pannonian region undergo reversible seasonal swelling and shrinkage driven by moisture content changes, superimposed on irreversible creep. Disentangling these components is important for assessing true hazard progression. This study co-located eight dual-frequency GNSS benchmarks with persistent scatterer positions on two loess slopes monitored over 26 months from mid-2022 to late 2024. GNSS 3D displacement vectors were projected onto the Sentinel-1 LOS geometry and compared with InSAR time series at daily interpolated resolution. The reversible seasonal component, with peak-to-trough amplitude of 6–9 mm, was reproduced by both techniques with RMS agreement of 1.1 mm. After seasonal signal removal, GNSS-derived horizontal creep rates of 3.8 and 6.2 mm/yr were consistent with InSAR LOS rates projected assuming pure downslope motion at observed slope angles. The study confirms that short (6–12 month) InSAR time series may substantially overestimate or underestimate permanent creep rates if acquired during anomalously wet or dry periods.
