title: A data-driven framework for setting photovoltaic panel cleaning thresholds from satellite soiling index time series
abstract: Cleaning PV panels too frequently wastes water and labour; cleaning too infrequently reduces energy yield. This paper develops a decision-support framework that converts a satellite-derived soiling index time series into economically optimised cleaning trigger thresholds. The approach ingests continuous NSI records derived from Sentinel-2 at 10 m resolution, modelled dust-deposition rates, and a simple energy-loss model relating NSI to irradiance transmittance reduction (calibrated from field measurements at two Serbian sites). An optimisation routine minimises total cost – cleaning cost plus lost-energy cost – over a 12-month rolling window, outputting a site-specific NSI threshold that triggers a cleaning recommendation. When tested retrospectively on three years of data from a 22 MW installation in Srem, the framework suggested 7 cleaning events per year compared to the operator's fixed schedule of 12, while maintaining predicted annual energy loss below 1.8%. Monte Carlo sensitivity analysis shows that the result is most sensitive to the assumed cleaning cost per unit area (±40% variation changes trigger threshold by ±18%).

title: A comparison of Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms for ε-differential privacy in distributed logistic regression
abstract: This paper presents a systematic empirical comparison of Laplace and Gaussian noise mechanisms applied to gradient perturbation in distributed logistic regression over horizontally partitioned tabular data. Experiments were conducted on three UCI-style health datasets split across 5, 10, and 20 simulated data silos. For each mechanism, privacy budgets ε ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0} were evaluated against classification accuracy, convergence rate, and gradient variance. The Gaussian mechanism consistently achieved lower variance at equivalent privacy levels when the number of silos exceeded 10, at the cost of a looser (δ, ε)-guarantee. At ε = 1.0 and 10 silos, Gaussian noise reduced accuracy loss to 1.8 percentage points compared with 3.1 for Laplace. The study also provides closed-form expressions for the optimal noise scale under a fixed communication budget constraint, which practitioners can directly apply when designing federated deployments under regulatory privacy requirements.

title: Gradient clipping strategies and their effect on model convergence under differential privacy
abstract: Gradient clipping is a prerequisite step before noise injection in differentially private stochastic gradient descent, yet the choice of clipping norm C substantially affects both convergence speed and the final model accuracy. This work evaluates five clipping strategies — fixed, adaptive per-layer, percentile-based, norm-bounded, and gradient-free — across four standard image classification benchmarks. Using a ResNet-18 backbone and privacy budgets ε ∈ {1, 3, 8}, we measure test accuracy, gradient norm distribution, and number of rounds to convergence. Adaptive per-layer clipping consistently reduced accuracy degradation by 2–4 percentage points relative to the fixed norm baseline at ε = 1. We also derive a theoretical bound relating clipping norm to the expected bias introduced into the gradient estimate, providing guidance for practitioners selecting C without prior knowledge of the gradient distribution. All code and configuration files are released publicly.

title: Federated learning under heterogeneous data distributions: a taxonomy and benchmark for medical classification tasks
abstract: Non-IID data distributions across clinical sites are among the principal obstacles to deploying federated learning in healthcare settings. This paper proposes a four-axis taxonomy — label skew, feature skew, quantity skew, and temporal skew — and constructs a controlled benchmark using a chest X-ray dataset with 112,000 images distributed across 8 simulated silos under each skew type and combinations thereof. Five aggregation algorithms (FedAvg, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, FedNova, and a tuned FedAvg baseline) are evaluated on pathology detection accuracy (AUC), communication rounds to convergence, and fairness across silos measured by standard deviation of per-silo AUC. Under severe label skew (Dirichlet α = 0.1), SCAFFOLD achieved the highest mean AUC (0.83) but required 40% more communication rounds than FedAvg. The benchmark datasets, partition scripts, and evaluation code are made available to facilitate reproducible comparison of future aggregation methods.

title: Privacy-preserving federated segmentation of brain MRI: a cross-institutional pilot with three Serbian hospitals
abstract: This paper reports a pilot federated learning study for white-matter lesion segmentation on T2-FLAIR brain MRI, conducted in collaboration with three hospital radiology departments in Serbia under a data-use agreement. Each site contributed between 280 and 520 annotated volumes; scanner models and acquisition protocols differed across sites, introducing genuine feature heterogeneity. A 2D U-Net was trained using FedAvg with per-round Gaussian noise injection calibrated to ε = 3, δ = 10⁻⁵. The federated model reached a mean Dice score of 0.761 on a held-out central test set of 90 volumes, compared with 0.779 for a centrally trained model on the same aggregate data and 0.703 for the best single-site model. Communication was secured using pairwise additive secret sharing for gradient aggregation. Runtime per round was 8.4 minutes on average across three sites using a bandwidth-limited VPN connection, making weekly model updates feasible in the clinical setting.

title: Accounting for privacy loss across heterogeneous rounds in federated learning with the Rényi differential privacy framework
abstract: Standard (ε, δ)-DP accounting accumulates privacy loss additively across training rounds, which can be overly pessimistic when rounds differ in batch size, data volume, or clipping norm. This work adapts the Rényi differential privacy (RDP) accountant to handle per-round heterogeneity, deriving a tighter composition theorem for the federated setting where participating silos vary between rounds. The theoretical improvement is validated on synthetic Gaussian mechanisms and on a real federated chest X-ray classification task with 6 silos that each participate in a randomly chosen 70% of rounds. Under our tighter accounting, the effective ε after 200 rounds at a target δ = 10⁻⁶ is 1.94 versus the classical bound of 2.61, a reduction of 25.7%. The improved accountant is implemented as an open-source Python library compatible with standard federated learning frameworks and adds negligible computational overhead.

title: Robustness of differentially private federated learning against Byzantine gradient poisoning
abstract: Differential privacy noise injected during federated training can inadvertently mask Byzantine poisoning attacks, but it can also degrade the effectiveness of Byzantine-robust aggregation rules that rely on gradient statistics. This paper studies the interaction between DP noise and four robust aggregation rules — Krum, coordinate-wise median, trimmed mean, and FLTrust — under varying attacker fractions (10%, 20%, 30% of silos) and privacy budgets (ε = 1, 3, 8). Experiments use a retinal fundus image classification task across 12 simulated silos with one genuine non-IID partition. At ε = 1 and 20% Byzantine fraction, all four aggregators suffered accuracy drops of at least 6 percentage points, indicating that strong privacy budgets interfere with attack detection. A mixed strategy combining moderate DP (ε = 3) with FLTrust recovered 97% of the clean-training accuracy while reducing attack success rate to below 5%. Practical recommendations for deploying robust-and-private aggregation in medical imaging pipelines are given.

title: Communication-efficient federated learning with sparsified and privacy-preserving gradient updates for cross-silo imaging
abstract: Bandwidth constraints in cross-silo federated learning motivate gradient compression, but compressing gradients before adding DP noise can amplify privacy leakage. This paper characterises the privacy cost of top-k sparsification combined with Gaussian noise for k ∈ {0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1} (fraction of parameters transmitted) and derives a modified sensitivity bound accounting for sparsification bias. A 3D U-Net trained for liver segmentation on a four-silo dataset (total 1,840 CT volumes from publicly available sources with simulated partitioning) was used for validation. At k = 0.01, communication per round dropped by 94% with an additional accuracy penalty of only 1.2 Dice points compared with full-gradient transmission at the same ε = 2. The modified accountant provides tighter guarantees than treating sparsification and noise as independent, reducing the reported ε by up to 0.4 at δ = 10⁻⁵. Ablation results across 8 sparsification schedules are provided.

title: Personalised federated learning via locally adapted noise schedules for clinical imaging under strict privacy constraints
abstract: A single global noise schedule in differentially private federated learning treats all silos uniformly, which is suboptimal when silos differ greatly in dataset size, class distribution, or sensitivity requirements. This work introduces a site-adaptive noise scheduling scheme in which each participating silo negotiates a local ε budget subject to a global (ε_g, δ) guarantee enforced by the aggregation server. The scheme is formalised using an extension of the moments accountant and evaluated on a mammography classification task across 7 simulated silos partitioned from the INbreast-style dataset (9,400 images, 4-class pathology grading). Silos with more than 1,200 images were allocated ε = 2 locally while smaller silos used ε = 4; the global guarantee was ε_g = 3.1 at δ = 10⁻⁶. Personalised local models achieved mean AUC 0.871 versus 0.849 for the globally uniform baseline. The aggregation protocol is compatible with secure aggregation and adds 3.2% overhead in round time.

title: Differential privacy in federated learning for healthcare: a practitioner-oriented survey of methods, metrics, and regulatory context
abstract: This survey systematically reviews differentially private federated learning methods published between 2016 and 2022, with a focus on deployment requirements in healthcare settings. It covers noise mechanisms, composition theorems, secure aggregation protocols, and aggregation algorithms, organising 114 reviewed papers along four dimensions: privacy-utility trade-off, communication cost, robustness, and regulatory alignment. A recurring finding is that the GDPR and the Medical Devices Regulation create practical constraints that existing benchmark comparisons rarely address, such as the need to document privacy loss for each training run and to obtain data processor agreements before gradient sharing. The survey also identifies gaps: fewer than 20% of reviewed papers consider genuinely non-IID distributions derived from real multi-site clinical data; adversarial robustness is evaluated in only 31% of papers that use DP. A structured checklist is proposed for authors and practitioners to ensure that reported privacy claims are reproducible and regulation-aware.

title: Membership inference attack resilience of differentially private federated models for chest pathology detection
abstract: Membership inference attacks (MIA) attempt to determine whether a specific patient record was used to train a federated model, posing a concrete re-identification risk in clinical deployments. This paper evaluates the empirical resilience of differentially private federated chest X-ray classifiers against three MIA variants — shadow-model, likelihood-ratio, and label-only — under privacy budgets ε ∈ {0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, ∞}. The dataset is a 14-class pathology classification task with 95,000 images distributed across 6 silos with Dirichlet α = 0.3. At ε = 1, all three attacks achieved accuracy within 3.2 percentage points of random guessing (50%), confirming that the DP guarantee translates to practical MIA resistance at this budget. At ε = 10, the shadow-model attack reached 61.4% accuracy. Experiments also show that even without DP, FedAvg is substantially more resistant to MIA than centralised training, with MIA accuracy 8.1 points lower in the federated baseline. The interaction between aggregation frequency and MIA risk is quantified.

title: Federated continual learning for evolving medical imaging tasks with differential privacy
abstract: Federated learning deployments in clinical settings must accommodate the gradual introduction of new pathology classes and new participating sites over time — a federated continual learning scenario — while preserving differential privacy and avoiding catastrophic forgetting of previously learned tasks. This paper formulates the problem and proposes an elastic weight consolidation variant adapted for the federated-and-private setting, where Fisher information matrices are estimated locally and shared after per-round noise addition. Experiments use a sequential four-task retinal imaging protocol: diabetic retinopathy grading, glaucoma screening, macular degeneration classification, and optic disc segmentation, introduced one task per 50 communication rounds across 8 silos at ε = 2. The proposed method retained 94.1% of the performance on previous tasks when a new task was added, compared with 81.3% for naive continual FedAvg and 96.4% for an offline multi-task centrally trained upper bound. Forgetting metrics and round-by-round AUC trajectories are reported for all four tasks.

title: Auditing differential privacy guarantees in deployed federated learning systems: a protocol and toolchain
abstract: Formal differential privacy proofs do not guarantee that an implementation correctly realises those proofs; implementation bugs, floating-point rounding, and framework-level optimisations can all violate the intended guarantee. This paper proposes an empirical auditing protocol for deployed federated learning systems that estimates the empirical ε̂ achievable by a worst-case adversary using membership inference as a statistical test, following and extending the framework of Steinke et al. The toolchain, called FedAudit, instruments the aggregation server to log per-round gradient norms and noise samples, then applies a hypothesis test to lower-bound ε̂ with 95% confidence. Validation on five intentionally misconfigured deployments (wrong clipping norm, incorrect noise scale, disabled gradient accumulation guard) shows that FedAudit detected all misconfigurations with an average auditing overhead of 4.7% additional communication rounds. Applied to a correctly configured cross-silo chest X-ray training run at declared ε = 2, the tool returned ε̂ ≤ 2.08 with high confidence, confirming the implementation. The toolchain is released as open-source software.

title: Evaluating EvoSuite Effectiveness on Java EE Enterprise Beans: A Replication Study
abstract: A number of published EvoSuite evaluations focus on standalone Java classes, leaving enterprise components with container-managed transactions and dependency injection comparatively underexplored. This replication study reproduces the methodology of a 2011 benchmark evaluation and extends it to 30 stateless and stateful session beans extracted from four production-like Java EE applications. The study measures line coverage, branch coverage, and mutation score under EvoSuite's default whole-suite strategy and its DynaMOSA variant. On plain utility classes, results align closely with the original benchmark. For session beans, line coverage drops by an average of 18 percentage points, attributed primarily to unreachable paths behind container lifecycle callbacks. Mutation score degrades even more steeply, falling 23 points below plain-class baselines. The paper characterises the categories of mutations that escape detection and proposes a lightweight mock-injection wrapper that recovers approximately 9 coverage points with modest configuration effort.

title: A Taxonomy of Testability Impediments in Monolithic Web Applications Scheduled for Cloud Migration
abstract: Organisations migrating legacy monolithic web applications to cloud platforms routinely encounter testing challenges that are poorly documented in the literature. This paper presents a taxonomy derived from a mixed-methods study combining a survey of 47 software engineers from 12 Serbian and Croatian companies with a document analysis of 18 months of issue trackers from five open-source migration projects hosted on a public forge. Grounded coding of survey responses and issue descriptions yielded 34 distinct impediment types, grouped into five top-level categories: tight database coupling, absent seam points, implicit global state, hard-coded infrastructure assumptions, and missing observability hooks. The taxonomy is cross-referenced with testing technique applicability, showing that coverage-guided fuzzing is blocked by 19 of the 34 impediment types without preprocessing. The paper concludes with a prioritised refactoring roadmap linked to each impediment category.

title: Instrumentation Overhead of Coverage-Guided Fuzzing in Resource-Constrained Containerised Environments
abstract: Coverage-guided fuzzers such as AFL and libFuzzer insert compile-time or binary-level instrumentation to track edge coverage. When these fuzzers are deployed inside containers with restricted CPU and memory quotas—as is common in cloud continuous integration pipelines—instrumentation overhead becomes a practical concern. This paper characterises overhead across four instrumentation strategies: AFL's compile-time SHM bitmap, AFL++'s LTO instrumentation, a LLVM SanitizerCoverage-based approach, and a binary-only QEMU mode, applied to five network-parsing libraries. Experiments are run inside Docker containers with CPU quotas of 0.5, 1, and 2 virtual cores and memory limits of 256 MB, 512 MB, and 1 GB. Results show that LTO instrumentation degrades throughput by 8–14% at 0.5 vCPU compared to 3–6% at 2 vCPU, while QEMU mode suffers 40–65% degradation regardless of quota. Memory quota has negligible effect above 512 MB. Practical guidance for CI pipeline configuration is derived.

title: Search-Based Generation of REST API Test Suites During Microservice Decomposition
abstract: When a monolithic application is decomposed into microservices, REST interfaces emerge incrementally and are often underspecified early in the process. This paper describes a search-based approach that generates test suites targeting emerging OpenAPI specifications, using a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm that balances endpoint coverage, status-code diversity, and response schema validity. The approach was applied to three industrial decomposition projects carried out by a software house in Novi Sad over an 18-month period. Across 87 newly created endpoints, the generated suites achieved 91% endpoint coverage and detected 23 integration faults not found by developer-written unit tests. The evolutionary algorithm converged in under 4 minutes per service on a standard CI agent. The paper analyses false-positive rates in schema validation assertions and proposes a relaxed matching strategy that reduces them by 61% without sacrificing fault detection.

title: Regression Test Selection Under Continuous Deployment: An Empirical Comparison of Change-Impact and Coverage-Matrix Strategies
abstract: Continuous deployment pipelines require fast regression feedback, making full suite execution impractical for large codebases. This paper compares two families of regression test selection strategies—static change-impact analysis and dynamic coverage matrix matching—across four Java microservice repositories with commit histories spanning 24 months and totalling 3 400 commits. For each commit, both strategies select a test subset; the selected subsets are evaluated against the full suite's fault detection record to compute selection safety (fraction of fault-revealing commits where at least one fault is surfaced). Change-impact analysis achieves 94.1% safety at a mean suite reduction of 68%, while coverage-matrix matching achieves 97.3% safety at 54% reduction. A hybrid configuration that applies coverage matrices to modified modules and change-impact to dependencies reaches 96.8% safety at 63% reduction. Execution time comparisons on a 4-core CI agent are provided for all strategies.

title: Automated Test Generation for Cloud-Native Applications: State of Practice and Open Problems
abstract: Cloud-native applications differ from their predecessors in their reliance on orchestration platforms, ephemeral infrastructure, and distributed tracing. These characteristics create a set of test generation challenges that cut across existing categories in automated testing research. This book chapter surveys 62 peer-reviewed papers published between 2014 and 2022 addressing test generation for containerised, serverless, or service-mesh-based systems. The survey categorises papers along four axes: testing target granularity, oracle type, environment fidelity, and migration context. Key findings include that 71% of papers assume full control over the deployment environment—an assumption frequently violated during legacy migration—and that fault injection oracles are used in only 14% of cloud-native studies despite being common in distributed systems research. The chapter closes with a research agenda structured around seven open problems, each stated as a falsifiable hypothesis amenable to empirical investigation.

title: Differential Testing of Containerised Legacy Versus Cloud-Native Rewrites Using Automatically Generated Input Corpora
abstract: When a legacy service is rewritten as a cloud-native application, developers need assurance that the two versions behave equivalently on all inputs relevant to production traffic. This paper applies differential testing—running both versions on the same inputs and flagging behavioural divergences—to three pairs of legacy-and-rewrite services from an anonymised financial sector client. Input corpora are generated by combining coverage-guided fuzzing on the legacy binary with a search-based strategy seeded from sanitised production request logs. Over 72-hour fuzzing campaigns, the approach surfaces 41 divergences across the three service pairs; 29 are confirmed bugs in the rewrite, 8 are intentional behavioural changes, and 4 are flaky due to timestamp sensitivity. Precision of the divergence detector (after automated timestamp normalisation) is 87%. The paper discusses the practical workflow for integrating this approach into a migration acceptance gate within a CI/CD pipeline.

title: Seed Corpus Construction Strategies for Structure-Aware Fuzzing of Binary Serialisation Formats in Migrated Data Services
abstract: Data services migrated from on-premise deployments to cloud platforms often retain binary serialisation formats—such as custom TLV encodings or legacy ASN.1 schemas—that are poorly covered by mutation-based fuzzers operating on raw bytes. This preprint proposes and compares four seed corpus construction strategies for structure-aware fuzzers targeting such formats: (1) grammar extraction from decompiled code, (2) network capture replay with format inference, (3) generative model sampling trained on captured payloads, and (4) manual schema transcription. Each strategy is evaluated on three data services from an open benchmark of migrated applications, using edge coverage, unique crash count, and corpus construction time as metrics. Grammar extraction yields the highest edge coverage (mean 73.1%) but requires the most effort. The generative model strategy, trained on 10 000 captured payloads per service, reaches 68.4% coverage with substantially less manual work and scales better to format variants introduced during migration.
venue: arXiv preprint (submitted to Journal of Systems and Software)

title: Blockchain-Based Recordkeeping in Agricultural Commodity Chains: Legal Status of the Distributed Ledger as Evidence
abstract: This conference paper examines whether records stored on a permissioned distributed ledger qualify as documentary evidence under Serbian civil procedure law and the Law on Electronic Documents. The analysis is structured around a simulated grain-trading scenario involving a five-party supply chain: two producers, an aggregator, a commodity broker, and a bank providing trade finance. The paper maps each transaction event to the corresponding procedural category of evidence and concludes that ledger entries satisfy the conditions for electronic documents under Serbian law only if the ledger is operated by a qualified trust service provider as defined by the Electronic Document Act. Where this condition is absent, ledger records can at best serve as circumstantial evidence. The paper recommends harmonisation with the EU eIDAS framework as a precondition for broader adoption.

title: Smart Contracts as Contractual Terms: Classification Problems Under Serbian Contract Law
abstract: This article addresses the threshold question of how self-executing code embedded in a broader commercial agreement should be classified under the typology of contractual terms recognised by Serbian contract law. The study examines four published commercial agreements from Serbian commodity exchanges (anonymised with exchange consent) that incorporate conditional payment triggers implemented in code. Applying the standard civilian doctrinal categories—essential terms, incidental terms, collateral stipulations, and conditions—the article argues that smart-contract settlement triggers most closely resemble suspensive conditions under Article 74 of the Law on Obligations, but that their irrevocable and automated character disrupts the condition's traditional requirement of future uncertainty. The article draws on comparable analysis from French, Italian, and German literature and identifies three interpretive approaches courts might adopt, rating each for coherence with the existing statutory framework.

title: Code as Lex Contractus? Examining the Limits of Party Autonomy When Contract Terms Are Encoded
abstract: This conference paper interrogates the claim, common in practitioner literature, that smart contract code constitutes the exclusive and self-sufficient lex contractus of a transaction. The paper examines this claim against the doctrinal framework of party autonomy in three civil-law systems: Serbian, Slovenian, and German. Using a matrix of 18 scenarios drawn from commodity and trade-finance contract practice, the paper identifies categories of contractual provision—mandatory consumer protections, public policy limits, form requirements, and remedies for defective consent—that code cannot validly displace. The paper argues that the lex contractus claim is accurate only for the performance layer of a transaction; the validity and interpretation layers remain fully subject to the governing national law. Practical guidance is offered for legal counsel drafting hybrid text-and-code agreements.

title: Defective Consent and Automated Execution: Error, Fraud, and the Impossibility of Mid-Performance Rescission in Smart-Contract Settlements
abstract: This article examines what happens under Serbian and Croatian contract law when a party claims defective consent—error in the nature of the subject matter or fraud—after a smart contract has automatically executed a settlement payment. The core problem is temporal: the grounds for rescission arise after the automated performance has already transferred value, potentially in a blockchain transaction that is technically irreversible. The study maps the timeline of a standard grain-trade settlement cycle (typically T+2) against the procedural requirements for raising a voidability claim and seeks an injunction under the Law on Enforcement and Security. The article concludes that irreversibility of on-chain settlement creates a structural gap in civilian rescission doctrine and proposes a mandatory cooling-off window for smart-contract commodity settlements analogous to consumer withdrawal rights, implemented at contract drafting level rather than through ex post judicial relief.

title: Oracles in Commodity Smart Contracts: Data Feed Providers as Third Parties Under Civil-Law Contract Doctrine
abstract: This preprint analyses the legal status of oracle services—external data-feed providers whose price or event data trigger automated settlements in commodity smart contracts—within the framework of civil-law third-party doctrine. The study is based on a review of 11 publicly accessible oracle service agreements and 6 commodity smart contract templates published by European agricultural technology companies. It identifies three possible characterisations of the oracle relationship: a stipulation for a third party (stipulatio alteri), a mandate, and an expert determination clause under Article 270 of the Law on Obligations. Each characterisation yields different liability consequences when a faulty data feed causes a wrongful settlement. The preprint argues that expert determination is the most coherent characterisation and outlines the due diligence and liability language that commodity contracts should incorporate when relying on oracle services.

title: Regulatory Treatment of Tokenised Commodity Receipts Under Serbian Capital Markets Law
abstract: This article examines whether tokenised warehouse receipts for agricultural commodities—receipts whose ownership and transfer are recorded on a distributed ledger—qualify as securities, financial instruments, or sui generis documents of title under Serbian capital markets legislation and the Law on the Capital Market. The analysis draws on a comparative review of similar regulatory determinations made by the Austrian FMA, the French AMF, and the Swiss FINMA between 2019 and 2023. The article concludes that under current Serbian law, tokenised warehouse receipts do not meet the definition of transferable securities but may qualify as financial instruments if structured with yield or profit-sharing features. It further argues that the existing regime leaves a regulatory gap for purely title-transfer tokens and proposes targeted amendments to the Law on the Capital Market, drawing on the EU's DLT Pilot Regime as a reference.

title: Governing Law Clauses in Cross-Border Smart-Contract Commodity Transactions: Party Choice, Connecting Factors, and Judicial Jurisdiction
abstract: This article examines how governing law clauses function—and where they fail—when embedded in smart contracts used for cross-border commodity trades between Serbian entities and EU-based counterparties. The analysis is structured around Rome I Regulation conflicts-of-law rules and their applicability to Serbia as a non-Member State, using three case studies: a wheat forward with a Slovak buyer, a sunflower oil spot contract with a Hungarian processor, and a natural gas swap with an Austrian utility. For each case study, the article identifies the applicable connecting factor under Rome I, assesses the extent to which party choice expressed in code satisfies the requirement of a 'clearly demonstrated' choice, and analyses which court would have jurisdiction under Brussels I bis if the contract is treated as a commercial matter. The article argues that code-expressed choice of law is formally valid under Rome I but evidentially weak and proposes standard natural-language recitals to accompany code-based agreements.

title: Poređenje brzine propagacije kortikalne šireće depresije između frontalne i parijetalne regije kod miševa soja FVB/N
abstract: Analizirani su obrasci širenja KŠD duž fronto-parijetalnog korteksa kod 18 miševa soja FVB/N koji su genetski predisponirani ka nižem pragu indukcije KŠD. Elektrode su postavljane u tri tačke duž sagitalne ose, a KŠD je indukovana pinsimulacijom. Brzina propagacije bila je statistički značajno veća u frontalnom korteksu (3,8 ± 0,5 mm/min) u poređenju sa parijetalnim (3,1 ± 0,3 mm/min; p = 0,003). Učestalost spontanih rekurentnih talasa bila je viša u grupi sa 12-satnom deprivacijom sna (2,3 ± 0,7 talasa/h) nasuprot kontrolnoj grupi (0,8 ± 0,4 talasa/h; p < 0,001). Nalazi upućuju na regionalne razlike u kortikalnoj ekscitabilnosti relevantne za razumevanje heterogenosti aure kod migrene.

title: Intrinsic optical signal imaging of cortical spreading depression propagation: a comparison with DC-potential recordings in rat somatosensory cortex
abstract: Cortical spreading depression (CSD) was simultaneously monitored using intrinsic optical signal (IOS) imaging and direct-current (DC) electrophysiology in ten Sprague-Dawley rats under isoflurane anaesthesia. A 14 × 14 mm cranial window was prepared over the somatosensory cortex. CSD was initiated by a focal 0.5 µL injection of 3 M KCl. The IOS revealed a haemodynamic response preceding the DC negative shift by 1.8 ± 0.3 s, consistent with an initial vasodilatory phase. Spatial correspondence between the wavefront boundaries estimated by the two methods was high (Dice coefficient 0.84 ± 0.06), though IOS overestimated the lateral spread by approximately 0.4 mm at the margins. The propagation velocity measured by IOS (3.4 ± 0.5 mm/min) did not differ significantly from DC-potential estimates (3.2 ± 0.4 mm/min; paired t-test, p = 0.18). These findings support the use of IOS imaging as a complementary, less invasive tool for high-resolution mapping of CSD wavefronts.

title: Uticaj sumatriptana na prag indukcije i brzinu propagacije kortikalne šireće depresije kod pacova
abstract: Ispitivan je efekat intraperitonealne primene sumatriptana (0,3 mg/kg i 1,0 mg/kg) na prag indukcije KŠD i njenu brzinu propagacije u 30 odraslih Wistar pacova podeljenih u tri grupe (n = 10 po grupi). KŠD je indukovana kontinuiranom topikalnom aplikacijom kalijum hlorida, a number of elicited CSD episodes per 30-minutni interval korišćen je kao mera praga. Visoka doza sumatriptana smanjila je broj epizoda za 42% u poređenju sa kontrolnom grupom (p = 0,008), dok niska doza nije pokazala statistički značajan efekat (p = 0,21). Brzina propagacije nije se značajno promenila u nijednoj grupi. Histološka analiza kortikalnog tkiva nije pokazala znake strukturnog oštećenja. Rezultati su konzistentni sa hipotezom da triptani deluju prevashodno na prag, a ne na mehanizme horizontalnog širenja KŠD.

title: Electrocorticographic correlates of visual aura symptoms: mapping CSD propagation direction against reported phosphene location in migraine patients – a pilot observational study
abstract: Seven adult patients with a confirmed diagnosis of migraine with visual aura underwent prolonged EEG monitoring during spontaneously occurring aura episodes. High-density 256-channel EEG was recorded, and slow cortical potential shifts consistent with CSD-like activity were identified in five of the seven participants. In these five cases, the estimated propagation direction of the slow potential wave, derived from source localisation applied to the DC-coupled signal, correlated spatially with the hemifield in which patients reported the onset of phosphenes or scotoma (concordance in 4/5 cases). Mean estimated propagation velocity was 2.9 ± 0.7 mm/min, lower than values typically observed in rodent models. The small sample size precludes firm conclusions, but the findings provide preliminary support for a direct correspondence between electrophysiological wave direction and subjective aura topography, motivating larger prospective studies.
venue: European Journal of Headache Research

title: Sex differences in cortical spreading depression threshold and propagation velocity in a rat model of hormonal fluctuation
abstract: Female Wistar rats (n = 24) were divided into four groups according to oestrous cycle phase confirmed by vaginal cytology: proestrus, oestrus, metoestrus and dioestrus. CSD was induced by KCl microinjection and monitored by a six-electrode linear array spanning 6 mm of parietal cortex. A separate group of 12 male rats served as reference. The number of CSD episodes elicited over 60 minutes was highest during the proestrus phase (4.1 ± 0.9 episodes) compared with dioestrus (2.4 ± 0.7; p = 0.004) and male controls (2.6 ± 0.8; p = 0.009). Propagation velocity did not differ significantly across cycle phases (range 3.0–3.3 mm/min). These data are consistent with clinical observations linking increased migraine frequency to hormonal transitions and suggest that oestrogen levels may specifically modulate CSD threshold rather than propagation speed.

title: Multisite local field potential recording during cortical spreading depression in freely moving rats: methodological considerations
abstract: Cortical spreading depression research has relied heavily on anaesthetised preparations, which may alter baseline excitability and neuromodulatory tone. This methodological report describes an implantable 16-channel silicon probe preparation tested in eight Sprague-Dawley rats instrumented for chronic recording. Animals recovered for 10 days post-surgery before KCl was delivered via a chronically implanted guide cannula. CSD episodes were detected in all eight animals with a success rate of 91% across 44 attempted inductions. Propagation velocity in freely moving animals (3.9 ± 0.6 mm/min) was significantly higher than values obtained in the same animals under isoflurane anaesthesia in a separate session (3.1 ± 0.5 mm/min; p = 0.002). Signal quality was stable across a seven-day recording window. The protocol provides a foundation for investigating CSD under conditions that more closely approximate the awake, naturally cycling brain relevant to migraine.

title: Klinički fenotipovi vizuelne aure i njihova moguća elektrofiziološka osnova: pregled literature i implikacije za translaciona istraživanja
abstract: Vizuelna aura migrene manifestuje se raznovrsnim fenomenima – od pozitivnih (fosfeni, zigzag linije) do negativnih (skotomi) – koji se razvijaju u karakterističnom vremenskom toku od 20 do 60 minuta. Ovaj pregledni rad sistematizuje kliničke opise vizuelnih fenomena aure iz 14 prospektivnih studija objavljenih između 2000. i 2023. godine i razmatra u kojoj meri parametri kortikalne šireće depresije zabeleženi u životinjskim modelima – pre svega brzina propagacije, smer širenja i amplituda DC pomaka – odgovaraju opisanom kliničkom toku. Analizirana je i uloga individualne varijabilnosti u kortikalnoj topografiji vidnog polja (V1 površina, ekscentričnost reprezentacije) kao mogućeg činioca koji doprinosi razlikama u fenomenologiji aure između pacijenata. Zaključuje se da direktna kvantitativna translacija parametara iz modela na glodarima zahteva korekciju za razlike u veličini korteksa i proporcijama vizotopske mape, te da su potrebne humanizovane komputacione simulacije.

title: Theta-burst transcranial magnetic stimulation alters cortical spreading depression susceptibility in rat occipital cortex
abstract: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is used clinically in migraine prevention, but its effects on CSD susceptibility are poorly characterised. Fourteen Wistar rats received five consecutive daily sessions of either active continuous theta-burst stimulation (cTBS, n = 7) or sham stimulation (n = 7) delivered over the occipital scalp. Forty-eight hours after the final session, CSD was induced by KCl and monitored with a four-electrode parieto-occipital array. Animals in the cTBS group exhibited a 35% reduction in the number of KCl-elicited CSD episodes per 60 minutes (1.9 ± 0.5 vs. 2.9 ± 0.6 in sham; p = 0.006). Propagation velocity was not significantly different between groups (3.1 ± 0.4 vs. 3.3 ± 0.5 mm/min; p = 0.37). Cortical excitability assessed by single-pulse motor-evoked potentials was reduced in the cTBS group at 48 h. Results indicate that cTBS reduces CSD frequency, possibly through long-term depression of cortical excitability, supporting a mechanism relevant to its clinical use in migraine prophylaxis.

title: Between Two Flags: Commemorative Ambiguity in Hungarian–Serbian Border Villages of Vojvodina
abstract: This article examines how inhabitants of three predominantly bilingual villages in the Bačka region navigate the coexistence of Serbian state commemorations and Hungarian community memorial events. Drawing on 34 semi-structured interviews conducted in 2009–2010 and an analysis of municipal council minutes spanning 1990–2010, the study maps the informal negotiations between local government representatives and minority cultural associations over the scheduling, language, and symbolism of public ceremonies. The findings indicate that commemorative ambiguity—the deliberate avoidance of explicit symbolic confrontation—functions as a practical strategy of inter-ethnic cohabitation rather than as genuine civic consensus. Village mayors systematically adopted overlapping event calendars that allowed both communities to claim symbolic ownership of the same public spaces without formal acknowledgement of underlying historical disputes. The article contributes to debates on 'banal multiculturalism' in post-socialist European peripheries and questions assumptions about state-directed memory consolidation at the local level.

title: Who Owns the Partisan Monument? Reassembling War Memory in a Vojvodinian Market Town
abstract: Post-socialist memorial landscapes in Vojvodina are characterised by selective neglect, quiet removal, and occasional renaming of monuments associated with the Yugoslav People's Liberation War. This ethnographic case study focuses on a single WWII partisan monument in a small Vojvodinian market town that became the object of competing claims by a Serbian veterans' association, a local history society, and a Hungarian cultural club between 2005 and 2012. Through participant observation over eight months and 21 in-depth interviews, the study reconstructs the social life of the monument and the layered interpretations attached to it. Three analytically distinct memory registers are identified: official state memory, family-based private memory, and ethnic minority counter-memory. The article shows that the monument's physical deterioration was not incidental but functioned as a form of distributed agency, allowing all parties to defer direct confrontation while gradually reshaping the commemorative meaning of the site.

title: Oral History as Contested Archive: Methodological Reflections from Multi-Ethnic Fieldwork in Vojvodina
abstract: This book chapter reflects on the methodological and ethical challenges of conducting oral history research in communities where the same historical events are remembered through mutually incompatible ethnic narratives. Drawing on fieldwork in four Vojvodinian municipalities between 2010 and 2014, the author examines how the researcher's perceived ethnic and linguistic positioning shapes interview dynamics, the selection of informants, and the interpretation of silence and omission in testimonies. The chapter argues that oral history in contested multi-ethnic settings requires researchers to treat discrepancy between accounts not as a data problem to be resolved but as primary evidence of the social organisation of remembering. Practical protocols for archiving contradictory testimonies ethically are proposed, including consent procedures that allow informants to revisit and revise deposited recordings. The chapter is situated within broader debates on positionality and reflexivity in qualitative sociology.

title: The Trianon Centenary in Vojvodina: Local Commemorations and Their Reception Among Serbian Residents
abstract: The centenary of the Treaty of Trianon in 2020 generated extensive commemorative activity within Hungarian communities across the Carpathian Basin, including in the Vojvodina region of Serbia. This article examines how Hungarian cultural organisations in three Vojvodinian towns organised centenary events in 2020, and how these events were received—through local press discourse and 28 follow-up interviews—by Serbian residents who were not direct participants. Data collection was adapted for pandemic conditions, combining online ethnographic monitoring of event live-streams and social media commentary with telephone and video-call interviews. The study finds that Serbian non-participants largely interpreted the commemorations as expressions of cultural identity rather than territorial claims, a reading that contrasts with national media framings in both Serbia and Hungary. However, a subset of older male Serbian respondents expressed discomfort rooted in wartime family memories, indicating that generational memory mediates reception. The article contributes to research on minority commemoration and majority perception in shared public space.

title: Silence as Memory Practice: Non-Commemoration of the 1944 Killings in Mixed Communities of Southern Bačka
abstract: The mass killings of ethnic Germans and Hungarians by Partisan forces in Vojvodina in late 1944 remained largely absent from official public commemoration in Serbia until the 2000s and continue to be inconsistently acknowledged at the local level. This article focuses on three mixed Serbian–Hungarian communities in Southern Bačka where no formal local commemoration of these events has taken place despite documented losses among the local Hungarian population. Based on 41 oral history interviews, archival research in municipal and church records, and analysis of local newspapers from 1990 to 2022, the study explores the social mechanisms sustaining this non-commemoration. The author identifies three overlapping mechanisms: institutional inertia in majority-controlled municipal bodies, self-censorship among Hungarian community leaders anxious about Serbian nationalist reactions, and an intergenerational thinning of embodied family memory. The article engages with theoretical frameworks of 'chosen silence' and 'mnemonic security dilemmas' and questions their applicability outside Western European contexts.

title: Digital Memorial Platforms and Ethnic Boundary-Making: A Comparative Analysis of Online Remembrance Sites in Vojvodina
abstract: Since approximately 2015 a number of ethnically organised civil associations in Vojvodina have established digital memorial platforms archiving photographs, genealogical data, and testimonies related to WWII and post-war losses within specific ethnic communities. This paper presents a comparative analysis of five such platforms, three associated with Hungarian organisations and two with German-descendant diaspora groups, examining their design logic, curation practices, and the narratives of victimhood they construct. Content analysis of approximately 3,400 individual memorial entries was combined with interviews with platform administrators and a survey of 112 users. The study finds that digital platforms tend to sharpen ethnic boundary-making compared to physical memorial sites, partly because they are designed and used at a spatial remove from the inter-ethnic relationships that moderate public commemoration in shared local spaces. Platform administrators expressed reluctance to link or cross-reference with platforms of different ethnic orientation even when the documented events overlapped historically.
venue: New Media and Collective Memory

title: Teaching the Difficult Past: History Teachers' Negotiation of Multi-Ethnic Memory in Vojvodinian Secondary Schools
abstract: History education in ethnically mixed secondary schools in Vojvodina presents teachers with the practical challenge of addressing events that are commemorated differently, or not at all, by students from different ethnic backgrounds. This qualitative study draws on semi-structured interviews with 19 history and civics teachers in seven Vojvodinian towns conducted in 2022–2023, supplemented by classroom observation in four schools. The study examines how teachers describe their decisions about which events to include, how much class time to devote to minority perspectives, and how they manage the emotional dynamics when students' family memories contradict textbook accounts. Most teachers reported relying on personal judgement rather than institutional guidance, and several described deliberate avoidance of events such as the 1944 mass killings. The findings point to a significant gap between official curriculum frameworks emphasising multiperspectivity and classroom practice constrained by local social pressures and teachers' own memorial positioning.

title: Whose Centenary Is It? Local Government Commemoration of the 1918 Annexation of Vojvodina in Serbian and Hungarian Community Newspapers
abstract: The centenary of the 1918 incorporation of Vojvodina into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes was commemorated through a range of official municipal events in 2018. This article analyses how these events were reported and framed in six local newspapers: three Serbian-language and three Hungarian-language, published in the same municipalities. Using comparative framing analysis of 214 articles published between September and December 2018, the study identifies systematic divergence in the selection of quoted voices, the use of evaluative language, and the placement of photographs. Serbian-language papers consistently framed municipal commemorations as occasions for civic cohesion and regional identity, while Hungarian-language papers foregrounded exclusion from the official programme and employed a significantly higher frequency of conditional or distancing language when reporting Serbian officials' speeches. The analysis contributes to research on minority press as a site of memory contestation.

title: Hierarchical Dirichlet Process Models for Tracking Topic Drift in Serbian Online News (2006–2011)
abstract: This paper applies a hierarchical Dirichlet process (HDP) topic model to a longitudinal corpus of approximately 1.2 million Serbian-language news articles collected between 2006 and 2011. Standard LDA struggles with corpora in which the number of topics is unknown and evolves over time; the HDP formulation sidesteps this by treating the number of topics as a random variable inferred from data. Gibbs sampling with a Chinese restaurant franchise prior is used for inference. The resulting topic trajectories are evaluated both intrinsically via held-out perplexity and extrinsically by comparing discovered topic sequences with manually annotated event timelines provided by three domain experts. The HDP model recovers 38 coherent topics on average across yearly slices, outperforming a fixed-K LDA baseline (K = 40) by 12 % on coherence measured by normalised pointwise mutual information. The paper also reports on preprocessing challenges specific to Serbian morphology, including the use of a lemmatiser developed at the University of Novi Sad.

title: Discourse Coherence Metrics as Predictors of Topic Stability in Forum Threads
abstract: Online forum threads present a distinct challenge for topic models because successive posts may shift register, introduce sub-topics, or address multiple participants simultaneously. This work investigates whether discourse coherence metrics—specifically lexical chain density and entity grid transition probabilities—can predict the degree of topic drift estimated by an HDP model fitted to a Croatian-language technology forum containing 87,000 threads and 640,000 posts. Coherence features are extracted post by post; an HDP posterior is computed over the full thread collection. Spearman correlations between coherence scores and per-thread topic entropy range from 0.31 to 0.47 depending on the metric, suggesting a moderate but consistent relationship. A logistic regression trained on the coherence features alone achieves 0.68 AUC in classifying threads as topically stable versus drifting, against a majority-class baseline of 0.52. The findings motivate incorporating discourse structure as a prior constraint in future Bayesian topic models for threaded dialogue.

title: Comparative Evaluation of Inference Algorithms for Dynamic Topic Models on Short Microblog Texts
abstract: Dynamic topic models (DTMs) extend LDA by coupling consecutive time slices through a state-space model on topic distributions. Their inference is computationally expensive and their performance on very short texts—typical of microblogging platforms—is not well characterised. This study benchmarks four inference strategies (mean-field variational EM, stochastic variational inference, collapsed Gibbs sampling, and particle MCMC) applied to a two-year Twitter-like dataset of 4.3 million Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian posts collected in 2013–2014. Evaluation uses held-out likelihood, topic coherence (NPMI), and wall-clock time on a 32-core server. Stochastic variational inference achieves the best coherence-to-runtime ratio, but collapsed Gibbs sampling produces topics rated higher by human assessors in a pairwise preference study (n = 120 judgements). Short text length degrades all methods substantially; aggregation of posts by user into pseudo-documents recovers 8–14 % of the coherence loss. Guidelines for practitioners working with low-resource Slavic microblogs are discussed.

title: Discourse-Aware Topic Segmentation of Long Conversational Threads Using Rhetorical Structure Theory Features
abstract: Standard bag-of-words topic models discard sentence order and rhetorical organisation, making it difficult to detect sub-topic boundaries within long conversational threads. This paper integrates Rhetorical Structure Theory (RST) discourse features—specifically nucleus–satellite relations and discourse connective counts—into a segmented topic model (seg-LDA) adapted for Serbian. An RST parser trained on a 12,000-sentence treebank is applied to thread posts; resulting relation vectors augment the term-document matrix fed to the model. Experiments on 4,500 manually segmented forum threads (drawn from a Serbian automotive forum with 11 years of history) show that RST-augmented seg-LDA reduces the absolute WindowDiff error by 6.1 percentage points compared to a plain seg-LDA baseline and by 9.8 points compared to TextTiling with TF-IDF features. Ablation confirms that nucleus–satellite directionality contributes more than connective counts alone. Annotator agreement on the reference segmentation (Cohen κ = 0.71) is reported in detail.

title: Non-Parametric Bayesian Topic Modelling for Low-Resource Languages: Methods, Resources, and Open Problems
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic overview of HDP-based topic models as applied to languages with limited annotated resources, drawing primarily on the authors' experience with South Slavic languages. The chapter covers four core areas: (1) morphological preprocessing strategies and their measurable effect on topic coherence in morphologically rich languages; (2) scalable inference algorithms suited to medium-sized corpora (up to 10 million tokens) on standard academic hardware; (3) publicly available multilingual corpora and lexical resources relevant for the Balkans region; and (4) evaluation protocols and their limitations when gold-standard topic annotations are absent. Concrete numerical comparisons are drawn from previously published experiments on Serbian, Croatian, Bosnian, and Slovenian corpora. The chapter concludes with a discussion of remaining open problems, including better integration of syntactic structure and handling of code-switching common in regional social media.

title: Correlated Topic Models with Neural Document Embeddings for Tracking Political Polarisation on Twitter
abstract: Correlated topic models (CTMs) extend LDA by placing a logistic-normal prior over topic proportions, allowing topics to exhibit positive or negative correlations. This work replaces the bag-of-words document representation with sentence-level embeddings produced by a multilingual transformer fine-tuned on a Serbian political text collection (430,000 sentences). The hybrid model is fitted to 780,000 tweets posted by users in Serbia during three parliamentary election cycles (2016, 2020, 2022). Topic correlations are used to construct a topic co-occurrence network; community detection on this network reveals two stable topic clusters identifiable as pro-government and opposition frames. A polarisation index derived from the network's modularity increases monotonically across the three election cycles (Q = 0.31, 0.38, 0.44). Results are partially validated by correlating user-level topic exposure scores with self-reported party preference collected through an opt-in survey of 610 Twitter users.

title: Assessing Temporal Stability of Topic Models: A Framework Based on Bootstrap Resampling of Longitudinal Corpora
abstract: A persistent practical problem with topic model deployments in longitudinal studies is that fitted topics can vary substantially across different random seeds or data subsamples, making it difficult to determine whether observed topic trends reflect genuine corpus dynamics or inference artefacts. This paper proposes a bootstrap resampling framework in which yearly corpus slices are resampled with replacement 200 times, a topic model is fitted to each resample, and topic-level stability is measured using a Jaccard-based topic matching score averaged across all bootstrap pairs. The procedure is demonstrated on three datasets: Serbian political commentary (2015–2022, 5.3 million tokens), a Romanian health-discussion corpus (2018–2022, 1.9 million tokens), and a bilingual Hungarian–Serbian corpus from the Vojvodina region (2014–2022, 2.7 million tokens). Results show that HDP-fitted topics are more stable by the proposed metric than fixed-K LDA topics when K is chosen by grid search, though at higher computational cost. Practical recommendations for corpus size and number of bootstrap iterations are provided.

title: Comparison of REBA and OWAS scores for repetitive upper-limb tasks on a fish-filleting line
abstract: REBA and OWAS are both widely used for ergonomic screening but yield different levels of body-segment detail. This study applied both methods in parallel to the same set of workers on a fish-filleting conveyor line in order to examine agreement and divergence in risk classification. Thirty workers were each observed for 60 minutes using 30-second interval sampling, yielding 3,600 observation pairs. REBA scores ranged from 3 to 11 (mean 7.4, SD 1.8); OWAS action categories ranged from 1 to 3. Spearman correlation between the two instruments was 0.59, and agreement on classifying workers as high-risk versus low-risk was 73%. REBA identified a larger proportion of workers requiring immediate action (43% vs. 27% by OWAS), primarily because it captures wrist and forearm posture separately. The paper discusses practical implications for choosing between methods given different organisational contexts and available observer time.

title: Self-reported discomfort patterns among bakery workers: a cross-sectional survey in Serbia and Croatia
abstract: Manual tasks in industrial bakeries—dough handling, tray loading, and oven operation—are physically demanding but rarely studied using standardised instruments. This cross-sectional survey administered a translated and validated version of the Cornell Musculoskeletal Discomfort Questionnaire to 214 bakery workers across seven plants in Serbia (n = 129) and Croatia (n = 85). Discomfort prevalence in the past week was highest for the lower back (61%), neck (47%), and right shoulder (44%). Logistic regression showed that workers on night shifts (OR 2.1, 95% CI 1.4–3.2) and those with more than ten years of tenure (OR 1.8, 95% CI 1.1–2.9) reported significantly higher lower-back discomfort. No significant country-level differences were detected after controlling for plant size and task type. The survey instrument showed acceptable internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.78). Results suggest that shift scheduling and tenure-based job rotation merit attention in bakery ergonomics programmes.

title: Ergonomic risk stratification in food manufacturing: a scoring framework integrating REBA outcomes and worker-reported discomfort
abstract: This paper describes the development and pilot application of a composite risk stratification tool that combines postural scores obtained by REBA with discomfort scores from a structured body-map survey. The tool assigns workstations to four risk tiers (negligible, low, moderate, high) by weighting REBA summary scores (0.6) and mean discomfort scores (0.4), with tier thresholds derived from a reference dataset of 18 food-processing workstations observed in three plants. Thirty-two workstations in a vegetable-canning facility were evaluated using the framework, and results were compared with rankings produced by two occupational health practitioners who assessed the same workstations independently. Agreement between the framework and the practitioners' consensus ranking was 78% at the tier level. The paper also reports inter-rater reliability for the REBA component (kappa 0.76) and discusses sensitivity of the tier boundaries to weighting variations. The tool is intended as a practical screening aid rather than a substitute for full ergonomics assessments.

title: Work-related musculoskeletal disorders in the agri-food sector: a scoping review of observational assessment studies published 2005–2018
abstract: Observational postural assessment methods have been applied in a wide range of food and agricultural production contexts, but the evidence base is fragmented across languages and publication venues. This scoping review systematically searched five databases and identified 61 studies published between 2005 and 2018 that applied REBA, OWAS, RULA, or a combination thereof in agri-food manual work settings. Studies covered meat processing (n = 21), fruit and vegetable handling (n = 14), dairy (n = 8), bakery and confectionery (n = 7), and mixed or unspecified food manufacturing (n = 11). The lower back and shoulders were the most frequently assessed high-risk body regions. Only 18 studies (30%) combined observational scoring with a validated discomfort or symptom questionnaire; 12 studies (20%) reported any follow-up on intervention outcomes. Methodological heterogeneity in sampling strategy, observation duration, and coding protocols limited cross-study comparison. The review maps gaps and suggests minimum reporting standards for future studies.

title: Trunk flexion angles and lower-back discomfort in manual pallet stacking: measurement by video coding and inclinometry
abstract: This study compared trunk flexion estimates obtained by REBA-based video coding with direct inclinometer measurements during manual pallet stacking tasks in a frozen-food distribution centre. Seventeen male workers completed a standardised stacking sequence at three pallet heights (floor, knee, and waist level) under laboratory-like conditions in the plant's training area. Inclinometer data were sampled at 50 Hz; video was coded frame-by-frame by two independent observers. REBA coding underestimated mean trunk flexion compared with inclinometry at floor-level stacking (mean REBA estimated angle 47° vs. 58° inclinometer, p < 0.001) but showed reasonable agreement at waist-height stacking (mean difference 4°, p = 0.18). Workers reported significantly higher lower-back discomfort (VAS scale, 0–10) after floor-level stacking (mean 4.8) than after waist-height stacking (mean 2.1). The findings have practical implications for the accuracy of REBA-based intervention thresholds in logistics and warehousing tasks attached to food-processing operations.

title: Prioritising ergonomic interventions in a meat-processing plant using a multi-criteria decision matrix
abstract: When multiple workstations require ergonomic attention and resources are limited, a structured prioritisation approach helps allocate effort. This paper describes the application of a weighted multi-criteria matrix to 24 workstations in a pork processing plant in Novi Sad. Criteria included REBA action category, OWAS action category, Nordic Musculoskeletal Questionnaire 12-month prevalence rates, exposure duration, and number of workers exposed. Criteria weights were elicited from five plant managers and five occupational health specialists using pairwise comparisons following the analytic hierarchy process. The two stakeholder groups assigned notably different weights to discomfort prevalence (managers 0.11 vs. health specialists 0.28). Final priority rankings were generated under both weight sets and compared; 17 of 24 workstations retained the same tier under both sets. Deboning and liver-trimming stations consistently ranked highest. The paper discusses how transparent weighting can support negotiation between management and health staff about intervention sequencing.

title: Discomfort survey translation and adaptation for use in Serbian food-manufacturing populations: psychometric testing of two instruments
abstract: Standardised discomfort instruments developed in English or Dutch are widely used in ergonomics research but require formal adaptation before application in other language and cultural contexts. This paper reports the forward-backward translation, expert review, cognitive interviewing, and psychometric testing of Serbian-language adaptations of the Cornell Musculoskeletal Discomfort Questionnaire and the Standardised Nordic Questionnaire. A convenience sample of 188 food-manufacturing workers from five plants in Vojvodina participated in test-retest reliability assessment (two administrations, 14-day interval) and a concurrent validity check against REBA-based postural scores. Cronbach's α values were 0.79 (Cornell) and 0.73 (Nordic). Intraclass correlation coefficients for test-retest ranged from 0.71 to 0.88 across body regions. Concurrent validity correlations with workstation-level REBA scores were moderate (r = 0.48–0.62). The adapted instruments and administration guidelines have been made available for use by other researchers through the department's public repository.

title: Ergonomic risk profiles across workstation types in a dairy processing facility: an integrative REBA and body-map analysis
abstract: Dairy processing combines highly mechanised stages with manual tasks such as curd cutting, mould filling, and packaging. This study mapped ergonomic risk profiles across 19 distinct workstation types in a mid-size dairy plant in central Serbia, using REBA observations (total n = 2,940 scored postures across 47 workers) combined with a body-map discomfort survey administered at end of shift over five consecutive working days. Cluster analysis grouped workstations into three distinct risk profiles: a low-risk cluster (n = 6 workstations) characterised by standing with neutral posture and low discomfort ratings; a moderate-risk cluster (n = 9) with elevated wrist and shoulder REBA sub-scores; and a high-risk cluster (n = 4) dominated by sustained trunk flexion and high lower-back discomfort. Mould-filling and bulk-container handling stations appeared consistently in the high-risk cluster. The paper proposes a condensed eight-item body-map instrument derived from the data that may be sufficient for routine screening in similar dairy contexts.

title: Compressed Measurement Matrices for Wideband Vehicular Channel Sounding at 5.9 GHz
abstract: This paper addresses the design of compressed measurement matrices suitable for reduced-rate wideband channel sounding in the 5.9 GHz ITS band. A pseudo-random binary sequence sounder with a 200 MHz bandwidth was modified to implement sub-Nyquist sampling governed by a structured random matrix whose mutual coherence was minimised through an iterative gradient procedure. Reconstruction used a reweighted L1 solver with delay-domain sparsity as prior. Static and slow-mobility scenarios were recorded on a 1.4 km suburban test route in Novi Sad, yielding 4 800 channel snapshots. Using 40 % of the Nyquist samples, the reconstructed power delay profiles matched the fully sampled reference within 1.1 dB median error across paths with power above −20 dB relative to the strongest. The paper reports the mutual coherence values achieved, reconstruction runtime, and sensitivity to the sparsity order assumed. Results support the feasibility of hardware-efficient vehicular sounders based on this framework.

title: Sparsity of the Delay-Doppler Domain in Urban V2V Channels: An Empirical Study
abstract: The degree of sparsity of vehicular vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) channels in the joint delay-Doppler domain is evaluated using data collected during a measurement campaign conducted in central Novi Sad and on a four-lane arterial road during weekday peak hours. A calibrated channel sounder based on a 200 MHz bandwidth sliding correlator at 5.9 GHz was mounted on two passenger vehicles maintaining separations between 15 m and 250 m. A total of 38 km of dual-mobility runs were recorded, yielding approximately 190 000 consecutive channel transfer functions. After two-dimensional DFT-based delay-Doppler transformation, a thresholding analysis shows that fewer than 6 % of delay-Doppler bins carry more than 95 % of the total channel energy in 87 % of observation windows of 50 ms duration. Sparsity level is found to depend significantly on vehicle speed, inter-vehicle separation, and the presence of reflectors such as trams and lorries. These empirical statistics directly motivate compressive reconstruction strategies.

title: Atomic Norm Minimisation for Continuous Delay-Doppler Parameter Estimation in Vehicle-to-Infrastructure Links
abstract: Standard grid-based sparse recovery for channel parameter estimation suffers from basis mismatch when true delays and Doppler shifts do not align with a predefined dictionary. This work applies atomic norm minimisation (ANM) as a gridless alternative for estimating continuous-valued multipath delay-Doppler pairs in vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) links. A convex semidefinite program is derived and solved using the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) with warm-start initialisation. Synthetic data generated from a geometry-based stochastic channel model parameterised by measured Novi Sad roadside data were used for algorithm validation. In low-to-moderate SNR regimes (0–20 dB) and with 35 % compressive rate, ANM achieved a root-mean-square delay estimation error of 2.3 ns compared to 8.7 ns for OGSBI under matched conditions. Computational complexity scales cubically with the number of scatterers and is evaluated for real-time feasibility. The results indicate ANM is viable for post-processing channel sounding data but remains too slow for online estimation at current solver speeds.

title: Measurement-Based Path Loss and Shadow Fading Models for 5.9 GHz V2X Links on Serbian Motorways
abstract: Dedicated path loss and shadow fading models for the 5.9 GHz DSRC/ITS-G5 band are derived from a large-scale measurement campaign conducted on three motorway segments in Vojvodina, totalling 210 km of one-way driving. Omnidirectional roof-mounted antennas were used on both a transmit vehicle and a receive vehicle, with vehicle separation varied from 10 m to 900 m. Additionally, roadside unit positions at four locations were used for V2I measurements. Approximately 2.1 million path loss samples were collected. Two-slope log-distance models are fit separately for line-of-sight and obstructed line-of-sight conditions, yielding break points at 140–180 m in LOS and first-slope exponents of 1.78–2.03. Shadow fading standard deviation is 3.1–4.6 dB in LOS and 5.4–7.2 dB in OLOS. Comparison with ETSI TR 102 861 reference values reveals systematic differences attributable to flat terrain and low traffic density typical of Vojvodina highways. The dataset has been archived for community use.

title: Channel Sounding and Propagation Characterisation for Connected Vehicles
abstract: This book chapter provides a systematic treatment of wideband channel sounding methodology as applied to vehicular communication environments. It covers transmit waveform design, synchronisation challenges in dual-mobility scenarios, antenna calibration, and post-processing steps including excess-delay windowing and Doppler analysis. The chapter then surveys empirical propagation findings from campaigns in urban, suburban, highway, and tunnel environments across Europe, with particular attention to studies in South-East Europe where measurement data remain scarce. A separate section discusses compressed-sensing-based sounding as a route to hardware cost reduction. The chapter closes with an evaluation of standardised and de facto channel models—including ITU-R M.2135, WINNER II, and geometry-based stochastic models—against empirical data and identifies gaps relevant to 5G NR-V2X and future 6G vehicular use cases. Intended for graduate students and practitioners entering the field.

title: Effect of Vehicle Body Geometry on Antenna Radiation Pattern Distortion and V2V Link Budget at 5.9 GHz
abstract: Roof-mounted antennas used in V2V channel sounding are subject to pattern distortion caused by the vehicle body acting as a finite ground plane. This study quantifies the distortion for three common passenger vehicle profiles using full-wave electromagnetic simulation (CST Microwave Studio) and validates the results against anechoic chamber measurements for one vehicle. Simulated elevation patterns deviate from free-space omnidirectional behaviour by up to 8.4 dB at angles below 10° elevation, which corresponds to the dominant propagation paths in inter-vehicle links at separations above 50 m. Incorporating the distorted patterns into a ray-tracing propagation simulation for a straight motorway geometry shifts predicted median path loss by 2.1–3.6 dB relative to an ideal omnidirectional antenna model and increases shadow fading standard deviation by up to 1.2 dB. Correction factors per vehicle type are tabulated. The implications for calibration of existing V2V measurement datasets that assumed ideal antennas are discussed.

title: Sparse Bayesian Learning with Learned Dictionaries for Delay-Doppler Reconstruction in Non-Stationary V2X Channels
abstract: Conventional sparse recovery for vehicular channel estimation relies on fixed Fourier dictionaries, which are mismatched to the non-stationary multipath structure arising at intersections and in dense urban traffic. This work proposes training a data-driven overcomplete dictionary on a labelled dataset of 6 800 delay-Doppler channel snapshots collected in four propagation scenarios in Novi Sad. Dictionary learning uses the K-SVD algorithm with a sparsity constraint of eight atoms per snapshot. The learned dictionary is then embedded in a sparse Bayesian learning framework for online reconstruction from compressively sampled pilot observations. On held-out test data, the learned-dictionary approach reduces normalised mean-squared channel estimation error by 3.1 dB on average compared to the fixed DFT dictionary at 30 % compressive rate. Performance gains are largest in intersection scenarios (4.7 dB) where the Doppler structure is irregular. Training, validation, and test splits are described, and sensitivity to dataset size is reported from 500 to 6 800 snapshots.

title: Sub-6 GHz and mmWave Dual-Band Wideband Channel Measurements for Vehicular Scenarios in Novi Sad
abstract: Simultaneous dual-band wideband channel sounding at 5.9 GHz (200 MHz bandwidth) and 28 GHz (500 MHz bandwidth) was conducted in four representative vehicular environments in Novi Sad: a multi-lane boulevard, a dense residential grid, an urban arterial with tram lines, and a peripheral motorway access road. A single measurement vehicle hosted both band-specific sounders driven by a common 10 MHz GPS-disciplined reference. Over 5 400 dual-band snapshot pairs were recorded under comparable mobility conditions. Key findings include: median RMS delay spread at 28 GHz is 63 % lower than at 5.9 GHz in LOS conditions and 41 % lower in NLOS; the inter-band correlation of instantaneous received power varies from 0.61 in LOS to 0.33 in NLOS; and at 28 GHz, the number of resolvable multipath components drops from a median of 7 to 3 in the NLOS case. These results constrain the design of dual-band channel models needed for heterogeneous V2X deployments.

title: Reconfigurable SDR Platform for Simultaneous Compressed and Full-Rate Vehicular Channel Sounding
abstract: A reconfigurable software-defined radio channel sounding platform is described that can operate in full-rate mode and compressed-sensing mode simultaneously on two parallel receive chains sharing a common wideband antenna. The platform uses two synchronised USRP X410 units controlled by a real-time FPGA fabric implementing the sub-Nyquist sampling pattern described by a pre-loaded measurement matrix. A mutual coherence optimisation procedure for the matrix is implemented on an embedded ARM processor with a runtime of under 4 seconds for matrices up to 256×1024. The platform was validated over a 3.2 km drive route at 5.9 GHz with 200 MHz bandwidth. Power delay profiles from the compressed chain at 38 % rate matched the full-rate reference to within 1.4 dB median discrepancy across identified paths. Latency, synchronisation error characterisation, and antenna switch timing are reported. Hardware schematics and configuration files are made available under an open hardware licence.

title: Mapping Natural Language Aggregation Phrases to SQL GROUP BY Clauses: A Rule-Based Baseline
abstract: Early text-to-SQL systems struggled to reliably translate aggregation-heavy questions such as 'total revenue per region' into syntactically and semantically correct GROUP BY constructs. This paper presents a rule-based baseline system that identifies aggregation intent through a manually curated lexicon of 340 aggregation-triggering phrases extracted from 1,200 business-report sentences in English. The system parses dependency trees produced by a standard syntactic parser and maps head nouns and verbal predicates to candidate SQL aggregation operators (SUM, COUNT, AVG, MAX, MIN). Evaluation is performed on a domain-specific dataset of 780 question–query pairs drawn from retail and logistics schemas. The baseline achieves 61.4% exact-match accuracy overall and 54.2% on multi-aggregate questions, establishing a reproducible lower bound for subsequent learned approaches. Error analysis identifies four systematic failure modes: implicit grouping keys, comparative superlatives, nested aggregations, and schema-dependent unit ambiguity. These findings informed the annotation scheme used in later work.
