title: Sequence-to-Sequence Models for Text-to-SQL with Schema Linking: An Empirical Study
abstract: Sequence-to-sequence architectures had shown strong performance on machine translation and summarisation, but their behaviour on structured output generation for SQL was less systematically studied, particularly when the output must respect an unseen database schema at inference time. This paper presents a controlled empirical comparison of five seq2seq configurations—two LSTM-based and three Transformer-based—evaluated on the BINum-SR dataset and a general-domain benchmark. Schema linking is implemented via three strategies: concatenation of column names into the source sequence, cross-attention over schema embeddings, and a hybrid gating mechanism. Results show that the hybrid gating approach improves exact-match accuracy by 8.3 percentage points on BINum-SR over simple concatenation and by 5.1 points on the general-domain benchmark. Execution accuracy improvements are smaller (3.9 and 2.7 points respectively), indicating that syntactically correct but semantically wrong queries remain a persistent issue. Ablation experiments confirm that column-type information (numeric vs. categorical) contributes independently to aggregation correctness.

title: Aggregation Correctness in Fine-Tuned Large Language Models for SQL Generation
abstract: Fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) for text-to-SQL achieves high overall accuracy on benchmark datasets, yet systematic errors on aggregation-heavy queries persist and are often obscured by aggregate metrics. This paper provides a targeted analysis of aggregation correctness in three LLMs (parameter counts 1.3B, 6.7B, and 13B) fine-tuned on a combined corpus of 18,000 question–SQL pairs drawn from BINum-SR and two public benchmarks. Aggregation correctness is measured along four dimensions: operator selection, grouping key identification, HAVING clause generation, and numeric type consistency. The 13B model achieves the highest operator selection accuracy (88.3%) but shows only 61.7% accuracy on HAVING clause generation, comparable to the 6.7B model (60.2%). Increasing training data volume for HAVING-clause examples from 900 to 2,700 samples raises HAVING accuracy to 71.4% for the 13B model without degrading other dimensions. Qualitative error analysis identifies a recurrent pattern where the model generates syntactically valid but logically inverted conditions in HAVING clauses for comparative questions.

title: Constructing a Serbian-Language Text-to-SQL Corpus for Business-Intelligence Domains
abstract: Most text-to-SQL resources are English-language, leaving low-resource Slavic languages without evaluation infrastructure. This paper describes the construction of SrpBI-SQL, a corpus of 2,640 Serbian-language question–SQL pairs covering four business domains: retail, public administration, healthcare, and transportation. Questions were authored by 18 annotators with instructions to avoid literal translations from English templates and to reflect natural Serbian phrasing, including morphological variation and pro-drop phenomena. Each question is paired with a gold SQL query verified by executing it against a populated test database and manually checking result correctness. A cross-lingual transfer baseline using multilingual model fine-tuning achieves 49.3% execution accuracy, compared to 71.8% for the English-trained model on matched English questions, quantifying the transfer gap. Morphological analysis of question tokens reveals that case inflection of table-referencing noun phrases is the primary source of schema linking errors in the transfer setting. The corpus is available for research use.
venue: Proceedings of the Balkan Conference on Language Resources and Technologies (BalcLaRT)

title: Prompt Engineering vs. Fine-Tuning for Text-to-SQL: Trade-offs in Accuracy, Latency, and Schema Sensitivity
abstract: With the availability of large pretrained language models accessible via API, practitioners face a choice between prompt-engineering approaches and full or parameter-efficient fine-tuning for text-to-SQL deployment. This paper provides a systematic comparison across three evaluation axes—execution accuracy, query latency, and sensitivity to schema perturbations—using four model families at varying parameter scales. Prompt-engineering conditions include zero-shot, few-shot with randomly selected examples, and few-shot with BM25-retrieved examples. Fine-tuning conditions include full fine-tuning and LoRA adaptation with ranks 8 and 32. On a combined evaluation set of 3,200 questions from BINum-SR and SrpBI-SQL, LoRA rank-32 fine-tuning achieves the best execution accuracy (76.4% English, 58.1% Serbian) while adding median latency of 340 ms per query on the test hardware. BM25-retrieved few-shot prompting reaches 68.9% English accuracy with no fine-tuning cost but degrades to 41.3% when 20% of column names are replaced with synonyms, indicating higher schema sensitivity. Results suggest that fine-tuning is preferable when schema stability can be assumed and latency budgets allow re-training cycles.

title: Schema-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Text-to-SQL in Evolving Enterprise Databases
abstract: Enterprise databases undergo frequent schema changes—column additions, renames, and table merges—that invalidate fine-tuned text-to-SQL models without retraining. This paper explores a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) framework in which schema metadata and representative question–SQL exemplars are dynamically retrieved from a vector store and injected into the model context at inference time, reducing the dependency on static fine-tuning. The framework is evaluated on a controlled schema-evolution benchmark constructed by applying 12 categories of schema mutation to five base schemas from BINum-SR. Execution accuracy is measured before and after mutations for fine-tuned, prompt-only, and RAG-augmented configurations. The RAG-augmented model retains 89.4% of its pre-mutation execution accuracy after column renames, compared to 54.7% for the fine-tuned model, and 82.1% vs. 61.3% after table merges. Retrieval quality, measured by the proportion of relevant exemplars in the top-5 results, correlates strongly (r = 0.74) with execution accuracy across mutation types. Computational overhead of retrieval adds a median of 180 ms per query.

title: Positron lifetime components in unirradiated and neutron-irradiated Fe–Mn–Ni model alloys: separation of vacancy and solute contributions
abstract: Fe–Mn–Ni ternary alloys with Mn content between 0.5 and 1.8 wt% and Ni between 0.3 and 1.2 wt% were neutron-irradiated in the RA-6 research reactor in Vinca to fluences of 1×10^18 and 5×10^18 n/cm² (E>1 MeV) at 290 °C. Positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy was applied before and after irradiation using a fast–fast coincidence spectrometer with ^22Na source and time resolution of 240 ps FWHM. Decomposition of lifetime spectra into three components was performed with PATFIT-88. In unirradiated alloys, a single component near 110 ps consistent with free positron annihilation in the bcc matrix was observed. After irradiation at the higher fluence, a second component of 185–210 ps appeared, attributed to monovacancies and di-vacancies, and a third component near 430 ps indicated vacancy clusters of estimated size 4–7 vacancies. Increasing Mn concentration correlated with enhanced cluster formation, suggesting Mn assists vacancy trapping. The results are consistent with a solute-drag mechanism for vacancy cluster stabilisation rather than purely thermal effects.

title: Isochronal annealing study of radiation-induced vacancy defects in A508 reactor pressure vessel steel monitored by PALS
abstract: Samples of A508 Cl.3 low-alloy steel irradiated to a fluence of 2×10^19 n/cm² (E>1 MeV) in a pressurised water reactor simulator loop were subjected to isochronal annealing from 200 °C to 600 °C in steps of 25 °C, each for 30 minutes. Positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy was performed after every annealing step. The mean positron lifetime increased from 145 ps in the as-irradiated state to a peak of 175 ps at 375 °C before recovering toward the matrix value of 108 ps at 550 °C. Two vacancy-related lifetime components were resolved: a 165 ps component dominant below 350 °C, assigned to vacancy–solute complexes, and a 290 ps component that peaked at 350 °C and vanished by 475 °C, assigned to vacancy clusters containing approximately 10–15 vacancies. The annealing sequence suggests that solute–vacancy complexes dissolve before cluster shrinkage dominates. Activation energies derived from the annealing curves were 0.87 eV for the lower-temperature stage and 1.34 eV for the cluster dissolution stage.

title: Depth-resolved defect profiling in ion-irradiated ferritic steel using a slow-positron variable-energy beam
abstract: A variable-energy positron beam with implantation energies from 0.5 to 30 keV was used to profile defect distributions in Fe–0.3Cu–1.5Mn–0.7Ni model steel specimens irradiated with 2 MeV Fe²⁺ ions to displacement damage levels of 0.01, 0.1, and 1 dpa at room temperature. Doppler broadening S and W parameters were recorded as a function of mean positron implantation depth (0–700 nm). VEPFIT analysis was applied to extract defect layer profiles. At 0.1 dpa, the S parameter peaked 0.015 above the unirradiated baseline in a layer centred near 400 nm, coinciding with the predicted damage peak from SRIM calculations. At 1 dpa, S parameter saturation was observed across 200–600 nm, consistent with vacancy cluster coalescence. A thin surface oxide layer (S parameter dip, first 20 nm) was identified in all samples, and its influence was deconvolved from bulk signals. Results demonstrate good correlation between ion-beam and reactor neutron irradiation at equivalent dpa levels below 0.1 dpa.

title: Comparison of positron annihilation and small-angle neutron scattering data for vacancy-cluster size estimation in irradiated RPV steels
abstract: Positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy and small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) were applied in parallel to a set of eight ferritic–bainitic reactor pressure vessel steel specimens spanning fluences from 5×10^17 to 8×10^19 n/cm². PALS measurements were performed on a locally built fast–fast system, while SANS experiments were conducted at the D11 instrument at the Institut Laue–Langevin, Grenoble. Vacancy cluster radii estimated from PALS via the Dryzek model ranged from 0.28 to 0.61 nm, covering 2 to approximately 20 vacancies. SANS number densities for features in the 1–3 nm range were 1.2–4.8×10^23 m^-3. Quantitative cross-comparison showed agreement within 20% for specimens irradiated below 3×10^19 n/cm², but divergence at higher fluences, where SANS resolves larger solute-rich clusters not resolved by PALS. The complementary sensitivity ranges of the two techniques are discussed in terms of positron trapping cross-sections and cluster compositions.

title: Effect of copper content on vacancy cluster evolution in neutron-irradiated Fe–Cu–Mn model alloys
abstract: Three Fe–Cu–Mn model alloys with Cu concentrations of 0.05, 0.15, and 0.40 wt% (fixed Mn at 1.2 wt%) were irradiated at 288 °C to a common fluence of 1×10^19 n/cm² (E>1 MeV). PALS spectra were decomposed using a maximum likelihood approach implemented in LT9.0 software. The dominant irradiation-induced lifetime component shifted from 168 ps in the low-Cu alloy to 215 ps in the high-Cu alloy, indicating that copper promotes the formation of larger vacancy clusters. Concurrent Coincidence Doppler broadening measurements confirmed increased high-momentum electron annihilation in the high-Cu alloy, consistent with Cu decorating vacancy clusters. Vickers hardness measurements showed increments of 28, 55, and 98 HV for the three alloys respectively, demonstrating a direct relationship between PALS-derived cluster size and mechanical hardening. These results support a cluster-obstacle hardening model and suggest that vacancy-Cu co-clustering rather than pure Cu precipitation controls early-stage hardening at this fluence.

title: Positron trapping at dislocation loops in ferritic steel: distinguishing loop-type contributions in lifetime spectra
abstract: A series of Fe–1.0Mn–0.5Ni model alloy specimens irradiated to fluences between 10^17 and 10^19 n/cm² were studied by PALS and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to examine the interplay between dislocation loop and vacancy cluster positron trapping. TEM identified 1/2⟨111⟩ and ⟨100⟩ type dislocation loops with mean diameters ranging from 2 to 22 nm. At low fluence (10^17 n/cm²), TEM revealed predominantly small ⟨100⟩ loops, and PALS showed a lifetime component near 130–135 ps consistent with loop-associated positron trapping at jogs and kinks rather than open-volume defects. At higher fluences, vacancy cluster lifetime components at 190–240 ps dominated. A two-trap rate equation model was fitted to separate dislocation and vacancy contributions, yielding a positron trapping coefficient for dislocations of μ_d = (1.1 ± 0.2)×10^-4 m²/s per unit dislocation density. These values agree within 15% with theoretical estimates from Brandt's model adapted for bcc iron.

title: Benchmark inter-laboratory comparison of PALS measurements on neutron-irradiated Fe–Cu model alloy specimens
abstract: An inter-laboratory exercise was organised among six European groups to assess reproducibility of positron annihilation lifetime spectroscopy measurements on a common set of neutron-irradiated Fe–0.15Cu model alloy specimens. Each laboratory used its own ^22Na-based fast–fast PALS system with time resolutions between 210 and 265 ps FWHM. Specimens at four irradiation fluences (10^17 to 5×10^18 n/cm²) were circulated. Mean positron lifetime values obtained by different laboratories agreed within ±3.5 ps at 1σ for unirradiated material and within ±6 ps for the most heavily irradiated specimens. Systematic differences in the fitted intensity of the long lifetime component (>300 ps) reached 8 percentage points between the best- and worst-resolved spectrometers, highlighting the importance of time resolution and source correction procedures. Recommended minimum spectrometer and analysis standards for RPV steel characterisation are proposed.

title: Thermal decomposition kinetics of sunflower husk under nitrogen atmosphere: a non-isothermal TGA study
abstract: Sunflower husks sampled from three processing sites in Vojvodina were subjected to non-isothermal thermogravimetric analysis at heating rates of 5, 10, 20, and 40 K min⁻¹ under nitrogen flow (50 mL min⁻¹). Three isoconversional methods—Ozawa–Flynn–Wall, Kissinger–Akahira–Sunose, and Friedman—were applied to conversion degrees from 0.1 to 0.9. Apparent activation energies ranged from 148 to 213 kJ mol⁻¹ across the conversion range, with a pronounced compensation effect observed between 0.4 and 0.6. The three-stage decomposition profile (hemicellulose, cellulose, lignin) was deconvoluted using Fraser–Suzuki peak fitting, yielding individual component contributions consistent with proximate analysis data. Kinetic triplets were determined and compared across sites; moisture and ash content influenced the pre-exponential factor but not activation energy substantially. The results provide a baseline kinetic dataset for process modelling of sunflower residue pyrolysis reactors in the region.

title: Effect of slow pyrolysis temperature on biochar yield and proximate composition from wheat straw
abstract: Wheat straw biochar was produced in a laboratory fixed-bed tube furnace at final temperatures of 300, 400, 500, 600, and 700 °C under nitrogen (100 mL min⁻¹) with a residence time of 60 minutes and a heating rate of 10 K min⁻¹. Biochar yield decreased from 39.2% at 300 °C to 24.7% at 700 °C on a dry-ash-free basis. Fixed carbon content increased from 38 to 72 wt%, while volatile matter fell from 46 to 11 wt%. Ultimate analysis showed H/C and O/C molar ratios declining sharply above 500 °C, indicating progressive aromatisation. BET surface area peaked at 600 °C (187 m² g⁻¹) before declining slightly at 700 °C, attributed to pore coalescence. pH increased monotonically from 6.8 to 9.4. Results are discussed in the context of European Biochar Certificate threshold values for stable carbon content and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon limits, measured by GC-MS for the 500 °C and 600 °C samples.

title: Distributed activation energy model applied to co-pyrolysis of wheat straw and lignite from the Kovin deposit
abstract: The distributed activation energy model (DAEM) was fitted to TGA data for wheat straw, Kovin lignite, and three blending ratios (25:75, 50:50, 75:25 straw:lignite by mass) at heating rates of 10 and 20 K min⁻¹. For pure wheat straw, the Gaussian activation energy distribution yielded a mean of 204 kJ mol⁻¹ with a standard deviation of 21 kJ mol⁻¹. Lignite exhibited a broader distribution (mean 231 kJ mol⁻¹, σ = 34 kJ mol⁻¹). Blending produced negative synergistic deviations from linearly interpolated values in the 350–450 °C range, interpreted as catalytic effects of inorganic matter in the lignite ash on cellulose decomposition. The model reproduced experimental mass loss curves with root-mean-square errors below 0.8% for all cases. Interactions between alkali metals in biomass ash and the organic matrix of lignite are proposed as the primary interaction mechanism.

title: Characterisation of biochars from Vojvodina agricultural residues against European Biochar Certificate criteria
abstract: Six biochar samples were produced from sunflower husks, wheat straw, and corn stover at 500 and 650 °C using identical slow pyrolysis conditions and subjected to full physicochemical characterisation aligned with European Biochar Certificate (EBC) version 9 criteria. Analyses included elemental composition (C, H, N, S, O), BET surface area, pore size distribution (Barrett–Joyner–Halenda method), pH and electrical conductivity in water extract, plant-available phosphorus, cation exchange capacity, and 16 EPA priority PAH congeners by GC-MS. All samples produced at 650 °C met EBC Basic grade for stable carbon (minimum 50% Corg). PAH totals ranged from 1.2 to 4.7 mg kg⁻¹ dry matter, below the EBC premium threshold of 6 mg kg⁻¹ for all samples. Heavy metal concentrations (Cd, Cr, Cu, Ni, Pb, Zn) remained well within limits. A scoring matrix comparing regional feedstocks is presented to guide commercial producers in Vojvodina.

title: Influence of feedstock particle size on pyrolysis kinetics and biochar surface area: a systematic TGA and reactor study
abstract: Wheat straw was milled and sieved to four particle size fractions: <0.25, 0.25–0.5, 0.5–1.0, and 1.0–2.0 mm. Non-isothermal TGA at 10 K min⁻¹ revealed that apparent activation energy (KAS method) varied from 192 to 218 kJ mol⁻¹ across size fractions, with the finest fraction exhibiting the highest values, attributed to reduced heat and mass transfer limitations revealing true chemical kinetics. Reactor experiments at 550 °C and 60 min residence time showed biochar yield differences of 2.1 percentage points between the smallest and largest fractions. BET surface area decreased from 210 to 143 m² g⁻¹ as particle size increased, linked to restricted volatile escape and re-condensation in larger particles blocking pores. A simple effectiveness factor model, adapted from heterogeneous catalysis, described the particle size–surface area relationship with R² = 0.94. Practical implications for biochar quality control in hammer-mill pre-processing are discussed.

title: Biochar amendment effects on sandy loam soils of Vojvodina: a two-season pot experiment with maize
abstract: This study bridges thermochemical production of biochar with its agronomic performance. Wheat straw biochars produced at 450 and 600 °C (characterised in prior work by the same group) were applied to sandy loam soil collected from the Bačka region at rates of 0, 10, 20, and 40 t ha⁻¹ equivalent. A pot experiment over two growing seasons (2018 and 2019) used maize (cv. Zlatni Jubilar) as the test crop. Plant dry biomass increased by 12–18% at 20 t ha⁻¹ for the 600 °C char in the first season, but differences were not statistically significant (p > 0.05, Tukey HSD) by the second season. Soil water retention improved significantly (p < 0.01) for all amended treatments. Soil pH rose by 0.3–0.8 units. Available phosphorus and potassium showed modest but consistent increases at higher application rates. The experiment underlines that production temperature affects agronomic response as strongly as application rate.

title: Py-GC/MS fingerprinting of biochars from three Vojvodina lignocellulosic feedstocks at two carbonisation temperatures
abstract: Analytical pyrolysis coupled with gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (Py-GC/MS) at 500 °C was applied to biochars previously produced from sunflower husks, wheat straw, and corn stover at 450 and 650 °C in a fixed-bed reactor. The objective was to identify residual volatile organic compounds indicative of incomplete carbonisation and to compare aromatic cluster formation as a function of feedstock and production temperature. Levoglucosan, furfural, and guaiacol derivatives were prominent in 450 °C chars and nearly absent in 650 °C samples, confirming greater thermal recalcitrance of the latter. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (fluorene, phenanthrene, pyrene) were detected in all 650 °C chars at concentrations consistent with EBC limits. A principal component analysis of 47 identified compounds separated samples primarily by production temperature (PC1, 61% variance) and secondarily by feedstock lignin/cellulose ratio (PC2, 19% variance). The dataset supports using Py-GC/MS as a rapid screening tool in biochar quality workflows.

title: Torrefaction pre-treatment of sunflower husks: mass and energy yields, grindability and subsequent pyrolysis kinetics
abstract: Sunflower husks were torrefied at 230, 260, and 290 °C for 30 minutes in a rotary tube furnace under nitrogen. Solid mass yields were 91.4, 82.7, and 71.3 wt% respectively. Energy densification ratios reached 1.08, 1.15, and 1.24. Grindability was assessed by measuring particle size distribution after standardised hammer milling; the Hardgrove Grindability Index analogue improved by 38% at 290 °C relative to raw husks. Non-isothermal TGA of torrefied samples at 10 K min⁻¹ showed that the hemicellulose decomposition shoulder (typically 250–320 °C) was suppressed proportionally to torrefaction severity. Apparent activation energy of the cellulose decomposition step increased from 198 kJ mol⁻¹ (raw) to 217 kJ mol⁻¹ (290 °C torrefied), attributed to reduced structural disorder and removal of easily decomposable fractions. A two-step torrefaction–pyrolysis process simulation using collected data predicted a 9% gain in biochar fixed-carbon content relative to single-step pyrolysis of raw husks.

title: Raman spectroscopic assessment of structural order in biochars: correlation with BET surface area and agronomic stability index
abstract: Fifteen biochar samples spanning four feedstocks and production temperatures from 350 to 750 °C were characterised by Raman spectroscopy (532 nm excitation). The D and G band parameters (position, full width at half maximum, and integrated intensity ratio ID/IG) were extracted from curve-fitted spectra. ID/IG decreased from 1.41 ± 0.08 at 350 °C to 0.87 ± 0.06 at 750 °C, reflecting increasing graphitic ordering. A linear correlation (R² = 0.86) was found between ID/IG and the H/C molar ratio from ultimate analysis, supporting Raman spectroscopy as a rapid structural proxy. BET surface area showed a non-monotonic relationship with ID/IG, peaking at intermediate disorder corresponding to 550–600 °C chars. An agronomic stability index, defined as the ratio of recalcitrant carbon (R50 method) to total organic carbon, correlated moderately with Raman D-band FWHM (R² = 0.74). The dataset supports integration of Raman spectroscopy into biochar certification screening workflows to reduce reliance on lengthy carbon stability incubation tests.

title: Temperature–residence-time response surface for biochar yield, fixed carbon and BET surface area: a central composite design study with corn stover
abstract: A central composite design with two factors—pyrolysis temperature (450–700 °C) and residence time (20–120 min)—was applied to fixed-bed slow pyrolysis of corn stover in a nitrogen atmosphere to map responses including biochar yield, fixed carbon content, volatile matter, BET surface area, and pH. Thirteen experimental runs (including five centre points) were executed. Response surface models were fitted using least-squares regression; lack-of-fit tests confirmed adequacy for all five responses (p > 0.1). Temperature was the dominant factor for all responses; residence time showed significant interaction with temperature for BET surface area (p = 0.023) and volatile matter (p = 0.041). Optimal conditions maximising a composite desirability function combining high fixed carbon (≥60 wt%) and high BET surface area (≥180 m² g⁻¹) while maintaining biochar yield above 28% were identified at 615 °C and 75 min. The validated optimum was confirmed experimentally with deviations below 4% for all predicted values. Design-of-experiment data are provided as supplementary material.

title: Effect of coplanar electrode gap width on sensitivity in microfluidic impedance cytometry: a simulation and experimental study
abstract: Coplanar electrode pairs fabricated on the floor of polydimethylsiloxane microchannels are widely used in impedance flow cytometry, yet the relationship between inter-electrode gap and measurement sensitivity for cells of different diameters remains poorly quantified. This study used COMSOL Multiphysics finite-element simulations to sweep gap widths from 10 µm to 60 µm in 5 µm steps for a 40 µm-wide channel, computing the electric field non-uniformity index and the simulated impedance contrast for spheres of 10, 15, and 20 µm diameter. Devices with three gap widths (15 µm, 30 µm, and 50 µm) were then fabricated by standard SU-8 photolithography and PDMS casting, with gold electrodes deposited by thermal evaporation. Impedance spectra were recorded using a lock-in amplifier at 11 logarithmically spaced frequencies between 100 kHz and 20 MHz for polystyrene bead suspensions. The 15 µm gap device yielded the highest impedance contrast for 10 µm beads (mean signal-to-baseline ratio 4.7 ± 0.4) but showed increased positional sensitivity, producing a coefficient of variation in peak magnitude of 18% compared with 9% for the 30 µm gap. Results are discussed in terms of a simple resistor–capacitor equivalent circuit whose parameters were extracted by nonlinear least-squares fitting.

title: Equivalent-circuit parameter extraction for MCF-7 and MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells measured by multi-frequency impedance cytometry
abstract: Distinguishing metastatic from non-metastatic breast cancer cells in a label-free manner is relevant to liquid biopsy applications. This work presents multi-frequency impedance measurements of two human breast cancer cell lines, MCF-7 (epithelial-like) and MDA-MB-231 (mesenchymal-like), in a polydimethylsiloxane microchannel with facing 30 µm-gap coplanar gold electrodes. Cells suspended in phosphate-buffered saline at a concentration of approximately 5 × 10⁵ cells/mL were driven through the channel at 50 µL/h. Impedance was sampled simultaneously at 500 kHz, 2 MHz, and 10 MHz using dual lock-in amplifiers. For each transit event, an equivalent circuit consisting of a cell membrane capacitance, cytoplasm conductance, and double-layer capacitance was fitted using a Levenberg–Marquardt algorithm. MCF-7 cells (mean diameter 18.3 ± 1.9 µm) showed membrane capacitance of 9.2 ± 1.4 pF, whereas MDA-MB-231 cells (mean diameter 15.1 ± 1.6 µm) showed 6.8 ± 1.1 pF after diameter normalisation. Classification by linear discriminant analysis on two extracted parameters achieved 79% accuracy on a test set of 312 events, indicating that equivalent-circuit parameters carry cell-type information beyond size alone.

title: Leukocyte interference in impedance-based circulating tumour cell detection: characterisation and a gating strategy
abstract: Circulating tumour cells are present at concentrations of roughly 1–10 per millilitre of blood against a background of several million leukocytes, making leukocyte impedance signatures the principal confound in label-free detection. This conference paper reports an experimental characterisation of impedance transit signals from peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) and granulocytes isolated from healthy donor blood using density-gradient centrifugation, measured in a 40 µm × 40 µm cross-section PDMS channel at five frequencies from 200 kHz to 15 MHz. Size-normalised opacity (ratio of impedance magnitude at 5 MHz to that at 500 kHz) was 1.31 ± 0.08 for PBMCs and 1.19 ± 0.06 for granulocytes across 1,840 measured events from five donors. Spiked MCF-7 cells at 1:1,000 dilution in PBMC suspension were recovered with 71% efficiency at a false positive rate of 4.2% using a two-dimensional gate on opacity and transit time. These results quantify the overlap between leukocyte subpopulations and tumour cells and suggest that a third frequency dimension may reduce false positives further.

title: Effect of electrode placement on skin conductance amplitude and latency in wearable EDA wristbands
abstract: Wearable EDA sensors are typically placed on the inner wrist, a site with lower sweat gland density than the fingers. This study quantified differences in phasic response amplitude, onset latency, and recovery time between inner wrist, outer wrist, and standard palmar (index and middle finger) placements across 28 participants exposed to 20 standardised auditory startle stimuli. All three placements used identical Ag/AgCl dry electrodes and the same acquisition circuit. Inner-wrist amplitude was on average 61% lower than palmar, outer-wrist amplitude was 73% lower, and latency was 0.6 s longer at the wrist placements. A linear calibration model relating wrist to palmar amplitude reduced normalised RMSE from 0.41 to 0.17. The results inform the design of normalisation procedures when comparing data collected with different wearable form factors.

title: Transient temperature field prediction in a batch meat-drying chamber using a lumped-capacitance model
abstract: A lumped-capacitance thermal model was developed for a pilot-scale batch chamber used in the fermented-sausage drying process. The chamber had a usable volume of 1.2 m³ and was loaded with 48 kg of product arranged on four trolley racks. Governing equations for air-side convection, product moisture evaporation, and wall thermal mass were coupled and solved with a fourth-order Runge–Kutta scheme in MATLAB. Sixteen type-K thermocouples distributed across three horizontal planes provided validation data over 72-hour drying cycles at set-point dry-bulb temperatures of 14–22 °C. The model reproduced measured air temperatures within ±0.6 °C RMS and surface product temperatures within ±1.1 °C RMS during steady-state phases. Discrepancies were larger during the first 90 minutes after loading, attributed to door-opening infiltration events not included in the model. Sensitivity analysis showed that the effective convective heat-transfer coefficient at the product surface was the dominant parameter, accounting for 61 % of output variance under Sobol decomposition. The model is suitable as a base for real-time control optimisation in small-scale meat-processing facilities.

title: Experimental mapping of velocity and temperature non-uniformity in a commercial batch drying cabinet
abstract: Airflow and temperature distributions inside a 3.6 m³ commercial batch drying cabinet for cured meat products were characterised using a 64-point hot-wire anemometry survey and a 32-point thermocouple grid. Measurements were taken at three fan-speed settings (low, medium, full: 380, 590, and 780 rpm) under empty-chamber and fully-loaded conditions. Velocity magnitudes ranged from 0.05 m/s in corner dead zones to 1.8 m/s near fan outlets. A uniformity index calculated over the product-zone cross-section deteriorated from 0.82 under empty conditions to 0.61 at full load at medium fan speed, indicating that standard empty-chamber commissioning tests overestimate uniformity by approximately 25 %. Temperature differences across the product zone reached 4.3 °C at the lowest fan speed. The data set was subsequently used to calibrate a RANS CFD model. Findings suggest that redistributing the inlet plenum geometry could increase the uniformity index to above 0.78 at full load without increasing fan energy consumption.

title: RANS-based CFD simulation of airflow patterns in a loaded batch drying chamber: turbulence model selection and mesh sensitivity
abstract: Three RANS turbulence closures—standard k–ε, realisable k–ε, and k–ω SST—were evaluated for their ability to reproduce measured airflow in a 3.6 m³ commercial batch drying cabinet loaded with 120 sausage sticks arranged on four trolleys. Geometry and boundary conditions were derived from the experimental survey reported in an earlier study. Meshes of 1.4, 3.1, and 6.7 million hexahedral cells were tested for grid independence; the medium mesh showed velocity predictions within 8 % of measurements at 91 % of probe locations. The k–ω SST model gave the best overall agreement with measured velocities (mean absolute error 0.09 m/s) and temperature field (mean absolute error 0.8 °C). Standard k–ε over-predicted recirculation zone extent by 34 %. Simulation run times on an eight-core workstation were 4.2 hours for the medium mesh with k–ω SST. The validated model was used to evaluate three plenum geometry modifications and identified a baffle arrangement that improved the uniformity index from 0.61 to 0.76.

title: Energy audit procedure for small-batch fermented-sausage drying facilities: methodology and case study
abstract: An energy audit methodology adapted to small-scale batch drying facilities producing fermented sausages was developed and tested in three meat-processing plants in Vojvodina with annual throughputs of 80–250 tonnes. The procedure comprised meter-based energy disaggregation, thermographic inspection of chamber envelopes, fan motor efficiency assessment, and latent-heat loss estimation from exhaust air psychrometric measurements. Specific energy consumption per kilogram of water removed ranged from 3.8 to 6.7 MJ/kg across the three sites, compared with a theoretical minimum of approximately 2.7 MJ/kg. The dominant loss mechanism at all sites was uncontrolled exhaust ventilation, accounting for 28–41 % of total heat input. Thermographic surveys revealed envelope thermal bridges contributing 9–14 % of losses. A simplified audit template was derived that can be executed with portable instruments in one working day. Estimated payback periods for the recommended measures ranged from 14 to 31 months at prevailing energy prices. The methodology is intended for adoption by regional meat-processing associations.

title: Integration of a plate heat exchanger for exhaust-air heat recovery in batch meat-drying chambers: thermal performance and payback analysis
abstract: A counter-flow plate heat exchanger was retrofitted to the exhaust ventilation duct of a 7.2 m³ batch drying chamber at a medium-sized salami producer in Novi Sad. The heat exchanger recovered heat from exhaust air (typically 16–19 °C, 85–92 % RH) and preheated incoming fresh air, reducing the thermal load on the refrigeration-based conditioning system. Continuous logging over 90 operating days captured 310 complete drying cycles. Average heat recovery effectiveness was 0.64, corresponding to a reduction in refrigeration compressor energy consumption of 18 % per cycle. Defrost intervals caused by condensate freezing on the cold side during winter operation were analysed; blockage events occurred in 7 % of cycles below outdoor temperatures of −5 °C and were mitigated by a timed bypass valve. Simple payback at measured performance was 2.9 years at 2019 Serbian industrial electricity tariffs. A parametric economic model explored sensitivity to electricity price increases between 10 and 40 %.

title: Psychrometric state tracking in batch drying chambers using low-cost sensor arrays: accuracy assessment and drift correction
abstract: Capacitive relative-humidity and NTC temperature sensors were evaluated as a low-cost alternative to chilled-mirror hygrometers for continuous psychrometric monitoring inside batch drying chambers. Twelve sensor nodes, each containing a Sensirion SHT31 element, were installed in a 3.6 m³ chamber and compared against a traceable chilled-mirror reference instrument at 24 operating points spanning 12–24 °C dry-bulb and 60–95 % relative humidity. Initial accuracy was within ±1.8 % RH and ±0.3 °C; however, sensors in the highest-humidity zones showed a drift of up to +3.4 % RH over 60 days of continuous operation. A polynomial drift-correction algorithm using periodic dry-reference events reduced residual drift to below ±1.0 % RH. Spatial gradients measured simultaneously at 12 nodes revealed dew-point differences up to 2.1 °C across the chamber, confirming that single-point monitoring as typically practised in industry gives a misleading picture of chamber psychrometric state. The sensor nodes cost approximately 35 EUR each and are considered economically viable for small-scale facilities.

title: Thermal modelling and energy simulation of batch dryers in the meat-processing sector
abstract: This chapter presents a systematic treatment of thermal process modelling approaches for batch drying chambers used in meat-product manufacturing, covering lumped-parameter, zonal, and full CFD-based methods. The discussion draws on experimental data from a series of studies conducted on pilot and industrial-scale chambers in Serbia and neighbouring countries. For each modelling approach, the required input data, calibration effort, computational cost, and achievable accuracy are compared in a structured matrix. Case studies illustrate the application of zonal models to multi-product loading configurations and the use of validated CFD results to inform simplified control logic. A section on energy simulation methodology covers integration of drying chamber models with compressor and heat-recovery subsystem models for facility-level energy balance calculations. The chapter concludes with practical guidance on selecting a modelling approach appropriate to the available measurement infrastructure and project objectives.

title: Baseline energy benchmarking of batch drying operations in the Vojvodina meat-processing cluster
abstract: Energy consumption data were collected from 21 meat-processing facilities in Vojvodina that operate batch drying chambers for fermented and cured products. A standardised data-collection protocol based on utility billing records, sub-meter readings, and operator interviews was applied across sites with annual production volumes ranging from 45 to 1 200 tonnes. Specific energy consumption per tonne of finished product ranged from 820 to 3 400 kWh/t, with a median of 1 580 kWh/t. Facilities with heat-recovery systems showed specific consumption 22–34 % below the cluster median. Statistical clustering identified three performance tiers; the lower two tiers were associated with chambers older than 15 years and lacking variable-speed fan drives. The benchmarking database is intended to support regional policy decisions on energy efficiency obligations for small and medium agri-food enterprises and to serve as a reference for future audit studies. Anonymised data from the 21 sites are provided as supplementary material.

title: Numerical investigation of heat exchanger placement strategies for exhaust-air heat recovery in compact batch drying chambers
abstract: CFD was used to evaluate five placement and duct-routing strategies for integrating a plate heat exchanger into the exhaust circuit of a compact 2.4 m³ batch drying chamber intended for small artisan meat producers. The chamber geometry imposed severe space constraints, limiting the available heat-exchanger face area to between 0.08 and 0.14 m². Simulations were run at steady-state for three representative drying-phase operating points (early, mid, and late cycle) characterised by exhaust air conditions measured in a preceding experimental campaign. Pressure drop penalties imposed by each placement strategy were evaluated alongside heat recovery effectiveness. Strategy D, placing the heat exchanger in a top-mounted roof plenum, achieved effectiveness of 0.59 with a pressure drop increase of only 8 Pa at the design fan operating point, compared with 14–27 Pa for duct-integrated alternatives. Annual energy savings were estimated at 1 140 kWh for a facility running 200 drying cycles per year, corresponding to approximately 170 EUR at current tariffs. Condensate drainage requirements for each strategy are discussed.

title: Dynamic zonal modelling of coupled heat and moisture transfer in batch meat dryers under variable ambient conditions
abstract: A dynamic zonal model dividing a 7.2 m³ batch drying chamber into 18 control volumes was developed to capture the effect of seasonal ambient-air variability on internal psychrometric conditions and product drying trajectories. The model couples air-side enthalpy and moisture balances with a simplified product-layer diffusion model using an effective moisture diffusivity fitted to experimental weight-loss curves. Ambient boundary conditions were drawn from a 12-month measured dataset comprising hourly dry-bulb temperature and relative humidity at a facility in Sremska Mitrovica. Simulations covering 480 drying cycles showed that cycle energy consumption varied by ±16 % across seasons, primarily driven by changes in the latent cooling load imposed on the refrigeration system. Control scenarios maintaining fixed dry-bulb set points versus dew-point set points were compared; dew-point control reduced energy variance to ±7 % and improved product weight-loss consistency. Model execution time per 96-hour cycle was under 40 seconds on standard hardware, making it suitable for embedded use in chamber control systems.

title: Fan speed modulation strategies for energy reduction in batch meat-drying chambers: simulation-based assessment
abstract: Variable-speed fan drive schedules were evaluated for a 7.2 m³ batch drying chamber using the validated dynamic zonal model described in a preceding study. Four drive schedules were compared against a fixed-speed baseline: constant low speed, constant medium speed, product-surface-moisture-triggered switching, and a model-predictive schedule using forecast ambient conditions. Simulated drying cycles of 96 hours at representative summer and winter ambient conditions were used as evaluation scenarios. The model-predictive schedule achieved the greatest energy reduction, 14.2 % relative to baseline, while maintaining product weight-loss uniformity coefficient of variation below 8 %. The moisture-triggered switching schedule reduced energy by 9.7 % with minimal control complexity and was identified as the most practical option for retrofit to existing chambers without online product monitoring capability. Fan mechanical life implications of frequent speed changes were estimated from a simplified fatigue accumulation model, suggesting that switching frequencies below six events per hour are unlikely to reduce bearing service life materially.

title: A Metamodel for IEC 61131-3 Structured Text: Design Rationale and Conformance Checking
abstract: IEC 61131-3 defines five programming languages for programmable logic controllers, yet no widely adopted formal metamodel exists for its Structured Text variant. This paper presents a metamodel covering the full grammar of Structured Text as defined in the third edition of the standard, implemented in Ecore within the Eclipse Modeling Framework. The metamodel comprises 47 metaclasses and 112 structural features. Conformance checking is realized through 34 OCL constraints covering type compatibility, scope resolution, and temporal execution order. The metamodel was validated against a corpus of 18 publicly available PLC project archives totalling approximately 120,000 lines of Structured Text, extracted from open automation repositories. Constraint violations found in the corpus are categorized by severity and related to common programming errors. The paper discusses design decisions around POUs, data types, and sequential function chart interoperability. The resulting artifact serves as a foundation for model-to-model and model-to-text transformation chains described in subsequent work.
venue: Journal of Systems and Control Engineering Research

title: Mapping UML Class Diagrams to IEC 61131-3 Function Blocks via ATL Transformations
abstract: Function blocks in IEC 61131-3 exhibit structural similarity to classes in object-oriented formalisms, yet practitioners lack automated tooling to carry designs expressed in UML into executable PLC artifacts. This paper defines an ATL transformation that maps a restricted profile of UML class diagrams—covering classes, associations, aggregations, and a subset of stereotypes—to IEC 61131-3 Function Block Declaration bodies in Structured Text. The transformation handles inheritance by flattening class hierarchies into self-contained function block bodies, preserving interface semantics through input and output variable mappings. An evaluation was conducted on five industrial-style case studies ranging from conveyor-belt sequencing to batch-reactor control, each containing between 8 and 31 classes. Generated code was compiled and executed on Beckhoff CX5130 hardware. Cyclic execution times of generated programs stayed within 5% of manually written equivalents. The paper also reports on maintainability metrics comparing generated and hand-written code using McCabe complexity and comment density.

title: Variability Modelling in PLC Software Families Using Feature Models and Configuration Constraints
abstract: Automation equipment manufacturers frequently produce families of machines that share a large fraction of control logic but differ in optional subsystems such as sensor types, drive configurations, or safety interlocks. Managing such variability through copy-paste code leads to maintenance burdens quantified here on a dataset of 14 PLC projects from a partner manufacturing firm. This paper proposes using FODA-style feature models, extended with numerical attributes for timing parameters, to represent the configuration space of a PLC software product line. A binding-time model distinguishes features configured at project generation time from those configured at runtime through parameter tables. A prototype implementation uses FeatureIDE for feature model editing and a Xtend-based generator to produce Structured Text artefacts for selected configurations. The approach was applied to a filling-machine product line with 23 optional features, yielding a single-source model from which 8 valid configurations were derived and verified against a test harness of 310 unit tests. Lines of code under manual maintenance were reduced by 61% compared to the previous fork-based approach.

title: An Xtext Grammar and IDE Support for a Subset of IEC 61131-3 Structured Text
abstract: Development of domain-specific tools for PLC programming is hampered by the absence of reusable, open parser infrastructure. This paper describes an Xtext grammar covering approximately 92% of the Structured Text syntax defined in IEC 61131-3 third edition, excluding only deprecated GOTO constructs and certain vendor extensions. The grammar is accompanied by scope provider rules for cross-reference resolution across compilation units, a type-inference engine handling implicit numeric widening, and formatter and outline view implementations for Eclipse IDE integration. Error recovery strategies are documented, as PLC source files from industrial environments frequently contain partial programs during edit sessions. A user study involving 11 automation engineers from three companies measured error detection time for introduced syntax and type errors; the IDE reduced median detection time from 14.3 minutes to under 2 minutes compared to a plain text editor workflow. The tooling is released under an open-source license and has been adopted in three subsequent research projects at partner institutions.

title: Model-Driven Engineering for PLC Software: A Mapping Study of the Literature 2005–2019
abstract: This mapping study systematically reviews the intersection of model-driven engineering and IEC 61131-3 PLC software development published between 2005 and 2019. A search across four digital libraries using a defined string yielded 741 candidate papers, of which 89 met inclusion criteria after title, abstract, and full-text screening by two independent reviewers. Papers are classified along five dimensions: MDE technique applied (metamodeling, model transformation, DSL, generative programming, formal verification), target IEC 61131-3 language, evaluation type, application domain, and tool maturity. Results show that Structured Text dominates as a generation target in 73% of papers, formal verification is underrepresented at 11%, and only 19% of studies report evaluation on industrial-scale models. The study identifies gaps in round-trip engineering, multi-language PLC projects, and systematic variability management. A replication package including the classification spreadsheet and search strings is made available.

title: Integrating Safety Requirements into PLC Product-Line Models Using SysML Parametric Diagrams
abstract: Safety-critical PLC applications require that timing and operational constraints derived from hazard analyses be traceable through to implementation. This paper proposes a model-based workflow in which SysML parametric diagrams capture quantitative safety constraints—maximum response times, watchdog periods, and safe-state transition conditions—derived from a HAZOP analysis artefact. A model-to-model transformation maps parametric constraint blocks to annotations on a feature model, and a subsequent model-to-text step embeds the constraints as pragma comments and runtime assertion code in generated Structured Text. The approach was demonstrated on a palletizer control application with 17 identified safety functions. All 17 functions produced traceable artefacts from HAZOP table rows to compiled PLC code. A traceability matrix was generated automatically and verified by a safety assessor against IEC 62061 SIL 2 requirements. The paper discusses limitations arising from the restricted expressiveness of IEC 61131-3 assertions and proposes extensions.

title: DSL Design for Conveyor Routing Logic: A Case Study in Abstraction Level Calibration
abstract: Choosing the right abstraction level for a domain-specific language is a practical design problem with limited empirical guidance. This paper reports a case study in which three successive DSL versions were designed, implemented, and evaluated for expressing conveyor routing logic in a logistics automation context. The first version mirrored the structure of IEC 61131-3 function block networks closely; the second introduced a graph-based topology language with implicit signal routing; the third added a declarative routing-rule layer. Each version was implemented as an Xtext grammar with an Xtend code generator producing Structured Text. Evaluation involved six automation programmers who completed identical routing tasks under a think-aloud protocol. Task completion time, error rate, and post-task questionnaire scores were recorded. The graph-based version produced the lowest error rate at 0.8 errors per task; the declarative version had the shortest median task time at 11.4 minutes but required the longest learning period. The paper derives three abstraction-level heuristics for industrial DSL design.

title: Towards Round-Trip Engineering for IEC 61131-3: Extracting Feature Models from Legacy PLC Codebases
abstract: Many manufacturing firms operate legacy PLC codebases developed without explicit variability management. Migrating such code to a product-line architecture requires recovering implicit variation points from existing programs. This paper presents a semi-automated extraction approach that applies clone detection to a corpus of related PLC projects to identify recurring code patterns, clusters patterns by structural similarity using a tree-edit distance metric, and maps clusters to candidate features in a FODA feature model. The approach was applied to a set of 11 related projects from an anonymised food-processing equipment manufacturer totalling 84,000 lines of Structured Text. Extraction identified 38 candidate features, of which domain experts validated 29 as genuine variation points. Six features required manual refinement. The recovered feature model was used to derive a product-line architecture, and one configuration was re-generated and compared against the original project using cyclomatic complexity and test pass rate as metrics. Results indicate functional equivalence for the regenerated configuration on the existing test suite.

title: A Benchmark Suite for PLC Code Generators: Construction, Metrics, and Baseline Results
abstract: Reproducible evaluation of PLC code generators is difficult because published studies use heterogeneous, proprietary case studies. This paper describes the construction of an open benchmark suite comprising 24 PLC control scenarios spanning motion control, process automation, and safety interlock domains. Each scenario is specified at three levels: a natural-language requirements document, a structured functional specification, and a reference implementation in Structured Text manually written by two authors independently and reconciled. Benchmark metrics include correctness (pass rate on a hardware-in-the-loop test harness using Wago PFC200 controllers), code size ratio to reference, cyclomatic complexity ratio, and compilation time. Baseline results are reported for three existing open-source code generators and for the authors' own generator. No generator achieves above 81% correctness across all scenarios; motion control scenarios prove most difficult. The benchmark suite and harness scripts are released under an open licence to enable comparative evaluation in future work.
venue: Empirical Software Engineering

title: Fee Collection Performance and Financial Sustainability of Irrigation WUAs in Serbia: A Panel Analysis 1997–2005
abstract: Water-user associations in Serbia depend almost exclusively on volumetric or area-based service fees, yet collection rates have been chronically low since the transition period. This study uses an unbalanced panel of 24 registered WUAs observed over the period 1997–2005 (189 association-year observations) to model fee collection performance as a function of organizational, agronomic, and socioeconomic predictors. Data were assembled from association financial ledgers, Serbian Water Management Directorate records, and two rounds of on-site audits. The mean collection rate across the panel was 61.4 percent, with a standard deviation of 19.2 percent and a declining trend after 2002 coinciding with drought years and reduced crop revenues. Fixed-effects regression identifies the ratio of full-time technical staff to irrigated area, the presence of a written conflict resolution procedure, and average farm size as the strongest positive predictors of collection performance. Associations dominated by smallholder members showed systematically lower collection rates, raising equity concerns about flat area-based fee structures.

title: Gender and Voice in Irrigation Governance: Women's Participation in WUA Bodies in Vojvodina and the Mačva Region
abstract: Women constitute a significant share of farm labor and land ownership in both Vojvodina and the Mačva region of western Serbia, yet their representation in water-user association governance bodies has received little empirical attention. This paper reports findings from a survey of 33 WUAs conducted in 2007–2008, recording gender composition of elected boards (n = 193 board positions), attendance at general assemblies, and self-reported influence over irrigation decisions across 148 female farm operators. Women held 7 percent of formal board positions nationally and reported lower perceived influence over delivery scheduling than male counterparts with equivalent farm sizes. Qualitative interviews with 22 women farmers identified scheduling meeting times, informal male networks in association leadership, and lack of written participation procedures as structural barriers. The paper does not claim these findings are specific to the region, but situates them within a broader literature on gender and collective water governance in Eastern Europe, and recommends modest procedural reforms consistent with existing association statutes.

title: Drought of 2012 and Its Effects on WUA Governance Stability in the Pannonian Plain: A Multi-Country Assessment
abstract: The severe drought that affected the Pannonian Plain in 2012 provides a natural stress test for irrigation governance institutions. This study examines how water-user associations in Serbia, Hungary, and Romania responded to acute water scarcity during that season, drawing on rapid post-season interviews with 47 WUA managers (18 Serbia, 16 Hungary, 13 Romania), internal conflict logs, and delivery records for the July–August 2012 peak demand period. The study finds that associations with pre-existing written rationing protocols distributed water more equitably during the crisis, as measured by the coefficient of variation of per-hectare delivery volumes (mean CV of 0.21 in associations with protocols vs. 0.44 in those without). Informal authority concentration increased in nearly all associations regardless of country, suggesting a common governance response to scarcity stress. The paper identifies four distinct coping strategies and discusses their implications for permanent institutional design improvements.

title: Thirty Years of Irrigation Institutional Reform in Serbia: A Longitudinal Assessment of Water-User Associations, 1985–2015
abstract: This paper synthesizes three decades of empirical data on irrigation governance in Serbia, tracing the trajectory of water-user associations from their origins as administrative extensions of socialist agricultural kombinats through the turbulent transition years and into the period of EU approximation. The evidence base spans original fieldwork conducted by the author and colleagues from 1995 to 2015, covering 41 WUAs in Vojvodina, Mačva, and the Morava corridor, and draws on 312 interviews, six rounds of financial record collection, and continuous monitoring of three indicator associations. The analysis applies a historical-institutional lens to trace how path dependence, external shocks (1999 conflict, 2012 drought, EU water framework directives), and organizational learning have shaped current governance outcomes. A composite institutional performance score is constructed and tracked at five-year intervals. Results indicate gradual but uneven improvement, with urban-adjacent associations in Vojvodina showing the strongest gains and remote smallholder associations the weakest. The paper closes with evidence-based recommendations for Serbia's ongoing Water Law revision process.

title: Water-User Association Responses to Land Consolidation Programmes in Vojvodina: Early Evidence from Three Pilot Districts
abstract: Serbia's land consolidation programme, accelerated after 2015, has reorganised land parcels across tens of thousands of hectares in Vojvodina, with direct but largely unstudied consequences for the membership composition, delivery infrastructure, and fee structures of irrigation water-user associations. This paper reports on fieldwork conducted in 2019–2020 in three pilot consolidation districts—Kula, Bečej, and Sremska Mitrovica—including interviews with 31 WUA officials and 54 farmers who experienced parcel reclassification, as well as analysis of revised cadastral and membership records. Consolidation increased average plot size from 1.2 to 2.9 ha in the study areas, reducing the total number of WUA member accounts by 34 percent. Fee revenue per hectare remained stable in two districts but dropped 18 percent in the third due to reclassification disputes. The paper identifies procedural gaps at the interface between the land consolidation authority and WUA governance structures and recommends formal coordination protocols.

title: Equity Outcomes Under Volumetric Versus Area-Based Water Pricing in Serbian Irrigation Districts: A Retrospective Comparison
abstract: Two dominant fee structures coexist in Serbian irrigation districts: flat area-based charges and volumetric pricing, the latter introduced experimentally in four Vojvodina associations after 2010. This retrospective study compares equity outcomes under the two regimes using a dataset covering twelve associations (seven area-based, five volumetric) over the period 2011–2022, constructed from association ledgers, meter installation records, and 88 farmer interviews conducted in 2022. Equity is measured via an adapted Lorenz curve applied to water volumes delivered per unit of crop area across farm-size quintiles. Volumetric associations show a lower mean delivery Gini of 0.29 compared to 0.41 in area-based associations, and this difference holds after controlling for scheme size, crop mix, and average farm scale. However, volumetric associations also exhibit higher administrative costs and greater non-payment incidence among farms below 3 ha. The paper concludes that volumetric pricing improves equity for mid-sized farms but may disadvantage the smallest users without accompanying subsidy mechanisms.

title: Oscillatory shear behaviour of wheat starch gels at concentrations between 5 and 15 % (w/w) as a function of heating rate
abstract: The viscoelastic properties of wheat starch gels prepared at concentrations of 5, 8, 10, 12, and 15 % (w/w) were characterised by small-amplitude oscillatory shear over the frequency range 0.01–100 rad/s at 25 °C. Gels were formed by heating aqueous dispersions from 25 °C to 95 °C at controlled rates of 1, 3, and 5 °C/min in a water-bath system, followed by quench cooling to 25 °C. Storage modulus G′ increased from 280 Pa at 5 % to 4 650 Pa at 15 % concentration when using a 1 °C/min heating rate. Faster heating rates consistently yielded lower G′ values across all concentrations, attributed to incomplete granule swelling and reduced amylose leaching, as confirmed by differential scanning calorimetry peak broadening. Loss tangent values below 0.1 at all concentrations indicated predominantly elastic behaviour. The results establish baseline rheological parameters for the starch systems subsequently studied under freeze–thaw conditions in later work.

title: Differential scanning calorimetry of retrogradation in mixed wheat starch–whey protein isolate gels stored at 4 °C for up to 28 days
abstract: Retrogradation kinetics in wheat starch gels (10 % w/w) containing whey protein isolate (WPI) at 0, 2, 4, and 6 % (w/w) were tracked by DSC over a 28-day storage period at 4 °C. Endothermic melting enthalpies of recrystallised amylopectin were measured weekly. In the control starch gel, melting enthalpy increased from 0.8 J/g on day 1 to 3.4 J/g on day 28. Inclusion of 4 % WPI reduced the day-28 enthalpy to 2.1 J/g, suggesting partial interference with amylopectin chain reassociation. The onset temperature of the retrogradation endotherm shifted upward by approximately 2.5 °C in protein-containing systems, implying formation of more thermally stable crystallites despite their reduced quantity. Fourier-transform infrared spectra showed increased β-sheet absorbance in WPI-containing gels after 14 days, indicating concurrent protein conformational changes. The data indicate that WPI at moderate concentrations delays but does not prevent starch retrogradation under refrigeration conditions.

title: Syneresis and gel network disruption in wheat starch–whey protein gels subjected to three freeze–thaw cycles at −18 °C and +20 °C
abstract: Wheat starch–whey protein isolate composite gels (10 % starch, 0–6 % WPI, w/w) were subjected to 1, 2, and 3 freeze–thaw cycles between −18 °C (freezing, 12 h) and +20 °C (thawing, 4 h) and evaluated for syneresis, texture profile analysis parameters, and storage modulus G′. Syneresis, expressed as percentage expelled water relative to initial gel mass, increased from 8.2 % after one cycle in the control gel to 27.6 % after three cycles. Addition of 4 % WPI reduced three-cycle syneresis to 14.3 %. Hardness and cohesiveness determined by texture profile analysis both declined progressively with cycling; hardness fell from 38 N (cycle 0) to 11 N (cycle 3) for the control, while the 4 % WPI system retained 22 N hardness after three cycles. Low-field NMR T2 relaxometry confirmed a shift in water population toward less-bound states with increased cycling. These data underpin formulation targets for frozen ready-meal sauce components.

title: Effect of freezing rate on ice crystal morphology and subsequent textural damage in starch-based gel matrices: a comparison of air-blast and cryogenic freezing
abstract: Ice crystal size distributions and their effect on textural parameters after thawing were compared for wheat starch gels (10 % w/w) frozen under three conditions: slow air freezing at −18 °C (90 min to reach thermal equilibrium), air-blast freezing at −35 °C with 3 m/s air velocity (18 min), and liquid nitrogen immersion (approximately 90 s). Cryosectioning and light microscopy with polarised light revealed mean ice crystal diameters of 312, 148, and 41 µm for the three respective methods. After thawing, hardness losses were 61, 34, and 12 % relative to the unfrozen reference, closely correlated with crystal size (r = 0.97). Scanning electron microscopy of freeze-dried gel sections confirmed greater network disruption in slowly frozen samples. The findings suggest that even without formulation changes, the freezing rate alone accounts for substantial textural variation, a factor often underrepresented in ready-meal product development discussions.

title: Incorporation of hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate as a partial replacement for native wheat starch in freeze–thaw-stable gels: rheological and calorimetric evaluation
abstract: Hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate (HPDSP) was substituted for native wheat starch at 25, 50, 75, and 100 % of the total starch fraction (total starch content fixed at 10 % w/w) in composite gels also containing 4 % (w/w) whey protein isolate. Gels were subjected to five freeze–thaw cycles (−18 °C / +20 °C). Syneresis after five cycles declined monotonically from 18.4 % in the native-starch control to 4.7 % in the 100 % HPDSP gel. DSC retrogradation enthalpy after five cycles was reduced from 2.8 J/g in the control to 0.6 J/g at full substitution. G′ retention across five cycles improved from 38 % (native) to 79 % (full HPDSP). However, hardness values measured at cycle 0 were lower in the HPDSP-rich gels (24 N at full substitution vs 38 N for native), indicating a fundamental trade-off between initial gel firmness and freeze–thaw resilience. The 50 % substitution level offered the most acceptable balance for simulated ready-meal sauce applications based on an overall textural quality index.

title: Cryoprotectant effects of trehalose and sucrose on wheat starch–pea protein isolate composite gels under repeated freeze–thaw cycling
abstract: Pea protein isolate (PPI) was used in place of whey protein isolate to formulate plant-based starch–protein composite gels (10 % wheat starch, 5 % PPI, w/w). Trehalose or sucrose was added at 0, 3, 6, and 9 % (w/w) to evaluate cryoprotection during five freeze–thaw cycles (−20 °C, 14 h freezing; +22 °C, 5 h thawing). Both sugars reduced syneresis and G′ loss, but trehalose was consistently more effective; at 6 % trehalose, syneresis after five cycles was 7.1 % compared with 10.4 % for the equivalent sucrose concentration and 22.8 % for the sugar-free control. DSC measurements showed that trehalose at 6 % increased the gel glass-transition temperature Tg by 8 °C relative to control, supporting a vitrification-based protection mechanism. Sensory texture scores (firmness and cohesiveness) from a semi-trained panel of 12 assessors confirmed acceptable textural quality at trehalose concentrations up to 6 %. Above 9 % both sugars introduced perceptible sweetness, limiting practical applicability in savoury matrices.

title: Mapping the mechanical phase diagram of starch–protein gels as a function of total biopolymer concentration and protein-to-starch ratio using a design-of-experiments approach
abstract: A central composite design with 30 experimental points was used to explore G′, G″, hardness, and syneresis after three freeze–thaw cycles as response variables across a formulation space defined by total biopolymer concentration (8–16 % w/w) and protein-to-starch mass ratio (0.1–0.7). Whey protein isolate and native wheat starch were used as model biopolymers. Response surface models with R² values between 0.88 and 0.94 were obtained for all four responses. The optimum region for maximising G′ retention and minimising syneresis simultaneously was identified at approximately 12–13 % total biopolymer and a protein-to-starch ratio of 0.35–0.45. At ratios above 0.5, phase separation was visually apparent in 11 of 14 formulations, detected by confocal laser scanning microscopy using Nile red and Nile blue dual staining. The resulting empirical model provides a practical formulation tool for frozen food product developers working with these particular biopolymers.

title: Sterol-dependent formation of detergent-resistant membrane fractions in Arabidopsis thaliana root cells
abstract: Detergent-resistant membranes (DRMs) are widely used as biochemical proxies for lipid raft microdomains. This study characterised the sterol composition and protein content of DRMs isolated from Arabidopsis thaliana root tissue using Triton X-100 extraction at 4 °C followed by sucrose density gradient ultracentrifugation. Gas chromatography–mass spectrometry revealed that DRMs were enriched in sitosterol and stigmasterol relative to the bulk membrane fraction, with a sterol-to-phospholipid molar ratio of 0.62 ± 0.08 in DRMs versus 0.21 ± 0.04 in non-raft fractions. SDS-PAGE and immunoblot analysis identified 23 proteins reproducibly enriched in the DRM fraction across three independent biological replicates. Pharmacological depletion of sterols using methyl-β-cyclodextrin at 5 mM reduced DRM buoyancy and abolished the enrichment of five of these proteins. The results confirm that sterol composition is a primary determinant of microdomain stability in Arabidopsis root membranes and provide a quantitative baseline for studies manipulating sterol biosynthesis pathways.

title: Temperature-induced changes in membrane microdomain organisation in sunflower (Helianthus annuus) seedlings
abstract: Plants adjust membrane lipid composition in response to temperature fluctuations, but how this affects microdomain organisation in agriculturally relevant species is poorly understood. We grew sunflower seedlings at 10 °C, 22 °C, and 34 °C for seven days and isolated plasma membrane vesicles by aqueous two-phase partitioning. Membrane fluidity was assessed by steady-state fluorescence anisotropy of 1,6-diphenyl-1,3,5-hexatriene (DPH) and its cationic trimethylammonium derivative (TMA-DPH). At 10 °C, DPH anisotropy in DRM fractions increased by 31% compared to 22 °C controls, indicating more ordered microdomains. Fatty acid profiling by GC-FID showed increased palmitic acid and decreased linolenic acid content at low temperature. The abundance of a 42 kDa protein tentatively identified as a plasma membrane H+-ATPase isoform was reduced in DRM fractions at 10 °C by approximately 40%, as determined by quantitative immunoblot. These findings suggest that temperature-driven changes in fatty acid saturation influence the partitioning of proton pumps between ordered and disordered membrane regions.

title: Aquaporin PIP2;1 associates with sterol-enriched microdomains in maize root plasma membranes
abstract: Plasma membrane intrinsic proteins (PIPs) are major water channels in plant cells, but their lateral organisation within the membrane is not fully resolved. We investigated the microdomain association of PIP2;1 in maize (Zea mays L.) root plasma membranes by combining DRM isolation with immunofluorescence microscopy and FRET-based proximity assays. Confocal immunofluorescence using anti-PIP2;1 antibody and filipin as a sterol marker revealed partial co-localisation in discrete puncta approximately 0.3–0.8 µm in diameter at the root hair zone. Co-immunoprecipitation from DRM fractions confirmed the presence of PIP2;1 in sterol-rich domains. FRET efficiency between Alexa 488-labelled anti-PIP2;1 and Alexa 555-labelled anti-sitosterol was 8.4 ± 1.2%, significantly above the negative control (2.1 ± 0.6%). Methyl-β-cyclodextrin treatment reduced plasma membrane water permeability measured by stopped-flow spectroscopy by 38%, consistent with a functional role for microdomain localisation in regulating aquaporin activity.

title: Effect of exogenous phytosterols on membrane microdomain properties and aluminium tolerance in barley root tips
abstract: Aluminium toxicity is a major limitation for crop production on acidic soils. Some evidence suggests that plasma membrane organisation affects Al3+ uptake and tolerance mechanisms, but the role of lipid microdomains in this context has not been directly tested. We supplemented barley (Hordeum vulgare cv. Zlatko) seedlings with exogenous sitosterol (0, 10, 25, and 50 µM) for 48 hours prior to exposure to 50 µM AlCl3 at pH 4.5. Root elongation, callose deposition, and Evans blue uptake were used as toxicity indicators. Exogenous sitosterol at 25 µM increased DRM sterol content by 22% and partially protected root elongation (62% of control versus 41% in unsupplemented Al-treated plants). Callose deposition, a marker of Al-induced cell wall damage, was reduced by 34% in sterol-supplemented seedlings. DRM-associated protein profiles were compared by 2D-DIGE, identifying three proteins with altered abundance that may contribute to tolerance. Results indicate a modulatory role for membrane microdomain composition in Al stress responses.

title: Lateral diffusion of a fluorescent lipid analogue in plant protoplast membranes measured by single-particle tracking
abstract: Lateral diffusion of lipids reflects the physical state and heterogeneity of biological membranes. We applied single-particle tracking (SPT) of the fluorescent lipid analogue BODIPY-FL-C12 in protoplasts isolated from tobacco (Nicotiana tabacum) leaf mesophyll cells. Trajectories of 1,847 individual particles were collected at 33 ms per frame using total internal reflection fluorescence (TIRF) microscopy and analysed with a mean square displacement approach. The distribution of diffusion coefficients was bimodal, with a slow-diffusing population (D = 0.08 ± 0.03 µm²/s) comprising 41% of trajectories and a faster population (D = 0.54 ± 0.12 µm²/s). Confinement analysis indicated that the slow population was transiently confined within domains of approximately 250 nm radius for periods of 0.8–2.4 s. Sterol depletion with 5 mM methyl-β-cyclodextrin collapsed the bimodal distribution into a single faster population (D = 0.49 ± 0.09 µm²/s), confirming that sterol-enriched microdomains underlie the confinement zones. The dataset provides quantitative parameters for biophysical modelling of plant membrane heterogeneity.

title: Proteomic inventory of detergent-resistant membranes from pepper (Capsicum annuum) fruit cells at three ripening stages
abstract: Fruit ripening involves major remodelling of cellular membranes, yet how lipid microdomain protein composition changes during this process has not been surveyed in pepper. We isolated DRMs from pericarp tissue of Capsicum annuum cv. Šorokšári at green, turning, and red stages by sucrose gradient ultracentrifugation. Label-free quantitative proteomics identified 318 proteins reproducibly detected in at least two of three biological replicates per stage. Clustering analysis revealed four abundance trajectories across ripening: proteins that increased monotonically (n = 47), decreased monotonically (n = 61), peaked at the turning stage (n = 38), and remained stable (n = 172). Notably, the abundance of a tonoplast aquaporin TIP1 homologue in DRM fractions increased 2.8-fold from green to red, while a GNOM-like ARF-GEF decreased 3.1-fold. Functional enrichment analysis highlighted vesicle trafficking and stress response categories as overrepresented among dynamically regulated proteins. The dataset is deposited in a public repository and constitutes a resource for future functional studies of pepper fruit membrane biology.

title: Influence of plant-derived glycosylated sterols on artificial bilayer permeability and thickness
abstract: Glycosylated sterols, including steryl glucosides (SGs) and acylated steryl glucosides (ASGs), are abundant in plant membranes but their specific biophysical contributions to membrane properties are rarely studied in isolation. We prepared large unilamellar vesicles (LUVs) composed of DPPC/DOPC/sitosterol (2:1:1) supplemented with increasing molar fractions (0, 2, 5, and 10 mol%) of purified sitosteryl-β-D-glucoside. Membrane permeability to calcein was assessed by dye leakage assay, and bilayer thickness was measured by small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) at the ESRF BM29 beamline during a collaborative visit. Addition of 5 mol% SG reduced calcein permeability by 19% compared to sterol-only controls and increased bilayer repeat spacing by 0.34 nm. At 10 mol%, crystalline domains were observed in electron microscopy, suggesting phase segregation. Differential scanning calorimetry showed a broadening of the main transition peak with increasing SG content. These results suggest that glycosylated sterols contribute to membrane order and reduced solute permeability in a concentration-dependent manner.
