title: Membrane microdomain disruption impairs nitrate uptake and NRT2.1 localisation in wheat roots under low nitrogen supply
abstract: Nitrate transporter NRT2.1 mediates high-affinity nitrate uptake in plant roots, but whether its activity depends on membrane microdomain integrity is unresolved. We grew wheat (Triticum aestivum cv. Zvezdana) under sufficient (5 mM KNO3) and deficient (0.1 mM KNO3) nitrogen regimes and applied methyl-β-cyclodextrin (mβCD) at 1 mM to disrupt microdomains. 15NO3− uptake measured by isotope ratio mass spectrometry was reduced by 47% in mβCD-treated, nitrogen-deficient roots compared to untreated nitrogen-deficient controls. Confocal immunofluorescence with anti-NRT2.1 antibody showed that sterol depletion caused a redistribution of the transporter from discrete plasma membrane foci to a more uniform distribution. Co-fractionation on sucrose gradients placed 68% of NRT2.1 signal in DRM fractions under nitrogen deficiency, falling to 29% after mβCD treatment. Complementary phylogenetic analysis identified conserved CRAC and CARC sterol-interacting motifs in the NRT2.1 transmembrane domain, suggesting a direct structural basis for microdomain affinity. Results indicate that microdomain integrity is required for normal high-affinity nitrate uptake.

title: Atomic force microscopy imaging of lipid raft-like domains in native plant plasma membrane sheets
abstract: Direct visualisation of membrane microdomains in native biological material remains technically demanding. We developed a protocol for preparing inside-out plasma membrane sheets from onion (Allium cepa) epidermal cells by mechanical unroofing on poly-L-lysine-coated mica, suitable for atomic force microscopy (AFM) imaging without fixation or staining. Peak Force Tapping AFM in PBS buffer revealed height-elevated domains of 0.5–1.2 nm above the surrounding bilayer, with lateral dimensions of 40–180 nm, consistent with liquid-ordered microdomain dimensions reported for model membranes. Domain abundance was approximately 3.8 domains per µm². Cholesterol oxidase treatment selectively flattened these domains, reducing their height contrast by 78%, confirming a sterol-dependent structural basis. Nanoindentation measurements showed that domain regions had a Young's modulus of 42 ± 9 MPa versus 18 ± 5 MPa in surrounding membrane, indicating higher stiffness. This preparation method provides a straightforward route to high-resolution membrane topography data for plant cell biology laboratories with AFM access.

title: Tracking Statutory Drift: How Labour Code Amendments Alter Inspection Practice in Serbia, 2001–2009
abstract: This article examines how successive amendments to the Serbian Labour Code between 2001 and 2009 changed the operative instructions used by labour inspectors. Using a documentary analysis of 214 inspection guidance circulars issued by the Labour Inspectorate, the study maps each change in statutory wording to a corresponding shift in inspection practice. A coding scheme with twelve interpretive categories was developed and applied independently by two legal analysts, yielding an inter-coder agreement rate of 88 percent. The results show that approximately one-third of statutory amendments generated no observable change in inspection circulars within eighteen months of enactment, while amendments touching wage calculation rules produced the fastest downstream changes—typically within three months. The article argues that the gap between legislative intent and enforcement adaptation is structurally predictable and proposes three indicators that legislators and ministry officials could monitor to reduce the lag. The findings have implications for the design of statutory language aimed at administrative bodies with limited legal staffing.

title: Purposive Interpretation and Its Limits in Serbian Administrative Tribunals
abstract: Administrative tribunals in Serbia have inconsistently applied purposive interpretation since the 2004 Administrative Procedure Act introduced a general duty to construe legislation in light of its stated objectives. This article analyses 312 tribunal decisions issued between 2005 and 2010, drawn from all five regional administrative courts, to assess how often purposive reasoning is invoked, how it is justified, and when it conflicts with literal reading. Decisions were coded for interpretive method, outcome direction, and whether the tribunal cited preparatory legislative materials. Purposive reasoning appeared in 19 percent of decisions, but explicit citation of travaux préparatoires occurred in fewer than 4 percent. Cases involving social welfare entitlements showed the highest rate of purposive reasoning, while tax and customs matters showed the lowest. The article identifies three doctrinal conditions under which tribunals retreat to literal interpretation even when purposive reasoning would be available, and discusses whether these patterns reflect judicial caution or an absence of interpretive training in the tribunal system.

title: Regulatory Impact Assessment in the Western Balkans: A Comparative Survey of Five Jurisdictions
abstract: This book chapter provides a comparative account of regulatory impact assessment (RIA) practice in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Montenegro, and Albania, drawing on material gathered through structured interviews with 47 civil servants and analysis of 89 published impact assessments produced between 2007 and 2012. The chapter examines four dimensions: the institutional location of RIA units, the methodological requirements imposed by law, the extent to which assessments address compliance costs for regulated entities, and the degree to which RIA findings influence final legislative texts. Findings indicate that RIA remains largely a formal procedural step in all five jurisdictions rather than a substantive analytical tool, with compliance cost sections being the most consistently omitted component. The chapter identifies differences between countries that have EU accession timetables and those that do not, finding a modest positive correlation between accession pressure and the completeness of published assessments. Policy recommendations address the minimum institutional conditions required for RIA to affect legislative outcomes.

title: Ambiguity by Default: Vague Standards in Employment Legislation and Their Administrative Consequences
abstract: Legislative vagueness is sometimes deliberate and sometimes a product of drafting failure; distinguishing the two matters for how administrators and courts should handle ambiguous provisions. This article develops a typology of vague standards drawn from a systematic reading of Serbian employment legislation in force as of January 2015, identifying 67 provisions that courts and inspectors have interpreted inconsistently. For each provision, the legislative history was examined to classify the vagueness as intentional delegation, unresolved compromise, or drafting oversight. Intentional delegation accounted for 29 of the 67 cases and was associated with greater interpretive convergence over time as administrative practice settled. Drafting-oversight cases showed persistent divergence even after five or more years. The article draws on administrative law theory and statutory drafting literature from Germany, Austria, and Croatia to propose a graduated response framework: different types of vagueness warrant different institutional responses, ranging from ministerial guidance circulars to legislative repair.

title: Compliance Monitoring Frameworks in EU Member States: Lessons for Candidate Countries
abstract: This conference paper presents findings from a structured comparison of compliance monitoring frameworks in four EU member states—Hungary, Romania, Slovenia, and Austria—with the aim of extracting design principles applicable to candidate countries undergoing administrative reform. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews with 22 senior officials in national labour and administrative inspection bodies, supplemented by analysis of institutional legal bases and annual inspection reports for the period 2012–2015. The comparison examines five design dimensions: mandate scope, sanctioning authority, inter-agency information sharing, appeal channel design, and performance measurement. Romania and Slovenia showed the most transferable institutional models for Western Balkan candidate countries given comparable administrative capacity levels. Austria's integrated inspection model, while effective, was judged to require a degree of digitalisation of business registers that is not yet present in candidate countries. The paper proposes a sequenced adoption pathway for Serbia and North Macedonia.

title: How Administrative Courts Read Collective Agreements: Interpretive Methodology in Labour Disputes in Serbia 2010–2017
abstract: Collective agreements occupy a hybrid legal space between contract and regulation, and their interpretation by administrative courts raises distinct methodological questions that are underexplored in Serbian legal scholarship. This article studies 178 administrative court decisions in which a collective agreement provision was the central interpretive question, covering the period 2010 to 2017. A content analysis framework was applied to identify which interpretive tools were used—textual, systematic, teleological, or comparative—and whether the court's chosen method produced consistent outcomes across factually similar cases. Systematic interpretation was the most frequently employed method but generated the highest rate of intra-court inconsistency: cases presenting materially identical collective agreement clauses were decided differently in 31 percent of instances. The article examines the doctrinal reasons for this inconsistency and argues that Serbian administrative courts lack a settled framework for handling the normative character of collective agreement language. Recommendations address both judicial training and collective bargaining drafting practice.

title: Sanctions Architecture in Labour Enforcement: A Comparison of Fixed Penalties, Discretionary Fines, and Administrative Orders in Four Balkan Jurisdictions
abstract: The choice between fixed-penalty systems, discretionary fines, and administrative orders in labour enforcement reflects assumptions about deterrence, administrative capacity, and employer behaviour that are rarely made explicit in legislative debates. This article compares sanction architecture in Serbia, Croatia, North Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina as of 2021, drawing on legislative texts, inspection authority annual reports, and 14 expert interviews with senior inspectors and legal advisers. Fixed-penalty systems—used predominantly in North Macedonia and Bosnia and Herzegovina—show higher collection rates but lower correlation with violation severity. Discretionary fine systems—used in Serbia and Croatia—show greater administrative burden but better targeting of repeat violators. Administrative orders without financial penalty are used as a first-response tool in all four jurisdictions but show low compliance rates without subsequent financial sanctions. The article proposes an evidence-based recalibration of Serbia's existing discretionary fine schedule, which has not been adjusted for inflation since 2013 and has lost approximately 40 percent of its real deterrent value.

title: Internal Compliance Units in Medium-Sized Enterprises: Structure, Mandate, and Effectiveness Under Serbian Labour Law
abstract: Serbian labour legislation imposes compliance obligations on enterprises without prescribing the internal structures through which those obligations should be discharged. This study examines the design and effectiveness of internal compliance units in 62 medium-sized enterprises (50–249 employees) operating in the Vojvodina region. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire administered to legal officers or HR directors, followed by semi-structured interviews in 18 of the enterprises. Compliance units were present in 45 of 62 enterprises but had defined written mandates in only 23 cases. Enterprises with written mandates and dedicated legal staff showed significantly fewer upheld violations in Labour Inspectorate records over the 2018–2021 period (mean 0.8 violations per enterprise versus 2.3 in enterprises without structured units). The study identifies six design variables—mandate scope, reporting line, staffing qualifications, update procedures, audit cycles, and record-keeping requirements—that differentiate high-performing from low-performing compliance units. Results suggest that a legislative opt-in model for certified compliance programmes, as used in Italian and German labour law, could reduce inspection burden while maintaining compliance levels.

title: Automated Regulatory Change Alerts: Prospects and Legal Constraints for Administrative Bodies in Serbia
abstract: Several EU member states have piloted automated systems that parse official gazettes and generate alerts for administrative bodies when legislative changes affect their operating mandates. This article examines whether such systems could be lawfully deployed by Serbian administrative inspection bodies and what legal constraints—concerning data access, official publication law, and institutional mandate—would apply. The analysis proceeds through three steps: a doctrinal review of the Official Gazette Act and e-Government Act, a comparison with equivalent legal frameworks in Estonia, Austria, and Croatia where automated monitoring tools are in use, and a structured assessment of the technical and legal minimum requirements for a compliant system in the Serbian context. The article concludes that no current statutory provision prohibits deployment, but that three specific gaps in the e-Government Act and one in the Administrative Procedure Act would need to be addressed through targeted amendment to provide a stable legal basis. A draft provision is proposed for each gap. The article does not address the software implementation itself but is intended to provide a legal baseline for potential pilot projects involving administrative bodies and technology partners.

title: Insulation ageing in power transformers: forty years of field data
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of insulation ageing phenomena in power transformers, drawing on forty years of continuous field data collected from substations across northern Serbia and the broader Pannonian region. The dataset encompasses oil-paper insulation samples from transformers ranging from 35 kV to 400 kV, covering diverse loading histories, ambient temperature profiles, and maintenance regimes. Key ageing indicators examined include degree of polymerisation of cellulose, furfural concentration in transformer oil, acidity index, and dielectric dissipation factor. Statistical modelling is applied to correlate measurable chemical markers with remaining transformer life, yielding revised ageing rate constants that account for real-world thermal cycling rather than idealised laboratory conditions. The findings challenge several assumptions embedded in current IEC thermal ageing models, particularly regarding the acceleration of ageing under intermittent overloading. Practical guidance is offered for utilities scheduling diagnostic intervals and planning end-of-life decisions. The paper concludes that transformer fleets managed with data-driven diagnostic protocols can safely extend service life by an average of seven to eleven years beyond conventional estimates, provided that moisture ingress is rigorously controlled.

title: Thermal modelling of oil-paper insulation in high-voltage transformers under cyclic loading
abstract: Accurate thermal modelling of oil-paper insulation systems is essential for predicting transformer ageing under realistic load cycles. This paper develops a refined thermal model that incorporates both top-oil and hot-spot temperature dynamics, validated against measurements taken from twelve 110 kV power transformers operating in industrial substations. The model extends the classical IEC 354 framework by introducing a load-dependent correction factor that accounts for non-uniform heat distribution in the winding geometry. Experimental data were obtained by embedding fibre-optic sensors at multiple winding positions during planned outages, enabling direct comparison with simulated temperature profiles over a twelve-month monitoring period. Results demonstrate that conventional models underestimate peak hot-spot temperatures by up to 8 °C under rapid load ramp conditions, which has significant implications for cumulative ageing calculations. A revised set of thermal constants is proposed for oil-immersed transformers with natural oil circulation and forced air cooling. The paper provides utility engineers with improved tools for dynamic rating and real-time thermal monitoring, contributing to safer and more economical transformer operation.

title: Partial discharge detection in transformer bushings using acoustic emission techniques
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) activity in transformer bushings represents one of the most critical precursors to catastrophic insulation failure in high-voltage power systems. This paper investigates the applicability of acoustic emission (AE) techniques for non-invasive PD detection in oil-impregnated paper bushings rated at 110 kV and 220 kV. Laboratory specimens were subjected to controlled PD conditions using a purpose-built high-voltage test cell, and AE signals were recorded with piezoelectric sensors mounted on the external bushing surface. Signal processing routines based on wavelet decomposition were developed to distinguish genuine PD events from electromagnetic interference and mechanical vibration artifacts commonly encountered in substation environments. Attenuation characteristics of the acoustic signal through bushing dielectric materials were mapped as a function of frequency, providing a basis for sensor placement optimisation. Field trials conducted at two transmission substations confirmed that the proposed method detects PD activity at discharge magnitudes as low as 150 pC without requiring transformer de-energisation. The approach offers a cost-effective complement to conventional electrical PD measurement, particularly for online monitoring where electrical coupling presents practical difficulties.

title: Dielectric response analysis for moisture assessment in power transformer insulation
abstract: Moisture contamination in cellulose-based transformer insulation is a primary driver of accelerated ageing and reduced dielectric withstand capability. This paper evaluates the use of frequency-domain dielectric spectroscopy (FDS) and return voltage measurement (RVM) as complementary diagnostic tools for quantifying moisture content in oil-paper insulation systems. A series of controlled laboratory experiments was conducted on model insulation assemblies with moisture concentrations ranging from 0.5 % to 4.5 % by dry weight of cellulose, stored in transformer oil with varying degrees of oxidation. Measured dielectric response curves were fitted to an extended Debye model, and the resulting parameters were correlated with gravimetrically determined moisture content using regression analysis. The influence of oil conductivity on the dielectric response was isolated and quantified, revealing that failure to account for oil condition leads to systematic overestimation of insulation moisture content by 30–60 % in aged transformers. Correction algorithms are proposed and validated against a set of field measurements from transformers with known service histories. The study provides practical guidance for utilities applying FDS diagnostics and highlights the importance of concurrent oil characterisation when interpreting dielectric response data.

title: Lightning impulse withstand characteristics of cast resin distribution transformers
abstract: Cast resin dry-type transformers are increasingly deployed in distribution networks due to their environmental safety and suitability for indoor installation. However, their behaviour under lightning impulse voltage stress differs substantially from that of oil-immersed designs, and standardised withstand levels may not fully reflect the insulation coordination challenges encountered in medium-voltage distribution systems. This paper reports systematic lightning impulse testing of cast resin distribution transformers rated 6 kV to 20 kV, conducted in accordance with IEC 60076-3 but extended to include a statistical series of reduced and full impulse shots. Failure analysis of specimens that sustained breakdown reveals the characteristic treeing patterns within epoxy resin and at the resin-conductor interface, which are distinct from those observed in oil-paper systems. A probabilistic breakdown model parameterised from the experimental data is presented, enabling improved insulation coordination margins for distribution network designers. The influence of temperature on impulse breakdown strength is also characterised across the range −25 °C to +80 °C. The results inform recommendations for enhanced testing protocols applicable to cast resin transformers installed in climatically demanding environments such as those found in the Pannonian region.

title: Condition-based maintenance strategies for aged power transformer fleets: a decision framework
abstract: Utilities operating large fleets of power transformers face mounting pressure to optimise maintenance expenditure while managing increasing insulation age risk. This paper proposes a structured decision framework for condition-based maintenance (CBM) of power transformers, integrating multi-parameter diagnostic data into a risk-ranked asset health index. Input parameters include dissolved gas analysis, furfural content, degree of polymerisation estimates, partial discharge measurements, and load history, each weighted according to their relative contribution to the probability of insulation failure as established from long-term field data. The framework employs a fuzzy logic inference engine to handle the inherent uncertainty in transformer condition assessment and produces a prioritised maintenance schedule expressed as probability of failure within a five-year horizon. Case studies from three regional distribution utilities are presented, demonstrating that application of the framework reduced unplanned transformer outages by 22 % over a three-year pilot period compared with time-based maintenance schedules. Economic analysis confirms that CBM adoption yields a net present value benefit of approximately 15 % over a twenty-year asset management horizon. The framework is designed for practical deployment without requiring specialist data science expertise, making it accessible to utility engineers responsible for asset management decisions.

title: Long-term behaviour of mineral insulating oil under operational stress in 110 kV autotransformers
abstract: Mineral insulating oil serves dual functions as a dielectric medium and cooling agent in power transformers, and its degradation over time directly affects insulation integrity. This paper presents a longitudinal study of oil quality evolution in a population of thirty-one 110 kV autotransformers operated continuously over periods ranging from twelve to thirty-five years. Oil samples were collected at biannual intervals and characterised for dielectric breakdown voltage, acidity number, interfacial tension, colour index, water content, and dissolved gas composition. Statistical analysis of the resulting time-series data reveals that oxidation inhibitor depletion follows a predictable exponential decay that correlates strongly with cumulative thermal load rather than calendar age alone. A threshold model for inhibitor refortification scheduling is derived and compared with current industry practice based on fixed interval oil reclamation. The study identifies transformer designs with inadequate nitrogen blanketing as exhibiting significantly accelerated oil deterioration, contributing to premature insulation ageing in the solid cellulose components. The findings have direct implications for oil maintenance scheduling policies and support the case for continuous online oil quality monitoring as a cost-effective supplement to periodic laboratory sampling.

title: Overvoltage protection coordination in high-voltage substations: case studies from the Serbian transmission network
abstract: Effective overvoltage protection is fundamental to the long-term preservation of transformer insulation in transmission substations. This paper examines protection coordination between metal oxide surge arresters, transformer insulation withstand levels, and protection relay settings at six 220 kV and 400 kV substations in the Serbian transmission network. Field measurements of switching overvoltages were recorded using calibrated capacitive voltage dividers during planned switching operations and compared with prospective overvoltage levels calculated using electromagnetic transient simulation. Discrepancies between simulated and measured peak voltages are attributed to network topology changes that occurred after the original protection coordination studies were performed, highlighting the need for periodic re-evaluation of protection schemes as networks evolve. Arrester energy absorption duties are recalculated for the current network configuration, and three substations are identified as carrying arrester ratings that no longer provide adequate safety margins. Remedial recommendations are formulated, including arrester replacement specifications and modifications to switching procedures that reduce prospective switching surge amplitudes. The paper demonstrates the practical value of combining field measurement campaigns with updated simulation models as a routine element of high-voltage asset management programmes.

title: Effect of Molecular Weight Distribution of Polymethacrylate Viscosity-Index Modifiers on the Low-Temperature Flow Behaviour of PAO-Based Gear Oils
abstract: This study examined how variations in the molecular weight distribution (MWD) of polymethacrylate (PMA) viscosity-index (VI) modifiers affect the rheological properties of polyalphaolefin (PAO-6) base oils at sub-zero temperatures. Three commercial PMA grades with weight-average molecular weights of 85 kDa, 120 kDa, and 210 kDa were blended into PAO-6 at treat rates of 1.5, 3.0, and 5.0 wt%. Dynamic viscosity was measured over the range −40 °C to 100 °C using a cone-plate rheometer. The MWD breadth, characterised by the polydispersity index, was found to correlate more strongly with low-temperature viscosity retention than did Mw alone. The 120 kDa grade with a polydispersity index of 2.1 yielded a VI improvement of 38 units while maintaining kinematic viscosity below 3 200 mPa·s at −30 °C, meeting ISO VG 220 cold-cranking limits. Blends containing the 210 kDa modifier showed gel-like behaviour below −25 °C, rendering them unsuitable for axle-gear service. The results provide formulation guidelines for selecting PMA treat rates under low-temperature constraints.

title: Oxidative Degradation Kinetics of Fully Synthetic Wind-Turbine Gear Oils: A Pressure Differential Scanning Calorimetry Study
abstract: Pressure differential scanning calorimetry (PDSC) was used to assess the oxidative induction times (OIT) of five commercially formulated fully synthetic gear oils intended for wind-turbine gearbox service. Measurements were conducted at oxygen pressures of 500 kPa and 700 kPa and at isothermal temperatures between 140 °C and 180 °C. Activation energies for the oxidative degradation pathway were derived using the Arrhenius relationship from isothermal OIT data; values ranged from 88 to 124 kJ·mol⁻¹ across the five oils. Three oils used hindered-phenol antioxidant packages; two used aminic inhibitors. Aminic-type antioxidants consistently provided higher OIT values at elevated temperatures but exhibited non-linear depletion above 170 °C, suggesting synergistic breakdown with the base stock. The derived kinetic parameters were validated against a parallel rotating-bomb oxidation test (RBOT) conducted under identical temperature conditions. Good agreement (R² = 0.91) between PDSC-derived lifetimes and RBOT results supports PDSC as a rapid screening method for gear-oil reformulation work.

title: Elastohydrodynamic Film-Thickness Behaviour of Estolide-Based Gear Oils at Elevated Temperatures Measured by Optical Interferometry
abstract: Estolides derived from oleic acid represent a renewable alternative to mineral and PAO gear-oil base stocks. This study reports central and minimum film thicknesses for three experimental estolide fluids and a PAO-6 reference measured using the optical interferometry technique on a ball-on-disc elastohydrodynamic (EHD) rig under fully flooded, isothermal conditions at 40, 60, 80, and 100 °C. Entrainment speeds ranged from 0.02 to 2.0 m·s⁻¹ at a Hertzian contact pressure of 0.7 GPa. The pressure–viscosity coefficients of the estolides, obtained by fitting Hamrock–Dowson predictions to measured film thicknesses, ranged from 12.6 to 16.1 GPa⁻¹ at 40 °C, compared to 20.3 GPa⁻¹ for PAO-6. Despite lower pressure–viscosity coefficients, two estolide fluids maintained minimum film thicknesses within 15% of the PAO-6 reference at 80 °C owing to higher bulk viscosities. Thermal-thinning effects became significant above 1.0 m·s⁻¹, reducing minimum film thickness by up to 30% relative to isothermal predictions. The findings suggest estolides are viable candidates for medium-duty enclosed-gear applications.

title: Thermal Degradation Products of Trimethylolpropane Trioleate in Synthetic Gear Oil Formulations Identified by GC-MS and FTIR
abstract: Trimethylolpropane trioleate (TMPTO) is widely used as a boundary-lubricity improver and co-base-stock in synthetic gear oils. This study characterised the thermal degradation products of TMPTO after ageing at 150, 170, and 190 °C for durations of 24, 72, and 168 hours under nitrogen and air atmospheres. GC-MS analysis of the aged samples identified sixteen distinct degradation compounds, including short-chain aldehydes, dicarboxylic acids, and lactones. Formation of malonaldehyde and nonanal was confirmed at temperatures above 170 °C in air, with concentrations reaching 430 mg·kg⁻¹ after 168 hours. FTIR spectra showed increasing carbonyl absorption at 1 710 cm⁻¹ and a diminishing ester carbonyl band at 1 735 cm⁻¹ with ageing time, providing a semi-quantitative degradation index. Viscosity increase in air-aged samples at 190 °C exceeded 28% after 72 hours due to oxidative polymerisation. The identified degradation pathways are discussed with reference to implications for antioxidant additive depletion and deposit formation on gear surfaces.

title: Effect of Graphene Oxide Nanoadditive Concentration on the Tribological Performance of a PAO-Based Wind-Turbine Gear Oil
abstract: Graphene oxide (GO) nanosheets were dispersed in a PAO-6 base oil at concentrations of 0.01, 0.05, 0.10, and 0.25 wt% using a combination of probe sonication and oleylamine surface functionalisation to prevent agglomeration. Dispersion stability was confirmed by dynamic light scattering over 30 days; the 0.05 wt% sample maintained a mean hydrodynamic size of 320 nm without precipitation. Tribological evaluation on a ball-on-disc rig at 1.0 GPa, 0.1 m·s⁻¹, and 60 °C showed that 0.05 wt% GO reduced the friction coefficient from 0.112 (base oil alone) to 0.081 and reduced wear volume by 43%. Concentrations above 0.10 wt% produced increased wear, attributed to agglomerate abrasion confirmed by SEM imaging of wear scars. Raman spectroscopy of the worn contact area revealed characteristic D and G bands of GO, consistent with a protective carbonaceous tribofilm. PDSC testing of the GO-containing blends confirmed no significant change in oxidative induction time relative to the base oil, indicating compatibility with the existing antioxidant package.

title: Evaluating CNN Architectures for Character-Level Recognition on Handwritten Yugoslav Cadastral Records
abstract: Historic cadastral documents from the former Yugoslav administrative system combine printed headers with handwritten numeric entries and often suffer from water damage and mechanical wear. We assembled a dataset of 6,200 character patches extracted from 310 cadastral folio pages held by the Republic Geodetic Authority, covering 47 distinct character classes including digits and Latin diacritics. Four convolutional architectures of increasing depth (2, 4, 6, and 8 convolutional layers) were trained from random initialisation and compared on recognition accuracy and inference speed. The six-layer network achieved the best trade-off, reaching 91.7% top-1 accuracy on the held-out test split. Error analysis showed that the most frequent confusions occurred between visually similar digit pairs (1/7, 3/8) and were concentrated in the highest-damage quartile of pages. We discuss implications for active data collection strategies targeting low-confidence regions.

title: Transfer Learning from Natural Image Datasets for Low-Resource Document OCR: A Systematic Comparison
abstract: When annotated document data is scarce, practitioners commonly initialise OCR convolutional models with weights from large natural image classification tasks. We systematically compare five initialisation strategies—random, ImageNet-pretrained AlexNet, VGG-16, ResNet-50, and a self-supervised contrastive model trained on unlabelled document scans—across four low-resource document domains: 19th-century Serbian newspapers, printed tax forms, faded handwritten ledgers, and typewritten wartime correspondence. Each domain provides only 500 annotated text lines for fine-tuning. Results show that contrastive pretraining on unlabelled document data outperforms ImageNet initialisation by 3.1 to 6.8 percentage points in character error rate across domains, with the largest gains on the typewritten corpus. ResNet-50 initialisation narrows the gap when fine-tuning exceeds 1,000 samples. The paper provides practitioner guidelines for choosing pretraining strategies under different data availability scenarios.

title: Table Structure Recognition in Degraded Financial Statements Using Hybrid CNN-CRF Models
abstract: Extracting tabular data from scanned financial statements requires reliable detection of row and column boundaries even when ruling lines are faint, broken, or absent. We frame table structure recognition as a pixel-labelling problem and train a hybrid model combining a convolutional encoder with a conditional random field output layer on 1,840 annotated page images drawn from the SerbBankScan-2018 corpus and a set of Romanian annual reports. The CRF encourages spatial consistency in predicted cell boundaries. On a held-out test set, the model achieves a cell-level F1 score of 82.6%, compared to 74.1% for a U-Net baseline without CRF. We report ablation results for CRF connectivity radius and training data mixture ratio. Qualitative analysis shows the main failure mode is multi-row merged cells, which account for 61% of false negatives.

title: Effect of Scan Resolution and JPEG Compression on OCR Accuracy for Structured Financial Forms
abstract: Financial document digitisation workflows often apply lossy compression and resolution downsampling to reduce storage costs. We conduct a factorial experiment measuring the combined effect of five resolution levels (100–300 dpi) and six JPEG quality settings (30–100) on character error rate and field-level extraction accuracy for 600 standardised Serbian tax forms. OCR is performed using both an off-the-shelf engine (Tesseract 5.0) and a domain-fine-tuned CRNN. Results show that resolution has a stronger main effect than compression quality: dropping from 300 to 150 dpi increases CRNN character error rate from 2.1% to 9.4%, while reducing JPEG quality from 100 to 50 at 300 dpi increases it only to 3.3%. Interactions between the two factors are significant only at resolutions below 150 dpi. We provide recommended operating thresholds for financial document archiving pipelines.

title: End-to-End Key-Value Extraction from Serbian Company Balance Sheets Using Transformer-Augmented OCR
abstract: Balance sheets follow a legally standardised structure in Serbian corporate reporting but exhibit large typographic variation between companies and fiscal years. We build an end-to-end pipeline that combines a domain-pretrained CRNN for transcription with a LayoutLM-style transformer that jointly attends over visual, positional, and textual features to assign recognised tokens to semantic fields (e.g. total assets, net profit, equity). Training uses 3,200 annotated balance sheet pages from the Business Registers Agency open data portal. On a held-out set of 400 pages, field-level extraction accuracy reaches 91.3% for printed documents and 84.7% for documents containing rubber-stamp annotations that partially occlude numeric values. Error rate is strongly correlated with page-level binarisation quality (Pearson r = 0.71). We release model weights and inference code.

title: Synthetic Data Augmentation for Low-Contrast Financial OCR: Rendering Pipeline and Evaluation
abstract: Collecting and annotating real degraded financial documents is time-consuming and may raise data-privacy concerns. We describe SynthFin, a rendering pipeline that generates photorealistic synthetic page images by compositing text layers with background textures sampled from a library of 2,200 scanned blank paper patches, then applying a chain of degradation operators: ink bleed, fading, Gaussian blur, random ruled-line suppression, and digital shadow gradients. We generate 120,000 synthetic line images covering Serbian, Croatian, and Bosnian financial form templates and use them to augment training data for a CRNN OCR model. Adding synthetic data reduces character error rate on real degraded test documents from 6.1% to 3.9% when the real labelled training set is limited to 500 examples, and provides no significant improvement beyond 4,000 real examples. The rendering pipeline and the paper texture library are made publicly available.

title: Release of deoxynivalenol from deoxynivalenol-3-glucoside during static in vitro gastrointestinal digestion of wheat bread
abstract: Deoxynivalenol-3-glucoside (DON-3G) is a plant-conjugated masked mycotoxin frequently detected in wheat and wheat-based products. Its fate during gastrointestinal passage is relevant to human exposure assessment but remains poorly characterised in food matrices. In this study, wheat bread spiked at three DON-3G concentration levels (50, 200, and 500 µg/kg) was subjected to a static in vitro digestion procedure following the standardised INFOGEST 2.0 protocol. Digestates from the oral, gastric, and small-intestinal phases were collected and analysed by HPLC-MS/MS for DON-3G and its hydrolysis product DON. Results showed that DON-3G remained largely intact through the oral and gastric phases, with less than 8% hydrolysis observed. In the small-intestinal phase, enzymatic activity led to release of free DON reaching 31–44% of the initial DON-3G content, depending on the concentration level tested. The data indicate that small-intestinal conditions, rather than gastric acidity alone, are the primary site of masked mycotoxin hydrolysis in this matrix. These findings suggest that exposure estimates based solely on DON analysis may underestimate total bioaccessible DON in bread consumers by up to one-third.

title: Comparison of bioaccessibility of zearalenone and zearalenone-14-glucoside in maize porridge using the INFOGEST static digestion model
abstract: Zearalenone (ZEN) and its masked form zearalenone-14-glucoside (ZEN-14G) co-occur in maize grain, yet dietary exposure assessments typically consider only the parent mycotoxin. This study compared the bioaccessibility of ZEN and ZEN-14G in maize porridge prepared from naturally contaminated grain (ZEN: 112 µg/kg, ZEN-14G: 64 µg/kg as determined by HPLC-MS/MS). The INFOGEST 2.0 static digestion protocol was applied, and digestates were extracted by solid-phase extraction prior to quantification. ZEN bioaccessibility reached 78% in the small-intestinal fraction, while ZEN-14G showed 52% conversion to ZEN and free ZEN-14G combined under the same conditions. Total molar bioaccessibility of ZEN equivalents from the combined mycotoxin load was 18% higher than would be predicted from ZEN analysis alone. Interestingly, the reducing conditions of the colonic simulation step did not substantially alter the ZEN:ZEN-14G ratio, suggesting that the small intestine is the critical compartment. Matrix effects from maize starch gelatinisation were assessed by comparing cooked and uncooked porridge and found to reduce ZEN bioaccessibility by approximately 12%. Results are discussed in the context of current tolerable daily intake values set by the European Food Safety Authority.

title: Effect of household cooking on the distribution of deoxynivalenol and its acetylated forms in pasta before and after the INFOGEST digestion
abstract: Acetylated derivatives of deoxynivalenol, 3-acetyl-DON (3-ADON) and 15-acetyl-DON (15-ADON), are regulated contaminants in EU legislation and are predominantly found in durum wheat and pasta products. This study examined how standard domestic cooking of pasta (boiling in water, 1:10 w/v, 10 min) affects the concentration and distribution of DON, 3-ADON, and 15-ADON in the pasta and cooking water, and subsequently how in vitro digestion transforms these forms. Spiked durum wheat semolina pasta was used at three fortification levels. After cooking, 22–38% of total trichothecene content migrated to cooking water, with 3-ADON showing preferential leaching compared with DON. Cooked pasta was then subjected to INFOGEST 2.0 static digestion. Both 3-ADON and 15-ADON showed partial deacetylation to DON during the small-intestinal phase, with conversion rates of 17% and 26%, respectively, at physiological enzyme concentrations. The combined effect of cooking and digestion altered the relative proportions of DON equivalents substantially compared with the unprocessed matrix. Data were used to recalculate estimated dietary exposure for a pasta-consuming adult population segment using conservative and mean consumption figures from the EFSA FoodEx2 database.

title: Epithelial transport of free and conjugated enniatin B across Caco-2 cell monolayers after simulated digestion
abstract: Enniatins are emerging Fusarium mycotoxins detected in small cereals and increasingly in cereal-based snack foods. Limited data exist on whether conjugated forms of enniatins, identified in recent metabolomics surveys, differ from the parent compound in their intestinal transport characteristics. This preliminary study employed a two-stage approach: enniatin B (ENN B) and its hydroxylated conjugate (hydroxy-ENN B) were subjected to the INFOGEST gastric and small-intestinal phases at concentrations of 1 and 5 µM, and the resulting digestion fractions were applied to differentiated Caco-2 monolayers (21-day post-seeding) at 37 °C for 120 minutes. Transepithelial transport was quantified by HPLC-MS/MS in apical and basolateral compartments. Apparent permeability coefficients (Papp) for ENN B averaged 14.2 × 10⁻⁶ cm/s, consistent with high passive permeability. Hydroxy-ENN B showed a Papp of 6.8 × 10⁻⁶ cm/s, indicating reduced but still substantial transport. Monolayer integrity was monitored by transepithelial electrical resistance; no cytotoxic disruption was observed at the concentrations tested. These data are preliminary due to the limited number of biological replicates (n = 3) and the use of spiked rather than naturally occurring conjugates; further validation with authentic standards is required.

title: Teacher beliefs about working memory and their influence on numeracy instruction practices in Vojvodina primary schools
abstract: Despite a substantial research literature on working memory and mathematics learning, relatively little is known about whether primary school teachers are aware of these findings and whether their beliefs shape instructional choices. This study used a mixed-methods design combining a structured questionnaire (n = 63 teachers from Hungarian-language primary schools across Vojvodina) with semi-structured interviews conducted with a subsample of twelve teachers. Quantitative items measured knowledge of working memory concepts and self-reported instructional practices such as chunking task sequences, avoiding dual-channel overload, and providing written task records. Only 31% of respondents could correctly identify a definition of working memory, yet 74% reported using practice strategies consistent with cognitive load principles, suggesting implicit rather than explicit knowledge. Interview data revealed that teachers attributed these practices to classroom experience rather than formal training. Teachers in urban schools reported slightly more deliberate use of load-reducing strategies than rural counterparts, though sample sizes preclude firm conclusions. Implications for pre-service and in-service teacher education curricula are discussed.

title: Cryoprotectant composition and cooling rate effects on viability recovery of industrially relevant Lactobacillus strains
abstract: Four cryoprotectant formulations (10% glycerol, 10% dimethyl sulfoxide, 5% glycerol + 5% skim milk, and 15% trehalose) were tested across three Lactobacillus strains used in lactic acid fermentation at a regional dairy ingredients manufacturer. Samples were frozen at controlled rates of 1°C/min, 5°C/min, and uncontrolled plunge to −80°C. Recovery was assessed by plate count at 24 h and 7 days post-revival. The glycerol–skim milk combination at 1°C/min produced the highest mean recovery across strains (94.3 ± 2.1%), while DMSO at plunge cooling gave the lowest (61.7 ± 6.4%). Acidification activity (pH drop per hour at 37°C) was retained above 90% of pre-freeze values only in glycerol–skim milk stocks. Practical guidelines for seed-lot preparation in small-scale dairy fermentation facilities are proposed on the basis of these data.

title: Stability of antibiotic-free plasmid retention in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) under fed-batch conditions: influence of specific growth rate
abstract: Plasmid retention in a recombinant Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) strain carrying a pET-based expression vector was monitored over 40-hour fed-batch cultivations at three different specific growth rates (0.10, 0.20, and 0.35 h⁻¹) without antibiotic selection pressure. Samples were taken every four hours and plated on selective and non-selective media to calculate plasmid retention fraction. At µ = 0.10 h⁻¹, retention remained above 92% throughout; at µ = 0.35 h⁻¹, retention fell below 70% after 28 hours. Flow cytometry using a chromosomally integrated GFP marker confirmed plasmid-free segregant fractions independently of plating. Volumetric productivity of the target protein (a recombinant chitinase) tracked plasmid retention closely. A simple population balance model was parameterised to the data and predicts retention behaviour within ±8% across the growth rate range tested.

title: Assessment of phenotypic heterogeneity within a Corynebacterium glutamicum lysine production strain after long-term glycerol stock storage
abstract: A commercial Corynebacterium glutamicum strain used in lysine production was revived from glycerol stocks stored at −80°C for periods of 1, 3, 5, and 8 years. After standardised revival and single-passage propagation, 200 colonies per stock age were characterised for growth rate on minimal medium, lysine secretion by HPLC, and cell morphology. Coefficient of variation in lysine titre per colony increased from 9% (1-year stocks) to 24% (8-year stocks). Mean titre per colony decreased by 11% over 8 years. Whole-genome sequencing of three low-titre and three high-titre colonies from each cohort identified no fixed mutations but showed varying proportions of a frameshift variant in the lysC gene encoding aspartate kinase. The finding indicates that long storage does not eliminate heterogeneity and that periodic single-colony isolation for stock renewal is warranted at intervals shorter than 5 years.

title: Root-cause analysis of an unexplained yield drop in a Streptomyces avermitilis avermectin fermentation: a case study from a regional pharmaceutical manufacturer
abstract: A pharmaceutical manufacturer operating a 50 m³ avermectin fermentation reported a 25–30% reduction in avermectin B1a titre over eight production campaigns without process parameter deviations. A structured root-cause investigation was conducted combining seed-lot genotyping by RAPD-PCR and MLST, fermentation broth metabolomics (LC-QTOF, 187 detected metabolites), and retrospective analysis of raw material certificates of analysis. Metabolomic comparison of high-yield and low-yield campaign broths at 120 h identified a consistent depletion of propionate and butyrate precursors in the low-yield group, tracing to a change in soybean meal supplier that altered the fatty acid profile of the medium. Seed-lot genotyping revealed no mutation accumulation. Supplementation with 0.4 g/L sodium propionate in subsequent validation runs restored titre to historical mean within two campaigns. This case illustrates that raw material variation, not strain instability, can masquerade as strain degeneration.

title: Quantitative metabolomics of submerged Bacillus licheniformis α-amylase fermentation at pilot scale: batch-to-batch reproducibility indicators
abstract: Twelve consecutive 200 L pilot-scale batches of Bacillus licheniformis NRRL B-1365 were operated under nominally identical conditions to establish metabolic reproducibility benchmarks for α-amylase production. Broth samples at 24, 48, 72, and 96 h were analysed by LC-QTOF after methanol–water extraction. Of 214 assigned metabolite features, 38 showed inter-batch relative standard deviation below 15% and were designated candidate process fingerprint markers. Valine, leucine, and 2-oxoglutarate concentrations at 48 h were the strongest predictors of final α-amylase activity (R² = 0.81 in partial least-squares regression). Between-batch coefficient of variation in final titre was 9.3%, attributed primarily to dissolved oxygen trajectory differences resulting from impeller wear. The 38-metabolite fingerprint provides a practical in-process monitoring panel for detecting off-trajectory batches before harvest.

title: Comparison of RAPD-PCR, AFLP, and whole-genome SNP calling for routine strain identity verification in industrial fermentation facilities
abstract: Three genotyping methods were benchmarked for their ability to discriminate between a production strain and spontaneous variants arising during fermentation of Bacillus subtilis for surfactin production. Thirty isolates from production seed banks at three facilities, along with 12 laboratory-generated spontaneous variants, were characterised. RAPD-PCR resolved clusters at the facility level but failed to separate closely related spontaneous variants in 4 of 12 cases. AFLP provided higher resolution but required two working days per sample set. Whole-genome SNP calling from Illumina short reads correctly identified all variants and provided information on the location and predicted functional impact of mutations. Sequencing cost per isolate was estimated at €38 in 2017 prices in a batch of 24 samples, already competitive with AFLP for batches above 16 isolates. Practical recommendations for selecting the appropriate method based on facility throughput and technical capacity are provided.

title: Seed-lot management practices in Eastern European fermentation industries: a survey of 34 facilities
abstract: A structured questionnaire survey of 34 fermentation facilities in Serbia, Hungary, Romania, and Bulgaria was conducted to document current seed-lot management practices. Facilities included enzyme producers, amino acid manufacturers, probiotic producers, and antibiotic manufacturers. Questions addressed cryopreservation methods, revival and passaging protocols, genotypic verification practices, frequency of stock renewal, and documentation systems. Only 41% of facilities performed any genotypic verification on revived working cell banks. Nineteen percent used no controlled-rate freezing. Median storage duration before replacement was 6.4 years, with high inter-facility variance. Facilities with ISO 9001 certification showed significantly better documentation practices but not significantly better technical protocols. The survey identifies specific practice gaps and proposes a minimum standard protocol set compatible with the resource constraints of small and medium-sized fermentation enterprises in the region.

title: Metabolomic signatures associated with phage contamination events in Lactococcus lactis cheesemaking fermentations
abstract: Six confirmed bacteriophage contamination events in a commercial Lactococcus lactis NZ9000 cheesemaking fermentation were retrospectively compared with 18 unaffected batches using archived broth samples from 4 h and 8 h post-inoculation. LC-QTOF metabolomics identified 22 metabolite features discriminating contaminated from unaffected batches at 4 h, before any detectable acidification lag was measurable by pH probe. Nucleotide pool metabolites (adenine, hypoxanthine, inosine) were consistently elevated in contaminated batches, consistent with phage-induced cell lysis releasing nucleic acid degradation products. A classification model built on seven metabolite ratios correctly assigned 23 of 24 batches in leave-one-out cross-validation. The study suggests that metabolomics-based early-warning monitoring could provide actionable contamination alerts one to two hours earlier than conventional pH-based detection.

title: Effect of dissolved oxygen setpoint transitions on metabolic state and genomic mutation frequency in a long-running Corynebacterium glutamicum glutamic acid fermentation
abstract: A 120-hour fed-batch fermentation of Corynebacterium glutamicum ATCC 13032 for glutamic acid production was operated with deliberate dissolved oxygen (DO) setpoint transitions (30%, 50%, and 70% air saturation, each held for 40 hours) to examine the effect of oxygen availability on both productivity and mutation accumulation. Glutamic acid titre was highest at 50% DO (48.3 g/L versus 41.1 g/L at 30% and 43.7 g/L at 70%). Whole-genome sequencing of 96 single colonies harvested from each DO phase identified mutation frequencies of 3.1 × 10⁻⁴, 1.8 × 10⁻⁴, and 5.6 × 10⁻⁴ mutations per genome per generation at 30%, 50%, and 70% DO respectively, with oxidative stress response genes overrepresented among mutations at 70% DO. The results caution against high-DO operation strategies adopted for productivity reasons without parallel strain stability monitoring.

title: Benchmarking untargeted and targeted metabolomics extraction protocols for spent fermentation broths of gram-positive bacteria
abstract: Extraction efficiency for intracellular and extracellular metabolomics was compared across five protocols applied to spent broths from three gram-positive production organisms (Bacillus subtilis, Lactobacillus plantarum, and Corynebacterium glutamicum): methanol quench with cold water wash, acetonitrile precipitation, boiling ethanol, alkaline hydrolysis, and a commercial metabolomics kit. Metabolite recovery was assessed for 40 reference compounds spanning amino acids, organic acids, nucleotides, and sugar phosphates spiked at two concentrations. Boiling ethanol performed best for Bacillus and Corynebacterium (mean recovery 84% and 88%), while cold methanol–water was superior for Lactobacillus (78%) owing to the higher content of cell-wall-bound metabolites released under gentler conditions. Repeatability across three operators and two LC-QTOF instruments was assessed by coefficient of variation; 31 of 40 reference compounds showed CV below 12% on the recommended protocols. Practical extraction decision trees for each organism class are provided.

title: Phenotypic and transcriptomic characterisation of a low-yield Bacillus subtilis isolate recovered from a degraded working cell bank
abstract: A low-yield variant of Bacillus subtilis ATCC 21332 was isolated from a working cell bank that had undergone 11 uncontrolled freeze–thaw cycles at a contract fermentation facility. The variant produced 38% less surfactin than the reference stock as measured by HPLC-ELSD. Whole-genome sequencing identified a single missense mutation in comA, encoding a response regulator of the competence and surfactin biosynthesis quorum-sensing pathway. RNA-seq comparing the variant with a revived reference stock at mid-exponential phase (OD600 = 2.1) revealed 214 differentially expressed genes (fold change > 2, adjusted p < 0.05), with downregulation concentrated in the srfAA–srfAD surfactin synthetase operon and accessory sigma factors. The study provides a mechanistic account of how a single mutation arising during improper cell bank storage translates into major productivity loss, and supports transcriptomic profiling as a diagnostic complement to titre measurement in strain degeneration investigations.

title: Multi-batch metabolomic monitoring as a diagnostic framework for production yield stability in industrial submerged fermentation: principles and a worked example with β-glucanase
abstract: This book chapter presents a systematic framework for using multi-batch metabolomic profiling to distinguish strain-based from process-based causes of yield instability in submerged bacterial fermentation. The framework is structured in four phases: baseline fingerprinting across a minimum of eight representative batches, statistical control charting of key metabolite ratios, principal component monitoring for trajectory deviation, and targeted hypothesis testing for identified anomalies. A worked example using a Bacillus licheniformis β-glucanase fermentation across 22 consecutive batches at a pilot facility is used throughout. In the example, a statistically significant metabolite shift at batch 14 was traced to a medium preparation change rather than strain mutation, demonstrating the discriminatory power of the framework. Data handling procedures, minimum detectable effect sizes, and the number of metabolites required for reliable discrimination are discussed. The chapter is aimed at process microbiologists and bioprocess engineers with access to LC-MS instrumentation.

title: Predicting Course Dropout from Early Moodle Activity Logs Using Logistic Regression
abstract: This study examined whether student dropout in an introductory programming course could be predicted from the first three weeks of Moodle activity logs. Log data from 412 students enrolled over two academic years were used. Features included weekly login frequency, time-on-task estimates derived from session timestamps, and quiz attempt counts. A logistic regression model trained on weeks one to three achieved an AUC of 0.71 on a held-out semester cohort, outperforming a baseline model using only prior academic grades (AUC 0.58). Precision at a 30 % recall threshold was sufficient to support early adviser notification. The study also identified that late-evening access patterns in week two were among the strongest predictors of dropout, a finding discussed in relation to work-study conflicts common among part-time students at the faculty. Limitations regarding class imbalance and cross-course generalisability are addressed.

title: Temporal Patterns in Student Engagement: A Sequence Clustering Approach
abstract: Engagement patterns in online course materials were analysed using sequence clustering applied to week-level activity vectors from 1,840 students across six undergraduate courses. Each student's 14-week activity profile was encoded as a categorical sequence over four engagement states (high, moderate, low, absent) derived by discretising composite activity scores. Sequences were clustered using a k-medoids procedure with a dynamic time warping distance metric. Five robust clusters emerged, labelled by dominant trajectory shape: consistently active, late starters, early decliners, sporadic engagers, and persistently absent. Cluster membership at week four was a significant predictor of final examination grade in a subsequent multinomial regression (pseudo-R² = 0.34). The paper discusses how cluster assignments could feed into adaptive course notifications. Data were drawn from three consecutive academic years (2010–2013) at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Novi Sad.

title: Applying Hidden Markov Models to Detect Shifts in Student Learning States from Clickstream Data
abstract: Hidden Markov models (HMMs) were fitted to weekly clickstream summaries of 620 students enrolled in a statistics course over one academic year, with the aim of identifying latent learning states and their transition dynamics. Observations consisted of five aggregated behavioural features per week: resource views, forum posts, quiz attempts, assignment submissions, and session duration. A three-state HMM, selected by BIC, was estimated using the Baum–Welch algorithm. The inferred states corresponded interpretably to disengaged, routine, and intensive study behaviours. Transition matrices indicated that recovery from the disengaged state became increasingly improbable after week seven. Students who spent more than four consecutive weeks in the disengaged state had a pass rate of 23 %, versus 81 % for those who did not. The paper examines model stability across two replication cohorts and discusses annotation validity through think-aloud interviews with a subsample of 18 students.

title: Cross-Course Generalisation of Clickstream-Based Performance Predictors: An Empirical Evaluation
abstract: Most clickstream-based prediction models are trained and tested within a single course, leaving their cross-course generalisability unclear. This paper reports a systematic evaluation in which six predictive models (logistic regression, random forest, gradient-boosted trees, an LSTM, a naive Bayes baseline, and a rules-based expert model) were trained on data from one course and evaluated on 11 other courses at the Faculty of Sciences. Data covered 3,100 unique students and 14 courses over three academic years. AUC values dropped by an average of 0.11 when models were applied without retraining to new courses, but transfer performance recovered to within 0.04 of in-course performance after fine-tuning on as few as 50 labelled instances from the target course. Feature importance was markedly inconsistent across courses, with quiz-attempt features being the most portable. The paper provides recommendations for practitioners deploying predictive analytics in heterogeneous institutional contexts.

title: Longitudinal Latent Profile Analysis of Learning Behaviours Across a Three-Year Study Programme
abstract: Most learning analytics studies examine single courses; this paper follows 890 students through an entire three-year bachelor's programme, applying longitudinal latent profile analysis (LLPA) to semester-aggregated behavioural indicators derived from Moodle logs. Six behavioural indicators per semester were used: mean weekly logins, resource coverage ratio, discussion board participation, assessment completion timeliness, peer review engagement, and estimated reading time. LLPA identified four latent profiles that were stable in composition but varied in prevalence across years. Profile membership at the end of year one predicted programme completion with an accuracy of 74 % (balanced accuracy 0.69). Transitions between profiles were more common at the boundary between year one and year two, coinciding with a curriculum redesign. The paper discusses implications for longitudinal early warning systems and presents an online Shiny dashboard prototype used to communicate risk scores to academic advisers.

title: Evaluating Fairness Properties of Clickstream-Based Grade Prediction Models Across Student Demographic Groups
abstract: Predictive models in learning analytics risk encoding historical inequities if their accuracy varies systematically across demographic groups. This paper audits six previously published and three newly trained clickstream-based grade prediction models using a dataset of 5,600 students from two Serbian universities, with demographic variables including gender, whether the student is the first in their family to attend university, and regional origin. Equalised odds differences across gender exceeded 0.08 in four of nine models, driven primarily by differing patterns of after-hours access between groups rather than differential academic performance. First-generation students were identified as a higher-risk group by models at a rate 1.4 times that of continuing-generation students at the same actual grade distribution. Reweighting training instances by demographic group membership reduced equalised odds gaps to below 0.03 with less than 1 % loss in overall AUC. The paper calls for routine fairness reporting as part of learning analytics deployments.

title: Leaf wetness duration and grey mould incidence in pepper under white clover living mulch
abstract: A two-season field trial compared pepper grown in bare soil, mown white clover living mulch, and unmown white clover living mulch at a site near Sremska Mitrovica. Electronic leaf wetness sensors were mounted at three canopy heights (0.1, 0.3, and 0.5 m). Cumulative leaf wetness duration over the growing season was 23 % longer in the unmown mulch treatment relative to bare soil, whereas mown mulch increased duration by only 9 %. Botrytis cinerea incidence at harvest was 11.4 % in unmown mulch, 7.8 % in mown mulch, and 5.1 % in bare soil. Mulch mowing frequency was subsequently manipulated in a supplementary experiment, showing that a 10-day mowing cycle reduced leaf wetness duration almost to bare-soil levels without eliminating weed suppression benefits. Logistic regression confirmed that cumulative leaf wetness duration explained 68 % of the variance in grey mould incidence across plots.

title: Humidity profiles within lettuce canopies intercropped with dill at three row-spacing configurations
abstract: Lettuce and dill were sown in alternating strips of 1, 2, and 4 row-pairs per strip in replicated plots over two spring seasons. Aspirated hygrometers logged relative humidity at 5 cm intervals from soil surface to canopy top at 30-minute intervals. Canopy-interior relative humidity in the 1-row-pair configuration averaged 4.1 percentage points above ambient during the 10:00–14:00 h window, compared with 1.8 pp in the 4-row-pair configuration. Dew point deficit at the leaf surface, computed from measured leaf temperature and ambient humidity, dropped below 0.5 °C for significantly longer periods in narrow-strip designs. Downy mildew (Bremia lactucae) natural infection ratings correlated with cumulative hours of near-zero dew point deficit (r = 0.77, p < 0.01). The 4-row-pair design reduced downy mildew area under disease progress curve by 38 % relative to sole-crop lettuce controls.

title: Understorey irradiance and photosynthetic rate of zucchini intercropped with tall fenugreek at two strip widths
abstract: Zucchini (Cucurbita pepo var. cylindrica) and fenugreek were grown in 1.0 m and 2.0 m alternating strips over one growing season. Photosynthetic photon flux density was logged continuously at 0.4 m canopy height using calibrated GaAsP photodiodes. At 60 days after sowing, zucchini understorey irradiance in the 1.0 m strip was 34 % of open-sky values compared with 61 % in the 2.0 m strip. Leaf-level net photosynthesis measured by portable infrared gas analyser was reduced by 22 % in the 1.0 m design. Despite lower photosynthesis, zucchini fruit yield in the 1.0 m design was statistically equivalent to sole-crop yield, attributed to compensatory fruit-set duration extending three weeks beyond the sole-crop harvest window. These results complicate simple assumptions that radiation reduction under narrow-strip intercropping necessarily translates to proportional yield penalties.

title: Effect of grass-clover living mulch on near-surface air temperature and vapour pressure deficit in tomato rows under semi-arid conditions
abstract: Measurements were taken across three summer seasons at an experimental station characterised by a pronounced summer drought. Thermocouple arrays and capacitance humidity sensors were installed within and above tomato canopy rows in plots with and without a grass–clover living mulch at three distance classes from the mulch–tomato boundary (0–0.2 m, 0.2–0.5 m, 0.5–1.0 m). Afternoon vapour pressure deficit at the tomato leaf boundary layer was on average 0.31 kPa lower in the mulched treatment. Canopy air temperature during peak irradiance was reduced by 1.6 °C in mulched plots. Alternaria alternata incidence was paradoxically 14 % higher in mulched plots despite the lower vapour pressure deficit, interpreted as a result of prolonged morning dew retention on fruit surfaces adjacent to moist mulch. These findings highlight that disease-risk assessment must account for temporal distribution of wetness, not just mean humidity levels.

title: Living mulch species identity alters fungal spore deposition rates and powdery mildew development in field-grown cucumbers
abstract: Cucumber was grown in plots with four mulch treatments: bare soil, crimson clover, creeping thyme, and perennial ryegrass, across two seasons. Rotorod spore samplers positioned at three heights within cucumber canopies collected hourly samples assessed microscopically for Podosphaera xanthii conidia. Spore deposition at 0.3 m height was 22 % lower above creeping thyme than above bare soil, attributed to reduced convective air mixing near the soil surface measured by cup anemometers. Powdery mildew area under disease progress curves were 19, 27, and 41 % lower in crimson clover, ryegrass, and creeping thyme treatments respectively relative to bare soil, in order of decreasing canopy airflow reduction. Mulch identity, rather than mere presence of a mulch, emerged as a meaningful variable for disease management, with structural density of mulch canopy explaining more variance than mulch biomass.

title: Canopy humidity dynamics in onion–parsley strip intercrops: field measurements and implications for Stemphylium leaf blight management
abstract: Onion and parsley were arranged in four strip width treatments (0.5, 1.0, 1.5, and 2.0 m) in a split-plot design replicated four times over two growing seasons. Aspirated thermocouple psychrometers recorded canopy relative humidity at 15-minute intervals. The 0.5 m strip treatment maintained relative humidity more than 5 percentage points above ambient for an average of 4.2 h per day during June and July, compared with 1.3 h in the 2.0 m treatment. Stemphylium vesicarium natural infection severity in onion was highest in the 0.5 m design (29 % leaf area affected) and lowest in the 2.0 m design (11 %). A threshold analysis suggested that keeping daily cumulative above-ambient humidity duration below 2 h is associated with subeconomic disease levels under the tested conditions. A practical strip-width decision table is presented for practitioners.

title: Strip intercropping geometry and timing of fungicide application in late blight management of potato: a two-year field study
abstract: Potato was intercropped with spring barley in alternating strips of 2 m and 4 m at an experimental site in Bačka. Fungicide spray timing was triggered either by calendar schedule (every 10 days) or by a leaf wetness–temperature decision rule adapted from the Blitecast model. Strip intercrops received on average 1.4 fewer fungicide applications per season under decision-rule timing without significant increase in Phytophthora infestans AUDPC compared with the calendar schedule under sole-crop conditions. Canopy relative humidity in 2 m potato strips was 3.2 pp lower than in sole-crop potato during the critical tuber-initiation period. Yield was not significantly different between strip widths or spray timing regimes. The study demonstrates that microclimate modification by a cereal companion can extend fungicide spray intervals by approximately 8 days without disease penalty under the tested continental climate.

title: Dew formation dynamics on leaf surfaces in living-mulched vegetable beds: nocturnal energy balance measurements
abstract: Nocturnal energy balance was measured in three replicated plots per treatment (bare soil, white clover living mulch, buckwheat living mulch) beneath determinate tomato canopies over 35 clear nights during summer. Net radiometers, soil heat flux plates, and sonic anemometers provided inputs to a simplified nocturnal energy balance. Dew formation onset was on average 38 minutes earlier in mulched treatments, and total overnight dew accumulation on artificial leaf replicas was 0.18 mm in bare soil, 0.29 mm in white clover, and 0.25 mm in buckwheat plots. Dew evaporation time after sunrise was extended by 47 minutes in white clover compared with bare soil. Early-morning leaf wetness duration, rather than total dew amount, was the variable most strongly associated with Alternaria spore germination in concurrent in situ germination trials. The energy balance analysis attributes the delay to suppressed upward sensible heat flux from the mulch surface.

title: Statistical Baseline Modelling of Modbus/TCP Traffic in a Substation Automation Network
abstract: This paper describes the construction of per-register statistical baselines for Modbus/TCP traffic captured over six months on a live substation automation testbed. For each register address, empirical distributions of inter-request intervals, payload values, and function code sequences were estimated using kernel density estimation with a Gaussian kernel and bandwidth selected by cross-validation. A one-class detector based on Mahalanobis distance thresholding over a 20-feature vector was evaluated against 14 manually injected attack scenarios, including replay, coil-write injection, and scan sweeps. At a false positive rate of 0.5%, the detector achieved a true positive rate of 91.4% across all attack types. The paper also quantifies the effect of seasonal load variation on baseline drift and proposes a sliding-window recalibration schedule with a 72-hour update period that maintains detection performance without human intervention. Results are compared with a fixed-threshold rule-based baseline, which achieved 67% TPR at the same FPR. The testbed comprised three Siemens-compatible PLCs connected over a deterministic switched Ethernet fabric.

title: One-Class SVM for Detecting Anomalous DNP3 Command Sequences in Water Treatment Control Systems
abstract: One-class support vector machines (OC-SVM) were applied to detect anomalous DNP3 application-layer command sequences in a water treatment SCADA testbed. Feature vectors were constructed from 15-second sliding windows using n-gram frequency histograms of function code and object group pairs, yielding 128-dimensional vectors after principal component analysis retaining 95% of variance. The OC-SVM used an RBF kernel; the nu hyperparameter was swept from 0.01 to 0.20 and selected via leave-one-out cross-validation on a 90-day normal-operation capture (approximately 4.2 million packets). Attack scenarios—unauthorised control block writes, time-sync spoofing, and application-layer flooding—were injected during a separate 14-day test period. The detector achieved an F1 score of 0.87 for unseen attack types not represented during training. Computational overhead was measured at under 3% CPU utilisation on an ARM Cortex-A9 industrial gateway, supporting inline deployment feasibility.

title: Characterising Normal Behaviour in Industrial Ethernet Networks: A Long-Term Measurement Study
abstract: This measurement study presents a 12-month passive capture of traffic from four industrial sites—two discrete manufacturing lines, one water utility, and one district heating plant—totalling approximately 680 GB of raw packet data. The study characterises normal traffic behaviour through 22 statistical descriptors per flow, including coefficient of variation of inter-packet gaps, entropy of destination port distributions, and autocorrelation structure of payload-length time series. Results show that industrial Ethernet traffic exhibits strong periodicity at scales of seconds to hours, with Hurst parameter estimates between 0.61 and 0.79 across sites, indicating long-range dependence. The study documents characteristic differences between Modbus, EtherNet/IP, and proprietary vendor protocols and quantifies seasonal variation. The dataset and feature extraction code are described in sufficient detail to support reproducibility. Findings inform design choices for unsupervised detectors and highlight risks of training on short captures.

title: Isolation Forest Applied to ICS Protocol Traffic: Sensitivity to Contamination Fraction and Window Length
abstract: Isolation Forest was evaluated as a detector for ICS protocol traffic anomalies under controlled variation of two critical hyperparameters: the contamination fraction estimate (ranging from 0.001 to 0.10) and the sliding-window aggregation length (1 s to 300 s). Experiments used a publicly described Modbus/TCP dataset generated on the authors' testbed across five attack classes. Detection rate and false alarm rate were measured at each combination using a 5×2 nested cross-validation design. The contamination fraction had a stronger effect on precision than recall; a mismatch of one order of magnitude reduced average precision from 0.91 to 0.63. Window length affected recall for short-burst attacks more than for persistent anomalies. An empirical calibration procedure based on unlabelled holdout data is proposed and benchmarked. The paper provides a practical guide for practitioners deploying tree-based anomaly detectors in environments where ground-truth labels are unavailable.

title: Autoencoder-Based Reconstruction Error for Anomaly Scoring in PROFINET IO Traffic
abstract: A shallow fully-connected autoencoder with a 48-32-16-32-48 architecture was trained on PROFINET IO cyclic data exchange traffic captured from an automotive body-assembly line. The encoder compressed 48-dimensional per-cycle feature vectors—including cycle time jitter, alarm status byte distributions, and data record checksum statistics—into a 16-dimensional bottleneck. Reconstruction error was used as an anomaly score. The network was trained on 30 days of normal operation (approximately 2.1 million cycles) using stochastic gradient descent with batch size 256. Anomaly scoring was tested against seven fault conditions introduced by a cooperating maintenance team, including sensor dropout, network congestion injection, and controller firmware substitution. The autoencoder achieved an area under the ROC curve of 0.94 across all fault types, compared with 0.81 for a PCA-based reconstruction baseline. Inference latency was 0.4 ms per cycle on a standard x86 edge server, compatible with 10 ms scan cycle requirements.
