title: Anomaly Detection in Industrial Control Systems
abstract: This book chapter surveys statistical and machine-learning approaches to anomaly detection in ICS environments, focusing on network-level traffic analysis rather than host-based or physical-process monitoring. The chapter covers the statistical properties of ICS traffic that distinguish it from enterprise IT traffic—determinism, periodicity, limited state space—and how these properties can be exploited by unsupervised methods. Covered algorithms include univariate control charts, multivariate Gaussian models, kernel density estimators, one-class SVMs, Isolation Forest, and autoencoders, with discussion of their assumptions, computational requirements, and suitability for embedded deployment. Protocol-specific considerations are provided for Modbus, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, and PROFINET. The chapter closes with a discussion of evaluation methodology challenges, including the scarcity of labelled datasets, the difficulty of representative attack injection, and the trade-off between false alarm rate and response latency. Representative results from the published literature are tabulated.

title: Evaluating the Effect of Protocol Encryption on Traffic-Based Anomaly Detection: OPC UA Security Mode Comparison
abstract: OPC UA supports three security modes—None, Sign, and SignAndEncrypt—and this paper evaluates how each mode affects the discriminability of traffic features used in unsupervised anomaly detectors. Experiments were conducted on a testbed comprising an OPC UA server, two client applications, and an embedded data historian. Seventeen traffic features extractable from unencrypted traffic were assessed for their availability under Sign and SignAndEncrypt modes using packet capture before and after the application layer. Under SignAndEncrypt, 11 of 17 features became unavailable or uninformative at the packet level; however, timing, packet length distribution, and session-level handshake frequency remained discriminative. A reduced 6-feature one-class SVM trained on these surviving features achieved a detection rate of 0.83 against four attack scenarios, compared with 0.91 for the full 17-feature detector on unencrypted traffic. The paper discusses the implications for passive inline monitoring architectures and proposes a broker-based decryption approach for trusted network segments.

title: A Labelled Packet-Level Dataset of Modbus/TCP Attacks for Evaluating Anomaly Detectors
abstract: This paper describes the collection, annotation, and release of a packet-level Modbus/TCP dataset captured on the ICS testbed at the University of Novi Sad. The dataset spans 21 days of normal operation and 6 days of controlled attack execution, comprising approximately 310 million packets. Eight attack scenarios were implemented: function code scanning, coil mass-write injection, replay with modified values, man-in-the-middle payload substitution, time-synchronisation offset injection, denial-of-service flooding, slow-rate polling exhaustion, and firmware update spoofing. Each packet is labelled with a binary normal/attack flag and a scenario identifier. The paper documents the testbed topology, PLC configuration, traffic generation scripts, and labelling methodology in sufficient detail for reproduction. Baseline results for five detectors—statistical process control, one-class SVM, Isolation Forest, autoencoder, and LSTM-based reconstruction—are reported to enable direct comparison by future researchers. The dataset is hosted on the university repository.

title: Threshold Calibration for ICS Anomaly Detectors Under Imbalanced Operating Conditions
abstract: Anomaly detectors for ICS traffic are typically calibrated by fixing the decision threshold to achieve a target false positive rate estimated on a clean training set. This paper investigates the miscalibration that results when the actual false positive rate at deployment differs from the target, and proposes a post-hoc calibration procedure using a small set of unlabelled operational data. The procedure fits a two-component beta mixture model to the empirical score distribution and uses the mixture weight of the anomalous component as a proxy for the contamination fraction. Experiments on four detectors (OC-SVM, Isolation Forest, autoencoder, and kernel density estimator) across three ICS protocol datasets show that the calibration procedure reduces the gap between nominal and actual FPR from a mean of 3.1 percentage points to 0.4 percentage points. The paper also quantifies sensitivity to the choice of beta mixture initialisation and provides practical recommendations for operators setting alert thresholds.

title: Comparing Score Aggregation Strategies for Multi-Protocol ICS Anomaly Detection
abstract: Industrial sites often run several ICS protocols concurrently; a single anomaly may manifest in traffic from multiple protocols or only one. This paper compares six score aggregation strategies—maximum, mean, product, Dempster-Shafer combination, learned linear combination, and a voting threshold rule—for combining per-protocol anomaly scores from Modbus, DNP3, and EtherNet/IP detectors deployed simultaneously on the same network segment. A testbed with all three protocol stacks was operated for 45 days, and 18 multi-protocol and single-protocol attack scenarios were injected over a 10-day evaluation period. The learned linear combination, trained on a 5-day clean holdout with synthetic contamination, achieved the highest balanced accuracy (0.91) but required labelled data for weight estimation. The Dempster-Shafer rule achieved 0.88 without labelled data. The maximum rule performed consistently below 0.80. Results provide concrete guidance for operators designing multi-sensor detection pipelines.

title: Protocol-Agnostic Anomaly Detection Using Byte-Level Feature Extraction from ICS Application Payloads
abstract: Most ICS anomaly detectors are designed for a specific protocol and rely on parsed field values. This paper investigates a protocol-agnostic approach in which raw application-layer payload bytes from the first 64 bytes of each PDU are used to construct feature vectors via byte-frequency histograms augmented with bigram entropy and mean absolute deviation of byte values. A one-class SVM and an Isolation Forest were trained on mixed-protocol captures from a testbed running Modbus, DNP3, and a proprietary vendor protocol for which no parser was available. The proprietary protocol represented 31% of traffic. Against seven attack scenarios including vendor-protocol-specific command injection, the protocol-agnostic detectors achieved AUROC values of 0.89 and 0.87 respectively, compared with 0.94 for a protocol-aware Modbus detector applied only to Modbus traffic. The paper discusses cases where protocol-agnostic features are sufficient and where parsed fields remain necessary, providing a decision framework for practitioners deploying detectors on heterogeneous industrial networks.

title: Comparison of PCA-based and kernel PCA-based feature extraction for microarray gene expression clustering
abstract: Microarray platforms produce high-dimensional gene expression matrices that require dimensionality reduction before meaningful clustering can be applied. This study evaluated principal component analysis (PCA) and kernel PCA with radial basis function, polynomial, and sigmoid kernels on five publicly available human tissue microarray datasets ranging from 200 to 3,400 samples. Clustering quality was assessed using adjusted Rand index and silhouette scores against histologically validated cell-type labels. Kernel PCA with RBF kernel outperformed linear PCA on three of the five datasets, with the largest gain observed in datasets with known nonlinear class boundaries. However, runtime scaled poorly beyond 2,000 samples. The study recommended linear PCA as a practical default for large datasets while flagging kernel variants for smaller, structurally complex datasets. All code and preprocessing scripts were deposited in a public repository. This early work established the benchmarking methodology later applied to single-cell data.

title: Spectral embedding methods for RNA-seq count data: sensitivity to normalisation choice
abstract: RNA sequencing count matrices require normalisation before downstream analysis, yet the interaction between normalisation method and spectral embedding has received limited systematic attention. This work tested six normalisation strategies—including TMM, DESeq2 size-factor, and upper-quartile normalisation—in combination with Laplacian eigenmaps and diffusion maps on eleven bulk RNA-seq datasets from the ENCODE project and one in-house dataset of 48 mouse liver samples. Two-dimensional embeddings were evaluated by how well they separated known tissue types and by stability under bootstrapped subsampling of 80% of genes. DESeq2 size-factor normalisation produced the most stable embeddings in eight of the twelve datasets. Diffusion maps were more sensitive to normalisation choice than Laplacian eigenmaps across the board. The results suggested that normalisation decisions should be reported alongside embedding parameters in publications, a practice that was inconsistently followed at the time. Reproducible analysis scripts were provided as supplementary material.

title: Graph-based dimensionality reduction for single-cell transcriptomics: a framework review
abstract: The emergence of single-cell RNA sequencing between 2010 and 2014 created demand for dimensionality reduction methods suited to data characteristics that differ from bulk RNA-seq: high sparsity, dropout events, and tens of thousands of cells. This book chapter surveyed t-SNE, Isomap, locally linear embedding, and early versions of graph Laplacian approaches as applied to scRNA-seq datasets available up to mid-2015. The chapter discussed parameter sensitivity, computational complexity, and the lack of standardised evaluation metrics specific to single-cell biology at that time. It noted that most published applications reported qualitative cluster separation in two dimensions without quantitative validation against independent biological ground truth. A proposed checklist for method reporting was included, covering dataset size, preprocessing steps, hyperparameter ranges explored, and software versions. The chapter served as background reading for a graduate bioinformatics course at the University of Novi Sad.

title: Benchmarking t-SNE perplexity settings on scRNA-seq datasets of varying cell-type complexity
abstract: The perplexity hyperparameter of t-SNE is routinely set to 30 in single-cell RNA sequencing analyses without systematic justification. This study tested perplexity values of 5, 10, 20, 30, 50, 100, and 200 on nine publicly available scRNA-seq datasets spanning 500 to 45,000 cells and between 3 and 28 annotated cell types. Clustering quality was measured using adjusted Rand index, Fowlkes–Mallows index, and normalised mutual information against curated cell-type labels. Results showed that optimal perplexity scaled approximately with the square root of the number of cells and that datasets with rare cell types (fewer than 1% of total cells) benefited from lower perplexity values. The default of 30 ranked in the top quartile of tested settings for only four of the nine datasets. Practical guidelines were proposed based on dataset size and estimated cell-type imbalance. R code for the full evaluation pipeline was released under an open-source licence.

title: Cross-protocol benchmarking of cell-type annotation transfer methods in single-cell RNA sequencing
abstract: Automated cell-type annotation transfer, in which labels from a reference dataset are projected onto a query dataset, is now routinely used to reduce the burden of manual curation. This study benchmarked seven annotation transfer methods—including Seurat label transfer, SingleR, scANVI, and CellTypist—across 24 reference–query dataset pairs that differed in tissue origin, sequencing protocol, and sequencing depth. The primary metric was macro-averaged F1 score against manually curated labels. Rare cell types with fewer than 50 cells in the reference performed poorly across all methods, with F1 scores consistently below 0.50. Methods based on probabilistic generative models outperformed correlation-based approaches when protocol mismatch was high. Annotation confidence scores were poorly calibrated in three of seven methods, with stated 90% confidence intervals containing the correct label only 71–78% of the time. Calibration curves and recommended confidence thresholds were provided for each method.

title: Sensitivity of Leiden and Louvain community detection to resolution parameter in scRNA-seq datasets: practical thresholds for stable partitions
abstract: Community detection algorithms applied to k-nearest-neighbour graphs are the dominant clustering strategy in single-cell RNA sequencing analysis, but their resolution parameter is often set without systematic justification. This study varied the resolution parameter from 0.1 to 3.0 in steps of 0.1 for both Leiden and Louvain algorithms across 15 scRNA-seq datasets spanning 1,200 to 120,000 cells and 4 to 35 annotated cell types. Stability was assessed by computing element-centric clustering similarity between adjacent resolution steps and by comparing recovered cluster counts to ground-truth cell-type counts from FACS-sorted validation data in five datasets. A plateau in element-centric similarity consistently appeared in the range 0.4–0.8 for Leiden and 0.3–0.6 for Louvain. Leiden partitions at the stability plateau matched ground-truth cell-type counts within ±2 clusters in 12 of 15 datasets. Louvain matched within ±2 in 9 of 15. A simple resolution-selection heuristic based on the stability plateau was implemented as an R package and deposited on CRAN.

title: Effect of ambient RNA contamination levels on UMAP topology and downstream cluster purity in droplet-based scRNA-seq
abstract: Ambient RNA contamination in droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing arises when cell lysis occurs in the cell suspension before encapsulation, depositing foreign transcripts into all droplets. While correction tools exist, the magnitude of distortion introduced at varying contamination levels and its effect on UMAP topology and cluster purity has not been characterised quantitatively. This study used SoupX to simulate contamination levels of 5%, 10%, 20%, and 40% in three clean reference datasets and measured the resulting change in UMAP structure using topological data analysis descriptors (Betti numbers at filtration thresholds derived from the k-NN graph) and cluster purity against known labels. Contamination above 15% produced statistically significant changes in first Betti numbers in all three datasets, indicating the formation of spurious loops in the embedding. Cluster purity degraded by a mean of 8.3 percentage points between 5% and 20% contamination. Contamination estimation and correction prior to dimensionality reduction was confirmed as a necessary preprocessing step rather than an optional one.

title: Towards a minimum reporting standard for single-cell RNA sequencing dimensionality reduction: a community survey and proposed checklist
abstract: Dimensionality reduction is a near-universal step in scRNA-seq data analysis, yet the parameters, software versions, and preprocessing decisions that precede it are reported inconsistently across publications. This preprint reports results of a survey of 214 scRNA-seq publications from 2020–2024, in which 38 items covering preprocessing, embedding configuration, clustering, and validation were coded for presence or absence of reporting. Random seed was reported in 18% of papers, initialisation strategy in 22%, and the number of principal components used as UMAP input in 54%. A minimum reporting checklist of 14 items was drafted based on item importance ratings collected from 73 researchers via structured questionnaire. The checklist was piloted on 20 manuscripts submitted to a regional bioinformatics journal, where authors revised their methods sections to incorporate flagged missing items. Adoption of the checklist as a journal submission requirement is under discussion with three journal editorial boards.

title: Emanacioni koeficijenti radona u lesnim sedimentima južne Bačke: uticaj granulometrije i vlažnosti
abstract: U radu su određeni emanacioni koeficijenti radona (ε) za 34 uzorka lesa i fosilnih paleozola sa šest lokaliteta u južnoj Bačkoj. Uzorci su prikupljani na dubinama od 0,5 do 4,0 m. Aktivnost Ra-226 merena je HPGe gama-spektrometrom, a emanacija radona pasivnom akumulacionom metodom pri kontrolisanoj temperaturi od 20 °C. Vrednosti ε kretale su se od 0,14 do 0,41, sa značajnom pozitivnom korelacijom sa sadržajem gline (r = 0,73, p < 0,01). Merenja pri različitim nivoima vlažnosti (5–25 mas. %) pokazala su porast ε od prosečno 38 % pri prelasku iz suvih u vlažne uslove. Rezultati ukazuju da litološka heterogenost lesnih profila mora biti uzeta u obzir pri modelovanju toka radona ka površini tla. Dobijeni podaci upoređeni su sa dostupnim vrednostima za sedimente Mađarske i Rumunije i pokazuju konzistentnost u okviru jednog sigma od regionalnog proseka.

title: Gamma-ray spectrometric survey of natural radionuclides in agricultural soils of the Srem region
abstract: A systematic gamma-ray spectrometric survey was conducted on 112 surface soil samples (0–10 cm depth) collected across the Srem agricultural plain between the Sava and Danube rivers. Samples were dried, homogenised and sealed for four weeks before measurement with an HPGe detector (relative efficiency 35 %, energy resolution 1.85 keV at 1332 keV). Activity concentrations of Ra-226, Th-232 and K-40 were determined along with Cs-137 as a reference anthropogenic tracer. Mean activity concentrations were 32.4 ± 4.1 Bq/kg for Ra-226, 41.7 ± 5.8 Bq/kg for Th-232 and 512 ± 63 Bq/kg for K-40. The calculated radium equivalent activity ranged from 88 to 156 Bq/kg, all values below the internationally recommended screening level of 370 Bq/kg. Spatial distribution maps generated by ordinary kriging revealed a zone of elevated Th-232 in the southwest of the study area, consistent with an outcrop of Miocene clay. The dataset forms a baseline for future radiological risk assessments in the region.

title: Radon exhalation rates from brick samples manufactured in the Pannonian Basin: comparison of accumulation chamber and activated charcoal methods
abstract: Radon exhalation rates were measured for 18 brick types from seven manufacturers in Serbia, Hungary and Romania using two independent methods: a sealed accumulation chamber with a solid-state silicon detector and activated charcoal canisters with liquid scintillation counting. Measurements were performed in parallel on the same cylindrical specimens (diameter 60 mm, height 50 mm) at 20 °C and 50 % relative humidity. Exhalation rates determined by the two methods agreed within 8 % for 14 out of 18 samples. The four discrepant samples had visible macro-cracks suggesting preferential diffusion pathways that inflate charcoal results. Mean surface exhalation rate across all bricks was 18.4 mBq m⁻² h⁻¹ (range 6.1–44.7 mBq m⁻² h⁻¹). A statistically significant correlation was observed between Ra-226 activity concentration and measured exhalation rate (r = 0.81), but the regression slope differed from theoretical predictions, indicating that pore geometry and tortuosity vary substantially between manufacturers. The data are directly applicable to indoor radon dose modelling in residential buildings.

title: Indoor radon concentrations in schools and kindergartens in Novi Sad: seasonal variation and correlation with building parameters
abstract: Passive radon measurements using CR-39 nuclear track detectors were carried out in 54 educational buildings (38 primary schools, 12 kindergartens, 4 secondary schools) in Novi Sad municipality over four consecutive seasons from autumn 2017 to summer 2018. Detectors were placed in ground-floor and first-floor classrooms. The annual mean indoor radon concentration ranged from 28 to 318 Bq/m³ across buildings, with an overall geometric mean of 74 Bq/m³. Seven buildings (13 %) exceeded the Serbian national reference level of 200 Bq/m³. Radon concentrations were significantly higher in winter than in summer (ratio 2.3 on average), consistent with reduced ventilation. Multiple regression analysis identified basement presence, year of construction before 1970, and concrete slab-on-ground floor type as significant predictors of elevated annual mean concentration (adjusted R² = 0.61). No significant correlation was found with building orientation or distance to major roads. Recommendations for targeted remediation in three high-priority buildings are provided.

title: Assessment of radiological hazard indices for ceramic tiles and natural stone flooring materials available in the Serbian market
abstract: Twenty-two ceramic tile types and twelve natural stone flooring products (granite, marble, limestone, travertine) commercially available in Serbia were analysed for Ra-226, Th-232 and K-40 activity concentrations using HPGe gamma spectrometry. Granite samples showed the highest Ra-226 concentrations (mean 78.3 Bq/kg, range 45–131 Bq/kg), while marble and limestone were consistently below 20 Bq/kg for all three radionuclides. The radium equivalent activity (Raeq) ranged from 21 Bq/kg for white Carrara-type marble to 231 Bq/kg for a dark red granite imported from Portugal. All values remained below the 370 Bq/kg screening threshold. The annual effective dose from external gamma exposure was estimated for a reference room with 40 m² of flooring, assuming 7000 h/year occupancy. Maximum doses were calculated for granite-floored rooms (0.41 mSv/year), which are elevated compared to ceramic tile floors (0.18 mSv/year on average) but remain within acceptable limits. Results are presented as a practical reference for architects and building inspectors.

title: Kartiranje geogenog radonskog potencijala u opštini Sremska Mitrovica primenom pasivnih detektora i podataka o sadržaju Ra-226 u tlu
abstract: Geogeni radonski potencijal (GRP) određen je za 63 merne tačke raspoređene po pravilnoj mreži u opštini Sremska Mitrovica. Na svakoj lokaciji izmerena je koncentracija radona u tlu na dubini od 80 cm pomoću akumulacionih komora sa CR-39 detektorom i gasa koji se pumpao kroz sonde, a uzet je i poremećeni uzorak tla za merenje Ra-226 i propusnosti tla za vazduh. GRP vrednosti kretale su se od 0,03 do 1,42 kBq m⁻³ po (kPa s m⁻²)^(0,5). Zona visokog GRP (> 0,5) identifikovana je duž poleđine desne obale Save, gde dominiraju aluvijalni glinoviti sedimenti sa povišenim Ra-226 (35–48 Bq/kg). Dobijena GRP karta poređena je sa podacima o izmerenim koncentracijama radona u 24 stambena objekta unutar zone, pri čemu je ustanovljena statistički značajna pozitivna korelacija (Spearman ρ = 0,68). Rezultati pružaju osnovu za prostorno planiranje u smislu preporuka za radonsku zaštitu novih objekata.

title: Uncertainty propagation in life-cycle inventory data for district heating: a comparison of Monte Carlo and analytical methods
abstract: Inventory data used in LCA of district heating systems often carry substantial uncertainty arising from metering gaps, seasonal variability, and use of proxy datasets. This paper compares two approaches for propagating that uncertainty through to characterised impact scores: Monte Carlo simulation (10 000 iterations) and first-order analytical error propagation. The analysis was applied to three hypothetical district heating configurations representing gas-only, gas-plus-solar-thermal, and gas-plus-biomass supply mixes, parameterised using data from publicly available Serbian energy statistics and the ecoinvent 3.9 database. Results show that Monte Carlo and analytical methods agree closely when input distributions are near-normal, but diverge by up to 18% at the 95th percentile for the biomass configuration, where fuel moisture content introduces a skewed distribution. The global warming potential indicator exhibited the lowest coefficient of variation (CV ≈ 9%) across all scenarios, while the particulate matter formation indicator showed the highest (CV ≈ 34%), driven primarily by uncertainty in stack emission measurements. The paper provides a practical workflow for practitioners who need to report uncertainty ranges in compliance with ISO 14044 without access to full probabilistic software.

title: Carbon footprint sensitivity to pipe network losses in district heating: results from monitored data in two Serbian cities
abstract: Distribution losses in district heating pipe networks can represent 10–25% of generated heat and significantly affect reported carbon footprint values, yet LCA studies often treat them as a fixed percentage. This paper uses twelve months of sub-metered thermal energy data from two Serbian cities (population 35 000 and 82 000) to characterise how distribution losses vary by outdoor temperature, load factor, and pipe age. A regression model was fitted to hourly data, and the resulting loss function was embedded in an LCA model built in Python using the brightway2 framework. For the larger city, substituting the monitored loss profile for a flat 15% assumption changed the annual carbon footprint by +6.2%, with the effect concentrated in the shoulder seasons when supply temperatures are reduced. The smaller city, which operates an older uninsulated network, showed a +11.8% shift. The work demonstrates that using monitored operational data rather than default values meaningfully affects conclusions about which supply-side interventions yield the greatest emission reductions. Raw monitoring data and the brightway2 calculation scripts are shared as supplementary material.

title: Integrating solar thermal into an existing gas-fired district heating network: an LCA perspective on phased decarbonisation
abstract: Solar thermal collectors are increasingly considered as a low-cost, low-emission supplement to gas-fired district heating, yet their full life-cycle impact including manufacturing, installation, and end-of-life has received limited attention in the context of mixed-fuel network decarbonisation. This paper models four phased integration scenarios in which flat-plate solar collectors supply between 5% and 25% of annual heat demand, using a reference network serving 12 500 dwellings in northern Serbia. Inventory data for the collector manufacturing stage were drawn from ecoinvent 3.9 European averages, adjusted for local installation practices based on interviews with three installation contractors. Results show a break-even point at approximately 9% solar share, below which the embodied emissions of the collector field outweigh avoided gas combustion emissions over a 20-year system lifetime. Above 15% solar share, global warming potential falls by 14–19% relative to the gas-only baseline, but eutrophication and land-use indicators increase marginally due to glycol antifreeze production. The paper includes a simplified decision chart intended to assist municipal energy planners without specialist LCA training.

title: Институционалне баријере у прекограничним R&D партнерствима: случај Србије и Румуније
abstract: Рад анализира институционалне препреке које отежавају формирање и одрживост заједничких истраживачко-развојних активности између српских и румунских предузећа у периоду 2010–2016. године. Коришћена је метода упоредне студије случаја на узорку од осам партнерских пројеката из сектора агроиндустрије и информационих технологија. Подаци су прикупљени путем 24 полуструктурисана интервјуа са директорима и руководиоцима иновационих одељења. Идентификовано је пет кључних категорија баријера: разлике у правном оквиру заштите интелектуалне својине, неускладјеност рачуноводствених стандарда, асиметрија у државним подстицајима за R&D, језичке баријере у техничкој документацији, и различите организационе културе управљања знањем. Налазе показују да правни оквир представља најучесталију баријеру у агроиндустрији, док културне разлике доминирају у ИТ сектору. Резултати доприносе разумевању регионалне специфичности институционалне средине на Западном Балкану.

title: Do Technology Gaps Deter Knowledge Transfer? Evidence from EU–Western Balkan R&D Joint Ventures
abstract: Using a sample of 112 R&D-intensive joint ventures involving at least one EU-based and one Western Balkan firm, this study tests whether the technology gap between partners facilitates or hinders intra-venture knowledge transfer. Firm-level data from Bureau van Dijk Orbis Europe and WIIW FDI databases covering 2009–2018 are combined with original survey data collected in 2019. A moderated regression framework is employed, with technology gap measured as the log difference in patent stock and R&D expenditure per employee. Findings show an inverted U-shaped relationship: moderate technology gaps are associated with higher knowledge transfer intensity, while very large gaps suppress transfer, consistent with the 'too-far-to-learn' hypothesis. The moderating role of joint governance structures is confirmed: ventures with co-managed IP agreements exhibit a flatter inverted-U curve, suggesting that contractual design can partially offset large capability disparities. Results are robust to alternative gap operationalisations and to the exclusion of outlier firms.

title: Regional Innovation Systems and Cross-Border Spillover Corridors: A Network Analysis of Vojvodina and Southern Transdanubia
abstract: This study maps the inter-firm and inter-institutional knowledge flow network spanning the Vojvodina region of Serbia and the Southern Transdanubia region of Hungary, using co-application data from Serbian and Hungarian national R&D funding registries and Interreg project databases over the period 2007–2020. A bipartite network of 214 organisations (firms, universities, technology transfer offices, and public research institutes) is constructed, and standard social network analysis metrics—degree centrality, betweenness centrality, and clustering coefficients—are computed for each node class. Results reveal two largely separate regional sub-networks bridged by a small number of structurally equivalent broker organisations, primarily large multinational firm subsidiaries and one technical university on each side of the border. The 'Novi Sad cluster' emerges as the denser of the two, with higher internal clustering but lower cross-border betweenness than the Pécs-centred cluster. Implications for Interreg IPA programming and Science Technology Park collaboration strategies are discussed.

title: Contractual Completeness and Post-Entry Learning in EU–Serbia R&D Joint Ventures: A Longitudinal Case Study
abstract: Relying on a ten-year longitudinal case study (2012–2022) of three R&D joint ventures between German and Serbian firms in the machinery and electronics sectors, this paper examines how the completeness and flexibility of initial joint venture contracts affect the evolution of learning routines over time. Process data were collected through repeated semi-structured interviews conducted in four waves, supplemented by document analysis of contract revisions, R&D activity logs, and internal training records. The analysis tracks changes in knowledge codification practices, personnel rotation schemes, and joint patent filing frequency. Findings indicate that ventures with initially more flexible, relational contracts showed a higher rate of learning routine development after years 3–5, whereas rigidly specified contracts were associated with earlier learning stagnation. One venture in the sample transitioned to a fully owned subsidiary by year seven, a trajectory linked to the exhaustion of mutual knowledge complementarities rather than contractual failure. Implications for contract design in EU-funded cross-border R&D schemes are drawn.

title: Tan-Delta Response as an Ageing Indicator in Medium-Voltage XLPE Cable Sections Under Accelerated Thermal Stress
abstract: This study examines the evolution of dissipation factor (tan-delta) in 10 kV cross-linked polyethylene cable samples subjected to accelerated thermal ageing at temperatures between 105 °C and 130 °C over periods of 250, 500, and 1000 hours. Twelve cable specimens, each 1.5 m in length, were prepared from a single commercial cable reel to minimise batch variability. Tan-delta measurements were performed at 0.1 Hz using a very-low-frequency test set at voltage levels of 1U0, 1.5U0, and 2U0. Results show a monotonic increase in tan-delta nonlinearity index beyond 750 ageing hours at 115 °C, with a mean increase of 43% relative to the unaged reference at 2U0. Morphological changes in the insulation were cross-checked using differential scanning calorimetry, confirming a reduction in crystallinity from 38% to 31% after 1000 hours at 130 °C. The findings support the use of tan-delta nonlinearity as a reliable early-stage ageing marker for condition-based maintenance scheduling.

title: Partial Discharge Pulse Shape Clustering in Oil-Paper and XLPE Insulation Using k-Means on Time-Frequency Features
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) pulses recorded from laboratory cable termination models were analysed using a time-frequency decomposition approach combined with k-means clustering to distinguish insulation types and defect categories. Two sets of specimens were prepared: oil-impregnated paper cable terminations at 20 kV and XLPE joint models at 10 kV, each containing artificially introduced voids of 1–3 mm diameter. PD signals were captured with a 500 MHz digital oscilloscope and a calibrated capacitive coupler. Discrete wavelet transform coefficients at decomposition levels 4 through 7 were used as input features after dimensionality reduction via principal component analysis retaining 92% of variance. Clustering yielded four stable groups corresponding to void discharges, surface discharges, electrical treeing inception, and external noise. Silhouette scores averaged 0.71 across twenty independent runs. The approach requires no labelled training data and correctly separated defect types in 87% of manually reviewed cases.

title: Electrothermal Coupled Simulation of a 110 kV XLPE Underground Cable in Trench Configuration Under Cyclic Load Profiles
abstract: A two-dimensional finite-element model of a 110 kV single-core XLPE underground cable laid in a flat-formation trench was developed to study the interaction between ohmic heating, soil thermal resistance, and insulation temperature distribution under realistic cyclic load profiles drawn from a 24-hour residential grid demand curve. The model geometry includes the conductor, semiconductor screens, insulation, metallic sheath, and a layered soil section with thermal resistivity varying between 0.9 and 1.4 K·m/W across a depth of 1.2 m. Simulations were run for a seven-day sequence using IEC 60287 conductor temperatures as benchmark validation. Peak conductor temperature reached 74.2 °C against an IEC estimate of 76.1 °C, a 2.5% deviation attributed to heat storage in the concrete duct. Insulation temperature gradient across the XLPE thickness ranged from 8.3 K to 14.7 K depending on load peak duration. Results indicate that short-duration load peaks below 45 minutes do not significantly elevate average insulation temperature but produce measurable dielectric stress concentration at the inner screen interface.

title: Dielectric Spectroscopy of Service-Aged 110 kV XLPE Cables Retrieved from a Serbian Transmission Network
abstract: Four sections of 110 kV XLPE cable decommissioned after 18 to 22 years of service were subjected to broadband dielectric spectroscopy in the frequency range 10−3 Hz to 103 Hz at a field stress of 5 kV/mm and ambient temperature. Complex permittivity was measured using a precision impedance analyser with a guarded three-electrode test cell adapted for cable cross-sections. The imaginary part of permittivity at 10−1 Hz showed values between 1.8 × 10−4 and 6.3 × 10−4, compared with 0.9 × 10−4 for a reference unaged cable sample from the same manufacturer. Deconvolution of relaxation peaks using the Havriliak-Negami model identified two dominant polarisation mechanisms attributed to oxidative byproducts and moisture ingress near the outer semiconductor screen. Correlation analysis against cable laying records indicated that sections with documented water-filled joints exhibited the highest imaginary permittivity values. The data set provides empirical benchmarks for field diagnostic acceptance criteria for 110 kV cable refurbishment decisions.

title: Integration of Distributed Fibre-Optic Temperature Sensing Data into a Cable Digital Twin for Joint Hotspot Detection
abstract: Distributed temperature sensing (DTS) data obtained from an optical fibre co-installed with a 110 kV XLPE cable circuit were used to calibrate and validate a digital twin model for hotspot detection at cable joints. The DTS system provided temperature readings at 1-metre spatial resolution along a 3.8 km route, sampled every 10 minutes over a six-month period. Joint locations were identified as thermal anomalies in the DTS profile; 11 of 14 joints produced detectable temperature elevations above the background cable sheath temperature, with deviations ranging from 1.4 K to 7.2 K at peak load. These measured temperatures were assimilated into the digital twin using a Kalman filter updating scheme, reducing the root-mean-square error of predicted conductor temperature from 3.8 K to 1.2 K at joint positions. One joint exhibiting a 7.2 K elevation was identified as a candidate for maintenance inspection; subsequent offline diagnostic measurement confirmed elevated tan-delta at that location. The paper describes the DTS signal preprocessing, outlier rejection, and the Kalman filter formulation in detail.

title: Benchmarking Physics-Informed Neural Networks Against Finite-Element Thermal Models for XLPE Cable Ageing Simulation
abstract: Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) were evaluated as a computationally efficient alternative to finite-element method (FEM) thermal simulations for estimating spatiotemporal temperature distributions in 110 kV XLPE cable insulation under variable load conditions. A reference FEM model using the geometry described in earlier work was used to generate a dataset of 1 200 temperature field snapshots at 15-minute intervals under four synthetic load profiles. The PINN architecture incorporated the heat conduction partial differential equation as a soft constraint in the loss function alongside data loss from 120 randomly sampled collocation points per snapshot. After training over 50 000 epochs, the PINN reproduced peak insulation temperatures with a mean absolute error of 0.9 K compared with FEM output, while inference time per time step was reduced by a factor of 340. The trained model was embedded in the digital twin framework described in prior publications and tested over a 30-day live monitoring window on the same 110 kV circuit used for DTS validation. Cumulative ageing index predictions agreed with the FEM-based reference within 3.6% over the test period.

title: Estimating dust deposition rates over flat terrain using mesoscale meteorological model output and sediment trap measurements
abstract: Dust deposition on outdoor surfaces in lowland environments depends on wind speed, source availability, and precipitation patterns that are not uniform across a region. This paper couples WRF-Chem v3.5 mesoscale simulations with a network of 22 passive sediment traps deployed across Vojvodina over 18 months (2012–2013) to produce gridded weekly deposition maps at 3 km resolution. Model-predicted dry deposition flux at trap locations showed correlation coefficients between 0.67 and 0.78 depending on season, with the weakest performance in summer when convective mixing dominated. Trap measurements at an instrumented PV test site near Zrenjanin averaged 1.2 g m⁻² week⁻¹ during the dry spring period and dropped to 0.3 g m⁻² week⁻¹ in winter. The modelled deposition maps were interpolated to daily resolution and stored as georeferenced raster products that can be ingested by satellite-based reflectance inversion workflows. Identified biases near agricultural tillage areas suggest a seasonal correction factor of 1.4 is needed for late April to June.

title: Detection of soiling on utility-scale photovoltaic arrays using multitemporal Landsat-8 OLI imagery
abstract: This study presents the first regional application of Landsat-8 OLI imagery to track surface soiling across two utility-scale PV installations in Serbia totalling 14.7 MW. Eighteen cloud-free scenes acquired between April 2014 and March 2016 were atmospherically corrected using the LaSRC algorithm. A reference clean-panel reflectance spectrum was established from post-rain acquisition dates confirmed by on-site rain gauge records. Departure from this reference, quantified as a normalised soiling index (NSI) computed in bands 2–4 (450–680 nm), was compared against gravimetric soiling measurements taken during scheduled maintenance visits. NSI explained 74% of variance in gravimetric soiling load across 48 paired observations. Spatial heterogeneity in soiling across array rows was visible at 30 m resolution, with windward rows showing 22% higher NSI than leeward rows. The methodology does not require co-located sensor networks and is applicable to any accessible Landsat archive scene, making it transferable to sites without ground instrumentation.

title: Transferability of soiling detection indices across sensor platforms: comparing Landsat-8 OLI and Sentinel-2 MSI results at a co-located test site
abstract: The proliferation of free satellite imagery raises the question of whether soiling indices calibrated on one sensor are directly applicable to another. Fifty-three co-located, near-simultaneous Landsat-8 OLI and Sentinel-2A MSI acquisitions over a 9.3 MW ground-mounted array in Bačka were processed through sensor-specific atmospheric correction pipelines (LaSRC and Sen2Cor 2.5 respectively) and compared. Band-equivalent reflectance values differed by a mean of 0.009 in the green band and 0.014 in the red band after cross-calibration. The NSI derived from Sentinel-2 had a standard deviation 30% lower than the Landsat equivalent, attributable to its 10 m spatial resolution resolving row-level soiling patterns undetectable at 30 m. A linear transfer function (slope 0.97, intercept 0.004, R² = 0.88) allows NSI values from the two sensors to be merged into a combined time series. Residual differences are attributed to differing overpass times and non-synchronous aerosol conditions rather than sensor radiometry.

title: Mapping aerosol optical depth over the central Balkans using fused MODIS and SEVIRI retrievals
abstract: Aerosol optical depth estimates used in surface reflectance correction and soiling-load estimation suffer from MODIS swath gaps that can leave a location without a valid observation for three or more consecutive days. This paper evaluates a spatiotemporal fusion of MODIS MOD04_L2 (Terra and Aqua combined) with MSG SEVIRI-derived AOD to fill these gaps over a domain covering Serbia, Hungary, Romania and Croatia. Fusion was performed using a weighted kriging interpolation constrained by SEVIRI's half-hourly temporal sampling at reduced spatial accuracy (0.05°). Validation against eight AERONET stations in the domain over 2015–2017 showed a mean absolute error of 0.036 AOD units for the fused product versus 0.028 for MODIS-only on days when MODIS data were available. Gap-filled estimates had MAE of 0.051. Coverage increased from 61% to 94% of station-days. The fused product is distributed as daily GeoTIFF files and is used operationally as input to the regional dust deposition model described in earlier work.

title: Seasonal variation in soiling rates at three climate zones across the Western Balkans: a comparative remote-sensing study
abstract: Soiling accumulation on PV surfaces is expected to differ between the continental climate of Vojvodina, the transitional climate of central Serbia, and the Mediterranean climate of the coastal Montenegro hinterland. This study applies a harmonised Sentinel-2-based NSI methodology to three operational PV plants (8–15 MW) over 24 months (2019–2021). NSI accumulation rates during dry periods averaged 0.0031 day⁻¹ in Vojvodina, 0.0019 day⁻¹ in central Serbia, and 0.0025 day⁻¹ in coastal Montenegro. Rain events reset NSI within one to three days at all sites when daily precipitation exceeded 4 mm, consistent with field observations. The Vojvodina site showed the strongest correlation between NSI and modelled dust deposition (r = 0.82), while the Montenegro site showed greater influence of sea-salt aerosol, which was detected as a distinct short-wave-infrared signature absent at inland sites. Differences in soiling composition require site-specific calibration of any pan-regional cleaning-schedule model.

title: Quantifying the effect of agricultural harvest dust on nearby photovoltaic array reflectance: a case study from the Bačka region
abstract: Cereal harvesting in the Pannonian Plain generates intense short-duration dust events that can deposit several grams per square metre on surfaces within a few kilometres of the source. Sentinel-2 imagery at 10 m resolution, acquired within two days before and after seven harvest events between 2019 and 2023 near a 6.4 MW PV installation, shows mean NSI increases of 0.031 per event, roughly equivalent to three weeks of background deposition. Dust transport direction inferred from WRF-simulated surface winds at harvest time was consistent with the observed within-array spatial pattern of NSI increase in all seven cases. Four events were associated with a reduction in measured AC power output of 1.9–4.3% that persisted until a subsequent rain episode. The time between harvest event and first effective rain ranged from 2 to 19 days in the study period. Findings suggest that PV plants adjacent to large arable fields should incorporate harvest season forecasts into their cleaning schedules.

title: Validation of DESIS hyperspectral soiling retrievals against UAV-borne multispectral surveys at a utility-scale PV plant
abstract: The DESIS hyperspectral sensor aboard the ISS provides 30 m imagery across 235 bands (400–1000 nm) that could enable mineralogically informed soiling retrieval at regional scale. This study compares DESIS-derived soiling maps with concurrent UAV surveys using a six-band multispectral camera (DJI Zenmuse P1 modified) flown at 40 m AGL over a 10.8 MW plant in eastern Vojvodina. Seven co-temporal acquisition pairs were collected between March 2023 and October 2024. DESIS soiling index values agreed with UAV-derived equivalents within a mean absolute difference of 0.008 NSI units; systematic offsets were traceable to residual smile effects in DESIS band 14–22 and corrected by a per-scene polynomial. Mineralogical class maps derived from DESIS showed 81% agreement with those derived from the UAV-based system when aggregated to 30 m. DESIS offers a pathway to global hyperspectral soiling monitoring once archive depth is sufficient; current revisit frequency of approximately 21 days for the study latitude remains a limitation.

title: Towards a European benchmark dataset for satellite-based PV soiling index validation: data collection protocol and preliminary results
abstract: Comparable validation of satellite-derived soiling indices requires standardised, openly accessible ground-truth data from multiple climatic regions. This preprint describes a protocol being developed within an ongoing collaboration to establish a European benchmark dataset covering nine PV sites across Serbia, Hungary, Greece, and Portugal. The protocol specifies gravimetric sampling procedures using standardised coupon holders, concurrent spectroradiometer measurements, rain gauge thresholds for defining natural cleaning events, and metadata standards for site geometry and panel tilt. Data collected at three Serbian sites between January 2025 and March 2026 are presented as a first conformance test. Preliminary inter-site comparison shows that normalised soiling indices derived from Sentinel-2 diverge by less than 0.005 NSI units from those derived under the protocol when atmospheric correction uncertainty is below 0.015 reflectance units. Full dataset release is planned following the completion of contributions from all nine sites. Comments on the protocol are invited before finalisation.

title: Unsupervised anomaly detection on Modbus traffic
abstract: Industrial control systems increasingly rely on Modbus, a legacy serial communication protocol widely deployed in manufacturing and critical infrastructure environments. Despite its prevalence, Modbus lacks built-in security mechanisms, making it highly susceptible to network-based attacks. This paper presents an unsupervised anomaly detection framework specifically designed for Modbus traffic analysis. The proposed approach leverages autoencoder-based neural networks trained exclusively on benign traffic to establish a baseline behavioural profile of legitimate industrial communications. Anomalies are identified by measuring reconstruction error against learned normal patterns, without requiring labelled attack data. The framework is evaluated on a synthetic dataset generated from a real-world programmable logic controller testbed, covering scenarios such as unauthorised function code injection, coil manipulation, and replay attacks. Experimental results demonstrate detection rates exceeding 94% across all attack categories, with a false positive rate below 2%. The paper also analyses the impact of traffic window size and encoding granularity on detection performance, offering practical guidance for deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments.

title: Threat modelling for smart building controllers
abstract: Smart building automation systems increasingly integrate heterogeneous controllers managing heating, ventilation, access control, and fire suppression, all connected over IP-based networks. This convergence introduces significant attack surfaces that are rarely addressed through systematic security engineering. This paper applies a structured threat modelling methodology—adapted from STRIDE and augmented with ICS-specific threat categories—to a representative smart building controller architecture. The analysis identifies seventeen distinct threat scenarios spanning spoofing of sensor inputs, tampering with actuator commands, and denial-of-service against building management gateways. For each threat, the paper proposes corresponding mitigations including cryptographic command authentication, rate-limiting policies, and network segmentation strategies. A comparative evaluation against an unmitigated baseline system is conducted using a simulation environment, demonstrating measurable risk reduction across all identified threat categories. The findings offer actionable security guidance for building automation vendors and facility managers deploying next-generation smart infrastructure.

title: A comparative study of intrusion detection architectures for SCADA networks
abstract: Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) networks form the backbone of critical infrastructure sectors including energy distribution, water treatment, and transportation. Protecting these networks from cyber intrusions requires detection systems capable of operating on highly specialised industrial protocols while maintaining low false-positive rates in continuous operation. This paper conducts a systematic comparative evaluation of five intrusion detection architectures—signature-based, specification-based, statistical anomaly, deep learning, and hybrid approaches—applied to a common SCADA testbed. Each architecture is assessed across four attack categories: reconnaissance, command injection, man-in-the-middle, and denial-of-service. Performance is measured in terms of detection accuracy, latency, resource consumption, and adaptability to concept drift. Results show that hybrid architectures combining specification-based rules with neural anomaly scoring achieve the best overall balance, while purely deep-learning-based systems exhibit higher sensitivity to protocol version variability. The paper concludes with a decision framework to guide practitioners in selecting appropriate detection strategies based on operational constraints.

title: Federated learning for distributed intrusion detection across IoT edge nodes
abstract: Internet of Things deployments in industrial and smart city environments generate massive volumes of heterogeneous network traffic across geographically distributed edge nodes. Centralising this data for intrusion detection raises significant privacy and bandwidth concerns, particularly in multi-stakeholder environments. This paper proposes a federated learning framework for distributed intrusion detection, wherein each edge node trains a local anomaly detection model on its own traffic and periodically shares only model gradient updates with a central aggregation server. The aggregated global model is then redistributed to participating nodes, enabling collective knowledge improvement without raw data exposure. The framework is evaluated on a purpose-built IoT testbed consisting of twenty-four heterogeneous edge devices simulating smart metering, environmental sensing, and industrial actuation scenarios. Results demonstrate that the federated approach achieves detection accuracy within 3% of a centralised baseline while reducing data transmission overhead by over 80%. The paper also investigates the robustness of the framework against poisoning attacks introduced by compromised edge nodes.

title: Threat modelling in IIoT supply chains: identifying lateral movement pathways
abstract: Industrial Internet of Things supply chains encompass multiple layers of hardware vendors, firmware providers, system integrators, and end operators, each introducing potential vulnerabilities that adversaries may exploit for lateral movement across organisational boundaries. This paper presents a threat modelling methodology tailored to IIoT supply chain architectures, extending traditional STRIDE analysis with supply-chain-specific threat categories including firmware substitution, third-party library poisoning, and vendor credential reuse. A reference IIoT architecture involving a six-tier supply chain is modelled, and attack graphs are constructed to identify the most probable lateral movement pathways between tiers. Quantitative risk scores are assigned using a modified CVSS-based scoring system adapted for operational technology contexts. The analysis reveals that firmware update channels and remote maintenance interfaces constitute the highest-risk lateral movement vectors. Mitigation recommendations include cryptographic firmware signing, role-based access segmentation across supply chain tiers, and continuous behavioural monitoring of maintenance sessions. The framework is validated through a tabletop exercise with industrial practitioners.

title: Network segmentation strategies for securing legacy OT environments
abstract: Operational technology environments in manufacturing and utility sectors frequently rely on decades-old equipment designed without cybersecurity considerations. Retrofitting strong security controls onto such systems is often impractical, making network segmentation one of the most effective available defences. This paper systematically evaluates five segmentation strategies—air-gapping, DMZ insertion, unidirectional gateways, micro-segmentation using software-defined networking, and VLAN-based isolation—across three representative legacy OT environments modelled after real-world process control architectures. Each strategy is assessed against a standardised threat catalogue derived from known ICS incident reports, covering scenarios such as ransomware propagation, historian server compromise, and remote access exploitation. The evaluation employs a simulation-driven methodology combining network topology modelling with attack path analysis. Results indicate that micro-segmentation combined with unidirectional gateways at critical zone boundaries provides the highest resilience against multi-stage attacks, though at significant configuration complexity. The paper provides a practical scoring matrix to assist security engineers in selecting segmentation approaches based on available resources and operational constraints.

title: Detecting replay attacks on DNP3 protocol in smart grid communications
abstract: DNP3 is a widely deployed communication protocol in smart grid environments, facilitating data exchange between substations, remote terminal units, and control centres. Despite extensions introduced in DNP3 Secure Authentication version 5, many deployments remain vulnerable to replay attacks due to misconfiguration or the use of older protocol variants. This paper presents a lightweight detection mechanism for DNP3 replay attacks based on temporal sequence analysis of application-layer message fields. The proposed detector monitors request-response timing patterns, sequence counter consistency, and message fragment ordering to identify anomalous retransmission behaviour indicative of replay activity. The mechanism is implemented as a passive network probe requiring no modifications to existing field devices. Evaluation on a hardware-in-the-loop smart grid testbed shows that the detector correctly identifies replay attacks with 97.3% precision and 95.8% recall, while maintaining a processing latency below 12 milliseconds per packet—well within operational requirements. The paper further discusses integration of the detector into existing security information and event management pipelines used in utility control centres.

title: Cybersecurity frameworks for critical infrastructure protection: a survey and gap analysis
abstract: Critical infrastructure sectors—including energy, water, transportation, and telecommunications—face an evolving and increasingly sophisticated threat landscape. Numerous cybersecurity frameworks have been developed to guide operators in assessing and improving their security posture, including NIST CSF, IEC 62443, NERC CIP, and ISA/IEC standards. Despite their widespread adoption, significant gaps remain in how these frameworks address emerging challenges such as cloud-connected OT environments, AI-driven attacks, and supply chain interdependencies. This survey systematically reviews twelve major cybersecurity frameworks applicable to critical infrastructure, evaluating them across dimensions of scope, implementation guidance, assessment methodology, and adaptability to ICS-specific threats. A structured gap analysis reveals that most frameworks inadequately address real-time anomaly detection requirements, provide insufficient guidance on IoT integration, and lack concrete metrics for evaluating detection and response effectiveness. The paper proposes a consolidated gap taxonomy and outlines a research agenda addressing the most critical deficiencies. It is intended as a reference for both practitioners implementing security programmes and researchers developing next-generation framework components.

title: Intrusion detection in resource-constrained IoT devices using lightweight recurrent models
abstract: Deploying intrusion detection directly on resource-constrained IoT devices such as microcontroller-based sensors and actuators presents fundamental challenges in terms of memory footprint, computational overhead, and energy consumption. This paper investigates the feasibility of implementing lightweight recurrent neural network models—specifically truncated LSTM and GRU variants—on devices with fewer than 256 KB of RAM. A model compression pipeline is developed that combines quantisation, pruning, and knowledge distillation to reduce model size by up to 94% relative to full-precision baselines, while preserving detection accuracy above 90% across standard IoT attack benchmarks. The compressed models are deployed on three representative IoT platforms and evaluated under realistic workload conditions. Power consumption measurements indicate that continuous on-device inference adds less than 4 mW overhead, making deployment feasible even on battery-powered nodes. The paper also proposes an adaptive inference strategy that dynamically reduces model complexity during high-load periods to prevent resource exhaustion. Results suggest that on-device intrusion detection is practically achievable for a broad class of constrained IoT deployments.

title: Effect of corona and atmospheric plasma pre-treatment on adhesion of water-based barrier coatings to folding boxboard
abstract: Folding boxboard (FBB, 270 g/m²) was pre-treated with corona discharge (dose range: 20–80 W·min/m²) and atmospheric-pressure air plasma (power 400 W, exposure time 0.5–4 s) before application of a water-based styrene–acrylic barrier coating at 10 g/m² add-on. Surface energy components were determined by the Owens–Wendt method using water, formamide, and diiodomethane probe liquids. Cross-cut adhesion tests (ISO 2409), peel force measurements (180° geometry), and WVTR measurements were conducted after coating. Plasma treatment at 2 s exposure raised the polar component of surface energy from 4.1 to 31.7 mJ/m² and reduced subsequent WVTR by 19 % relative to untreated controls, attributable to improved coating uniformity. Corona treatment yielded similar adhesion gains but required at least 60 W·min/m² to achieve equivalent peel forces. Neither treatment altered bulk fibre properties as assessed by zero-span tensile testing.

title: Dimensional stability of offset-printed game cards under controlled humidity cycling: a comparison of three substrates
abstract: Playing-card grade duplex board (280 g/m²), a single-ply chromoboard (300 g/m²), and a laminated grey-core board (320 g/m²) were printed with a standard four-colour offset process and then subjected to humidity cycling between 30 % and 75 % RH at 22 °C in eight-hour half-cycles over ten days. In-plane dimensional change (machine and cross directions), out-of-plane curl index, and surface gloss (75° geometry) were recorded after each cycle. The grey-core laminate exhibited the lowest mean curl index (0.12) and dimensional change (0.11 % in the cross direction), while the single-ply chromoboard showed curl indices reaching 0.41. Ink coverage density had no statistically significant effect on dimensional change (p > 0.05, ANOVA) but was positively correlated with gloss loss in the cross-direction high-humidity phase. These findings carry direct implications for game manufacturers specifying substrates for card components intended for humid climates.

title: Sorption isotherms of microfibrillated cellulose films and their modification by carboxymethylation: measurement and modelling
abstract: Freestanding films of microfibrillated cellulose (MFC) and carboxymethylated MFC (CM-MFC, degree of substitution 0.18 and 0.32) were produced by solvent-casting and their water vapour sorption isotherms measured at 23 °C across eleven relative humidity steps from 11 % to 97 % using a dynamic vapour sorption (DVS) instrument. The Guggenheim–Anderson–De Boer (GAB) model fitted all isotherms satisfactorily (root mean square error < 0.8 %). CM-MFC films showed markedly higher monolayer moisture contents (Wm = 6.4–7.9 g/100 g dry) than unmodified MFC (Wm = 4.1 g/100 g dry), consistent with the introduction of hygroscopic carboxymethyl groups. Tensile testing at each equilibrium humidity point revealed that elastic modulus dropped by 65 % for CM-MFC (DS 0.32) between 43 % and 75 % RH, compared to 38 % for unmodified MFC. The results confirm that although carboxymethylation improves film-forming properties, it substantially compromises mechanical performance in moderately humid environments.

title: Spray-applied nanocellulose-reinforced barrier coatings on recycled paperboard: processing window and moisture-barrier performance
abstract: Cellulose nanocrystals (CNC) at concentrations of 0.5, 1.5, and 3.0 wt% were dispersed in a water-based styrene–acrylic emulsion and applied to recycled testliner (150 g/m²) by ultrasonic spray coating. Processing parameters (spray flow rate, nozzle distance, substrate temperature) were optimised using a Box–Behnken design with WVTR as the response. The optimum condition (flow rate 3.2 mL/min, nozzle distance 15 cm, substrate temperature 55 °C) yielded a WVTR of 31.4 g/m²·24h at 38 °C/90 % RH for the 1.5 wt% CNC formulation, a 29 % reduction relative to CNC-free controls at equivalent add-on (9 g/m²). Atomic force microscopy confirmed increased surface tortuosity at 1.5 wt%, consistent with a tortuous-path diffusion mechanism. At 3.0 wt% CNC, agglomeration degraded coating uniformity and WVTR increased. Contact angle measurements showed no significant loss of hydrophobicity over 14 days of open storage.

title: Oxygen and water vapour barrier properties of bilayer coatings combining polyvinyl alcohol and bio-based polyester dispersions on kraft paper
abstract: Bilayer barrier coatings were prepared by applying a PVA base layer (8 g/m²) followed by a bio-based aliphatic polyester dispersion (BPE) top layer (6 g/m²) on 80 g/m² bleached kraft paper. Single-layer PVA and BPE coatings at equivalent total add-on (14 g/m²) served as references. Oxygen transmission rate (OTR, ISO 15105-2) and WVTR were measured at 23 °C at 50 % and 80 % RH. At 50 % RH the bilayer achieved an OTR of 4.2 cm³/m²·24h·atm, compared to 6.8 for BPE alone and 3.1 for PVA alone. At 80 % RH, PVA single-layer OTR rose sharply to 148 cm³/m²·24h·atm due to plasticisation by moisture, whereas the bilayer retained 18.7 cm³/m²·24h·atm because the BPE top layer limited moisture penetration to the PVA layer. WVTR of the bilayer was 38 % lower than PVA alone at 80 % RH. The bilayer approach offers a feasible path to improving PVA-based systems under high-humidity conditions without resorting to fossil-derived polymers.

title: Activation energy for grain boundary diffusion in Fe–14Cr ODS alloys determined by dilatometric sintering experiments
abstract: Cylindrical compacts of mechanically alloyed Fe–14Cr powder dispersed with 0.35 wt% Y₂O₃ were sintered in a push-rod dilatometer under flowing Ar–5%H₂ between 1050 °C and 1300 °C at heating rates of 2, 5, and 10 K/min. Shrinkage–temperature curves were analysed using the Master Sintering Curve approach. An apparent activation energy of 312 ± 18 kJ/mol was obtained for the dominant densification mechanism, consistent with grain boundary diffusion of chromium in iron. Relative density at 1250 °C reached 96.8% after 60 min isothermal holding. SEM cross-sections showed a bimodal grain size distribution with mean grain diameters of 1.4 µm and 6.2 µm. The Y₂O₃ particles, with a mean diameter of 28 nm as measured by TEM dark-field imaging, remained coherently distributed at grain boundaries. The results provide a quantitative basis for selecting sintering schedules that balance densification against undesirable grain growth.

title: Effect of milling time on oxide dispersion homogeneity and densification behaviour of Fe–18Cr–2W powder compacts
abstract: Fe–18Cr–2W base powder was co-milled with 0.50 wt% Y₂O₃ in a planetary ball mill for 10, 20, 40, and 80 h under Ar atmosphere. Chemical homogeneity of the as-milled powders was assessed by EDS mapping on polished cross-sections; oxygen content was tracked by inert-gas fusion analysis. Extending milling from 40 to 80 h did not further reduce the inter-particle composition range but increased lattice strain from 0.18% to 0.31% as measured by X-ray line broadening. Sintering at 1250 °C for 2 h yielded relative densities of 91.2%, 94.7%, 96.1%, and 96.3% for the four milling conditions. Vickers hardness at room temperature peaked at 410 HV for the 40 h condition. Porosity morphology changed from irregular to rounded between 20 h and 40 h milling, suggesting a transition in the rate-controlling densification mechanism. Results indicate a practical upper limit of approximately 40 h for this composition.

title: Coarsening kinetics of Y₂O₃ dispersoids in sintered Fe–14Cr alloys during isothermal annealing at 900–1100 °C
abstract: Samples of Fe–14Cr–0.35Y₂O₃ sintered to 97% relative density were isothermally annealed for times between 1 h and 200 h at 900, 1000, and 1100 °C. Dispersoid size distributions were measured from TEM bright-field micrographs on at least 300 particles per condition. Mean particle radius followed a t^(1/3) power law consistent with Ostwald ripening controlled by volume diffusion, with an apparent coarsening rate constant of 2.1 × 10⁻³ nm³/s at 1000 °C. Activation energy derived from the temperature dependence was 290 kJ/mol. Above 1000 °C, a fraction of particles larger than 80 nm adopted faceted morphologies indicative of partial dissolution and re-precipitation. Vickers hardness declined from 395 HV to 340 HV over 200 h at 1100 °C, correlating with the increase in mean particle radius from 14 nm to 31 nm. The data are compared with published results for MA957 and PM2000 alloys.

title: Comparison of conventional and spark plasma sintering of Fe–14Cr–0.5Ti–0.35Y₂O₃ ODS alloy
abstract: Mechanically alloyed Fe–14Cr–0.5Ti powder with 0.35 wt% Y₂O₃ was consolidated by conventional vacuum sintering at 1280 °C for 2 h and by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 1150 °C, 50 MPa, with a 5 min dwell. Relative densities were 96.4% and 99.1% for the two routes respectively. EBSD maps revealed a mean grain size of 3.8 µm after conventional sintering and 1.1 µm after SPS. The fine-grained SPS microstructure showed a higher fraction of low-angle grain boundaries (34% vs. 19%). Room-temperature tensile strength was 820 MPa for conventional and 1050 MPa for SPS samples. Compression creep tests at 700 °C and 100 MPa indicated a steady-state creep rate of 8.4 × 10⁻⁸ s⁻¹ for SPS versus 2.1 × 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹ for conventional material. The stress exponent was 6.1 for both, suggesting dislocation climb as the rate-controlling creep mechanism.

title: Porosity evolution during multi-step sintering of Fe–Cr ODS compacts: a quantitative stereological study
abstract: Multi-step sintering schedules for Fe–14Cr–0.35Y₂O₃ compacts were designed with a controlled intermediate hold at 900 °C to suppress grain growth prior to final densification at 1250 °C. Porosity was characterised on polished cross-sections by image analysis at each thermal stage. Total porosity decreased from 18.4% in the green compact to 3.1% after the final step; open porosity closed below 1% at relative densities above 93%. Pore size distributions shifted from a broad range of 0.5–40 µm to a narrow sub-micron population. Three-dimensional pore reconstruction from focused ion beam serial sectioning at the intermediate stage revealed an interconnected network with a tortuosity factor of 2.7. Grain boundary pinning by Y₂O₃ particles maintained a mean grain size below 2 µm throughout densification, in contrast to single-step sintering at 1250 °C which produced grains of 4.5 µm. The multi-step schedule reduced variability in Vickers hardness across the compact cross-section from ±28 HV to ±11 HV.

title: High-temperature tensile creep of spark plasma sintered Fe–14Cr–2W–0.35Y₂O₃ at 650–750 °C
abstract: Spark plasma sintered Fe–14Cr–2W–0.35Y₂O₃ samples with relative density of 99.3% were tested in uniaxial tension at 650, 700, and 750 °C under stresses between 60 and 180 MPa in a controlled Ar atmosphere. Minimum creep rates ranged from 3.2 × 10⁻⁹ s⁻¹ at 60 MPa/650 °C to 4.7 × 10⁻⁶ s⁻¹ at 180 MPa/750 °C. Stress exponents were 5.8 at 650 °C and 5.1 at 750 °C, and the apparent activation energy was 338 kJ/mol, exceeding the self-diffusion activation energy of Fe–14Cr (approximately 270 kJ/mol) and suggesting a threshold stress effect. Threshold stresses of 18, 14, and 9 MPa were estimated at the three temperatures by linear extrapolation of (ε̇)^(1/n) versus stress plots. Post-creep TEM showed subgrain formation and dislocation pile-ups at Y₂O₃ particles. Rupture times at 700 °C/120 MPa exceeded 320 h, comparing favourably with literature data for MA957.

title: Influence of Ti and Hf co-additions on dispersoid chemistry and sintering densification in Fe–14Cr ODS alloys
abstract: Fe–14Cr powders were co-milled with Y₂O₃ and additions of 0.5 wt% Ti, 0.2 wt% Hf, or a combined 0.5 wt% Ti + 0.2 wt% Hf for 40 h. After SPS consolidation at 1150 °C/50 MPa, atom probe tomography was used to characterise the chemical composition of dispersoids in each variant. In the Ti-only alloy, dispersoids were identified as Y–Ti–O nanoclusters with Y:Ti atomic ratios near 1:1.4; the Hf-only variant showed Y–Hf–O particles enriched in Hf at particle cores. The combined addition produced a mixed Y–Ti–Hf–O dispersoid population with a mean radius of 3.8 nm, smaller than either single-addition variant (5.1 nm and 4.6 nm respectively). Number densities reached 4.1 × 10²³ m⁻³ for the combined addition. Relative density after SPS was 99.4% for all variants. Microhardness at 700 °C was highest for the combined alloy at 285 HV. These results suggest that Hf co-addition refines the dispersoid distribution without impairing densification.

title: Grain boundary segregation of Cr and W in sintered Fe–14Cr–2W–0.35Y₂O₃ studied by STEM-EDS and EELS
abstract: Cross-sectional TEM lamellae prepared from Fe–14Cr–2W–0.35Y₂O₃ samples sintered at 1250 °C for 2 h were examined using aberration-corrected STEM combined with EDS mapping and EELS at individual grain boundaries. Cr enrichment of 2.1–3.8 at% above the bulk composition was measured at general high-angle boundaries; low-angle boundaries showed no statistically significant enrichment. W was detected at grain boundaries adjacent to Y₂O₃ particles at concentrations up to 1.9 at%, suggesting co-segregation driven by elastic misfit. EELS O K-edge spectra confirmed stoichiometric Y₂O₃ at particles away from boundaries, while particles at triple junctions showed a modified spectral signature consistent with partial Y–Fe–O phase formation. Grain boundary segregation profiles fitted to McLean-type isotherms gave segregation enthalpies of −42 kJ/mol for Cr and −61 kJ/mol for W. These values are discussed in terms of their implications for grain boundary embrittlement at intermediate temperatures.

title: Effect of Metallic Grain Silos on Short-Range Propagation at UHF Frequencies
abstract: Steel grain silos are common features of large-scale farms in Central and Eastern Europe and act as strong specular and diffuse scatterers at UHF frequencies. This study characterises the scattering signature of cylindrical steel silos with diameters of 6 m and 12 m and heights between 10 m and 24 m, using scaled physical models and full-scale outdoor measurements at 868 MHz. Physical-optics simulations were performed using a commercial electromagnetic solver and compared against measured bistatic radar cross-section data. For a single 12 m diameter silo, the shadow region shows a 12–18 dB signal deficit relative to free-space conditions at distances of 20–80 m beyond the structure. Cluster-silo arrangements of four silos spaced 5 m apart produce additional multipath components with delay spreads up to 85 ns. The results are compiled into a set of correction factors applicable to standard propagation models used in sensor network link-budget calculations.

title: Seasonal Variation of Ground Dielectric Properties and Its Impact on Surface-Wave Propagation in Vojvodina Farmland
abstract: Surface-wave contributions to received signal power are sensitive to soil permittivity and conductivity, both of which vary substantially across agricultural seasons. This study presents twelve months of continuous soil moisture and temperature measurements at two depths (5 cm and 30 cm) on a test plot near Futog, alongside co-located propagation measurements at 169 MHz and 868 MHz. Soil complex permittivity was inferred from time-domain reflectometry probes and validated against gravimetric samples. At 169 MHz the surface-wave component contributes measurably to received power at ranges below 300 m during spring thaw and post-harvest irrigation periods, with signal-level variations of up to 6 dB attributable solely to soil-state changes. At 868 MHz the surface-wave term is negligible beyond 50 m under all conditions. A seasonal correction table is derived for use with the Irregular Terrain Model adapted for flat plains.

title: Link Budget Analysis for LoRa-Based Soil Sensor Networks on Large Arable Farms
abstract: LoRa physical-layer technology has attracted attention for precision agriculture owing to its long range and low power consumption. However, published link budgets typically assume open-field conditions and do not account for the cluttered near-ground environments common on operational farms. This chapter reviews propagation constraints specific to arable farming contexts: vegetation attenuation, terrain micro-relief, and scattering from farm infrastructure. Using empirical path loss data collected on three farms in the Bačka region totalling 4800 individual link measurements, revised link-budget worksheets are derived for three LoRa spreading factors (SF7, SF10, SF12) at 868 MHz with antenna heights of 1 m at the sensor and 6 m at the gateway. The analysis shows that SF12 provides reliable coverage up to 1.8 km under worst-case crop conditions, compared with 3.5 km quoted under flat open-air assumptions. The chapter also discusses gateway placement optimisation and the role of site surveying in deployment planning.

title: Polarisation Diversity Performance of a Compact Dual-Polarised Patch Antenna for Agricultural LoRaWAN Gateways
abstract: Gateway antennas for agricultural LPWAN installations are often mounted on existing farm structures at heights that introduce significant mutual coupling with metallic surroundings. This paper describes the design, simulation, and measurement of a compact dual-polarised microstrip patch antenna operating at 868 MHz, intended for flush or near-flush mounting on steel grain silos. The antenna was designed in HFSS with a 4 mm thick Rogers 4003C substrate and a slot-coupled feed arrangement to achieve port isolation above 28 dB. Prototype fabrication and anechoic-chamber characterisation confirmed a peak gain of 4.1 dBi on each port with cross-polar discrimination above 22 dB across the 3 dB beamwidth. Field trials at two silo installations showed a 4.6 dB median improvement in received SNR at sensor nodes in the silo shadow region when using polarisation-diversity combining at the gateway, compared with a single-polarisation reference.
