title: LMS Log Data as a Proxy for Learner Engagement in Technical Adult Courses: Possibilities and Limitations
abstract: Learning management systems generate detailed interaction logs that are increasingly used as indicators of learner engagement. This study assessed whether log-derived metrics—session frequency, resource access counts, forum contributions, and quiz attempt patterns—could predict knowledge transfer outcomes in a 12-week technical adult course delivered via Moodle at two Serbian employers. The dataset comprised 143 learners and 2.7 million log events. Regression analysis showed that session frequency (β=0.28, p<0.01) and repeated quiz attempts (β=0.19, p<0.05) significantly predicted post-training TKTS scores, but together explained only 19% of variance, indicating that log data captures a limited portion of the learning process. Resource access counts were not predictive after controlling for session frequency. The paper argues for combining log analytics with periodic self-report data rather than relying on logs alone, and proposes a data collection protocol compatible with GDPR constraints applicable in Serbian industry contexts.

title: Designing Assessment Rubrics for Competency-Based IT Retraining Programmes: Lessons from a Cross-Sector Pilot
abstract: This paper reports on a 14-month action research cycle in which assessment rubrics were developed, implemented, and iteratively revised for three IT retraining programmes targeting adult workers transitioning from non-IT sectors. The programmes were delivered in partnership with two training providers in Vojvodina and covered topics including database administration basics, network configuration, and software testing. A rubric design team comprising instructional designers, subject-matter experts, and HR representatives collaboratively authored dimension definitions and anchor descriptors. Rubrics were piloted with 94 participants; inter-rater reliability testing (using Cohen's weighted kappa) between trainer pairs ranged from κ=0.58 to κ=0.74 across dimensions, with procedural accuracy dimensions scoring most consistently. Post-pilot revision reduced ambiguous descriptors by 37% as rated by a blind review panel. The study highlights the central role of anchor examples drawn from authentic work tasks in achieving rater alignment, and provides a rubric template adaptable to other technical domains.

title: Supervisor Involvement in Pre- and Post-Training Activities: Effect on Knowledge Application in Technical Workplaces
abstract: Transfer of training research consistently identifies workplace environment as a stronger predictor of knowledge application than training design variables. This study examined the specific contribution of direct supervisor involvement—operationalised as pre-training briefing, goal-setting conversations, and post-training debriefs—to knowledge transfer outcomes among 167 employees completing mandatory safety and technical update courses at industrial firms in Novi Sad, Zrenjanin, and Kikinda. A three-group design compared workers whose supervisors received structured involvement prompts (n=58), those whose supervisors received only informational materials (n=54), and a no-intervention control (n=55). Six-week follow-up TKTS scores were significantly higher in the structured prompt group (M=3.61, SD=0.52) compared to control (M=3.14, SD=0.59; t(111)=4.87, p<0.001). Effect size was moderate (d=0.84). Cost analysis estimated that the supervisor preparation materials required approximately 45 minutes per cohort to administer, suggesting a favourable effort-to-outcome ratio for routine deployment in industrial training programmes.

title: Aligning Micro-Credential Course Architecture with National Qualifications Framework Levels: A Practitioner's Guide for Serbian Training Providers
abstract: The Serbian National Qualifications Framework (SNQF) provides eight reference levels, but published guidance on how short non-formal courses should map their learning outcomes to these levels remains sparse. This preprint presents a step-by-step workflow developed and tested with six training providers in the ICT and construction sectors during 2024–2025. The workflow includes an outcome statement audit, a level-descriptor comparison matrix, an evidence documentation template, and a gap-closure planning sheet. Three providers completed the full workflow and submitted micro-credential programmes for SNQF referencing; two received recognition at level 4 and one at level 5. Feedback from accreditation reviewers at the National Qualifications Agency is included as anonymised commentary. The guide is intended as a working document for practitioners and will be revised following a broader consultation planned for late 2025.

title: Capillary-driven flow transitions in rectangular microchannels etched in borosilicate glass
abstract: This study characterises the spontaneous imbibition of aqueous glycerol solutions in rectangular microchannels with cross-sections ranging from 20 × 50 µm to 100 × 200 µm, etched by wet chemical methods in borosilicate glass substrates. The Lucas–Washburn equation is tested against measured meniscus advance rates for channels of three aspect ratios and five glycerol concentrations (0–40 wt%). Deviations from the classical square-root-of-time dependence are observed for channels narrower than 40 µm and rationalised through a modified friction factor that accounts for corner flow contributions. Contact angles were determined by the captive-bubble method at 25 °C and ranged from 14° to 31° depending on surface pre-treatment with piranha solution. The results provide a calibration dataset for designing passive-pumping sections in early lab-on-chip architectures and highlight the sensitivity of imbibition kinetics to residual organic contamination on glass walls.

title: Formation of monodisperse water-in-oil droplets in a glass co-flow capillary device
abstract: A co-axial glass capillary device was fabricated by nesting a tapered inner capillary (tip diameter 40–120 µm) inside a square outer capillary (500 µm side). Deionised water was pumped through the inner capillary into a continuous phase of mineral oil containing 2 wt% Span 80 surfactant. Droplet diameter and generation frequency were measured optically as functions of inner flow rate (0.1–2.0 µL/min), outer flow rate (2–20 µL/min), and tip diameter. At capillary numbers Ca < 0.01 for the outer phase, dripping was the dominant regime and produced droplets with coefficients of variation below 3.5 %. Jetting onset was mapped across a Ca–flow-rate-ratio plane. Droplet diameter correlated with the ratio of inner to outer volumetric flow rates to the power of 0.38, consistent with published scaling laws. The dataset was used to establish operating windows for subsequent electrowetting experiments.

title: Electrowetting-on-dielectric actuation of sessile water droplets on parylene-C coated ITO electrodes
abstract: Sessile droplets of deionised water (0.1–10 µL) were placed on indium tin oxide electrodes coated with 2 µm of parylene-C as the dielectric layer, with an additional hydrophobic fluoropolymer top coat. Contact angle changes were recorded by side-view imaging under applied DC voltages of 0–80 V. The Lippmann–Young equation described the response accurately up to 55 V, beyond which contact-angle saturation set in at a static value near 50°. Dielectric breakdown was not observed below 100 V for parylene-C thicknesses ≥ 1.8 µm. Droplet sliding on tilted substrates was achieved at voltages ≥ 30 V for inclinations above 7°. The charge trapping effect was quantified by comparing advancing and receding contact angle hysteresis before and after ten actuation cycles. Parylene-C is proposed as a practical dielectric for EWOD devices fabricated without clean-room lithography.

title: Droplet splitting and merging in a planar EWOD array: timing, voltage sequences, and volume reproducibility
abstract: A planar digital microfluidic device with a 4 × 8 array of square electrodes (2 mm pitch) was fabricated on printed circuit board substrates coated with SU-8 dielectric and Teflon AF hydrophobic layers. Droplets of 1–5 µL of 10 mM KCl solution were manipulated in a silicone oil filler medium. Splitting was achieved by activating two flanking electrodes simultaneously while deactivating the central electrode; success rate was 98 % for 2 µL droplets but fell to 71 % for 1 µL droplets, attributed to increased line tension effects at smaller scales. Merging of two 1 µL droplets required actuation sequences of 80 ms per step at 60 V. Volume reproducibility of split daughter droplets was ±2.8 % (n = 50). A finite-element model of electric-field distribution in the device reproduced the splitting force to within 15 %. Results define practical design rules for digital microfluidic sample preparation.

title: PDMS flow-focusing junction for controlled generation of sub-100 µm droplets: fabrication tolerances and size prediction
abstract: Soft-lithography replicas in polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) of flow-focusing junctions were fabricated from SU-8 masters. Orifice widths of 25, 40, and 60 µm were tested. The continuous phase was fluorinated oil FC-40 containing 0.5 wt% perfluoropolyether-based surfactant; the dispersed phase was deionised water. Droplet diameters between 18 and 95 µm were produced by varying flow rate ratios from 5:1 to 25:1 (continuous:dispersed). A power-law fit to diameter versus flow-rate ratio gave exponents of −0.29 to −0.34 across orifice sizes, with R² > 0.97. Channel dimension reproducibility across five separately cast devices showed ±3 µm variation, leading to ±6 % variation in mean droplet diameter at fixed flow conditions. Oxygen plasma bonding quality was assessed by burst-pressure tests; bonds sustained pressures up to 180 kPa without delamination. The work provides a practical calibration procedure applicable when photolithography resolution is limited.

title: Thermal effects on EWOD actuation: contact-angle response and dielectric properties of parylene-C between 5 °C and 60 °C
abstract: EWOD devices using parylene-C dielectric layers were characterised over a temperature range of 5–60 °C to assess suitability for temperature-controlled biochemical assays. The static contact angle of water on fluoropolymer-coated parylene-C decreased from 112° at 5 °C to 101° at 60 °C in the absence of applied voltage, consistent with a linear temperature coefficient of −0.18 °/°C. The threshold voltage for droplet motion on a tilted substrate (10° inclination) increased by approximately 4 V over the same range, attributed to a decrease in dielectric constant from 3.12 to 2.87. Impedance spectroscopy at 1 kHz showed a 7 % reduction in capacitance per unit area. No irreversible degradation of the parylene-C layer was observed after 20 thermal cycles between 5 °C and 60 °C. A correction factor for the Lippmann–Young equation incorporating the measured temperature dependence is proposed.

title: Open digital microfluidics on a hydrophobic-patterned substrate: droplet dispensing from a reservoir without a top plate
abstract: This work examines the dispensing and transport of droplets in an open (single-plate) EWOD configuration, eliminating the top ground plate used in conventional sandwich devices. Hydrophilic anchoring sites were patterned by selective UV–ozone treatment of a Teflon AF coating to confine droplets during voltage-off states. Droplets of 0.8–3 µL of phosphate-buffered saline were dispensed from a 20 µL reservoir by activating a sequence of three 2 mm electrodes adjacent to the reservoir. Complete separation from the reservoir required 1.2–1.5 s at 70 V for droplets ≥ 1 µL. Evaporation rate in the open configuration at 25 °C and 40 % relative humidity was measured at 3.2 nL/s for a 2 µL droplet, reaching 5 % volume loss in approximately 300 s; a mineral oil overlay reduced this to below 0.5 % loss over the same period. The configuration simplifies optical access and is suitable for coupling with overhead fluorescence detection.

title: Sequential alkaline extraction of arabinoxylan from oat hulls: yield, substitution degree, and monosaccharide composition
abstract: Arabinoxylan (AX) was extracted from dehulled oat (Avena sativa L., cv. Nikola) hulls using stepwise NaOH treatment at 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0 M concentrations. Extraction yield ranged from 4.1 to 11.8 g per 100 g dry hull depending on alkali concentration, with the 1.0 M fraction giving the highest purity (87.3% AX by Megazyme assay). Arabinose-to-xylose (A/X) ratios determined by HPAEC-PAD were 0.61, 0.54, and 0.48 for the three fractions respectively, indicating progressive de-substitution with stronger alkali. Ferulic acid content, measured by HPLC-DAD after saponification, decreased from 2.3 to 0.7 mg g⁻¹ across fractions. Molecular weight (Mw) by SEC-RI coupling ranged between 185 and 412 kDa. Results confirm that alkali concentration controls both the structural and molecular character of recovered AX, with consequences for downstream functional performance.

title: Viscometric behaviour of mixed oat arabinoxylan–beta-glucan solutions: shear rate dependence and temperature effects
abstract: Solutions of isolated oat hull arabinoxylan (AX, Mw 312 kDa, A/X 0.58) and oat bran beta-glucan (BG, Mw 447 kDa) were prepared individually and as binary mixtures at total polysaccharide concentrations of 0.5, 1.0, and 2.0% (w/v). Apparent viscosity was measured on a Haake RotoVisco rotational viscometer over a shear rate range of 0.1–100 s⁻¹ at 20, 37, and 60 °C. Both pure fractions exhibited shear-thinning behaviour above 1.0% concentration. In binary mixtures at 1:1 mass ratio, apparent viscosity at 37 °C and 10 s⁻¹ was 18% higher than predicted by additive behaviour, suggesting weak synergistic interaction. Power-law fitting gave flow behaviour indices (n) of 0.72–0.88 across conditions. Activation energy of flow calculated from Arrhenius plots was 12.4 kJ mol⁻¹ for AX and 16.1 kJ mol⁻¹ for BG solutions. Mixture rheology data are discussed in the context of bolus viscosity in the upper gastrointestinal tract.

title: Prebiotic potential of oat hull arabinoxylan fractions assessed by in vitro batch fermentation with human faecal inoculum
abstract: Four AX fractions from oat hull differing in Mw (89, 185, 312, and 498 kDa) and A/X ratio (0.42–0.68) were subjected to simulated in vitro batch fermentation using pooled human faecal inoculum from four healthy adult donors. Fermentation was conducted at 37 °C for 4, 8, 16, and 24 h in phosphate-buffered medium. Short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) profiles were determined by GC-FID; bacterial enumeration used qPCR targeting Bifidobacterium spp., Lactobacillus spp., and Clostridium coccoides–Eubacterium rectale group. Total SCFA production at 24 h ranged from 28.4 to 51.7 mmol L⁻¹ across fractions. The 312 kDa fraction showed the highest prebiotic index (PI = 3.14, calculated per Palframan formula) and the greatest Bifidobacterium enrichment (2.4-log increase vs. negative control). A/X ratio and Mw together accounted for 78% of variance in PI by multiple regression. The 89 kDa fraction was almost completely fermented by 8 h, limiting bifidogenic effect.

title: Effect of extrusion pre-treatment on extractability and molecular weight of beta-glucan from spelt hulls
abstract: Spelt hulls were subjected to twin-screw extrusion at barrel temperatures of 100, 130, and 160 °C and a screw speed of 180 rpm prior to aqueous extraction of beta-glucan. Extraction yield, Mw by SEC-MALS, and apparent viscosity at 1% solution concentration were compared against unextruded controls. Extraction yield increased from 0.9% (control) to 2.1% at 130 °C, but decreased to 1.6% at 160 °C due to partial thermal degradation. Mw dropped progressively from 318 kDa (control) to 204 kDa (160 °C treatment). Intrinsic viscosity followed the same trend (3.4 to 2.1 dL g⁻¹). In vitro batch fermentation (24 h, faecal inoculum) showed that the 130 °C extrusion-derived fraction maintained a PI of 2.81 versus 2.96 for the control, suggesting that moderate Mw reduction did not substantially impair prebiotic activity. Data presented at the 11th International Symposium on Cereal Bioactives.

title: Comparative characterisation of dietary fibre fractions from hulled and de-hulled oat varieties: structural, physicochemical, and fermentability differences
abstract: Hull fractions from four hulled (H1–H4) and two commercially de-hulled (D1–D2) oat varieties were extracted and characterised for total dietary fibre (AOAC method 991.43), AX content (phloroglucinol-HCl after hydrolysis), beta-glucan content (Megazyme kit), Mw by SEC-MALS, and apparent viscosity (1% solution, 37 °C, 10 s⁻¹). Hulled variety H3 gave the highest combined AX+BG content (21.4 g 100 g⁻¹ total dietary fibre), an AX/BG ratio of 3.8, and a mean Mw of 287 kDa for the mixed extract. In vitro fermentation (24 h) yielded PI values of 2.6–3.4 across all varieties, with hulled varieties outperforming de-hulled ones on average by 0.5 PI units. Correlation analysis across all varieties confirmed that AX/BG ratio (r = 0.74) and Mw (r = 0.68) were independent positive predictors of PI. These results assist variety selection for fibre-enriched cereal product development.

title: Influence of particle size reduction by ball milling on arabinoxylan extractability and viscometric behaviour in oat hull fractions
abstract: Oat hulls were ball-milled for 10, 30, 60, and 120 min at 400 rpm before extraction of arabinoxylan with 1.0 M NaOH. Particle size distribution of milled material was characterised by laser diffraction (d₅₀ reduced from 312 to 48 µm at 120 min). AX extraction yield increased monotonically from 9.4% (unmilled) to 14.7% (120 min), while Mw by SEC-MALS decreased from 308 to 201 kDa and A/X ratio was unchanged at 0.55–0.58 across all milling times. Apparent viscosity at 37 °C and 10 s⁻¹ (1% solution) fell from 84 to 38 mPa·s, consistent with Mw reduction. In vitro fermentation showed PI declined from 2.98 (unmilled) to 2.41 (120 min milling). A 30 min milling time represented a practical optimum, increasing yield by 28% while reducing Mw by only 12% and PI by less than 5%. Findings inform mechanical pre-processing strategies for hull-derived AX production.

title: AX/BG ratio as a predictor of prebiotic index across hull fractions from seven cereal species: a multivariate analysis
abstract: Hull fractions from oat, spelt, barley, rye, einkorn, emmer, and Khorasan wheat were characterised for AX content, BG content, AX/BG ratio, total dietary fibre, Mw (SEC-MALS), and A/X ratio. All fractions were subjected to 24 h in vitro batch fermentation with pooled faecal inoculum (n = 5 donors). Prebiotic index ranged from 1.84 (barley hull) to 3.41 (oat hull). Pearson correlations identified AX/BG ratio (r = 0.82, p < 0.01) and AX Mw (r = 0.77, p < 0.01) as the strongest positive predictors of PI, while BG Mw showed a weaker positive association (r = 0.54, p = 0.04). A stepwise linear regression model including AX/BG ratio and AX Mw explained 81% of PI variance (adjusted R² = 0.81). Principal component analysis separated oat and spelt hulls from other species along a PC1 axis dominated by AX content and Mw. Results support the use of structural parameters as screening tools for prebiotic functionality across diverse cereal hulls.

title: Compressed Version Vectors for Causal Consistency in Wide-Area Replication
abstract: Version vectors grow linearly with the number of replicas, making them impractical for deployments with hundreds of nodes. This paper proposes a bitmap-based compression scheme that reduces per-message vector overhead by representing contiguous causal histories as range tokens. We implement the scheme inside a prototype key-value store built on top of a modified Erlang/OTP release handler, and evaluate it on a five-site testbed spanning three continents using Yahoo Cloud Serving Benchmark workloads. With 64 replicas, compressed vectors consume 61% less bandwidth than standard version vectors while introducing a median decoding overhead of 1.3 µs per operation. Causal consistency violations, measured by replaying operation logs against a reference checker, remain at zero across 12 million client operations. The trade-off between compression ratio and worst-case decode time is characterised analytically, and guidelines for choosing the compression window are derived from the experimental results.

title: A Benchmark Suite for Causal Consistency Checkers in Eventually-Consistent Stores
abstract: Testing whether a distributed data store truly enforces causal consistency requires workloads that expose subtle ordering violations that do not appear under simple read-your-writes scenarios. We present CausalBench, a benchmark suite of 14 parameterised workload generators targeting concurrency patterns known to stress causality enforcement: write skew, missing update, and phantom causal cycle. Each generator is accompanied by an oracle derived from happens-before axioms. We apply CausalBench to three open-source eventually-consistent stores and find that two of them exhibit causal violations under specific client session patterns that their test suites do not cover. The benchmark is released as open-source and is designed to integrate with standard cluster deployment tools. Runtime of the full suite on a three-node cluster is under eight minutes, making it suitable for continuous integration pipelines.

title: Hybrid Logical Clocks Under Asymmetric Network Delay: An Empirical Analysis
abstract: Hybrid logical clocks (HLCs) combine physical time with a logical counter to produce timestamps that are both causally correct and close to wall-clock time. Their behaviour under asymmetric network delay—common in continental and intercontinental links—has not been systematically studied. We instrument an HLC implementation in a distributed object store and inject synthetic delay asymmetries ranging from 10 ms to 400 ms using a traffic shaping framework. We measure clock drift, maximum offset from reference UTC, and the frequency of logical counter increments as a function of asymmetry ratio and message rate. At 200 ms one-way asymmetry and 5 000 operations per second, HLC physical components drift by up to 47 ms from NTP-synchronised wall time, while the logical component absorbs the remainder correctly. We compare three published HLC variants and show that one variant's drift bound proof does not hold when NTP correction pulses are delayed. Practical recommendations for deployment in intercontinental settings are provided.

title: Dotted Version Vectors Revisited: Garbage Collection and Scalability
abstract: Dotted version vectors were introduced to solve the sibling explosion problem in bucket-based replicated stores. However, the original garbage collection protocol requires a full-mesh coordination round that stalls under node failures. We analyse the original protocol's liveness properties under asynchronous failure models and identify two scenarios in which the GC round never completes. We then propose a modified GC protocol that uses a stable vector derived from the minimum observed dot set across a quorum, avoiding the need for all-to-all coordination. Correctness is argued through an invariant proof using TLA+; the full specification (470 lines) is made publicly available. We implement the modified protocol in a two-thousand-line Rust library and run it on a six-node cluster under Jepsen-style fault injection. The modified protocol completes GC cycles in all tested failure scenarios, with a median cycle latency of 210 ms versus a 1 400 ms timeout failure rate of 23% in the original.

title: Causality in Multi-Master Database Replication: A Practitioner's Survey
abstract: Multi-master replication has been commercially deployed for decades, yet causality enforcement remains inconsistently specified and implemented across products and open-source systems. This chapter surveys causality-related mechanisms in eight multi-master architectures, covering both relational and document-oriented systems. We categorise mechanisms along four axes: clock substrate (physical, logical, or hybrid), granularity of causal tracking (key, session, or operation), garbage collection strategy, and conflict resolution policy. For each combination we describe at least one concrete deployed system and identify published or empirically observed anomalies. The chapter closes with a taxonomy of open problems, including the interaction between causality enforcement and row-level security policies, and the challenge of maintaining causal metadata across schema migrations.

title: Interval Tree Clocks with Bounded Identifier Space for Resource-Constrained Devices
abstract: Interval tree clocks (ITCs) allow dynamic join and leave of participants without coordinator involvement, making them attractive for sensor networks where nodes are added and removed frequently. The original formulation does not bound the identifier space, which grows with the number of fork operations and can exhaust memory on microcontrollers. We propose a rebinding operation that rebalances the identifier tree when it exceeds a configurable size threshold, and prove that rebinding preserves the partial order on events. We implement the bounded ITC in C with a 4 KB memory footprint and deploy it on STM32-based sensor nodes in a laboratory building monitoring scenario. Over a 30-day trial with 22 nodes and approximately 800 000 events, the identifier tree never exceeded 3.2 KB, and no causality violations were detected by an offline checker processing the event log.

title: Measuring Staleness in Geo-Distributed Key-Value Stores: Metrics and a Continuous Monitoring Tool
abstract: Eventual consistency guarantees convergence but provides no bound on staleness in practice; actual staleness depends on network topology, load, and replication implementation. We define three operational staleness metrics—version lag, wall-clock lag, and causal depth lag—and implement a non-intrusive monitoring agent that injects tracer key-value pairs and tracks their propagation across replicas. The agent imposes less than 0.4% additional write load and 0.1% read load in our tests. We deploy the tool against a three-region key-value store deployment and record staleness distributions over 72-hour windows under varying load. Version lag follows a heavy-tailed distribution with a 99th percentile of 2.1 seconds at moderate load, rising to 11.4 seconds at 90% capacity. We release the monitoring agent as open-source and describe its integration with a standard time-series alerting stack.

title: Building a Sentiment-Annotated Corpus for Serbian Online News: Design Decisions and Inter-Annotator Agreement
abstract: The paper describes the construction of SentiNoviSad-News, a 180,000-token corpus of online news texts from five Serbian web portals, manually annotated for sentiment polarity at the sentence level. Three trained annotators applied a five-point scale (strongly negative to strongly positive) with a neutral category. Inter-annotator agreement was measured using Krippendorff's alpha, yielding a mean of 0.61 across the three annotation pairs, with the lowest agreement observed in sentences containing irony markers. The authors discuss specific challenges arising from Serbian morphological complexity, including clitic placement and negation scope, which affect polarity assignment differently than in analytically structured languages. A subset of 12,000 sentences was subsequently used to train and evaluate a baseline Naive Bayes classifier, achieving 71.3% accuracy on a held-out test set. The corpus design, annotation guidelines, and inter-annotator disagreement cases are described in detail to support replication.

title: Evaluative Adjectives in Serbian Political Commentary: Corpus Evidence for Semantic Drift 2000–2015
abstract: This study tracks the semantic trajectories of thirty-two evaluative adjectives in a longitudinal corpus of Serbian political commentary spanning 2000 to 2015, totalling approximately 9.1 million tokens. The corpus was compiled from digitised archives of four Belgrade and Novi Sad newspapers. Using distributional semantic modelling with word2vec (skip-gram, window size 5, 300 dimensions), the authors compute cosine similarity between decade-internal semantic neighbourhoods of each target adjective and quantify directional shifts in collocational profile. Fourteen of the thirty-two adjectives show statistically significant neighbourhood drift (p < 0.05 after Bonferroni correction). Qualitative analysis of the most shifted items reveals a pattern of pejoration linked to political discourse polarisation after 2008. The paper situates its findings within established accounts of evaluative language change in post-transitional societies and identifies methodological limitations of applying distributional models to diachronic journalistic data of moderate size.

title: Negation and Sentiment Reversal in Serbian: Rule-Based vs. Machine Learning Approaches
abstract: Negation poses consistent problems for sentiment classifiers in morphologically rich languages. This paper compares two approaches to handling negation in Serbian news sentences: a hand-crafted rule-based system encoding morphosyntactic negation patterns derived from the Serbian Reference Grammar, and a bidirectional LSTM classifier trained on the SentiNoviSad-News corpus. Experiments were conducted on a 9,400-sentence evaluation set, 23% of which contained negated sentiment expressions. The rule-based system achieves 67.8% F1 on negated sentences but degrades on long-distance negation (more than three tokens between negation marker and target). The LSTM model achieves 74.2% F1 on the same subset when trained with negation-augmented examples. Error analysis identifies impersonal constructions and rhetorical questions as the main remaining failure modes for both systems. The paper recommends a hybrid pipeline for production use and releases the evaluation set under a Creative Commons licence.

title: Lexical Ambiguity in Automated Genre Classification of Serbian Press Texts
abstract: Genre classification of Serbian newspaper articles is complicated by shared vocabulary across news report, commentary, and interview genres. This chapter examines how lexical ambiguity—specifically nouns and verbs that carry both descriptive and evaluative senses depending on genre context—affects the performance of three text classification models: a TF-IDF support vector machine, a fastText model, and a fine-tuned multilingual BERT variant. The study uses a 45,000-article corpus annotated for genre by editorial staff of two Serbian online portals. Accuracy figures for the three models are 81.4%, 84.7%, and 88.9% respectively on a balanced test set of 4,500 articles. The chapter analyses the 200 most frequent misclassified articles and shows that 61% involve at least one high-ambiguity lemma in a topic-prominent position. Implications for the preprocessing and feature-engineering choices in Serbian NLP pipelines are discussed, and a list of 94 high-ambiguity lemmas is provided as an appendix.

title: A Comparative Study of Sentiment Lexicons for Serbian: Coverage, Polarity Consistency, and Domain Sensitivity
abstract: Four existing sentiment lexicons with Serbian-language coverage are systematically compared: two derived by automatic translation from English resources, one compiled manually by a Croatian team and adapted for Serbian orthography, and one developed in-house at the University of Novi Sad. Coverage is assessed against a 500,000-token news corpus; polarity consistency is measured by comparing polarity labels for the 2,300 lemmas present in all four resources. Agreement on polarity label reaches only 58.4% across all four resources for the shared lemma set, with the largest divergences in political and economic vocabulary. Domain sensitivity is evaluated by tracking how each lexicon performs as a feature source in a logistic regression classifier trained on three domain-specific sub-corpora: crime reporting, economic news, and sports commentary. No single lexicon dominates across all three domains. The paper recommends ensemble weighting strategies and provides quantitative diagnostics to guide lexicon selection for downstream tasks.

title: Cross-Register Stability of Sentiment Scores in Serbian: News, Social Media, and Institutional Reports
abstract: Sentiment classifiers trained on one register frequently degrade when applied to another. This preprint investigates the extent of that degradation for Serbian by training identical logistic regression and transformer-based models on three registers separately and evaluating each on the other two. Registers are represented by corpora of comparable size: 95,000 sentences of newspaper text, 87,000 sentences of public Facebook page posts from verified news outlet accounts, and 42,000 sentences from published annual reports of Serbian public institutions. Accuracy drops of 8–19 percentage points are observed in cross-register evaluation, with the largest drop from social media to institutional text. Feature analysis identifies modal verbs and discourse particles as the primary sources of register-specific divergence in polarity signal. The paper proposes a lightweight domain-adaptation step using 500 annotated target-register sentences that recovers 60–70% of the accuracy loss. Code and evaluation data are available on the authors' institutional repository.

title: Measured natural frequencies of lightweight steel-joist floors in residential buildings: a database from northern Serbia
abstract: This paper reports fundamental natural frequency measurements from 24 lightweight steel-joist composite floor panels in six residential buildings constructed between 2002 and 2008 in the Vojvodina region. Floor panels ranged from 4.2 m to 7.8 m in span, with composite concrete topping thicknesses of 60–90 mm. Ambient vibration testing was performed using a four-channel accelerometer array and a 24-bit data-acquisition unit; frequency response functions were estimated via the peak-picking method. Measured fundamental frequencies ranged from 5.8 Hz to 14.3 Hz, with a mean of 9.1 Hz and a coefficient of variation of 0.21. Predicted frequencies from simplified analytical formulas specified in European practice overestimated measured values by an average of 12.4%, with the discrepancy correlating moderately with panel aspect ratio. The dataset is made available as a supplementary file and is intended to support calibration of probabilistic floor frequency models.

title: Probabilistic characterisation of occupant-induced floor loads in open-plan office buildings
abstract: Occupancy-induced loads on composite floors in open-plan offices exhibit significant spatial and temporal variability that is poorly captured by deterministic design values. This paper presents a statistical characterisation of floor loads derived from a monitoring campaign conducted over 14 months in three office buildings in Novi Sad. Distributed live loads were inferred from a combination of pressure-mat sensor grids and periodic manual occupancy counts. Measurements yielded time-averaged areal load intensities between 0.18 and 0.54 kN/m², with the 95th percentile reaching 0.71 kN/m². The data are modelled using a Gamma distribution, and parameters are estimated by maximum likelihood. Autocorrelation of the load process in time is described by an exponential decay model with a correlation length of approximately 3.5 days. The characterised load model is intended for use within time-variant reliability formulations for serviceability assessment, and the parameter estimates are compared with assumptions embedded in Eurocode 1 National Annex values for Serbia.

title: Calibration of serviceability limit state criteria for vibration in composite floors using FORM and Monte Carlo simulation
abstract: Current serviceability limit state criteria for vibration in composite floors are expressed as deterministic bounds on weighted peak acceleration. This paper reformulates these criteria within a reliability framework and calibrates target reliability indices against observed rates of occupant complaints reported in a survey of 11 buildings. First-order reliability method (FORM) and direct Monte Carlo simulation with 10⁶ samples are both applied, and results are compared to assess the adequacy of linearisation. The principal random variables considered are floor natural frequency, modal damping ratio, effective mass, and walking force amplitude. The FORM results agree with Monte Carlo estimates to within 4% for the cases studied. A target reliability index of β = 1.5 over a 50-year reference period is found to correspond to a complaint probability of approximately 8%, consistent with widely cited acceptability thresholds. Sensitivity factors indicate that modal damping ratio contributes the largest share of response variance (38–44%), followed by walking force amplitude (29–33%).

title: Load combination rules for simultaneous gravity and vibration serviceability checks in lightweight steel floors
abstract: Design standards treat gravity ultimate limit state and vibration serviceability checks as independent verifications, yet the load cases that govern each check are not independent: a heavier floor imposed load increases structural mass, which lowers natural frequency and affects vibration response. This paper investigates whether current load combination rules in European standards are consistent when applied simultaneously to gravity strength and vibration serviceability objectives. A series of Monte Carlo experiments, each with 5×10⁵ trials, is conducted for floor panels with spans of 5, 6.5, and 8 m. Random variables include dead load, imposed load, frequency, damping, and walking force. Results show that the load combination factor ψ₁ = 0.5 for office imposed loads tends to underestimate the co-occurrence probability of both limit state exceedances by a factor of 1.4–2.1 in the parameter space studied. Revised combination factors are proposed together with an assessment of their sensitivity to the assumed correlation between imposed load intensity and floor occupancy density.

title: Influence of non-structural elements on the dynamic properties of composite steel-concrete floors: experimental evidence
abstract: Non-structural elements such as raised access floors, partition walls, and mechanical service installations are known to alter the effective dynamic stiffness and damping of composite floor systems, yet their contributions are usually ignored or crudely approximated in design. This study reports controlled experiments on a full-scale composite floor mock-up (6.0 m × 4.5 m, 75 mm composite slab on cold-formed steel joists at 600 mm centres) built inside the structural dynamics laboratory at the Faculty of Civil Engineering Subotica. The floor was tested in six progressively furnished configurations. Fundamental frequency increased by 6–11% with the addition of a raised floor system, and effective modal damping ratios increased from a baseline of 1.1% to 3.8% in the fully furnished state. A regression model relating damping ratio to furnishing load per unit area is developed and validated against an independent dataset of five in-situ measurements. The model parameters and their uncertainty bounds are reported for use in probabilistic floor assessment procedures.

title: Bayesian updating of floor frequency models using in-situ acceleration measurements
abstract: Predicted natural frequencies of composite floor systems carry uncertainties arising from material variability, geometric tolerances, and idealised boundary conditions. When in-situ measurements become available after construction, Bayesian methods offer a principled approach to updating frequency predictions and the associated reliability estimates. This paper applies a Bayesian updating procedure to a population of 18 composite floor panels for which both pre-construction analytical predictions and post-construction ambient vibration measurements are available. A conjugate normal-normal prior-likelihood model is used for the frequency bias factor, and posterior distributions are derived in closed form. The posterior mean bias factor shifts from 0.88 (prior) to 0.93 (posterior) after incorporating measurements, and the posterior variance decreases by 34%. The updated reliability indices for the vibration serviceability limit state increase by 0.18–0.31 units relative to prior estimates, with the largest updates occurring for panels whose measured frequencies deviated most from predictions. The procedure is straightforward to implement and is demonstrated with a worked numerical example.

title: Variance-based sensitivity analysis of peak floor accelerations under stochastic pedestrian loading
abstract: This study applies Sobol' variance decomposition to identify which uncertain input parameters most strongly control the peak weighted acceleration of a composite steel-concrete floor panel under stochastic pedestrian loading. Eight input variables are considered: fundamental frequency, modal damping ratio, effective modal mass, floor span, step frequency distribution parameters, dynamic load factor, walking speed, and pedestrian weight. A surrogate model based on polynomial chaos expansion (PCE) of degree four is constructed from 1 200 deterministic evaluations and used to compute first-order and total-order Sobol' indices efficiently. First-order indices show that modal damping ratio (S₁ = 0.39) and the mean of the step frequency distribution (S₁ = 0.27) together account for approximately two-thirds of output variance. Total-order indices reveal moderate interaction effects between step frequency and walking speed. The PCE surrogate predicts peak acceleration with a root-mean-square error of 2.3% relative to direct simulation, confirming its adequacy for sensitivity analysis.

title: Comparative assessment of floor frequency prediction formulas in European and North American design standards
abstract: Several design standards and guidance documents offer simplified formulas for predicting the fundamental natural frequency of composite steel-concrete floor panels, including provisions in Eurocode 3 and 4, the SCI P354 guide, and the AISC Design Guide 11. These formulas differ in their treatment of composite action, continuity conditions, and the contribution of non-structural mass. This paper evaluates the accuracy and consistency of six commonly used formulas against a compiled database of 61 measured floor frequencies drawn from published literature and from the authors' own measurements in Serbia and Hungary. Predicted-to-measured frequency ratios are computed for each formula, and their bias and coefficient of variation are reported. The SCI P354 formula shows the lowest bias (mean ratio 1.03, CV 0.14), while the most conservative formula overestimates by a mean of 19%. The reliability implications of adopting different formulas in limit state checks are quantified using a simplified reliability model.

title: Stochastic finite element modelling of cold-formed steel joist floors accounting for cross-section thickness variability
abstract: Cold-formed steel sections used as floor joists exhibit dimensional variability arising from the strip-steel coiling and roll-forming process. Thickness deviations from nominal values of ±5–8% are common, and their effect on structural stiffness is typically neglected in reliability analyses. This paper implements a stochastic finite element model of a composite floor in which joist wall thickness is treated as a spatially correlated random field, discretised using the midpoint method onto a mesh of 240 elements. Correlation lengths estimated from 180 coupon measurements from three production batches range from 0.4 m to 1.1 m. Monte Carlo simulation with 20 000 realisations is used to propagate thickness variability through to natural frequency and peak acceleration. Results indicate that thickness variability contributes approximately 7% of the total variance in fundamental frequency, a contribution that is secondary to mass and damping uncertainties but non-negligible for high-precision reliability assessments. Recommendations for production tolerance specifications are derived from the reliability results.

title: In-situ vibration measurements and serviceability assessment of composite floors in a newly constructed student dormitory
abstract: This paper reports on a serviceability investigation of composite steel-concrete floors in a six-storey student dormitory completed in 2021 in Subotica, Serbia. Floors consist of cold-formed steel C-joists at 400 mm spacing composite with a 70 mm lightweight concrete slab. Concerns about vibration comfort were raised by facilities management during the first months of occupancy. Ambient vibration testing using a roving accelerometer configuration and heel-drop excitation tests were carried out on twelve floor panels across four storeys. Measured fundamental frequencies ranged from 6.9 to 10.4 Hz, and peak-weighted accelerations under standardised single-pedestrian walking exceeded the criterion aw,rms = 0.5 m/s² on four panels. A reliability analysis incorporating the measured frequency and damping data is performed using the updated Bayesian model from earlier work, and failure probabilities are compared to a serviceability target of 10⁻². Remedial measures, including addition of constrained-layer damping mats, are evaluated numerically and their effect on reliability estimated.

title: Reliability-based design optimisation of composite floor panel geometry for simultaneous strength and vibration serviceability targets
abstract: This paper formulates a reliability-based design optimisation (RBDO) problem for composite steel-concrete floor panels in which both ultimate strength and vibration serviceability reliability constraints are imposed simultaneously. Decision variables are joist depth, flange width, slab thickness, and joist spacing. The objective is to minimise steel material volume per unit floor area subject to β ≥ 3.8 for the ultimate limit state and β ≥ 1.5 for vibration serviceability. The RBDO is solved using a sequential approximate optimisation algorithm that decouples the deterministic optimisation from the reliability evaluations. A database of 5 400 deterministic evaluations is used to build response surface models for both limit state functions. Results for a 6 m × 9 m floor bay show that the vibration serviceability constraint is active at the optimum in 78% of the design space explored, governing over the strength constraint for joist spacings above 500 mm. Material savings of 12–17% relative to conservative deterministic designs are demonstrated without violating either reliability target.

title: Time-variant serviceability reliability of composite floors subject to gradual degradation of composite action
abstract: The serviceability performance of composite steel-concrete floors may deteriorate over time as shear connectors degrade under repeated cyclic occupancy loads, progressively reducing composite action and lowering the floor's fundamental frequency. This paper develops a time-variant reliability model for vibration serviceability in which the degree of composite action decreases according to a gamma process with parameters estimated from push-out fatigue test data reported in the literature. The model is combined with a stochastic occupancy load process and Monte Carlo simulation to compute the probability of first exceedance of a peak acceleration limit over a 50-year design life. Results for a reference 6.5 m span panel show that the annual probability of serviceability exceedance increases by a factor of approximately 2.8 between year 1 and year 50 under a moderate-use office occupancy scenario. Inspection and maintenance strategies are evaluated: a single inspection at year 25, combined with connector replacement if composite action has fallen below 70%, reduces the lifetime exceedance probability by 41%.

title: Characterisation of crowd-induced floor loading during university examination periods: a sensor-based study
abstract: University examination halls experience short-duration crowd occupancy events with loading intensities that differ substantially from the sustained distributed loads assumed in standard design. This paper reports a monitoring campaign covering six examination sessions in a university building in Novi Sad equipped with cold-formed steel composite floors. Occupancy was tracked via door-mounted infrared counters and a pressure-sensing floor tile grid embedded in one bay. Peak areal load intensities reached 0.89 kN/m² during synchronised seating and standing transitions. Dynamic load factors associated with near-synchronous crowd movement were extracted from accelerometer records and found to exceed single-pedestrian values by factors of 1.6–2.3. Statistical models for load intensity and dynamic load factor are fitted and compared with values cited in AISC Design Guide 11 and a recent draft amendment to EN 1991-1-1. The data suggest that crowd-synchronisation effects are underrepresented in current serviceability guidance for educational occupancies, and revised characteristic values are proposed for consideration in the Serbian National Annex revision process.

title: Threshold-based segmentation of wrist accelerometer signals for daily activity detection
abstract: This paper examines simple adaptive-threshold segmentation applied to raw three-axis accelerometer data collected from a wrist-worn logger at 50 Hz. A dataset of eight activities was recorded from 22 volunteers aged 20–45 in a controlled laboratory setting over two sessions, yielding approximately 18 hours of labelled data. Activity segments were classified using a k-nearest-neighbour classifier operating on time- and frequency-domain handcrafted features. Segmentation quality was evaluated with a boundary-detection F1 score, achieving 0.81 on held-out subjects. Classification accuracy reached 87.3% in a leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. The study identifies walking, stair ascent, and typing as the three activities where threshold-based segmentation introduces the most boundary errors. Results suggest that adaptive thresholds calibrated per subject reduce over-segmentation by 14% relative to a global threshold. The work provides a reproducible baseline for subsequent deep-learning comparisons on the same corpus.

title: Comparing window length and overlap strategies for wrist IMU activity classification with SVM
abstract: Fixed sliding-window partitioning is the dominant preprocessing step in inertial-sensor activity recognition, yet the interaction between window length and overlap ratio is rarely studied in isolation. This work collects a six-axis IMU dataset (accelerometer and gyroscope) from 30 participants performing ten activities of daily living over three recording days, totalling roughly 27 hours. Windows from 0.5 s to 4 s at overlaps of 0%, 25%, 50%, and 75% are evaluated with a support-vector machine classifier using a radial basis function kernel. A grid search over window parameters shows that 2 s windows at 50% overlap maximise mean F1 across activities at 0.883, while very short windows (0.5 s) degrade recognition of slow-transition activities such as meal preparation by up to 11 percentage points. The paper provides ablation tables covering all 20 window configurations and discusses implications for battery-constrained continuous monitoring on wrist devices.

title: A compact 1-D convolutional network for on-device wrist gesture classification
abstract: This paper introduces a one-dimensional convolutional architecture designed to classify 12 discrete wrist gestures using raw six-axis IMU signals sampled at 100 Hz. The model consists of four depthwise-separable convolutional blocks followed by global average pooling and a softmax output layer, resulting in 38 000 trainable parameters and a binary size of under 160 KB after 8-bit quantisation. A dataset of 3 600 gesture instances from 25 subjects was used for training and evaluation in a stratified ten-fold setup. The quantised model achieves 93.1% macro-averaged accuracy on a Cortex-M4 development board with an inference latency of 11 ms per 500 ms window at 168 MHz, compared to 94.7% for a full-precision baseline that requires a server-class GPU for real-time execution. The paper provides a systematic ablation over kernel sizes (3, 5, 9, 15 samples), showing that kernels of 9 samples consistently outperform others for transient gesture signals.

title: Effect of sensor placement variance on wrist-worn IMU activity recognition models
abstract: Consumer wrist wearables are not worn in a standardised position, yet most public activity-recognition datasets assume a fixed device orientation. This study quantifies how placement variability—defined as rotation about the longitudinal and transverse wrist axes within ±30°—affects model performance. Fifteen participants wore two IMU nodes simultaneously at two offset positions during a 45-minute scripted activity protocol covering eight classes. A 1-D CNN trained on data from one position was tested on the offset position without retraining, showing an average accuracy drop of 9.4 percentage points. Three mitigation strategies were compared: rotation-augmented training (−3.1 pp drop), gravity-component removal preprocessing (−4.8 pp drop), and a lightweight domain-adversarial adaptation layer (−2.6 pp drop). The study concludes that rotation-augmented training offers the best accuracy-complexity trade-off for deployment on resource-limited hardware and provides the augmentation parameters used.

title: Benchmarking structured pruning strategies for activity recognition CNNs on ARM Cortex-M targets
abstract: This paper systematically evaluates four structured pruning methods—filter magnitude pruning, geometric median pruning, Taylor expansion criterion pruning, and activation correlation pruning—applied to a baseline depthwise-separable 1-D CNN trained for ten-class activity recognition from wrist IMU data. Pruning is performed at five sparsity levels (10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50% filter removal) with fine-tuning after each level. Evaluation covers accuracy on a held-out test set of 14 subjects and measured inference latency and RAM consumption on two Cortex-M targets (M4 at 168 MHz, M7 at 216 MHz). At 40% filter removal, Taylor-criterion pruning retains 95.4% of baseline F1 and reduces latency by 31% on the M4 target, while magnitude pruning at the same level retains only 91.7% F1. The paper provides reproducible pruning recipes and the scripts used for cycle-accurate on-device profiling.

title: Quantifying temporal resolution requirements for wrist IMU-based hand hygiene event detection in clinical settings
abstract: Automated hand hygiene monitoring via wrist-worn inertial sensors has been proposed as an alternative to direct observation in healthcare environments. This paper investigates how sampling rate reduction—from 200 Hz down to 12.5 Hz—affects detection performance of a handwashing recognition CNN deployed on a sub-wrist badge device. Data were collected from 18 nursing-school volunteers performing standardised six-step handwashing sequences, soap-and-rinse variants, and eight confounding activities over 14 recording sessions. A fixed 1-D CNN architecture is retrained independently at each sampling rate; F1 for the handwash class remains above 0.90 down to 25 Hz but drops to 0.74 at 12.5 Hz. Power consumption of the sensing front-end scales approximately linearly with sample rate, motivating a 25 Hz operating point that reduces sensing energy by 75% relative to 100 Hz with less than 2 percentage-point F1 loss. The dataset and annotation protocol are described in sufficient detail for replication.

title: Encoder-Based Swing Angle Estimation for a Laboratory-Scale Overhead Crane: Accuracy Bounds Under Rope Elasticity
abstract: Swing angle estimation in overhead cranes commonly relies on hoist drum encoder signals under the assumption of an inextensible rope. This paper quantifies the estimation error introduced by rope elasticity using a 1:8 scale laboratory testbed with a 0.8 m rope and payloads ranging from 1 kg to 5 kg. A two-mass model is fitted to static and dynamic rope-extension measurements obtained from a 50 N strain-gauge load cell sampled at 500 Hz. Results show that the inextensible-rope assumption introduces a steady-state angle error of up to 1.8° at full load and a transient overshoot error of up to 3.1° during acceleration phases. A correction factor derived from the identified rope stiffness (measured at 3 420 N/m) reduces mean absolute angle error from 1.4° to 0.3° across twelve standardised motion profiles. The findings motivate explicit inclusion of rope elasticity parameters in encoder-based state estimators for real-time crane control.

title: A Lumped-Parameter Model for Double-Pendulum Load Swing in Overhead Cranes with Flexible Hook Assembly
abstract: When a crane hook assembly has appreciable mass and the payload is attached by a secondary sling, the dynamics approximate a double pendulum rather than a simple pendulum. This paper derives a four-degree-of-freedom lumped-parameter model accounting for hook mass, sling length variability, and hoist-rope elasticity. Model parameters are estimated from free-swing experiments on a laboratory testbed using nonlinear least squares applied to encoder and accelerometer signals recorded at 1 kHz. Twenty-four configurations spanning hook masses of 0.3–1.2 kg, primary rope lengths of 0.4–1.2 m, and sling lengths of 0.1–0.5 m are tested. The model predicts swing period with a mean error of 1.2% and peak swing amplitude with a mean error of 6.8%. A comparison with the equivalent single-pendulum approximation shows that the double-pendulum model reduces amplitude prediction error by a factor of 2.9 for short sling-to-rope length ratios. The parametric structure is designed to support online updating from encoder measurements.

title: Rope-Tension Sensor Placement Optimisation for Parameter Observability in Crane Digital Twins
abstract: The number and location of rope-tension measurement points affect how well physical parameters can be recovered from sensor data in online model-updating schemes. This paper formulates sensor placement as a determinant maximisation problem over the Fisher information matrix derived from the four-parameter double-pendulum model. Three candidate placements are considered: single sensor at the drum, single sensor at the hook, and dual sensors at both locations. Observability is analysed for eighteen operating scenarios combining three payload levels and six rope lengths. Results show that single drum-mounted tension measurement provides adequate stiffness observability (condition number below 120) only for rope lengths above 0.6 m, while the dual-sensor configuration maintains condition numbers below 95 across all scenarios. Adding a hook-mounted sensor increases measurement cost but reduces mean parameter estimation error by 34% in hardware validation. Practical installation constraints and cable routing in industrial bridge cranes are discussed.

title: Digital Twin Synchronisation Fidelity Under Communication Delays in an Edge-Cloud Crane Monitoring Architecture
abstract: Industrial crane monitoring increasingly uses edge-cloud architectures where sensor data is transmitted over factory Ethernet or 5G links before reaching the model-updating service. This paper characterises the degradation of digital twin synchronisation fidelity as a function of introduced communication delay, packet loss rate, and update frequency. Delays are emulated using a traffic shaping appliance inserted between the testbed dSPACE unit and an edge server running the parameter estimation service on an 8-core ARM Cortex-A72 board. Delay levels from 2 ms to 80 ms and packet loss rates from 0% to 5% are tested. With 20 ms delay and 1% packet loss, swing angle prediction error increases from 0.3° (local, zero-delay baseline) to 0.8°. A predictor-corrector scheme using last-known parameter estimates reduces this to 0.5°. At 80 ms delay, the predictor-corrector no longer provides benefit, and the paper discusses threshold conditions for deciding between local and remote model updating.

title: Benchmarking Parametric and Data-Driven Digital Twins for Crane Load-Swing Prediction Over Extended Operating Cycles
abstract: This paper compares two digital twin strategies for predicting load swing over operating cycles of four hours: a continuously updated parametric model (the four-parameter recursive least-squares twin described in prior work) and a long short-term memory (LSTM) network trained on 40 hours of crane operation data recorded at the laboratory testbed. Both twins receive the same encoder and rope-tension inputs at runtime. Over fourteen four-hour test cycles, the parametric twin achieves mean absolute swing prediction error of 0.41° and maintains this across payload changes without retraining. The LSTM twin achieves 0.38° mean error when payload distribution matches training data but degrades to 0.79° on out-of-distribution payload conditions. Computational cost per inference step is 0.14 ms (parametric) versus 0.22 ms (LSTM) on the edge server hardware. The paper argues that for operating environments with frequent payload variation, parametric updating retains an interpretability and generalisation advantage that partially offsets the marginal accuracy benefit of data-driven approaches in matched conditions.

title: Comparing Parametric Survival Models for Employee Sick-Leave Duration in a Manufacturing Context
abstract: Duration of employee sick-leave spells is modelled as a time-to-event outcome using six parametric survival distributions: exponential, Weibull, log-normal, log-logistic, gamma, and generalised gamma. Data consist of 2,840 anonymised absence records collected over six years from a mid-sized manufacturing company in Vojvodina, with administrative right-censoring affecting 18% of spells. Model fit is assessed via AIC, BIC, and the integrated Brier score evaluated on a held-out 20% split. The log-normal model provides the best overall fit (AIC difference of at least 14 against all alternatives). Covariate effects of job category, prior absence history, and season of onset are quantified as accelerated failure time parameters. Predicted median absence durations for high-risk employee subgroups differ from observed medians by no more than 2.1 days on average. The study documents practical considerations for applying survival analysis when absence records originate from heterogeneous HR systems with inconsistent date coding.

title: Semi-Supervised Labelling Strategies for Time-Series Classification When Annotation Costs Are High
abstract: Industrial sensor streams rarely arrive with dense expert annotations. This paper compares four semi-supervised strategies—self-training, label propagation on a dynamic time-warping similarity graph, co-training with two views derived from time and frequency domains, and entropy-regularised expectation-maximisation—on three datasets covering vibration monitoring, power consumption, and network traffic. Each dataset is progressively subsampled to simulate label budgets of 5%, 10%, and 20% of total sequences. At a 10% label budget, entropy-regularised EM outperforms the other strategies in two of three datasets and ties in one, with macro-F1 gains over supervised-only baselines ranging from 4.1 to 9.8 percentage points. Self-training degrades performance on the smallest dataset when initial classifier confidence is poorly calibrated. A practical recommendation framework is derived linking preferred strategy to dataset size, class imbalance ratio, and annotation cost per instance. Limitations include sensitivity to the choice of similarity kernel parameters.

title: Calibration of Probabilistic Classifiers on Imbalanced Biomedical Time Series
abstract: Probabilistic outputs of classifiers trained on imbalanced clinical time-series data are frequently poorly calibrated, with systematic overconfidence for the majority class. This study evaluates five post-hoc calibration techniques—Platt scaling, isotonic regression, temperature scaling, beta calibration, and a Bayesian binning approach—applied after training gradient-boosted trees and recurrent neural networks on two biomedical datasets: a 1,120-patient post-operative complication monitoring dataset and a 640-patient readmission risk dataset, both exhibiting class imbalance ratios between 7:1 and 12:1. Calibration is measured using the expected calibration error and reliability diagrams computed on stratified test folds. Beta calibration consistently reduces ECE by 30–45% relative to uncalibrated outputs across both models and datasets. Isotonic regression overfits when the positive-class test count falls below 60 instances. The interaction between resampling strategy during training and post-hoc calibration method is examined, showing that combining SMOTE with temperature scaling produces well-calibrated outputs at lower computational cost.

title: Transfer Learning for Workforce Absence Prediction Across Organisational Units with Distributional Shift
abstract: Absence prediction models built on data from one organisational unit often fail when deployed to a different unit with a distinct workforce composition or working-time regime. This paper formalises the problem as a covariate-shift transfer learning task and evaluates three adaptation strategies: importance weighting with kernel mean matching, fine-tuning a pre-trained gradient-boosted model on a small target-unit sample, and a multi-source domain adaptation method using optimal transport. Experiments use anonymised records from five organisational units of a logistics company, treated in rotation as the target domain. Fine-tuning with as few as 60 target-unit labelled examples achieves AUC improvements of 0.07–0.12 over a source-only model. Optimal-transport adaptation performs comparably to fine-tuning when labelled target data are unavailable but requires careful regularisation of the transport plan. The paper also discusses privacy constraints on cross-unit data sharing and proposes a federated variant of the fine-tuning strategy.

title: Bayesian Updating of Absence Risk Scores with Streaming Organisational Covariates
abstract: Workforce absence risk models are typically trained once and deployed statically, ignoring covariate changes such as schedule modifications, team restructuring, or seasonal shifts. This paper proposes an online Bayesian updating scheme in which a logistic regression absence risk model is maintained as a posterior distribution over coefficients, refreshed weekly as new organisational covariate observations arrive. Sequential importance resampling is used to track posterior mass efficiently, with a degeneracy threshold triggering full resampling. The approach is evaluated on 36 months of weekly data from a call-centre with 480 employees. Compared with a fixed retrained model, the online Bayesian model reduces mean absolute error in monthly absence rate forecasts by 14% and detects structural breaks in absence patterns 2.3 weeks earlier on average. Computational overhead is modest: each weekly update completes in under 90 seconds on a single CPU core. Practical guidance on setting the degeneracy threshold is provided.

title: Few-Shot Time-Series Classification via Prototypical Networks with DTW-Based Embedding Distance
abstract: Prototypical networks, originally developed for image classification, are adapted here for time-series classification tasks where only 5–20 labelled examples per class are available. The standard Euclidean embedding distance is replaced with a differentiable approximation of dynamic time warping (soft-DTW), enabling end-to-end training of the embedding network. The approach is evaluated across six benchmark time-series datasets from the UCR archive and two proprietary industrial datasets provided by partner companies, covering episode lengths from 50 to 800 time steps. On the UCR benchmarks, the DTW-based prototypical network matches or exceeds the accuracy of the Euclidean variant in 5 of 6 datasets at 5-shot settings, with gains of up to 5.4 percentage points. On the industrial datasets, accuracy at 10-shot reaches 73% and 68% respectively, representing improvements of 8–11 percentage points over nearest-centroid baselines. Training time per episode is approximately 2.3 times that of the Euclidean variant due to soft-DTW's quadratic complexity.

title: Federated Survival Analysis for Multi-Site Absence Prediction Without Sharing Individual Records
abstract: Training a shared survival model across multiple employers while preserving data privacy is practically important but methodologically underexplored. This paper implements federated learning for the Cox proportional hazards model using two aggregation strategies: FedAvg applied to gradient updates of the partial likelihood and a federated ADMM decomposition that keeps the concordance-based objective intact across sites. Four simulated federation scenarios are constructed using absence data from three partner organisations (total n = 9,400 employee-years), partitioned by site, occupation group, and both simultaneously. Federated Cox with ADMM achieves C-index within 0.02 of the centralised model across all partition scenarios, while FedAvg degrades by 0.04–0.07 under non-IID occupational partitioning. Communication rounds required for convergence range from 18 to 34 depending on heterogeneity. Differential privacy noise is added to gradient updates, and the resulting privacy–utility trade-off is characterised at three privacy budget levels. The study highlights practical challenges in synchronising censoring indicators across federates.

title: Production of exopolysaccharides by Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus strains isolated from traditional Serbian dairy products
abstract: Seven strains of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus isolated from artisanal kajmak and yoghurt samples collected across Vojvodina were screened for exopolysaccharide (EPS) production in MRS broth at 37 °C and 42 °C. EPS yield was quantified gravimetrically after ethanol precipitation, ranging from 78 mg/L to 312 mg/L depending on strain and incubation temperature. Monosaccharide composition was determined by GC-MS analysis of alditol acetate derivatives, revealing galactose and glucose as dominant units with rhamnose present in three strains. Molecular weight distribution was estimated by gel permeation chromatography with dextran standards, yielding weight-average molecular masses between 0.8 × 10⁶ and 2.4 × 10⁶ Da. Differences in EPS yield correlated with distinct banding patterns observed in SDS-PAGE of cell wall protein extracts, suggesting strain-specific regulatory variation. Results provide baseline data for selecting EPS-overproducing strains suitable for downstream rheological and food technology studies.

title: Influence of carbon source on exopolysaccharide yield and monosaccharide composition in Streptococcus thermophilus ST14
abstract: The effect of substituting lactose with glucose, sucrose, or fructose as the sole carbon source on EPS biosynthesis by Streptococcus thermophilus ST14 was examined in batch fermentation at pH 6.5 and 42 °C. EPS concentrations after 18 h ranged from 124 mg/L on fructose to 431 mg/L on lactose, measured after TCA deproteinisation and ethanol precipitation. Monosaccharide profiles determined by GC-MS showed that the galactose-to-glucose ratio shifted from 1.8:1 on lactose to 1.1:1 on glucose, suggesting metabolic flux differences upstream of the Leloir pathway. Bacterial growth curves measured by optical density at 600 nm indicated that EPS overproduction on lactose was not attributable to differences in maximum growth rate. Fourier-transform infrared spectra confirmed the presence of characteristic polysaccharide absorption bands at 1060 cm⁻¹ and 1150 cm⁻¹ across all conditions. Findings indicate that carbon source selection is a practical lever for tuning EPS composition prior to structural applications.

title: Chain conformation of a high-molecular-weight EPS from Lactobacillus helveticus LH03 in dilute aqueous solution
abstract: The solution conformation of an exopolysaccharide with a weight-average molecular mass of 1.9 × 10⁶ Da, isolated from Lactobacillus helveticus LH03, was characterised by static light scattering, dynamic light scattering, and viscometry over a concentration range of 0.01–1.0 mg/mL in 0.1 M NaCl at 25 °C. The radius of gyration was 142 nm and the hydrodynamic radius was 98 nm, giving a ρ-ratio of 1.45, consistent with a stiff, worm-like chain rather than a compact globule. The Mark–Houwink exponent of 0.78 was determined from intrinsic viscosity measurements across eight molecular weight fractions obtained by ultrafiltration. ¹H and ¹³C NMR spectra recorded at 500 MHz confirmed a repeating unit composed of β-D-galactose, α-D-glucose, and α-L-rhamnose in a 2:1:1 ratio. Temperature-dependent changes in hydrodynamic radius between 10 °C and 60 °C were modest (less than 12%), indicating good thermal stability of the chain in solution. Results are discussed in terms of side-chain branching and electrostatic persistence length.

title: Effect of exopolysaccharide-producing starter cultures on texture and syneresis in set-type soy yoghurt
abstract: Soy milk standardised to 3.8% protein and 2.5% fat was inoculated with single-strain cultures of Streptococcus thermophilus ST14 (EPS-producing) and a non-EPS-producing isogenic mutant, and incubated at 42 °C to a final pH of 4.5. Texture profile analysis performed with a back-extrusion probe on a texture analyser showed that EPS-producing cultures increased firmness from 18 ± 2 N to 31 ± 3 N and consistency from 94 ± 8 N·s to 157 ± 12 N·s. Syneresis, measured by centrifugation at 700× g for 10 min at 4 °C, was reduced from 38.4 ± 1.6% to 22.1 ± 1.3% by EPS production. Dynamic oscillatory measurements on the final gel at 10 °C showed G′ values of 320 Pa and 180 Pa for EPS-producing and non-producing variants respectively at 1 Hz. Confocal laser scanning microscopy of rhodamine B-stained samples revealed a more uniform protein network in EPS-producing gels. Sensory evaluation by a trained panel of 12 members found no significant difference in flavour scores between treatments.

title: Comparison of exopolysaccharide biosynthesis gene clusters in twelve lactic acid bacteria strains from Vojvodina dairy samples
abstract: Whole-genome sequences of twelve lactic acid bacteria strains, including representatives of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. bulgaricus, Lactobacillus helveticus, Streptococcus thermophilus, and Leuconostoc mesenteroides, were obtained by Illumina paired-end sequencing (2 × 150 bp) and assembled using SPAdes v3.13. EPS biosynthesis gene clusters were identified by BLAST-based comparison with the reference eps cluster of S. thermophilus ATCC 19258. Cluster sizes ranged from 14 kb to 31 kb, and gene organisation varied substantially across genera. Priming glycosyltransferase genes (epsD homologues) were present in all twelve genomes, whereas chain-length-determining wzz-like genes were found in only seven. Maximum-likelihood phylogenetic analysis of concatenated glycosyltransferase protein sequences showed that cluster organisation correlated weakly with taxonomy (bootstrap support > 70% for three clades) but correlated more strongly with EPS monosaccharide composition as determined in earlier wet-lab experiments. Gene cluster data are deposited in a public repository and accession numbers are provided.

title: Gel-forming potential and biothickening capacity of an EPS from Lactobacillus helveticus LH03 in oat-based fermented beverages
abstract: An exopolysaccharide from Lactobacillus helveticus LH03, previously characterised structurally, was added at concentrations of 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, and 1.0% (w/v) to commercially prepared oat drink (3.0% beta-glucan, 1.0% protein, 1.5% fat) fermented with a standard yoghurt starter at 42 °C. Apparent viscosity at a shear rate of 50 s⁻¹ increased from 12 mPa·s in the control to 94 mPa·s at 1.0% EPS addition. Small-amplitude oscillatory measurements at 10 °C showed a crossover from liquid-like to solid-like behaviour between 0.3% and 0.5% EPS, with G′ reaching 48 Pa at 0.5%. Water-holding capacity assessed by centrifugation improved from 61% to 84% at 0.5% EPS. Particle size distribution measured by laser diffraction showed no significant aggregation attributable to EPS addition. A storage stability test at 4 °C over 21 days showed less than 8% change in apparent viscosity, indicating adequate physical stability. These data support application of the LH03 EPS as a biothickener in plant-based fermented beverages.

title: Encapsulation of probiotic Lactobacillus rhamnosus NS-2 in EPS-reinforced alginate beads and survival under simulated gastrointestinal conditions
abstract: Alginate beads with and without 0.5% (w/v) co-encapsulated Lactobacillus rhamnosus NS-2 exopolysaccharide were prepared by ionic gelation in 0.1 M CaCl₂ and evaluated for encapsulation efficiency, bead morphology, and probiotic viability during a two-step in vitro digestion protocol (2 h at pH 2.0 followed by 3 h at pH 7.0 with 1% bile salts). Encapsulation efficiency was 98.4 ± 0.6% for EPS-reinforced beads versus 96.1 ± 0.8% for plain alginate beads. Mean bead diameter measured by optical microscopy was 1.8 ± 0.2 mm for both formulations. After simulated gastric transit, viable counts in EPS-reinforced beads were 8.6 log CFU/g compared to 7.2 log CFU/g in plain alginate, a statistically significant difference (p < 0.01, Tukey test). Swelling ratio in simulated intestinal fluid was higher for EPS-reinforced beads (1.62 versus 1.38), suggesting greater hydrophilicity. Scanning electron microscopy revealed a smoother surface and fewer surface cracks in EPS-reinforced beads. No cytotoxicity toward Caco-2 cells was detected at bead concentrations up to 5 mg/mL.

title: Thermodynamic and kinetic analysis of EPS release during lactic acid fermentation of lupin milk monitored by inline mid-infrared spectroscopy
abstract: Lupin milk prepared from Lupinus albus seeds (3.5% protein, 5.2% carbohydrate) was fermented with Streptococcus thermophilus ST14 at 40 °C and monitored continuously for 10 h using an inline attenuated total reflectance mid-infrared probe. Partial least squares regression models calibrated on 42 off-line EPS reference samples achieved root mean square errors of cross-validation of 18 mg/L across the range 0–450 mg/L. EPS accumulation followed a biphasic pattern: a lag phase of approximately 2 h coinciding with active acidification (pH drop from 6.8 to 5.5) was followed by a production phase with a maximum rate of 41 mg/L/h between pH 5.5 and 4.8. Apparent activation energy for EPS release, estimated from fermentations conducted at 37, 40, 43, and 46 °C, was 58 ± 5 kJ/mol. Simultaneous monitoring of the amide I band indicated that protein aggregation commenced at pH 5.3 ± 0.1, approximately 20 min after onset of rapid EPS accumulation. Results support a model in which EPS mediates steric repulsion that temporarily retards protein network formation.
