title: Interaction between lactic acid bacteria exopolysaccharides and pea protein isolate in fermented gel systems: effect on microstructure and large-deformation rheology
abstract: Pea protein isolate (PPI, 85% protein, supplied as a commercial powder) was dispersed at 5% (w/v) in phosphate buffer (pH 7.0) and mixed with EPS fractions from Lactobacillus helveticus LH03 and Leuconostoc mesenteroides LM-19 at 0–1.0% (w/v) prior to fermentation by Streptococcus thermophilus ST14 at 42 °C. Large-deformation rheological properties were measured by large-amplitude oscillatory shear (LAOS) using a rheometer equipped with a 40 mm parallel plate. Lissajous–Bowditch plots at strain amplitudes of 1–1000% revealed strain-stiffening behaviour in all EPS-supplemented gels not observed in EPS-free PPI gels. Fracture stress increased from 820 ± 45 Pa (control) to 1410 ± 90 Pa at 0.5% LH03 EPS. Confocal microscopy using dual labelling (rhodamine B for protein, calcofluor white for polysaccharide) confirmed co-localisation of EPS with protein strands rather than pore filling. Zeta potential measurements at pH 4.5 were less negative in EPS-containing systems (−8 mV versus −18 mV), consistent with charge screening. Results suggest that EPS–PPI interaction is electrostatic at the gel surface and contributes to increased fracture resistance.

title: Accuracy Assessment of a Closed Levelling Loop on the Danube–Tisa–Danube Canal: A Case Study of Benchmark Stability
abstract: A first-order closed levelling loop of approximately 74 km was measured along the Danube–Tisa–Danube canal system in Vojvodina to evaluate benchmark stability over a five-year interval. Measurements were carried out using a Leica DNA03 digital level with invar rods, following the instructions of the national first-order levelling specification. Height differences from two independent epoch campaigns were compared after separate least-squares adjustments. Differences at individual benchmarks ranged from 0.4 mm to 3.1 mm, with a root-mean-square discrepancy of 1.6 mm across 31 stable points. Four benchmarks showed systematic trends consistent with shallow foundation settlement and were flagged for removal from the reference network. The study demonstrates that even in low-relief terrain, subsidence linked to irrigation-related groundwater extraction can affect benchmark integrity at the millimetre level. Recommendations are made for re-measurement intervals and for complementing the levelling loop with GNSS-derived ellipsoidal heights to detect horizontal displacements.

title: Helmert Variance Component Estimation Applied to Heterogeneous Levelling Data from Mixed Instrument Types
abstract: Levelling networks are increasingly measured using instruments of different generations and manufacturers, resulting in observations with heterogeneous precision characteristics. This paper investigates the application of Helmert variance component estimation (VCE) to adjust a test network comprising 18 benchmarks measured with three instrument classes: a classic optical level, a digital level with barcode rod, and a self-recording digital level with automatic data logging. Observations were collected in a controlled test network at the FTN campus in Novi Sad over three sessions. The Helmert VCE procedure was implemented in a custom C++ adjustment programme. Results showed that assigning a single a priori variance to all observations led to underestimation of uncertainty for the optical instrument by 23% and overestimation for the digital self-recording instrument by 17%. The estimated variance components converged within four iterations in all test cases. The study confirms that VCE substantially improves the realism of formal precision estimates in mixed-instrument campaigns and should be considered standard practice in network adjustment software.

title: Geodetic Monitoring of Vertical Displacements at the Novi Bečej Lock Complex Using Epoch-by-Epoch Levelling
abstract: The Novi Bečej lock complex on the Tisa River was subjected to geodetic deformation monitoring over a period of four years using first-order spirit levelling. A monitoring network of 22 object points and 8 reference benchmarks founded on bedrock was established in 2013. Annual levelling campaigns were completed between 2013 and 2016 using a Trimble DiNi 0.3 digital level. Adjusted height differences between successive epochs were tested for statistical significance using the global congruency test and point-by-point tests with a significance level of 5%. Significant vertical displacements were detected at five object points on the downstream lock gate foundation, with maximum cumulative settlement of 4.8 mm over the four-year period. The displacement pattern was consistent with consolidation of the compressible fluvial sediment layer identified in the geotechnical investigation. No displacement exceeding the threshold of 2 mm per year was recorded at reference benchmarks, supporting the stability assumption. Results were provided to the public enterprise managing the waterway infrastructure.

title: Variance Component Estimation in Kinematic Levelling: Stochastic Model Refinement for Moving-Sensor Surveys
abstract: Kinematic levelling systems, where the level instrument or sensor moves continuously along a profile, produce observations with strongly autocorrelated residuals that violate the standard assumption of uncorrelated observations in least-squares adjustment. This paper develops a stochastic model for kinematic levelling in which the cofactor matrix is parameterised by two variance components: one for white noise and one for a first-order autoregressive process. Helmert VCE is applied iteratively to estimate both components simultaneously. The method was tested on a 2.3 km kinematic levelling profile measured with a motorised digital level mounted on a low-speed trolley along a railway embankment near Subotica. The autoregressive correlation length was estimated at 4.2 m, and inclusion of the correlation model reduced the formal standard deviation of adjusted heights by 28% compared with the uncorrelated model. An independent check using geodetic pillars at 200 m intervals confirmed agreement at the 0.8 mm level. The parameterisation approach is straightforward to implement within existing adjustment software.

title: Comparison of Hydrostatic and Spirit Levelling for Monitoring the Foundation Plate of a Gravity Dam
abstract: A portable hydrostatic levelling system (HLS) consisting of six interconnected vessel sensors and a central data logger was installed on the foundation inspection gallery of a gravity dam on the Drina River to compare its performance with periodic first-order spirit levelling. Both systems observed the same 12 measurement points over an 18-month period from 2017 to 2019. The HLS provided continuous readings at 30-minute intervals, while spirit levelling was conducted at six-month intervals. Temperature compensation was applied to HLS data using co-located PT100 sensors. After adjustment, the root-mean-square difference between the two methods at corresponding epochs was 0.6 mm, well within the combined measurement uncertainty. The HLS detected a seasonal differential settlement pattern of ±1.1 mm amplitude correlated with reservoir water level changes, which would not have been resolved by the biannual levelling schedule. The study supports the use of HLS as a complement to periodic spirit levelling for continuous structural health monitoring of dam foundations.

title: Influence of Rod Temperature Correction on Millimetre-Level Levelling in Continental Climate Conditions
abstract: Invar levelling rods carry a manufacturer-supplied thermal expansion coefficient that is assumed constant, but field conditions in continental climates with large diurnal temperature swings can introduce systematic errors if corrections are applied carelessly. A controlled field experiment was conducted along a 6 km levelling line in the Vojvodina plain during July and October 2018, using three independently calibrated invar rod pairs. Temperature sensors were attached at five heights on each rod at 20-minute logging intervals. Two correction strategies were compared: a single ambient temperature reading per setup versus an integrated temperature profile using the multi-sensor log. Differences in computed height differences between the two strategies reached up to 0.18 mm per kilometre during the July campaign when temperature gradients along the rod exceeded 4°C. In October, the difference fell to below 0.05 mm per kilometre. The results quantify the practical relevance of rod temperature profiling for surveys targeting sub-millimetre accuracy and provide guidance for instrumentation choices in routine first-order levelling.

title: Robust Estimation Strategies in Levelling Network Adjustment: L1-Norm and Danish Method Compared to Standard Least Squares
abstract: Gross errors in levelling observations, arising from misidentification of benchmarks, transcription errors, or atmospheric refraction anomalies, can propagate into adjusted heights if not detected before or during adjustment. This study compares three adjustment strategies for a simulated and a real levelling network: standard least squares, L1-norm minimisation, and the iteratively reweighted Danish method. The real network consisted of 38 benchmarks and 112 height difference observations measured across the Fruška Gora foothills in 2020. Artificial gross errors of 2 mm, 5 mm, and 10 mm were injected into randomly selected observations in the simulated data. Detection power was assessed through Monte Carlo trials with 500 realisations per scenario. The Danish method correctly flagged 87% of injected 5 mm errors while producing zero false positives in the uncontaminated dataset. L1-norm adjustment was more conservative, flagging 71% of the same errors. Standard least squares absorbed the errors into adjusted heights with no flagging. Practical guidance is offered for selecting the appropriate strategy based on network redundancy.

title: Vertical Displacement Monitoring of a Flood Control Embankment Using Periodic Precise Levelling: Vojvodina Lowland Test Site
abstract: A 3.8 km section of a flood control embankment on the left bank of the Tisa River near Senta was instrumented with 44 levelling benchmarks embedded in the embankment crest and toe. Four levelling campaigns were conducted between 2022 and 2025 during different seasonal pore-pressure conditions. Heights were adjusted in each epoch using a free-network least-squares model and subsequently transformed to a common datum using stable external reference points. Observed crest settlements ranged from 2.1 mm to 14.7 mm, with larger settlements concentrated at a 420 m section underlain by organic-rich fill identified in borehole logs. Seasonal reversible settlements of up to 3 mm were also observed, attributed to shrink-swell behaviour of the embankment material during dry summers. A simple regression model relating cumulative settlement to fill thickness yielded a correlation coefficient of 0.78. The monitoring data have been incorporated into the embankment management plan of the relevant water management authority.

title: Baseline correction strategies for electrodermal activity signals acquired during free movement
abstract: Electrodermal activity (EDA) recorded during ambulatory tasks is corrupted by motion-induced baseline drift that complicates extraction of tonic and phasic components. This study compared five baseline correction strategies—median filtering, polynomial detrending (orders 2–5), empirical mode decomposition, wavelet-level suppression, and a high-pass Butterworth filter at 0.05 Hz—applied to 30-minute recordings from 24 healthy volunteers who performed a structured set of postural and locomotion tasks. Ground-truth phasic events were confirmed by synchronous video annotation of standardised startle stimuli. Phasic response recovery rate and false-positive rate were the primary metrics. Wavelet-level suppression at the fifth decomposition level achieved the highest recovery rate (91.4%) and the lowest false-positive rate (7.2%), outperforming polynomial detrending in every condition. The method was computationally inexpensive enough to run on a low-power microcontroller at 16 Hz sampling, suggesting applicability in real-time wearable pipelines. Recommendations for parameter selection depending on movement intensity are provided.

title: Short-window HRV features for sympathovagal balance estimation during orthostatic stress
abstract: Standard heart rate variability (HRV) analysis conventionally requires five-minute stationary segments, which limits applicability in dynamic monitoring. This paper evaluates the accuracy of sympathovagal balance indices derived from 30-second, 60-second, and 120-second RR-interval windows during a tilt-table orthostatic stress protocol applied to 18 healthy adults. ECG was recorded at 1000 Hz and beat detection was performed with a Pan-Tompkins algorithm. Six frequency-domain and four non-linear features were computed per window length and compared against the five-minute reference using intraclass correlation. The LF/HF ratio estimated from 60-second windows correlated strongly (ICC = 0.83) with the reference, whereas 30-second windows yielded acceptable agreement only for the non-linear feature SD1/SD2 (ICC = 0.78). Results suggest that 60-second windows represent a practical compromise for wearable monitoring applications where extended stationary intervals are unavailable.

title: Fusion of EDA and PPG-derived HRV for binary stress classification in an office task paradigm
abstract: Psychophysiological stress detection often relies on a single modality, which limits robustness. This work investigated whether fusing electrodermal activity features with HRV features derived from wrist PPG improves binary stress/rest classification compared with either modality alone. Forty-two office workers performed a 20-minute neutral reading baseline followed by a 20-minute Stroop-and-arithmetic stress protocol while wearing a custom dual-sensor wristband. Forty-one time-domain, frequency-domain, and statistical features were extracted per two-minute epoch. Linear discriminant analysis, k-nearest neighbours, and a support vector machine with radial basis function kernel were evaluated under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation. The SVM applied to the fused feature set achieved 82.4% balanced accuracy, compared with 71.6% for EDA alone and 68.9% for HRV alone. Feature importance analysis identified phasic EDA amplitude and RMSSD as the top contributors.

title: Wearable multi-modal biosensor platform for autonomous nervous system monitoring: design and validation
abstract: This paper describes the design, implementation, and laboratory validation of a wrist-worn biosensor platform that simultaneously acquires PPG at 100 Hz, two-channel EDA at 32 Hz, skin temperature at 4 Hz, and a three-axis accelerometer at 100 Hz. The analogue front-end uses separate instrumentation amplifier chains for each modality, and a low-power ARM Cortex-M4 microcontroller manages data acquisition, local buffering, and Bluetooth Low Energy transmission. Current consumption was measured at 3.8 mA in full-acquisition mode, yielding approximately 36 hours of operation from a 140 mAh LiPo cell. Signal quality was validated against clinical-grade reference equipment (Biopac MP160) using simultaneous 10-minute recordings from 12 volunteers at rest. Pearson correlation coefficients exceeded 0.97 for PPG and 0.95 for EDA across all participants. The platform schematic and firmware are described in sufficient detail to support replication.

title: Respiratory rate estimation from wrist PPG using frequency-domain and adaptive filtering approaches
abstract: Respiratory rate (RR) can be estimated from the PPG waveform via respiratory-induced intensity variation (RIIV) and baseline wander, but wrist-worn sensors introduce noise that challenges established methods. This study compared a fast Fourier transform peak-picking method, an adaptive comb filter, and an autoregressive model for RR estimation from wrist PPG against a thoracic impedance belt reference during rest, slow walking (3 km/h), and moderate walking (5 km/h). Data from 20 participants were used. At rest, all three methods achieved mean absolute error below 1.5 breaths/min. During walking at 5 km/h, the adaptive comb filter maintained MAE of 2.1 breaths/min, whereas FFT peak-picking degraded to 4.8 breaths/min due to harmonic contamination from cadence. Accelerometer-based gait frequency was used as a notch reference in the comb filter, which was the primary source of improvement.

title: Personalisation of stress classification models using transfer learning from a population baseline
abstract: Physiological stress classifiers trained on population data often generalise poorly to new individuals due to inter-subject variability in autonomic responses. This paper proposes a transfer learning approach in which a base model is pre-trained on data from 60 participants collected in a standardised laboratory stress protocol, and then fine-tuned per individual using as few as 10 labelled two-minute epochs from a brief personal calibration session. A convolutional neural network operating on raw EDA and PPG segments was used. Personalised models achieved mean balanced accuracy of 85.7% in leave-one-protocol-out evaluation, compared with 77.2% for the population model without fine-tuning. Calibration sessions shorter than four minutes were sufficient for the improvement to stabilise. The approach is practically viable for consumer wellness applications where brief on-boarding is acceptable.

title: Signal quality index for real-time rejection of corrupted PPG epochs in ambulatory monitoring
abstract: Continuous wrist PPG recordings in daily life contain segments rendered uninformative by movement artifacts, sensor detachment, or optical interference. This work presents a lightweight signal quality index (SQI) computed from four features—normalised pulse amplitude, skewness of the inter-beat interval distribution, spectral entropy, and template correlation—fused by a logistic regression classifier trained on 4800 30-second epochs labelled by expert review. The SQI was validated on an independent dataset of 18 participants performing unscripted daily activities over four hours. At a threshold selected for 95% specificity, sensitivity for acceptable-quality epoch detection was 87.3%. When the SQI was used to gate HRV feature extraction, the RMSSD estimation error relative to simultaneous ECG decreased from 31.4 ms to 9.8 ms. The index runs in under 2 ms on a Cortex-M4 at 120 MHz.

title: Autonomic nervous system indicators during simulated driving: a multi-modal wearable study
abstract: Driver fatigue and cognitive load alter autonomic regulation, but controlled studies using validated wearable sensors in realistic driving scenarios remain scarce in the region. Twenty-six healthy adults completed two 40-minute drives in a steering-wheel-and-pedal simulator under low-traffic (baseline) and high-traffic (load) conditions on separate days. EDA, PPG, and skin temperature were collected continuously from the custom wrist platform, and subjective cognitive load was rated with the NASA-TLX scale at 10-minute intervals. Mixed-effects linear models showed significant increases in EDA tonic level (p < 0.001) and LF/HF ratio (p = 0.018) and a decrease in SDNN (p = 0.007) during high-traffic conditions. Skin temperature did not differ between conditions. Correlations between NASA-TLX score and EDA tonic level were moderate (r = 0.54). The dataset is archived and available for benchmark use.

title: Modeling Periodic Task Schedulers with Timed Automata: A Comparative Study of Fixed-Priority Policies
abstract: This paper examines the representation of fixed-priority preemptive scheduling policies for periodic real-time tasks using networks of timed automata in the UPPAAL modeling language. Three common policies—Rate Monotonic, Deadline Monotonic, and Earliest Deadline First—are encoded as timed automata templates. Task sets comprising between 4 and 12 tasks with utilization factors ranging from 0.55 to 0.95 are analyzed. Reachability queries are used to verify that no task misses its deadline under worst-case execution times derived from measurement campaigns on an ARM Cortex-M3 microcontroller. Results show that the UPPAAL state-space exploration scales acceptably for task sets up to eight tasks but exhibits exponential blowup beyond ten tasks with dense timing constraints. A partial-order reduction heuristic is proposed and reduces verification time by 34% on average for the tested benchmarks. The work provides a practical comparison of encoding styles and documents known pitfalls when translating C-based scheduler logic into timed automata.

title: Counterexample-Guided Refinement of Timed Automata Models for Embedded Control Software
abstract: Counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (CEGAR) has been applied successfully in untimed model checking, but its adaptation to timed systems introduces challenges due to the continuous-time semantics of clock constraints. This paper presents a semi-automated refinement workflow in which counterexamples produced by UPPAAL are parsed and classified as spurious or genuine using a lightweight simulation layer that replays the trace against instrumented C source code running on a hardware-in-the-loop testbed. Spurious counterexamples trigger automatic tightening of guard constraints in the timed automaton. The method is evaluated on three industrial-grade embedded control modules: a brushless DC motor controller, a pressure regulation unit, and a CAN-bus message dispatcher. In all three cases, spurious counterexamples were eliminated within at most four refinement iterations, and at least one genuine property violation was uncovered in the pressure regulation module that had not been detected by testing. The toolchain is implemented in Python and interfaces with UPPAAL via its command-line verification engine.

title: Compositional Verification of Hierarchical Real-Time Controllers Using Interface Automata
abstract: Large embedded systems are typically structured as hierarchies of interacting controllers, and monolithic verification of the complete system is often infeasible. This paper proposes a compositional approach in which each subsystem is represented by an interface timed automaton that abstracts away internal timing details while preserving observable input–output timing behavior. Assume-guarantee reasoning rules are adapted for timed settings to allow independent verification of subsystems. The approach is validated on a modular programmable logic controller platform consisting of five interacting modules responsible for conveyor belt sequencing in an automated packaging line. The full system contains 47 clock variables; direct UPPAAL verification exhausted memory (32 GB) within two minutes, whereas the compositional approach terminated in under four minutes with full memory headroom. Three safety properties and one liveness property are verified. The paper also discusses conditions under which the interface abstraction is sound and complete.

title: Schedulability Verification Under Jitter Constraints Using Parametric Timed Automata
abstract: Clock jitter in interrupt-driven embedded systems causes execution time variability that is difficult to capture with classical worst-case execution time analysis alone. This paper applies parametric timed automata, as supported by the IMITATOR tool, to represent jitter bounds as symbolic parameters and synthesize schedulability constraints expressed as linear inequalities over those parameters. A set of benchmarks is constructed from firmware traces collected from an STM32F4 microcontroller running a custom RTOS, with jitter measured over 10,000 task activations. For a five-task system, the synthesized parameter constraints closely match empirically derived safe operating regions, with a 97.3% overlap measured by volume of the feasibility polytope. The paper discusses the relationship between parametric synthesis results and traditional response-time analysis bounds and identifies cases where parametric synthesis yields tighter results. Limitations regarding scalability beyond six parameters are documented.

title: Formal Methods for Embedded Systems: Concepts and Practice
abstract: This book chapter provides a pedagogically structured introduction to formal verification techniques applicable to embedded software, with emphasis on timed automata and model checking. It covers the theoretical foundations of timed transition systems, the syntax and semantics of UPPAAL timed automata, and query specification using a subset of CTL adapted for real-time properties. Case studies drawn from automotive and industrial automation domains illustrate property specification for mutual exclusion, bounded response time, and absence of livelock. The chapter also surveys lightweight alternatives such as runtime verification and static analysis, positioning them relative to exhaustive model checking in terms of coverage guarantees and scalability. Practical guidance is given on modeling conventions that help manage state-space size, including clock resets, zone-based representation, and symmetry reduction. The chapter is aimed at graduate students and practicing engineers with a background in C programming and basic automata theory.

title: Encoding AUTOSAR Timing Constraints as UPPAAL Queries: A Systematic Mapping
abstract: The AUTOSAR standard defines a rich set of timing constraints for automotive software components, including age constraints, reaction constraints, and synchronization constraints. Translating these into formal queries suitable for timed automata model checkers is non-trivial, and no systematic mapping has been published in the open literature. This paper presents a structured mapping procedure covering all nine timing constraint categories defined in AUTOSAR Timing Extensions R4.4. Each category is mapped to one or more UPPAAL TCTL queries, with accompanying timed automata observer patterns that monitor constraint satisfaction without modifying the system model. The mapping is implemented as an XSLT transformation applied to AUTOSAR ARXML descriptions. Validation is performed on two publicly available AUTOSAR benchmark sets and one proprietary ECU configuration provided by an industrial partner under an NDA. The observer patterns add on average 3.1 automata components and increase verification time by a factor of 1.8 across 14 benchmark instances.

title: Runtime Monitoring of Hard Real-Time Properties Derived from Timed Automata Specifications
abstract: Model checking provides exhaustive verification guarantees but requires a complete and accurate model of the system under verification. When model accuracy cannot be guaranteed—for instance, in systems that interact with uncertain physical environments—runtime monitoring of formally specified properties can complement offline verification. This paper describes a method for synthesizing lightweight runtime monitors from UPPAAL timed automata property specifications. The synthesis procedure extracts a deterministic timed observer automaton from each property and compiles it to C code instrumented into the embedded firmware. Monitor overhead is evaluated on an ARM Cortex-M7 platform across five task sets; the worst-case execution time overhead per monitoring step is 1.4 µs, and RAM usage per monitor instance ranges from 48 to 312 bytes depending on the number of clocks in the observer. The method is applied to a hydraulic actuator controller where four safety properties are monitored at runtime without violating any scheduling constraints. Detected violations trigger graceful degradation rather than hard shutdown.

title: Intraepidermal nerve fibre density at the distal leg correlates with warm detection threshold loss in diabetic polyneuropathy
abstract: Skin punch biopsies (3 mm) were obtained from the distal leg (10 cm above the lateral malleolus) in 47 patients with electrophysiologically confirmed diabetic polyneuropathy and 22 age- and sex-matched controls without diabetes. Sections were immunostained for PGP 9.5 and intraepidermal nerve fibre density (IENFD) was calculated as fibres per millimetre of epidermal length using confocal microscopy at 40× magnification. Mean IENFD was 3.1 ± 1.4 fibres/mm in patients versus 8.6 ± 2.1 fibres/mm in controls (p<0.001). Within the patient group, IENFD correlated inversely with warm detection threshold at the foot (r=−0.61, p<0.001) but not with vibration detection threshold, suggesting that confocal-based IENFD selectively reflects C- and Aδ-fibre integrity. Patients with painful neuropathy showed intermediate IENFD values rather than the lowest values, consistent with published data suggesting that severe deafferentation may paradoxically reduce spontaneous pain. The technique was feasible in routine outpatient settings with minimal adverse effects.

title: Autonomic sudomotor dysfunction and its relationship to somatic small-fibre loss in type 2 diabetes
abstract: We assessed sudomotor function using quantitative sudomotor axon reflex testing (QSART) at four standard sites (forearm, proximal and distal leg, foot) in 55 patients with type 2 diabetes who had also undergone skin punch biopsy at the distal leg and thigh. QSART total output volume was reduced in 67% of patients compared with age-adjusted normative values. Correlation between QSART volume at the distal leg and IENFD at the same site was moderate (r=0.48, p=0.0003), indicating partial co-localisation of somatic and autonomic small-fibre pathology. Patients in the lowest IENFD tertile had a 3.2-fold higher odds of abnormal QSART at the foot (95% CI 1.4–7.5). Sudomotor deficits were not significantly associated with painful versus painless neuropathy categorisation. Duration of diabetes and HbA1c averaged over the preceding three years were independent predictors of QSART abnormality in multivariable logistic regression. These findings support combined somatic-autonomic assessment when characterising small-fibre involvement.

title: Cluster analysis of QST profiles identifies three sensory phenotypes in painful diabetic neuropathy
abstract: Quantitative sensory testing data from 98 patients with painful diabetic neuropathy were analysed using hierarchical agglomerative clustering (Ward's method) on 13 DFNS-standardised parameters expressed as z-scores relative to a local healthy reference group (n=75). Three stable clusters emerged. Cluster 1 (n=37, 38%) showed predominantly loss of thermal and mechanical detection with near-normal pain thresholds, corresponding to a sensory-loss phenotype. Cluster 2 (n=33, 34%) displayed widespread thermal and mechanical hyperalgesia alongside preserved detection, consistent with a sensitised phenotype. Cluster 3 (n=28, 29%) combined mechanical hypoaesthesia with preserved thermal function and dominant cold allodynia. Pain intensity on the Numeric Rating Scale did not differ significantly across clusters (mean 6.1–6.6), but the sensitised cluster reported higher scores on the affective dimension of the McGill Pain Questionnaire. HbA1c and neuropathy symptom scores did not predict cluster membership. These phenotypes may have relevance to mechanism-based treatment stratification.

title: Repeatability of intraepidermal nerve fibre density measurement across two biopsy sessions six months apart
abstract: Test-retest reliability of IENFD measurement was evaluated in 28 adults with stable diabetic polyneuropathy who underwent bilateral distal-leg punch biopsies at baseline and after six months without change of treatment. Each biopsy pair yielded three non-adjacent 50-µm sections stained with anti-PGP 9.5 antibody; fibres were counted by two independent observers blinded to time point and patient identity. Intraclass correlation coefficient for IENFD between sessions was 0.87 (95% CI 0.76–0.93), indicating good reliability. Within-session inter-rater ICC was 0.91. Mean IENFD did not change significantly over the six-month period (3.4 ± 1.5 vs 3.3 ± 1.6 fibres/mm, p=0.58). The coefficient of variation for repeated measures was 12%, suggesting that changes of approximately 20% or greater in IENFD would be detectable as likely true change in intervention studies. Laterality effects were negligible. These data provide a basis for sample size calculations in longitudinal treatment trials using IENFD as an endpoint.

title: Proximal-to-distal gradient of IENFD loss and its correlation with length-dependent QST changes in diabetic neuropathy
abstract: To characterise the length-dependent nature of small-fibre pathology, we obtained punch biopsies from three sites—distal leg, proximal leg (mid-thigh), and distal forearm—in 44 patients with diabetic neuropathy confirmed by nerve conduction studies and 22 controls. QST was performed at corresponding sites. IENFD at the distal leg was 3.2 ± 1.3 fibres/mm, at the proximal leg 5.7 ± 1.9, and at the forearm 7.1 ± 2.0; controls showed 8.5 ± 1.7, 11.2 ± 2.2, and 11.9 ± 2.1 at the same sites (all between-group differences p<0.001). The distal-to-proximal IENFD gradient was significantly steeper in patients than controls (p=0.003 for interaction). Warm detection threshold loss also followed a distal-predominant pattern and correlated with IENFD at each paired site (r values 0.57–0.71). Large-fibre parameters assessed by nerve conduction showed weaker correlations with IENFD (r=0.18–0.34). These data confirm that morphological and functional small-fibre measures capture a length-dependent neuropathy pattern largely independent of large-fibre findings.

title: Sensory phenotype and small-fibre morphology in patients with type 1 versus type 2 diabetic neuropathy
abstract: We compared QST profiles and IENFD between 38 patients with type 1 diabetes-associated painful neuropathy and 41 with type 2 diabetes-associated painful neuropathy, matched for neuropathy symptom score, age, and sex. Mean disease duration was longer in the type 1 group (18.3 vs 12.7 years, p=0.02). IENFD was similarly reduced in both groups (3.0 ± 1.2 vs 3.3 ± 1.5 fibres/mm, p=0.28). QST phenotype distribution differed: the sensitised cluster was more prevalent in the type 2 group (41% vs 24%, p=0.09), while the sensory-loss phenotype was numerically more common in type 1 (43% vs 32%), though differences did not reach significance after correction for multiple comparisons. Glycaemic variability, estimated from continuous glucose monitoring in a subset of 41 participants, was associated with lower IENFD independent of mean HbA1c (β=−0.31, p=0.04). Body mass index was an independent predictor of the sensitised phenotype in the type 2 subgroup. These exploratory findings warrant replication in larger cohorts.

title: Small-fibre neuropathy in prediabetes: IENFD and QST findings in patients with impaired fasting glucose
abstract: Whether small-fibre pathology precedes clinical diabetic neuropathy is debated. We recruited 35 adults with impaired fasting glucose (IFG; fasting plasma glucose 6.1–6.9 mmol/L, confirmed on two occasions) and no symptoms of neuropathy, along with 35 normoglycaemic controls matched for age, sex, and body mass index. Distal-leg IENFD was reduced in the IFG group relative to controls (6.1 ± 2.0 vs 8.3 ± 1.9 fibres/mm, p<0.001). On QST, warm detection threshold was mildly elevated in IFG participants (mean z-score +0.82 ± 1.1 vs +0.12 ± 0.9, p=0.003). Mechanical detection and vibration thresholds did not differ significantly. Seven IFG participants (20%) had IENFD below the fifth percentile of the control distribution, constituting subclinical small-fibre loss. Waist circumference and triglyceride level were associated with reduced IENFD within the IFG group. These data suggest that small-fibre pathology can be detected before symptomatic neuropathy in prediabetes and may be driven partly by metabolic syndrome components beyond hyperglycaemia.

title: Patient-reported outcome measures in painful diabetic neuropathy: concordance with QST phenotype and IENFD
abstract: Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) are widely used in clinical trials but their relationship to objective measures of small-fibre integrity is poorly characterised. We administered four validated instruments—the Brief Pain Inventory, Neuropathic Pain Symptom Inventory, DN4, and Norfolk QoL-DN—to 82 patients with painful diabetic neuropathy who had also completed the DFNS QST battery and skin punch biopsy. Total NPSI score correlated weakly with IENFD (r=−0.22, p=0.047) but moderately with the number of gain-of-function QST parameters exceeded (r=0.44, p<0.001). The burning pain sub-score of NPSI correlated with paradoxical heat sensation frequency (r=0.38, p=0.0005). Norfolk QoL-DN total score was more strongly associated with loss-of-function QST parameters (r=0.51, p<0.001) than with gain-of-function parameters. IENFD was not significantly correlated with any individual PRO after adjustment for pain intensity. These findings indicate that PROs capture different constructs from biopsy-based morphology and suggest that composite endpoints including both morphological and functional measures may better characterise treatment response.

title: Longitudinal change in intraepidermal nerve fibre density over two years in patients with type 2 diabetic neuropathy: predictors and relationship to QST
abstract: We followed 61 patients with established type 2 diabetic neuropathy for 24 months with annual distal-leg skin punch biopsy and DFNS QST assessment. Mean IENFD declined from 3.2 ± 1.4 to 2.6 ± 1.3 fibres/mm over two years (mean change −0.6 fibres/mm, 95% CI −0.9 to −0.3; p<0.001). Eighteen patients (30%) showed clinically meaningful decline (>20% reduction). Baseline HbA1c above 8.5% and the presence of the sensitised QST phenotype at baseline were independent predictors of IENFD decline in multivariable linear regression (β=−0.28 and −0.41 respectively, both p<0.05). Patients who achieved improved glycaemic control (HbA1c reduction ≥1%) showed attenuated IENFD decline relative to those without improvement (−0.3 vs −0.8 fibres/mm, p=0.03). Change in warm detection threshold correlated with change in IENFD (r=0.47, p=0.0002). This prospective dataset supports IENFD as a sensitive endpoint for longitudinal studies and identifies glycaemic optimisation as a modifiable factor associated with slower morphological deterioration.

title: Corneal confocal microscopy versus skin punch biopsy as indices of small-fibre loss in diabetic neuropathy: a head-to-head comparison
abstract: Corneal confocal microscopy (CCM) offers a non-invasive alternative to skin punch biopsy for assessing small-fibre integrity. We compared CCM-derived corneal nerve fibre length (CNFL) and density (CNFD) with distal-leg IENFD in 53 patients with diabetic neuropathy across the full severity range and 25 controls. Both CCM metrics correlated significantly with IENFD (CNFL r=0.58, CNFD r=0.52, both p<0.001). Agreement between abnormality classification (below fifth percentile of control distribution) was 74% for CNFL and 70% for CNFD relative to IENFD. Discordant cases tended to have intermediate severity; three patients had normal IENFD but abnormal CCM, possibly reflecting early corneal involvement preceding distal-leg depletion. CCM metrics correlated with warm detection threshold comparably to IENFD (r values 0.49–0.55). The two techniques provided complementary rather than interchangeable information: IENFD better predicted the length-dependent QST pattern while CCM was more strongly associated with autonomic measures. Both methods are feasible in a clinical research setting.

title: Sensory phenotype stability over 12 months and its morphological correlates in painful diabetic neuropathy
abstract: Whether QST-defined sensory phenotypes are stable over time or shift between categories is unknown. We re-assessed 74 patients with painful diabetic neuropathy using the full DFNS battery and skin punch biopsy at baseline and 12 months without change of analgesic treatment. Phenotype assignment (sensory-loss, sensitised, cold-dominant) was reproduced in 68% of patients at 12 months. Transitions between phenotypes were most common from sensitised to sensory-loss (n=9, 36% of sensitised group), consistent with progressive deafferentation. Patients who transitioned from sensitised to sensory-loss showed a mean IENFD reduction of 0.8 fibres/mm, significantly greater than those with stable phenotypes (0.2 fibres/mm, p=0.01). Stable sensory-loss phenotype at both time points was associated with the lowest IENFD values at both assessments. These results suggest that phenotype instability partly reflects morphological progression and that repeated QST and biopsy assessment may be needed to capture the dynamic nature of neuropathic pain mechanisms in diabetes.

title: Sequential fixture planning for multi-stage prismatic machining: datum scheme propagation and accumulated error analysis
abstract: In multi-stage CNC machining of prismatic parts, each setup introduces its own positional uncertainties that accumulate through the datum chain. This paper formalises a graph-based method for tracking datum scheme propagation across up to five setups, applied to a steel gearbox housing machined in three operations on a horizontal machining centre. The housing measures 410 × 260 × 195 mm with seven precision bores. For each transition between setups, the change in datum reference frame was expressed as a homogeneous transformation matrix, and tolerance stack-up was computed using worst-case and statistical (root-sum-square) approaches. Results indicated that switching from a 3-2-1 to a 2-1-1 primary support arrangement in the second setup reduced worst-case bore positional error from 68 μm to 44 μm. Coordinate measuring machine measurements on five sample parts confirmed the predicted improvement. The method is expressed in a spreadsheet tool distributed as supplementary material.

title: Clamping force optimisation to minimise surface form error in face milling of thin aluminium plates
abstract: Excessive or unevenly distributed clamping forces distort thin aluminium plates before cutting begins, producing residual form errors after the part is unclamped. This study examines four clamping force magnitudes (50, 100, 200, and 400 N per clamp) and three clamp layouts for 6061-T6 aluminium plates of 280 × 160 × 6 mm. A contact finite-element model was developed in Code_Aster to compute pre-machining deformation fields, and the resulting surface geometry was imported into a virtual machining kernel to predict post-machining flatness deviation. Experimental face-milling trials on a Doosan DNM 400 machining centre were conducted with a Kistler dynamometer plate to measure actual clamping forces in situ. Flatness was assessed on a Zeiss Contura CMM. At 200 N with a symmetric clamp layout, predicted flatness deviation was 9.3 μm against a measured value of 11.1 μm. Clamping at 400 N increased measured flatness deviation to 27 μm. An optimum force range of 120–180 N was identified for the tested geometry.

title: Effect of fixture wear on positional accuracy over a production batch: simulation and shop-floor measurement
abstract: Fixture locating pins and support pads wear progressively during batch production, shifting the effective datum reference frame and degrading part accuracy. This study models locator wear as a linear function of accumulated contact cycles, with wear coefficients determined from pin-on-disc tribometer data for hardened steel pins contacting grey cast iron workpieces. The worn geometry was introduced into successive FE analyses at intervals of 50, 150, 300, and 600 parts. Predicted drift in a reference bore position reached 28 μm after 600 parts, consistent with CMM measurements on production parts sampled from an automotive subcontractor's line. Control chart analysis of the measurement data revealed an out-of-control signal at part 480, corresponding to a predicted drift of 23 μm. The paper proposes a simple maintenance decision rule based on the simulated drift curve and the drawing tolerance band, enabling scheduled pin replacement before the process drifts out of tolerance.

title: Residual stress redistribution after unclamping in milled thin-walled frames: measurement and FE comparison
abstract: When a thin-walled frame is released from its fixture after milling, pre-existing bulk residual stresses redistribute and the part springs back. Predicting this springback is necessary for tight-tolerance assembly, yet it is rarely incorporated into fixture planning. In this study, initial residual stress fields in 7075-T651 aluminium plate stock were characterised by the contour method at two cross-sections. These stress fields were introduced as initial conditions in an Abaqus simulation of a four-step milling and unclamping sequence applied to an L-shaped frame with 3 mm flanges. Springback deflection at the frame tip was predicted as 62 μm and measured at 71 μm using a laser displacement sensor, a difference of 13%. A sensitivity analysis showed that a 20% error in the input residual stress magnitude altered the predicted springback by only 8 μm, suggesting the model is robust to moderate uncertainty in the stress characterisation. Implications for fixture height compensation are discussed.

title: Fixture layout design for CNC machining of thin-walled workpieces
abstract: This book chapter reviews analytical and computational methods for designing fixture layouts for thin-walled prismatic workpieces, covering the progression from purely geometric deterministic approaches to compliance-aware finite-element-based optimisation. The chapter discusses the kinematics of the 3-2-1 locating principle, its limitations when part stiffness is non-uniform, and how penalty-function and gradient-based optimisation methods have been applied to reduce machining errors. Practical guidance is provided on selecting element types, applying boundary conditions, and validating models with CMM data. Case studies drawn from aluminium aerospace brackets and steel automotive housings illustrate trade-offs between fixture complexity, setup time, and achievable accuracy. A section on multi-stage machining addresses datum chain management. The chapter closes with an outline of open research questions concerning dynamic effects during interrupted cutting and real-time force monitoring.

title: Sensitivity of machining accuracy to locator position uncertainty in a modular fixture system
abstract: Modular fixture systems allow rapid reconfiguration but introduce positional uncertainty at the T-slot and pin connections. This paper quantifies how small random displacements of locators—modelled as uniform distributions over ±30 μm, ±60 μm, and ±100 μm—affect the positional accuracy of a 14 mm H7 bore machined in a cast aluminium bracket. Monte Carlo simulation with 10 000 samples was combined with a pre-computed FE influence matrix to obtain distributions of bore positional error at low computational cost. Simulations show that locator uncertainty of ±60 μm inflates the 99th-percentile bore positional error from 18 μm (rigid fixture) to 51 μm, which exceeds the drawing tolerance of ±40 μm for 8% of the simulated parts. Sensitivity indices computed by the method of Sobol indicated that the primary support pad positions account for 63% of output variance. Reducing primary pad uncertainty to ±30 μm through tighter T-slot machining returned the non-conformance rate below 1%.

title: Comparison of deterministic and response-surface fixture optimisation methods for a five-axis milled aerospace rib
abstract: A thin Ti-6Al-4V aerospace rib (500 × 80 × 4 mm web) machined on a five-axis DMG Mori DMU 50 was used as a test case to compare three fixture optimisation strategies: deterministic gradient-based optimisation using an FE influence matrix, a response-surface method built from 48 central-composite-design experiments, and a direct FE-based genetic algorithm. All three methods targeted minimum peak deformation at the web mid-plane. The gradient-based method converged in 2.1 minutes and reduced peak deformation from 55 μm (baseline layout) to 21 μm. The response-surface method reached 24 μm in 3.8 minutes including design-of-experiment runs. The genetic algorithm achieved 19 μm but required 38 minutes. Validation experiments using a contact profilometer showed measured peak deformations of 24, 27, and 22 μm respectively, suggesting the genetic algorithm result was partially offset by unmodelled dynamic effects. The paper recommends the gradient-based method for early-stage process planning and the genetic algorithm for final fixture validation where computation time permits.

title: Compliance error compensation through fixture height adjustment in multi-setup CNC milling of magnesium alloy panels
abstract: Magnesium alloy AZ31B panels with nominal thickness 4 mm are milled in three setups to produce a component for portable device enclosures. Compliance errors accumulated over the three setups are addressed through deliberate fixture height adjustments computed from FE predictions of inter-setup deformation. For each setup transition, the deformed profile of the datum surface was measured by a structured-light scanner, compared to the FE-predicted profile, and used to update support pad heights via a least-squares fitting procedure. The method was implemented on a standard three-jaw modular fixture with shimmed support pads. Over a trial batch of 20 parts, mean flatness deviation of the finished panel was reduced from 38 μm to 16 μm relative to a baseline without compensation. The structured-light scan added approximately 4 minutes per part to total setup time. Discussion covers the trade-off between compensation fidelity and setup overhead for small and medium batch sizes.

title: Data-driven identification of critical locator positions using machining error measurements from a production cell
abstract: Historical CMM data from 840 parts machined over six months in an automotive production cell were used to identify which of eleven fixture locators most strongly correlated with out-of-tolerance events. A partial-correlation analysis was performed between each locator's estimated contact force—inferred from strain gauges installed on three support pads—and dimensional deviations at four critical features per part. Two primary locators on the bottom datum surface showed partial correlations above 0.6 with bore-position errors, while the remaining locators showed correlations below 0.2. An FE influence matrix built for the housing workpiece confirmed that these two locators govern the compliance response at the critical bores. Replacing the two conventional support pads with adjustable hydraulic pads and setting a target clamping force of 850 N reduced the monthly non-conformance rate from 3.2% to 0.8%. The paper demonstrates that passive production data can guide model-informed fixture modification without dedicated experiments.

title: Cartographic Evidence for Settlement Abandonment in the Southern Banat Wetland Margins, 1780–1880
abstract: Using five successive topographic survey series—the First, Second, and Third Military Surveys of the Habsburg Empire together with two mid-nineteenth-century civilian cadastral editions—this paper reconstructs the contraction and disappearance of 27 seasonal and permanent settlements along the former Tamiš river margins in southern Banat between 1780 and 1880. Settlement outlines, road networks, and building clusters were georeferenced and overlaid in a GIS environment, allowing measurement of built footprint areas across the five time slices. Results show a reduction of total identified built area from approximately 48 hectares in 1780 to under 12 hectares by 1880, concentrated in nine consolidated villages. The paper discusses hydraulic engineering works, military border reorganisation, and malaria as compounding factors driving abandonment. Archival correspondence from the Timișoara regional administration is cited to contextualise demographic data. The methodology is proposed as transferable to similar wetland-edge settlement studies elsewhere in the Carpathian Basin.

title: Roof Form Variation in Vernacular Houses of the Tisza River Corridor: A Photographic and Measured Survey
abstract: A systematic photographic and measured survey of 162 surviving pre-1918 rural dwellings along a 120-kilometre stretch of the Tisza corridor in northern Serbia and southern Hungary was conducted during field campaigns in 2013 and 2014. Roof pitch, ridge orientation, eave height, and material (thatch remnants, fibre cement replacement, or original ceramic tile) were recorded for each structure. Statistical grouping revealed three dominant roof form clusters: low-pitched hipped roofs (42%), gabled roofs with steep pitch (35%), and transitional half-hipped variants (23%). A geographic pattern was observed, with hipped forms prevailing south of Senta and gabled forms more frequent north of the Serbian–Hungarian administrative boundary. The paper argues that the boundary does not reflect any historical administrative division and that the distribution likely relates to differing carpentry guild traditions active during the reconstruction period following the 1830s drainage works. Twenty-six structures recorded in the 1960s photographic archive of the Museum of Vojvodina could be located and re-photographed, enabling a partial longitudinal comparison of condition change.

title: Measuring Deformation in Earthen Wall Construction: Photogrammetric Monitoring of Six Pisé Farmhouses in Vojvodina
abstract: Six farmhouses built with rammed earth (pisé) walls in the period 1870–1920, located in three municipalities in central Vojvodina, were monitored using close-range photogrammetry over two survey campaigns separated by eighteen months (2016 and 2018). Dense point clouds were generated from terrestrial image sets captured with a calibrated medium-format camera, and difference maps between the two epochs were computed to identify areas of measurable displacement or surface loss. Detected displacement exceeded 5 mm in 34 discrete zones across the six buildings, concentrated at sill level and at the base of openings. One structure showed a continuous horizontal crack consistent with differential foundation settlement of approximately 12 mm. The paper presents the processing workflow, discusses sources of error in epoch-to-epoch comparison, and proposes a simplified monitoring protocol suitable for municipal heritage offices with limited equipment budgets. The data confirm that visual inspection alone underestimates active deformation in earthen wall buildings.

title: Building Material Zones in the Pannonian Agricultural Landscape: A Macro-Scale Reading of Cadastral and Census Data, 1869–1910
abstract: Habsburg-era census summaries and cadastral descriptions for 178 settlements across present-day Vojvodina, southern Hungary, and eastern Croatia were digitised and geocoded to map the distribution of dominant building materials—adobe brick, fired brick, timber frame, and rammed earth—at the settlement level for the census years 1869, 1880, 1900, and 1910. The resulting GIS dataset reveals a clear transition zone running roughly north-northwest to south-southeast, east of which fired brick becomes dominant earlier (by 1880) correlating with proximity to established brickyards along main waterways. Adobe brick maintains a higher share in settlements more than 30 kilometres from rail infrastructure through 1910. The paper discusses the limitations of census material categories, including inconsistent local classification of mixed-wall construction. A supplementary table lists the 178 settlements, their sources, and the coded material percentages for each census year. The findings provide a baseline for interpreting the survival rates of earthen and timber vernacular structures today.

title: Documenting the Stajić Estate at Čerević: Archival Reconstruction and Current Condition Assessment
abstract: The Stajić estate at Čerević on the Fruška Gora slopes is a late nineteenth-century Serbian merchant family estate comprising a residential villa, two utility buildings, a walled garden, and a partly surviving orchard terrace. The paper presents a documentation campaign combining archival research in the Museum of Vojvodina and the Historical Archive of Sremska Mitrovica, terrestrial photogrammetry, and hand-measured drawings produced in 2021. Retrieved archival material includes a partial set of construction drawings dated 1897 and two historic photographs from approximately 1920. Comparison between the 1897 drawings and current survey reveals the demolition of a northern wing and the infilling of a loggia on the garden facade. The current condition assessment identifies structural cracking in the basement retaining wall, moisture damage across 60% of the interior plaster surfaces, and complete loss of the original joinery in secondary rooms. The estate is listed as a category III cultural monument and the paper provides a metric basis for a future conservation management plan.

title: Self-monitoring patterns in adult distance learners: a preliminary survey in rural Vojvodina
abstract: This paper reports baseline data on self-monitoring behaviours among 214 adult learners enrolled in distance continuing-education programmes offered through two higher education institutions in Vojvodina. Participants completed a Serbian-language adaptation of the Metacognitive Awareness Inventory at the start and end of a single semester. Rural respondents (defined by municipality population below 10,000) scored significantly lower on procedural self-monitoring sub-scales than their urban peers (p < .03, Cohen's d = 0.41), while no statistically significant difference emerged on declarative knowledge sub-scales. Qualitative follow-up interviews with 18 participants suggested that irregular internet access and occupational unpredictability were the primary disruptors of planned study routines. The study argues that instrument adaptation and context-sensitive baselines are necessary preconditions for any longitudinal intervention targeting this population, and outlines a measurement protocol subsequently used in the authors' later work.

title: Designing for reflection: a framework for structuring embedded prompts in instructional video for adult learners
abstract: Drawing on a review of 63 empirical studies published between 2000 and 2013, this book chapter synthesises evidence on the placement, phrasing, and density of reflective prompts embedded within instructional video. The chapter distinguishes between pre-video orienting prompts, mid-video pause-and-write prompts, and post-video consolidation tasks, evaluating each against outcomes including comprehension, transfer, and self-reported metacognitive activity. Evidence is strongest for mid-video prompts placed at conceptual boundaries rather than fixed time intervals, and for prompts that invite learners to connect new content to prior experience rather than simply summarise. The chapter proposes a four-component design framework—Activate, Encounter, Interrogate, Consolidate—and discusses feasibility constraints specific to low-bandwidth rural delivery contexts. Practical guidelines for practitioners working within resource-constrained institutions are provided, along with a checklist instrument intended for formative evaluation of existing video materials.

title: Video replay frequency as an indicator of self-regulatory effort: an LMS log analysis
abstract: This study examined whether learners' voluntary replay behaviour within an asynchronous video-based course predicts end-of-course metacognitive regulation scores and academic achievement. Log data were extracted from a Moodle installation serving 187 adult learners across three distance courses at the Faculty of Education in Sombor over one academic year. Replay events were classified as full-segment replays, partial scrub-backs under 30 seconds, and chapter-marker revisits. Hierarchical regression analysis showed that chapter-marker revisits uniquely predicted metacognitive regulation scores (β = 0.29, p = .008) after controlling for prior academic achievement and device type, while full-segment replays were negatively associated with final grades (β = −0.18, p = .04). Rural learners produced significantly fewer replay events overall (t(185) = 3.12, p = .002), which the authors attribute to data-cost management rather than lower engagement. Implications for dashboard design and adaptive release strategies are discussed.

title: Two-year trajectories of metacognitive regulation among adult distance learners exposed to structured video instruction: a longitudinal cohort study
abstract: This paper presents the first two waves of a planned four-wave longitudinal study tracking metacognitive regulation in a cohort of 143 adult learners enrolled in distance teacher-training courses. Participants completed the Serbian Metacognitive Regulation Scale (SMRS) at enrolment and again twelve months later. The SMRS comprises three sub-scales: planning, monitoring, and evaluation. Mixed-effects growth models showed significant improvement in monitoring (b = 0.31, SE = 0.08, p < .001) and evaluation (b = 0.22, SE = 0.09, p = .015) over twelve months among learners in courses that used structured video modules with embedded prompts, compared to negligible change in a matched comparison group using text-based materials. Planning sub-scale scores did not differ between groups. Effect sizes were modest (conditional R² = 0.19). Attrition analysis indicated that rural participants dropped out at a higher rate (28 % vs. 14 %), introducing potential bias discussed in detail. The design and instrument are described fully to facilitate replication.

title: Perceived video quality and its relationship to metacognitive engagement: learner reports from low-connectivity rural settings
abstract: Forty-two adult distance learners in rural municipalities of Vojvodina and Mačva participated in semi-structured interviews examining how buffering interruptions, low resolution, and audio distortion influenced their willingness to engage in reflective activities while watching instructional video. Interview transcripts were analysed using thematic analysis following Braun and Clarke's six-phase procedure. Four themes emerged: interruption-induced disengagement, compensatory note-taking, avoidance of embedded prompt tasks under poor conditions, and retrospective reflection after connectivity improved. Participants described a clear threshold effect: brief buffering (under 5 seconds) was tolerated without disrupting reflection, whereas longer interruptions caused most participants to abandon the current segment entirely and rarely return. These findings suggest that technical delivery quality should be treated as an independent variable in intervention studies, not a background assumption. Recommendations for adaptive streaming and offline-download options are offered.

title: Reviewing a decade of longitudinal research on technology-mediated metacognition in adult distance education: a scoping review
abstract: This scoping review synthesises 47 empirical studies published between 2013 and 2023 that used longitudinal designs (minimum two measurement points, minimum six months apart) to examine technology-mediated metacognitive outcomes in adult distance learners. Studies were identified through four databases and screened independently by two reviewers; inter-rater agreement was κ = 0.81. Included studies are distributed across 19 countries, with marked underrepresentation of South-Eastern and Eastern European contexts. The majority used self-report instruments only (72 %); combined log-data and self-report designs remain rare (19 %). Effect sizes where reported ranged from d = 0.11 to d = 0.73 for monitoring outcomes, with substantial heterogeneity. Key gaps include insufficient attention to rural access conditions, near-complete absence of studies tracking learners beyond two years, and limited replication across cultural contexts. The review closes with a proposed minimum reporting standard for future longitudinal studies in this area.

title: Everyday metacognitive talk: how adult distance learners in rural settings describe their regulation strategies in WhatsApp study groups
abstract: This preprint reports a discourse analysis of 1,840 messages exchanged in six WhatsApp groups formed spontaneously by adult distance learners enrolled in a teacher-continuing-education programme. Groups ranged from 5 to 11 members; all participants resided in rural municipalities. Messages were collected over one semester with informed consent and coded using a scheme derived from the SMRS sub-scale definitions. Planning-related talk accounted for 38 % of metacognitive utterances, monitoring for 44 %, and evaluation for 18 %. Peer monitoring prompts—messages in which one learner explicitly questioned another's understanding—were positively correlated with individual SMRS monitoring scores at semester end (r = 0.41, p = .007). The data suggest that informal peer communication channels carry metacognitive regulation functions that do not appear in LMS logs, and that these channels may partially compensate for reduced instructor presence in rural delivery contexts. Full coded dataset is attached as supplementary material.

title: Effect of moisture content on the gelatinisation behaviour of wheat starch during single-screw extrusion at low feed rates
abstract: Wheat starch was extruded using a single-screw extruder at moisture contents of 18, 22, 26, and 30 wt% and barrel temperatures between 100 and 160 °C. Degree of gelatinisation was quantified by differential scanning calorimetry on extrudate cross-sections, comparing residual enthalpy with that of unprocessed starch. At 22 wt% moisture and 140 °C, gelatinisation exceeded 91%, while at 18 wt% it reached only 73% under identical thermal conditions. X-ray diffraction patterns confirmed progressive loss of the A-type crystalline structure with increasing moisture and temperature. Specific mechanical energy input correlated positively with degree of gelatinisation (R² = 0.87). Extrudate expansion ratio increased from 1.4 to 2.1 as moisture decreased from 30 to 18 wt%. These results establish baseline processing windows for subsequent blend studies and indicate that moisture content is a stronger determinant of gelatinisation completeness than barrel temperature within the ranges tested.

title: Melt viscosity of thermoplastic starch plasticised with glycerol and sorbitol: a twin-screw extrusion study
abstract: Thermoplastic starch (TPS) was prepared from corn starch plasticised with glycerol (15, 20, 25 wt%) and sorbitol (10, 15 wt%) in a co-rotating twin-screw extruder. In-line melt viscosity was measured using a slit-die rheometer mounted at the die exit, operating at apparent shear rates from 10 to 500 s⁻¹. Power-law fitting yielded consistency indices between 1 800 and 4 400 Pa·sⁿ and flow behaviour indices between 0.28 and 0.41, confirming strong shear-thinning character. Increasing total plasticiser content from 25 to 35 wt% reduced the consistency index by approximately 38%. Sorbitol-containing blends showed higher consistency indices than pure glycerol formulations at equivalent plasticiser levels, attributed to lower molecular mobility at processing temperatures. Off-line tensile testing showed elongation at break increasing from 42 to 118% as glycerol content rose from 15 to 25 wt%. The in-line approach reduced sample loss compared to off-line capillary rheometry and provided continuous steady-state data over 30-minute runs.

title: Quantifying starch gelatinisation during reactive extrusion: comparison of DSC, XRD and in-line near-infrared spectroscopy
abstract: Three analytical approaches for quantifying gelatinisation of corn starch during twin-screw extrusion were compared: off-line DSC (residual enthalpy method), off-line XRD (crystallinity index by Ruland–Vonk integration), and in-line near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy using a fibre-optic probe inserted into the barrel at the metering zone. Extrudates were collected at barrel temperatures of 110, 130, 150, and 170 °C at fixed moisture (24 wt%) and screw speed (150 rpm). DSC and XRD results agreed within ±4 percentage points across all conditions, both showing full gelatinisation above 150 °C. The in-line NIR signal at 2 100 nm (associated with starch–water hydrogen bonding) showed a monotonic decrease with increasing barrel temperature and correlated with DSC gelatinisation degree with R² = 0.93 after partial least squares calibration using 40 extrudate samples. NIR response lagged behind set-point temperature changes by approximately 18 s, consistent with the estimated mean residence time in that barrel zone. The calibration model transferred to wheat starch with acceptable prediction error (RMSEP = 3.8%), suggesting moderate cross-crop applicability.

title: Influence of extrusion processing parameters on the oxygen barrier of starch–pea protein composite sheets: a practical guide for packaging line scale-up
abstract: Reactive extrusion and biopolymer barrier properties for food packaging are reviewed with focus on starch–protein systems. This chapter covers the physical chemistry of starch gelatinisation and protein denaturation under thermomechanical stress, in-line measurement strategies including slit-die rheometry and fibre-optic NIR spectroscopy, and methods for relating processing parameters to oxygen and water vapour barrier performance of the resulting sheets. Practical guidelines are provided for screw design selection, barrel temperature profiling, and moisture management. Data from pilot-scale (11-kg/h throughput) and laboratory-scale (2-kg/h) systems are compared to illustrate scale-up challenges: specific mechanical energy decreased by 23% at pilot scale at equivalent screw speed and temperature, necessitating adjusted barrel temperature profiles to maintain equivalent gelatinisation degrees. The chapter concludes with a decision framework for formulators selecting between single-step reactive extrusion and two-step blending followed by compression moulding, based on required property targets and available equipment.

title: Effect of nanoclay addition on melt flow and film permeability of reactively extruded corn starch–whey protein blends
abstract: Montmorillonite nanoclay (Cloisite Na⁺ type, surface-treated with aminopropyltriethoxysilane) was incorporated at 1, 3, and 5 wt% into corn starch–whey protein concentrate blends (80:20 w/w) during reactive twin-screw extrusion. X-ray diffraction of extrudates showed intercalated structures at 1 and 3 wt% clay (d-spacing increase from 1.18 to 1.54 nm) and partially exfoliated morphology at 3 wt% as confirmed by TEM. In-line melt viscosity at 100 s⁻¹ increased by 18% at 3 wt% clay compared to clay-free blends. Compression-moulded films at 3 wt% clay showed WVTR reductions of 34% and OTR reductions of 41% relative to unfilled blend, measured at 23 °C and 50% RH. Tensile strength increased from 13.2 to 17.6 MPa, while elongation at break decreased from 38 to 22%. At 5 wt% clay, agglomerate formation reduced barrier improvement and caused surface defects in films. Thermogravimetric analysis showed onset degradation temperature rising by 8 °C at 3 wt% clay.

title: In-line monitoring of starch conversion during reactive extrusion using ultrasonic velocity measurements: feasibility and calibration
abstract: Ultrasonic pulse velocity (UPV) sensors were mounted on the barrel of a co-rotating twin-screw extruder to monitor melt density and conversion state of corn starch at three axial positions. Measurements were taken continuously at 10 Hz during extrusion of TPS at moisture contents of 20–30 wt% and barrel temperatures of 120–160 °C. Ultrasonic velocity correlated with melt density (R² = 0.89) and inversely with melt temperature-corrected specific volume estimated from off-line pycnometry. A partial least squares model calibrated against DSC-measured gelatinisation degrees of 40 offline-sampled extrudate sections yielded RMSECV of 4.1 percentage points in cross-validation. Signal quality was acceptable above 130 °C but deteriorated in zones with significant air entrainment near the feed throat. Comparison with the previously validated NIR approach showed comparable prediction accuracy but better robustness to formulation changes: when the model was tested on a pea protein–starch blend not included in calibration, the UPV model gave RMSEP of 5.6% versus 9.1% for NIR. The technique requires no optical access and may be more suitable for industrial installation.

title: An Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter for State Estimation with Randomly Missing Measurements in Linear Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of state estimation in discrete-time linear systems when sensor readings are lost according to a Bernoulli dropout model with unknown and possibly time-varying dropout probability. An adaptive Extended Kalman Filter (AEKF) is derived in which the measurement noise covariance matrix is updated online using a sliding-window innovation sequence. The estimator is validated on a two-tank laboratory hydraulic process with artificially induced packet losses at rates between 10 % and 40 %. At a 30 % dropout rate the proposed AEKF reduces root-mean-square state-estimation error by 18 % relative to a standard EKF with fixed covariance. The paper also provides a stability analysis based on the conditional Riccati recursion under Bernoulli observations, showing mean-square boundedness for dropout rates below a derived threshold. Simulation results over 5 000 Monte Carlo runs confirm the analytical bounds. The method is intended as a lightweight baseline suitable for implementation on embedded controllers with limited computational resources.

title: State Estimation Under Intermittent Observability: Survey and Taxonomy
abstract: Intermittent observability arises when measurements reach an estimator irregularly due to network packet loss, sensor failure, or deliberate scheduling. This book chapter surveys the theoretical and applied literature on the topic, organising contributions into four categories: (i) stochastic dropout models and their effect on Riccati-equation stability, (ii) scheduled and event-triggered sensing strategies that trade communication load against estimation accuracy, (iii) hybrid approaches that couple model-based filters with data-driven imputation, and (iv) application domains including networked control, smart grids, and autonomous vehicles. The chapter identifies open problems, particularly the lack of principled methods for selecting imputation strategy based on gap statistics and system dynamics, and discusses evaluation protocols and benchmark datasets available to the community. Approximately 140 references are covered, spanning work from 2000 to 2018.

title: Long Short-Term Memory Networks for Gap Filling in Wind-Power Generation Time Series: Sensitivity to Gap Length and Training Window
abstract: Short gaps in wind-power generation measurements are routinely handled by interpolation, but gaps exceeding one hour are common during communication outages and require a model-aware approach. This paper trains LSTM networks on data from three wind farms in Serbia and northern Romania, covering 26 months of ten-minute averaged active-power output alongside meteorological variables. A systematic experiment varies gap length from 10 minutes to 6 hours and training-window size from 30 to 180 days. Results show that LSTM outperforms linear interpolation and autoregressive models for gaps longer than 40 minutes, reducing normalised RMSE by 14–31 % depending on season and meteorological regime. Performance degrades noticeably when training data do not cover the season of the gap; a simple online fine-tuning step using the 48 hours preceding each gap partially recovers this loss. The study quantifies the trade-off between model retraining frequency and error reduction.

title: Combining Interacting Multiple Models with Neural-Network Likelihood Approximation for Fault Detection in Smart Metering Infrastructure
abstract: Smart meters occasionally transmit corrupted or entirely missing readings that, if undetected, propagate errors into billing and grid-state estimation. This paper integrates an Interacting Multiple Model (IMM) filter with a feedforward neural network that approximates the innovation likelihood in place of the analytical Gaussian expression. The hybrid estimator runs four parallel models corresponding to normal operation, communication fault, meter hardware fault, and temporary voltage anomaly. The neural-network component is pre-trained on labelled fault episodes extracted from a 36-month archive of hourly smart-meter readings from a residential district in Novi Sad, comprising 1 840 meters. On a held-out test set the hybrid IMM achieves an F1-score of 0.87 for fault-type classification, compared with 0.74 for a Gaussian IMM baseline. Fault-detection latency is reduced from a median of 3 time steps to 1 time step. Computational cost per time step is evaluated on a Raspberry Pi 4 to assess embedded deployability.

title: Event-Triggered Kalman Filtering with Data-Driven Threshold Selection for Battery Management in Microgrids
abstract: In battery energy storage systems (BESS) used in islanded microgrids, continuous transmission of cell-voltage and temperature measurements strains the communication channel. Event-triggered filtering sends measurements only when the innovation exceeds a threshold, but fixed-threshold policies perform poorly under varying load profiles. This paper proposes a policy-gradient reinforcement learning agent that adapts the triggering threshold online based on recent estimation-error history and channel occupancy. The combined event-triggered Kalman filter and RL agent is tested on a 48 V, 30 kWh lithium iron phosphate battery bank connected to a laboratory microgrid testbed at the Faculty of Technical Sciences. Over 14 days of realistic load-profile experiments, the adaptive policy reduced communication events by 38 % relative to a fixed-threshold policy while maintaining maximum state-of-charge estimation error below 1.8 %. The paper analyses stability of the closed-loop estimation loop using a Lyapunov-based argument under bounded inter-event times.
