title: Sliding-Mode Current Control of a Boost Converter Feeding a Constant-Power Load: Stability Analysis and Experimental Validation
abstract: Constant-power loads (CPLs) introduce a negative incremental impedance into DC distribution systems, destabilising converters designed under linear assumptions. This paper presents a sliding-mode controller (SMC) for a boost converter supplying a CPL, where the sliding surface is constructed from the inductor current error and a weighted integral of the output voltage error. A reachability condition is derived analytically using Filippov's method, and a large-signal Lyapunov function is proposed to estimate the domain of attraction as a function of converter parameters and CPL power level. The controller is implemented on a dSPACE DS1104 platform connected to a 200 W laboratory prototype with a 48 V output bus. Experimental results show that the SMC maintains output voltage regulation within ±1.2% under CPL step changes from 50 W to 180 W, outperforming a PI baseline whose overshoot exceeds 8% under the same transient. Switching frequency variation is characterised and kept within a ±4 kHz band around 50 kHz through a hysteresis boundary adjustment scheme. The findings confirm that the derived domain-of-attraction estimate is conservative by roughly 15% compared to measured stability boundaries.

title: Interconnection and Damping Assignment Passivity-Based Control for a Bidirectional Buck-Boost Converter in a Battery-PV Microgrid
abstract: This paper applies interconnection and damping assignment passivity-based control (IDA-PBC) to a bidirectional buck-boost converter that interfaces a lithium-iron-phosphate battery bank with a 48 V DC bus in a laboratory-scale photovoltaic microgrid. The converter model is expressed as a port-Hamiltonian system, and the desired closed-loop Hamiltonian is shaped by solving the matching equations numerically for a set of operating points spanning 10–90% state of charge. Damping injection is tuned to place the dominant closed-loop poles at a natural frequency of 800 Hz with a damping ratio of 0.7. A comparison with a conventional PI current controller is carried out under three scenarios: solar irradiance ramp (200 to 900 W/m² over 5 s), CPL connection (100 W step), and battery charge-to-discharge transition. The IDA-PBC controller reduces bus voltage deviation by 38% during CPL connection and eliminates the 12 ms oscillatory transient observed with the PI controller during mode transitions. All tests are conducted on a 300 W hardware prototype; control execution runs at 20 kHz on an STM32H7 microcontroller.

title: Comparative Assessment of Nonlinear Control Methods for DC-DC Converters Under Constant-Power Loading: A Simulation Study
abstract: Four nonlinear control strategies—sliding-mode control (SMC), feedback linearisation (FL), IDA-PBC, and active disturbance rejection control (ADRC)—are systematically compared for a boost converter supplying a CPL rated at 0–250 W on a 48 V bus. All controllers are implemented in MATLAB/Simulink using averaged and switched converter models. Performance metrics include settling time, peak voltage deviation, steady-state error, and robustness to ±20% parameter variation in inductance and capacitance. Simulation sweeps cover CPL power levels from 50 W to 230 W in 20 W steps. SMC achieves the shortest settling time (1.8 ms) but exhibits the highest sensitivity to inductor current measurement noise. IDA-PBC shows the best parameter robustness, with voltage deviation below 3% across all tested inductance variations, while FL degrades noticeably when the CPL power exceeds 80% of the rated converter power. ADRC offers a compromise but requires careful bandwidth selection. The paper provides a decision framework linking converter operating conditions to the preferred control strategy and identifies parameter ranges where each method is preferable. Results are intended to guide controller selection in low-voltage microgrid design.

title: Adaptive Sliding Surface for a DC-DC Converter Microgrid Node: Handling Variable Constant-Power Load Profiles from EV Charging
abstract: Electric vehicle (EV) chargers connected to a DC microgrid bus exhibit dynamic CPL behaviour whose power demand varies over a wide range and at rates that fixed-gain controllers handle poorly. This work proposes an adaptive sliding-mode controller in which the sliding surface coefficients are updated online by a model reference adaptive scheme driven by the voltage tracking error. The adaptation law is derived using Lyapunov's second method, ensuring convergence of the coefficient estimates. The controller is validated on a 500 W buck converter prototype connected to a programmable electronic load programmed with a recorded EV charging profile (CHAdeMO-equivalent current waveform, 0–10 kW equivalent, scaled to testbed ratings). Over a 300 s test sequence, the adaptive SMC keeps the bus voltage within ±1.5 V of the 48 V setpoint, compared to ±4.3 V for a fixed-surface SMC tuned at nominal conditions. Adaptation transient time after a large power step (150 W in 20 ms) is 11 ms. Computational load on the dSPACE DS1104 is 34 µs per control cycle at 20 kHz, leaving sufficient margin for additional supervisory functions.

title: Passivity-Based Droop Control for Parallel DC-DC Converters in a Low-Voltage Microgrid with Mixed Load Types
abstract: Parallel operation of multiple DC-DC converters in a microgrid requires coordinated current sharing alongside tight voltage regulation. This paper formulates a droop control law within the IDA-PBC framework so that current sharing and bus voltage objectives are encoded directly in the desired Hamiltonian. Two 200 W boost converter modules are operated in parallel on a 48 V bus supplying a mixed load composed of a resistive component (60 W) and a CPL (up to 120 W). The interaction between the droop coefficients and the closed-loop passivity condition is analysed, and a feasibility region in the droop-gain/damping-injection parameter space is identified. Hardware experiments demonstrate load sharing error below 4% across the full CPL range and a bus voltage deviation under 1 V during simultaneous CPL step and resistive load connection. Interactions between the two converter control loops are characterised via impedance measurements using a Bode 100 analyser, confirming stable phase and gain margins of 45° and 8 dB respectively at the worst-case operating point.

title: Procena referentne evapotranspiracije primenom metode FAO Penman-Monteith u uslovima ograničenih meteoroloških podataka u Vojvodini
abstract: Metoda FAO Penman-Monteith (FAO-PM) smatra se standardnim pristupom za procenu referentne evapotranspiracije (ETo), ali zahteva niz meteoroloških ulaznih podataka koji u praksi često nisu dostupni. U radu je ispitana mogućnost zamene nedostajućih podataka o vlažnosti vazduha i brzini vetra vrednostima preuzetim iz regionalne klimatološke baze za period 2000–2011. na osam meteoroloških stanica u Vojvodini. Rezultati su upoređeni sa merenjima na lizimetarskoj stanici u Rimskim Šančevima. Utvrđeno je da zamena podataka o vlažnosti klimatološkim prosecima unosi grešku ETo od prosečno 4,1% na mesečnom nivou, dok zamena podataka o brzini vetra povećava grešku na 7,8%. Kombinovana zamena oba parametra daje ukupnu mesečnu grešku ispod 9%, što se ocenjuje prihvatljivim za potrebe operativnog zakazivanja navodnjavanja. Preporučuje se primena korekcijskih faktora izvedenih za svaku stanicu posebno.

title: Modeliranje vodnog bilansa parcele soje primenom modela CROPWAT 8.0 i verifikacija na osnovu terenskih merenja vlažnosti zemljišta
abstract: U radu je prikazana primena modela CROPWAT 8.0 za simulaciju dekadnog vodnog bilansa parcele soje (sorta NS Maximus) tokom vegetacijske sezone 2015. godine na području Bačke. Ulazni meteorološki podaci preuzeti su sa automatske stanice u Bečeju, a karakteristike zemljišta određene su laboratorijskim analizama uzoraka sa dubine do 90 cm. Simulirani sadržaj vode u zemljištu upoređen je sa FDR merenjima na četiri dubine u nedeljnim intervalima. Modelom je u proseku precenjen sadržaj vode za 6,4 mm u fazi vegetativnog porasta, što se pripisuje izostanku parametrizacije kapilarnog uspona u modelu. Primenom korekcije na osnovu pedotransfernih funkcija za glinasta ilovača tla, greška je smanjena na 3,1 mm. Zaključuje se da CROPWAT može biti pouzdan alat za operativno navodnjavnje u regionu uz adekvatno podešavanje parametara tla.

title: Prostorna interpolacija referentne evapotranspiracije u Vojvodini korišćenjem kriging metode i digitalnog modela reljefa
abstract: Referentna evapotranspiracija (ETo) procenjena metodom FAO-PM izračunata je na osnovu dnevnih podataka sa mreže od 12 meteoroloških stanica u Vojvodini za period 2010–2019. Na osnovu godišnjih suma ETo izvršena je prostorna interpolacija primenom obične kriging metode i kriging sa spoljašnjim trendom, gde je nadmorska visina iz digitalnog modela reljefa (SRTM, 30 m) korišćena kao pomoćna promenljiva. Unakrsna validacija pokazala je da kriging sa spoljašnjim trendom daje RMSE od 11,3 mm/godišnje ETo, u poređenju sa 18,7 mm kod obične kriging metode. Razlike u prostornoj raspodeli ETo unutar ravničarskog dela Vojvodine su relativno male (maksimalna amplituda 42 mm/god.), ali postaju značajne u pojasu Fruške Gore (razlika do 87 mm/god.), što ukazuje na potrebu za zasebnom parametrizacijom pri regionalnom planiranju navodnjavanja.

title: Sensitivity of FAO-PM evapotranspiration estimates to systematic biases in input climate variables: a Monte Carlo approach applied to Pannonian lowland conditions
abstract: Systematic measurement biases in temperature, humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation affect the accuracy of FAO Penman-Monteith evapotranspiration (ETo) calculations, but their relative importance under Pannonian lowland climate conditions has not been quantified comprehensively. A Monte Carlo framework was constructed in which each of the four input variables was independently perturbed with normally distributed errors parameterised from documented sensor calibration uncertainties. A total of 10,000 realisations were run for each of three representative months (April, July, October) using baseline data from Novi Sad station (2010–2022). Results indicate that ETo is most sensitive to air temperature biases in spring (a +1 °C bias causes a +3.8% change in monthly ETo), while wind speed biases dominate uncertainty in summer months (a +0.5 m/s bias causes +6.2%). Relative humidity biases contribute less than 2.5% across all months under the tested range. These findings support prioritisation of anemometer maintenance in operational agrometeorological networks used for irrigation advisory services.

title: Procena efekta malčiranja na smanjenje evaporacije iz zemljišta i ukupnih potreba za navodnjavanjem paprike u uslovima Bačke
abstract: Terenski ogled sproveden je tokom dve vegetacijske sezone (2023. i 2024.) na Oglednom polju Rimski Šančevi s ciljem kvantifikacije uticaja polietilenskog malča na evaporaciju iz zemljišta i potrebe za navodnjavanjem paprike (Capsicum annuum L., sorta Zlatni medal). Postavljeno je šest tretmana u tri ponavljanja: crni PE malč, beli PE malč i kontrola (bez malča), uz dve norme navodnjavanja (puno i ograničeno – 70% ET). Evaporacija iz zemljišta procenjena je primenom jednačine FAO-56 dvofaznog modela, a vlažnost zemljišta praćena FDR sondama. U prvoj godini, crni malč smanjio je sezonu evaporacije za 41% u poređenju sa kontrolom; u drugoj godini efekat je iznosio 37%. Ukupna norma navodnjavanja pri punoj ET bila je manja za 58 mm (crni malč) i 41 mm (beli malč) u odnosu na kontrolu. Prinos paprike u tretmanu crni malč–puna ET bio je za 12% viši od kontrole.
